source: Frozen 2 Forest of Shadows (Kamilla Benko) (z-library.sk, 1lib.sk, z-lib.sk).epub

chapters.title: 序章
chapters.en:
THE SKY WAS AWAKE, and so was the forest.

Anna of Arendelle hugged her cloak tight as the bare branches clacked like teeth above her and the wind tugged at her braids. She peered into a bush. As far as she knew, bushes weren’t supposed to have eyes. But then again, five-year-old princesses weren’t supposed to be alone outside the castle at night, either. And yet here she was…although Anna hadn’t started off the night alone. Her sister, Elsa, was somewhere out here in the snowy woods, too. Possibly hiding in the very bush that Anna tiptoed closer to at this moment.

Three years older than Anna, with wide blue eyes and a shy smile, Elsa was the kind of girl who could sit for hours without swinging her legs and whose tidy white-blond plait always hung straight down her back. Grown-ups often remarked how well-behaved Anna’s big sister was…but they didn’t know Elsa the way Anna did. Underneath the polite and poised exterior was a mischievous sense of fun. All Elsa needed was an excuse, and Anna was happy to be just that: Elsa’s excuse to slip into her cloak and sneak out of the castle to build a snowman and play hide-and-find under the northern lights. Which was exactly what they were doing now. Elsa had already found Anna in a tree’s hollow, but Anna had been looking for Elsa for what seemed like forever…or at least five minutes.

The leaves rustled again, and Anna clapped her hands over her mouth to stop a giggle from escaping. Yes, there was definitely someone watching her from the snow-covered thicket. Holding her breath, she stepped closer. She was pretty sure it was Elsa, but there was always a chance it could be a Huldrefólk, one of the rumored hidden people who dwelled in the streams, under the rocks, and in the bedtime stories told by their mother, Queen Iduna. Anna’s heart beat faster. If it was a Huldrefólk, she just had to see their tail. She’d always wondered if their tails were flowing like a horse’s, or bushy like a fox’s, or long and skinny like a mouse’s.

But Anna had a feeling she knew who the figure hiding behind the bush was. Anna parted the leaves, and in the colorful glow of the dancing sky, she caught a glimpse of blond hair. So, not a Huldrefólk. Just a sister.

Laughing, Anna shook the bush. “I found you! Your turn to be the Crusty Troll!”

Elsa didn’t respond.

“I said, I found you.” Anna peered through the foliage. “It’s my turn to hide—that’s the rule. Come on out!”

Anna’s sister turned her head, and that’s when Anna realized her mistake. It wasn’t blond hair she had spotted in the shifting light.

It was white fur.

Anna’s scream stuck in her throat as a giant white wolf prowled out from the thicket with unusual grace, its long limbs uncurling like smoke. Its fierce yellow gaze fixed on her, and Anna’s eyes ran down its huge, horse-sized body…to see four fearsome paws, each the size of one of the large shields of her father, King Agnarr. But that wasn’t the worst of it.

No, the worst was the red-stained fur around its claws and jaw.

Red. The color of blood.

What had happened to her sister?

“Elsa!” Anna screamed. “Where are you?”

The wolf leapt.

Anna ran.

Her heart slammed in her chest, each breath a sharp knife as she tried to run faster, and faster—but she knew she couldn’t outrun a wolf. Spotting a fallen log, she dove behind it, her knees tucked to her chest as she tried to make herself as small as possible. Though her lungs ached for air, Anna held her breath, not wanting to give herself away with even the tiniest exhale. One second passed, then another, and another. Had she lost the wolf?

Snow fell thick and silent. Anna shivered, wishing she’d listened to Elsa when she’d told her not to wear her most beautiful green cloak but to put on her everyday thick woolly brown one instead.

Elsa. Where was Elsa?

As quiet as a shadow, Anna peered around the log, half expecting to come nose-to-snout with the wolf. Instead, all she saw was an army of trees casting ghastly shadows onto the snow-covered ground. And as the wind picked up, so did Anna’s ice-cold fear. If she walked through the fresh snow, the wolf would be able to see exactly which direction she’d gone. And if she didn’t walk through the snow…she might never find her sister.

Red on white.

Blood on fur.

Anna couldn’t stay behind the log forever. Peeling off her cloak, she arranged it on the ground, bunching it into the shape of a five-year-old girl taking a nap. Then she moved into a crouching position. So far, so good. She took a slow, steady step backward. And then another, and another, carefully weaving her way in reverse between the trees, the same way the Huldrefólk in her mother’s bedtime stories were said to travel so they could keep their tails hidden. But Anna didn’t have a tail to hide. Instead, she was leaving a fresh trail of footprints in the snow—footprints that would always lead away from where she actually was.

“Elsa,” she whispered, “you’ve won hide-and-find. Please come out.”

But still there was no reply. The snow fell faster, so Anna moved faster, darting between trees, diving behind boulders, and all the while scanning the snowy woods for a sign of her sister—any sign. But there was not a footprint to be seen. It was as though her sister had been erased. As though…but the thought was too horrible for Anna to finish.

From somewhere nearby, the wolf howled.

Anna froze. She knew that sound. It was the same sound her father’s hunting dogs made when they’d picked up the scent of a fox. The wolf howled again, but this time it was a little farther away. Anna’s decoy had worked! She spun around and ran. The snow fell faster, the thick flakes clumping on her eyelashes and making it hard to see.

“Elsa!” The name ripped from her throat. “Elsaaaa! El—” She choked on the word.

There, standing in front of her, wasn’t her sister, but the wolf.

Once more, its fierce yellow eyes were fixed right on her.

How had it gotten ahead of her? There was no time to think—only to run.

Anna pumped her legs, sending snow flying up around her. She couldn’t stop. Her entire world was snow and fear and cold, and then suddenly—endless sky! Anna stumbled to a halt. She was at the edge of a cliff. An inky expanse of nothingness lay before her, but she knew whatever she found lurking behind her would be far worse.

Hot breath.

Sharp claws.

Sharper teeth.

“ELSA!” she yelled again.

But Elsa did not appear. If her sister wasn’t here by now, something horrible must have happened. Pain seared itself across Anna’s shoulder blades. She had hesitated for too long. The wolf’s claws had connected with her back. Anna stumbled forward.

She plunged over the edge—

And woke up.

A cool, comforting hand was on her forehead, and as she blinked, Anna saw her mother’s face sharpen into focus. The queen’s blue-gray eyes shone with concern, and her chestnut brown hair cascaded down one shoulder, loose from its usual upsweep of braids and bangs. A large burgundy scarf, stitched with a multitude of snowflakes and complete with purple fringe, had been thrown over her shoulders and was covering up a lavender nightgown.

Anna shot up. “Where’s Elsa? Did the wolf get her?”

“Anna, it’s all right.” Her mother sat and wrapped an arm around her. “All is well.”

“There was snow,” Anna said, her heart still pounding. “And trees! I was running, and then…I slipped!” She struggled to sit up against her pillows. “Elsa was there, and then she wasn’t. I was so worried!”

Her father strode forward with a tray bearing mugs of hot chocolate. “You had a bad dream,” he said. His ruddy blond hair, usually brushed back neatly, was tousled, as if he’d just come in from a midnight ride. For some reason, he was wearing his navy-blue uniform resplendent with badges and golden epaulets instead of a nightshirt. Bending, he placed the tray on the bedside table. “Elsa is in her room, asleep, as we all should be at this hour.”

But that didn’t seem quite right. The last thing Anna remembered was being awake in this same bed, watching the dancing sky through her window, wanting to wake Elsa up to…do something. But what? Anna squinted her eyes, trying to remember through the pounding in her head. Odd. That’s all she could remember. The only thing after that was the outline of her nightmare: a mountain, a wolf, and bitter cold.

Her father settled next to her mother and handed a warm mug to Anna. “Drink up,” he said. The steam uncurled from the mug, moving with the same effortless grace as the wolf.

Anna shivered, still a bit shaken, but she had never said no to hot chocolate. She took a sip, and as the liquid slipped down to her belly, it warmed her stomach.

Her mother patted her knee. “You know, when I have a bad dream, I always imagine crumpling up the nightmare and tossing it out the window so that Frigg has something else to fish for besides the moon and the sun. You remember the old story I used to tell you about Frigg the Fisherman, right?”

Anna did, but she shook her head. She wanted her mother to keep talking. She leaned back as her mother began the tale of the boastful fisherman who kept casting his nets for bigger prizes and accidentally found himself stuck in a nighttime ocean of stars. Anna soaked in the comforting presence of her mother, who always smelled like calming lavender.

The memory of the nightmare faded, replaced by what was real: her cozy bedroom decorated with pink wallpaper, thick ornate rugs, an oval painting of Arendelle Castle that she loved to admire, a tapestry of queens, and flickering candles in the sconces on the walls. Though no flames burned in the fireplace, a few embers still glowed like dropped jewels. And her parents there beside her were the coziest details of all. Anna’s eyes grew heavy.

“Feeling better?” her father whispered when her mother finished her tale.

Anna nodded, and he smiled.

“Everything is always better with hot chocolate,” he said.

“We should wake Elsa up.” Anna’s eyes fluttered as she held up her empty mug. “She’d like this.”

She almost missed her mother and father exchange a fleeting glance at her words. There was a shift in the room, as if a cloud had drifted past the window.

“Elsa needs her sleep,” her mother said. “And you should try to get some rest, too. Agnarr, can you please hand me that extra pillow?”

Anna’s father stood and walked over to the white-painted chair that had been dragged from its place by the wall and now stood between Anna and the fireplace. Another pillow and a crumpled pile of blankets lay on the floor around it, as if it were a makeshift bed.

Anna looked from the floor to her parents. They only stayed in her room if she was really ill….“Were you sleeping in here?” Anna asked. “Am I sick?”

“You’re just fine,” her father said with a soft smile. Picking up the pillow, he placed it under Anna’s head while her mother tucked the blankets tight. Anna wiggled her toes to loosen the covers just a bit as her parents extinguished the lights and headed for the door.

“Sweet dreams, Anna,” her mother whispered from the doorway, the light from the hallway outlining her and Anna’s father.

“Sweet dreams…” Anna murmured back, sinking deeper into her pillow.

The patch of light grew smaller and smaller, until, at last, it vanished as the door clicked shut. Anna listened to the sound of her parents’ footsteps recede before she turned her cheek to stare out her window.

The sky was asleep now, the ribbons of color from the northern lights tucked beneath a patchwork quilt of clouds. But the moon stayed bright. It glared down at her like one of the wolf’s yellow eyes. Watching. And waiting. But for what?

Cold again, Anna pulled the covers over her head, but sleep never came.
chapters.zh:
天空醒着，森林也是。

阿伦黛尔的安娜把斗篷紧紧裹在身上，光秃秃的树枝在她头顶上方像牙齿般咔嗒作响，风拽扯着她的辫子。

她朝一丛灌木里张望。

据她所知，灌木是不该长眼睛的。

不过话说回来，五岁的小公主也不该在夜里独自待在城堡外面。

可她偏偏就在这儿……虽然安娜这夜一开始并不是独自一人。

她的姐姐艾莎，也在这片雪林里的某处。

说不定就藏在这丛灌木里——安娜此刻正踮着脚，悄悄朝它靠近。

艾莎比安娜大三岁，有着一双宽宽的蓝眼睛和腼腆的微笑，是那种能安安静静坐上几个钟头都不晃腿的女孩，她那条整齐的浅金色辫子总是笔直垂在背后。

大人们常夸安娜的姐姐有多乖……可他们并不像安娜那样了解艾莎。

在那副礼貌而端庄的外表之下，藏着一颗爱调皮捣蛋的心。

艾莎只需要一个借口，而安娜就很乐意充当那个借口：有了安娜，艾莎便能披上斗篷，溜出城堡，去堆个雪人，在北极光下玩捉迷藏。

他们现在正是这么做的。

艾莎早已在树洞里找到了安娜，而安娜找艾莎却仿佛找了整整一辈子……至少也有五分钟了吧。

树叶又沙沙响了起来，安娜赶紧用手捂住嘴，不让自己笑出声。

没错，雪盖的灌木丛里肯定有人正盯着她。

她屏住呼吸，又靠近了些。

她几乎可以肯定那是艾莎，可也总有可能是一只“胡尔德民”——那些传说中居住在溪流里、岩石下，以及她们母亲伊杜娜王后讲的睡前故事里的隐遁之民。

安娜的心跳得快了起来。

如果真是胡尔德民，她一定要看看他们的尾巴。

她一直好奇，他们的尾巴是像马尾巴那样飘逸，还是像狐狸尾巴那样蓬松，又或是像老鼠尾巴那样又长又细。

不过安娜有种预感，她知道藏在灌木后面的身影是谁。

安娜拨开树叶，在舞动的天空那绚烂的光晕里，她瞥见了一抹金发。

所以，不是胡尔德民。

只是个姐姐。

安娜笑着摇晃那丛灌木。“我找到你了！

轮到你当‘硬壳地精’了！”艾莎没有回应。“我说，我找到你了。”安娜透过枝叶张望。“该轮到我藏了——这是规矩。

快出来呀！”姐姐转过头，安娜这才意识到自己搞错了。

在变幻的光影里，她瞧见的并不是金发。

是白色的毛。

一只巨大的白狼以一种奇异的优雅从灌木丛中踱步而出，修长的四肢像烟一般舒展开来，安娜的尖叫卡在了喉咙里。

它那凶猛的黄眼睛死死盯住她，安娜的目光顺着它那匹马般庞大的身躯向下移……看见四只可怕的爪子，每一只都和她父亲阿格瑞国王那面大盾牌一般大小。

但这还不是最糟的。

不，最糟的是它爪子和下颌周围那染红的毛。

红。

血的颜色。

她姐姐出什么事了？“艾莎！”安娜尖叫起来。“你在哪儿？”白狼纵身扑来。

安娜拔腿就跑。

她的心在胸口砰砰狂跳，每吸一口气都像刀割一样，她拼命想跑得更快、更快——可她知道自己跑不过狼。

看到一根倒下的原木，她猛地躲到后面，双膝蜷到胸前，尽量把自己缩得小小的。

尽管肺里渴求着空气，安娜还是屏住呼吸，连最轻微的一声呼气都不愿让自己泄露出去。

一秒过去了，又一秒，再一秒。

她甩掉狼了吗？

雪无声地密密落下。

安娜打了个寒颤，真希望自己听了艾莎的话——艾莎让她别穿那件最好看的绿斗篷，换上日常那件厚实的棕色羊毛斗篷。

艾莎。

艾莎在哪儿？

安娜像影子一样悄无声息，从原木后探出头，半是预料会和狼来个鼻尖贴鼻尖。

然而她看到的，只有一支树的大军，把森然的影子投在雪地上。

风越刮越紧，安娜那冰冷的恐惧也跟着越来越重。

要是她踩着新雪走，狼就能清清楚楚知道她去了哪个方向。

可要是她不走雪地……也许就永远找不到姐姐了。

红在白上。

血在毛上。

安娜不能永远躲在原木后面。

她脱下斗篷，在地上铺开，把它团成一个五岁小女孩打盹的形状。

然后她蹲下身来。

目前为止，还算顺利。

她缓缓地、稳稳地向后退了一步。

再一步，又一步，她小心地倒退着在树间穿行，就像母亲睡前故事里说的胡尔德民那样赶路，好把自己的尾巴藏起来。

可安娜没有尾巴需要藏。

相反，她在雪地上留下了一串崭新的脚印——一串永远会把追踪者引向她不在之处的脚印。“艾莎，”她轻声说，“你赢了捉迷藏。

快出来吧。”可依旧没有回应。

雪下得更急了，安娜也移动得更快，在树间疾窜，躲到大石后面，同时始终在雪林里搜寻姐姐的踪迹——任何踪迹都行。

可连一个脚印都看不见。

仿佛姐姐被凭空抹去了一般。

仿佛……但这个念头太可怕，安娜不敢想完。

近处某地方向，狼嗥叫起来。

安娜僵住了。

她认得那声音。

那声音和她父亲的猎犬嗅到狐狸气味时发出的一模一样。

狼又嗥了一声，但这一次远了一些。

安娜的诱饵奏效了！

她猛地转身跑了起来。

雪下得更急，厚厚的雪片黏在她的睫毛上，让她几乎看不清。“艾莎！”这个名字从她喉咙里撕裂而出。“艾莎——

艾——”这个字卡在了她喉咙里。

站在她面前的，不是姐姐，而是那只狼。

那双凶猛的黄眼睛再次死死盯住她。

它是怎么跑到她前头的？

没时间思考了——只能跑。

安娜拼命蹬动双腿，雪沫在她四周飞溅。

她停不下来。

她的整个世界都是雪、恐惧和寒冷，然后忽然——无垠的天空！

安娜踉跄着停住脚步。

她站到了悬崖边。

眼前是一片墨黑虚无，可她知道，身后潜伏着的东西只会更可怕。

炽热的呼吸。

锐利的爪子。

更锐利的牙齿。“艾莎！”她再次大喊。

可艾莎没有出现。

如果姐姐到现在还不在这里，那一定发生了可怕的事。

一阵剧痛灼过安娜的肩胛骨。

她犹豫得太久了。

狼的爪子已经抓上了她的后背。

安娜向前踉跄。

她坠下悬崖——然后醒了过来。

一只冰凉而安抚的手贴在她额头上，安娜眨着眼，看清了母亲的脸。

王后那蓝灰色的眼睛满含关切，栗棕色的头发从平日盘起的辫子和刘海上散落下来，瀑布般垂在一侧肩头。

一条绣满雪花、缀着紫色流苏的大酒红色围巾搭在她肩上，盖住了一件淡紫色的睡袍。

安娜猛地坐起。“艾莎在哪儿？

狼抓到她了吗？”“安娜，没事的。”母亲坐下，伸手搂住她。“一切都好。”“有雪，”安娜说，心还在狂跳。“还有树！

我在跑，然后……我滑倒了！”她挣扎着靠在枕头上坐起来。“艾莎本来在，然后就不见了。

我好担心！”父亲端着一个托盘走过来，托盘上放着几杯热可可。“你做了个噩梦，”他说。

他那一头红润的金发平日总是整齐地向后梳，此刻却乱蓬蓬的，仿佛刚从午夜的骑马中归来。

不知为何，他穿的不是睡衣，而是那身缀满徽章、饰着金色肩章的海军蓝制服。

他弯下腰，把托盘放到床头柜上。“艾莎在在自己的房间，睡着了，这个时辰我们都该如此。”可这话听着不太对劲。

安娜最后记得的，是自己醒着躺在这张床上，透过窗户望着舞动的天空，想叫醒艾莎去……做点什么。

可是什么呢？

安娜眯起眼睛，想在一阵阵头痛中努力回忆。

奇怪。

她能记起的就只有这些。

那之后的唯一片段，就是她噩梦的轮廓：一座山，一只狼，和刺骨的寒冷。

父亲在母亲身旁坐下，把一杯温热的饮料递给安娜。“喝吧，”他说。

热气从杯中袅袅升起，带着和那只狼一样从容的优雅。

安娜打了个寒颤，仍有些惊魂未定，但她从没对热可可说过“不”。

她抿了一口，暖流顺着喉咙滑进肚子，暖了她的胃。

母亲拍拍她的膝盖。“你知道，每当我做噩梦，我总想象把噩梦揉成一团，从窗口扔出去，好让弗丽格除了月亮和太阳，还能钓点别的东西。

你还记得我以前讲给你听的渔夫弗丽格的老故事吧？”安娜记得，却摇了摇头。

她想让母亲继续讲下去。

她向后靠去，听母亲讲起那个爱吹牛的渔夫——他不断撒网，想要更大的收获，却意外困在了夜晚的星海里。

安娜沉浸于母亲令人安心的陪伴中，母亲身上总有股宁静的薰衣草香。

噩梦的记忆淡去了，取而代之的是真实的一切：她那贴着粉色壁纸、铺着厚实华丽地毯的舒适卧室，一幅她最爱欣赏的阿伦黛尔城堡椭圆画，一幅历代王后的挂毯，还有壁灯里摇曳的烛火。

壁炉里虽已没有火苗，几颗余烬却仍像散落的宝石般发着光。

而陪伴在身旁的父母，是所有温馨细节里最暖的。

安娜的眼皮沉了下来。“好些了吗？”母亲讲完故事时，父亲轻声问。

安娜点点头，他笑了。“有了热可可，什么事都会好起来，”他说。“咱们该叫醒艾莎。”安娜举起空杯子，眼皮直眨。“她会喜欢这个的。”她差点没注意到，父母在自己这句话后交换了一个匆匆的眼神。

屋里的气氛变了，仿佛一片云从窗外飘过。“艾莎需要睡觉，”母亲说。“你也应该试着休息一下。

阿格瑞，能把那额外的枕头递给我吗？”安娜的父亲站起身，走向那把白漆椅子——它被人从靠墙的位置拖了过来，此刻立在安娜和壁炉之间。

椅子周围的地板上还放着另一个枕头和一摞皱巴巴的毯子，仿佛那是张临时搭的床。

安娜把目光从地板移到父母身上。

他们只在她真的病了时才会留宿她房间……“你们睡在这儿吗？”安娜问。“我生病了？”“你很好，”父亲温柔地笑着说道。

他拿起枕头，垫在安娜头下，母亲则把毯子掖得紧紧的。

父母熄了灯，朝门口走去，安娜动了动脚趾，把被子松了松。“好梦，安娜，”母亲在门口轻声说，走廊的光勾出她和安娜父亲的轮廓。“好梦……”安娜喃喃回应，更深地陷进枕头里。

那片光亮越来越小，终于，随着门咔嗒一声关上，彻底消失了。

安娜听着父母的脚步声渐渐远去，才侧过脸，凝望窗外。

此刻天空睡了，北极光那一条条彩带被藏进了一床拼布云的被子下。

可月亮依旧明亮。

它像狼的一只黄眼睛那样，瞪着她。

注视着。

等待着。

可是在等什么？

寒意又起，安娜把被子拉过头顶，却始终无法入睡。

sentences.en: THE SKY WAS AWAKE, and so was the forest.
sentences.zh: 天空醒着，森林也是。

sentences.en: Anna of Arendelle hugged her cloak tight as the bare branches clacked like teeth above her and the wind tugged at her braids.
sentences.zh: 阿伦黛尔的安娜把斗篷紧紧裹在身上，光秃秃的树枝在她头顶上方像牙齿般咔嗒作响，风拽扯着她的辫子。

sentences.en: She peered into a bush.
sentences.zh: 她朝一丛灌木里张望。

sentences.en: As far as she knew, bushes weren’t supposed to have eyes.
sentences.zh: 据她所知，灌木是不该长眼睛的。

sentences.en: But then again, five-year-old princesses weren’t supposed to be alone outside the castle at night, either.
sentences.zh: 不过话说回来，五岁的小公主也不该在夜里独自待在城堡外面。

sentences.en: And yet here she was…although Anna hadn’t started off the night alone.
sentences.zh: 可她偏偏就在这儿……虽然安娜这夜一开始并不是独自一人。

sentences.en: Her sister, Elsa, was somewhere out here in the snowy woods, too.
sentences.zh: 她的姐姐艾莎，也在这片雪林里的某处。

sentences.en: Possibly hiding in the very bush that Anna tiptoed closer to at this moment.
sentences.zh: 说不定就藏在这丛灌木里——安娜此刻正踮着脚，悄悄朝它靠近。

sentences.en: Three years older than Anna, with wide blue eyes and a shy smile, Elsa was the kind of girl who could sit for hours without swinging her legs and whose tidy white-blond plait always hung straight down her back.
sentences.zh: 艾莎比安娜大三岁，有着一双宽宽的蓝眼睛和腼腆的微笑，是那种能安安静静坐上几个钟头都不晃腿的女孩，她那条整齐的浅金色辫子总是笔直垂在背后。

sentences.en: Grown-ups often remarked how well-behaved Anna’s big sister was…but they didn’t know Elsa the way Anna did.
sentences.zh: 大人们常夸安娜的姐姐有多乖……可他们并不像安娜那样了解艾莎。

sentences.en: Underneath the polite and poised exterior was a mischievous sense of fun.
sentences.zh: 在那副礼貌而端庄的外表之下，藏着一颗爱调皮捣蛋的心。

sentences.en: All Elsa needed was an excuse, and Anna was happy to be just that: Elsa’s excuse to slip into her cloak and sneak out of the castle to build a snowman and play hide-and-find under the northern lights.
sentences.zh: 艾莎只需要一个借口，而安娜就很乐意充当那个借口：有了安娜，艾莎便能披上斗篷，溜出城堡，去堆个雪人，在北极光下玩捉迷藏。

sentences.en: Which was exactly what they were doing now.
sentences.zh: 他们现在正是这么做的。

sentences.en: Elsa had already found Anna in a tree’s hollow, but Anna had been looking for Elsa for what seemed like forever…or at least five minutes.
sentences.zh: 艾莎早已在树洞里找到了安娜，而安娜找艾莎却仿佛找了整整一辈子……至少也有五分钟了吧。

sentences.en: The leaves rustled again, and Anna clapped her hands over her mouth to stop a giggle from escaping.
sentences.zh: 树叶又沙沙响了起来，安娜赶紧用手捂住嘴，不让自己笑出声。

sentences.en: Yes, there was definitely someone watching her from the snow-covered thicket.
sentences.zh: 没错，雪盖的灌木丛里肯定有人正盯着她。

sentences.en: Holding her breath, she stepped closer.
sentences.zh: 她屏住呼吸，又靠近了些。

sentences.en: She was pretty sure it was Elsa, but there was always a chance it could be a Huldrefólk, one of the rumored hidden people who dwelled in the streams, under the rocks, and in the bedtime stories told by their mother, Queen Iduna.
sentences.zh: 她几乎可以肯定那是艾莎，可也总有可能是一只“胡尔德民”——那些传说中居住在溪流里、岩石下，以及她们母亲伊杜娜王后讲的睡前故事里的隐遁之民。

sentences.en: Anna’s heart beat faster.
sentences.zh: 安娜的心跳得快了起来。

sentences.en: If it was a Huldrefólk, she just had to see their tail.
sentences.zh: 如果真是胡尔德民，她一定要看看他们的尾巴。

sentences.en: She’d always wondered if their tails were flowing like a horse’s, or bushy like a fox’s, or long and skinny like a mouse’s.
sentences.zh: 她一直好奇，他们的尾巴是像马尾巴那样飘逸，还是像狐狸尾巴那样蓬松，又或是像老鼠尾巴那样又长又细。

sentences.en: But Anna had a feeling she knew who the figure hiding behind the bush was.
sentences.zh: 不过安娜有种预感，她知道藏在灌木后面的身影是谁。

sentences.en: Anna parted the leaves, and in the colorful glow of the dancing sky, she caught a glimpse of blond hair.
sentences.zh: 安娜拨开树叶，在舞动的天空那绚烂的光晕里，她瞥见了一抹金发。

sentences.en: So, not a Huldrefólk.
sentences.zh: 所以，不是胡尔德民。

sentences.en: Just a sister.
sentences.zh: 只是个姐姐。

sentences.en: Laughing, Anna shook the bush. “I found you!
sentences.zh: 安娜笑着摇晃那丛灌木。“我找到你了！

sentences.en: Your turn to be the Crusty Troll!” Elsa didn’t respond. “I said, I found you.” Anna peered through the foliage. “It’s my turn to hide—that’s the rule.
sentences.zh: 轮到你当‘硬壳地精’了！”艾莎没有回应。“我说，我找到你了。”安娜透过枝叶张望。“该轮到我藏了——这是规矩。

sentences.en: Come on out!” Anna’s sister turned her head, and that’s when Anna realized her mistake.
sentences.zh: 快出来呀！”姐姐转过头，安娜这才意识到自己搞错了。

sentences.en: It wasn’t blond hair she had spotted in the shifting light.
sentences.zh: 在变幻的光影里，她瞧见的并不是金发。

sentences.en: It was white fur .
sentences.zh: 是白色的毛。

sentences.en: Anna’s scream stuck in her throat as a giant white wolf prowled out from the thicket with unusual grace, its long limbs uncurling like smoke.
sentences.zh: 一只巨大的白狼以一种奇异的优雅从灌木丛中踱步而出，修长的四肢像烟一般舒展开来，安娜的尖叫卡在了喉咙里。

sentences.en: Its fierce yellow gaze fixed on her, and Anna’s eyes ran down its huge, horse-sized body…to see four fearsome paws, each the size of one of the large shields of her father, King Agnarr.
sentences.zh: 它那凶猛的黄眼睛死死盯住她，安娜的目光顺着它那匹马般庞大的身躯向下移……看见四只可怕的爪子，每一只都和她父亲阿格瑞国王那面大盾牌一般大小。

sentences.en: But that wasn’t the worst of it.
sentences.zh: 但这还不是最糟的。

sentences.en: No, the worst was the red-stained fur around its claws and jaw.
sentences.zh: 不，最糟的是它爪子和下颌周围那染红的毛。

sentences.en: Red.
sentences.zh: 红。

sentences.en: The color of blood.
sentences.zh: 血的颜色。

sentences.en: What had happened to her sister? “Elsa!” Anna screamed. “Where are you?” The wolf leapt.
sentences.zh: 她姐姐出什么事了？“艾莎！”安娜尖叫起来。“你在哪儿？”白狼纵身扑来。

sentences.en: Anna ran.
sentences.zh: 安娜拔腿就跑。

sentences.en: Her heart slammed in her chest, each breath a sharp knife as she tried to run faster, and faster—but she knew she couldn’t outrun a wolf.
sentences.zh: 她的心在胸口砰砰狂跳，每吸一口气都像刀割一样，她拼命想跑得更快、更快——可她知道自己跑不过狼。

sentences.en: Spotting a fallen log, she dove behind it, her knees tucked to her chest as she tried to make herself as small as possible.
sentences.zh: 看到一根倒下的原木，她猛地躲到后面，双膝蜷到胸前，尽量把自己缩得小小的。

sentences.en: Though her lungs ached for air, Anna held her breath, not wanting to give herself away with even the tiniest exhale.
sentences.zh: 尽管肺里渴求着空气，安娜还是屏住呼吸，连最轻微的一声呼气都不愿让自己泄露出去。

sentences.en: One second passed, then another, and another.
sentences.zh: 一秒过去了，又一秒，再一秒。

sentences.en: Had she lost the wolf?
sentences.zh: 她甩掉狼了吗？

sentences.en: Snow fell thick and silent.
sentences.zh: 雪无声地密密落下。

sentences.en: Anna shivered, wishing she’d listened to Elsa when she’d told her not to wear her most beautiful green cloak but to put on her everyday thick woolly brown one instead.
sentences.zh: 安娜打了个寒颤，真希望自己听了艾莎的话——艾莎让她别穿那件最好看的绿斗篷，换上日常那件厚实的棕色羊毛斗篷。

sentences.en: Elsa.
sentences.zh: 艾莎。

sentences.en: Where was Elsa?
sentences.zh: 艾莎在哪儿？

sentences.en: As quiet as a shadow, Anna peered around the log, half expecting to come nose-to-snout with the wolf.
sentences.zh: 安娜像影子一样悄无声息，从原木后探出头，半是预料会和狼来个鼻尖贴鼻尖。

sentences.en: Instead, all she saw was an army of trees casting ghastly shadows onto the snow-covered ground.
sentences.zh: 然而她看到的，只有一支树的大军，把森然的影子投在雪地上。

sentences.en: And as the wind picked up, so did Anna’s ice-cold fear.
sentences.zh: 风越刮越紧，安娜那冰冷的恐惧也跟着越来越重。

sentences.en: If she walked through the fresh snow, the wolf would be able to see exactly which direction she’d gone.
sentences.zh: 要是她踩着新雪走，狼就能清清楚楚知道她去了哪个方向。

sentences.en: And if she didn’t walk through the snow…she might never find her sister.
sentences.zh: 可要是她不走雪地……也许就永远找不到姐姐了。

sentences.en: Red on white.
sentences.zh: 红在白上。

sentences.en: Blood on fur.
sentences.zh: 血在毛上。

sentences.en: Anna couldn’t stay behind the log forever.
sentences.zh: 安娜不能永远躲在原木后面。

sentences.en: Peeling off her cloak, she arranged it on the ground, bunching it into the shape of a five-year-old girl taking a nap.
sentences.zh: 她脱下斗篷，在地上铺开，把它团成一个五岁小女孩打盹的形状。

sentences.en: Then she moved into a crouching position.
sentences.zh: 然后她蹲下身来。

sentences.en: So far, so good.
sentences.zh: 目前为止，还算顺利。

sentences.en: She took a slow, steady step backward.
sentences.zh: 她缓缓地、稳稳地向后退了一步。

sentences.en: And then another, and another, carefully weaving her way in reverse between the trees, the same way the Huldrefólk in her mother’s bedtime stories were said to travel so they could keep their tails hidden.
sentences.zh: 再一步，又一步，她小心地倒退着在树间穿行，就像母亲睡前故事里说的胡尔德民那样赶路，好把自己的尾巴藏起来。

sentences.en: But Anna didn’t have a tail to hide.
sentences.zh: 可安娜没有尾巴需要藏。

sentences.en: Instead, she was leaving a fresh trail of footprints in the snow—footprints that would always lead away from where she actually was. “Elsa,” she whispered, “you’ve won hide-and-find.
sentences.zh: 相反，她在雪地上留下了一串崭新的脚印——一串永远会把追踪者引向她不在之处的脚印。“艾莎，”她轻声说，“你赢了捉迷藏。

sentences.en: Please come out.” But still there was no reply.
sentences.zh: 快出来吧。”可依旧没有回应。

sentences.en: The snow fell faster, so Anna moved faster, darting between trees, diving behind boulders, and all the while scanning the snowy woods for a sign of her sister—any sign.
sentences.zh: 雪下得更急了，安娜也移动得更快，在树间疾窜，躲到大石后面，同时始终在雪林里搜寻姐姐的踪迹——任何踪迹都行。

sentences.en: But there was not a footprint to be seen.
sentences.zh: 可连一个脚印都看不见。

sentences.en: It was as though her sister had been erased.
sentences.zh: 仿佛姐姐被凭空抹去了一般。

sentences.en: As though…but the thought was too horrible for Anna to finish.
sentences.zh: 仿佛……但这个念头太可怕，安娜不敢想完。

sentences.en: From somewhere nearby, the wolf howled.
sentences.zh: 近处某地方向，狼嗥叫起来。

sentences.en: Anna froze.
sentences.zh: 安娜僵住了。

sentences.en: She knew that sound.
sentences.zh: 她认得那声音。

sentences.en: It was the same sound her father’s hunting dogs made when they’d picked up the scent of a fox.
sentences.zh: 那声音和她父亲的猎犬嗅到狐狸气味时发出的一模一样。

sentences.en: The wolf howled again, but this time it was a little farther away.
sentences.zh: 狼又嗥了一声，但这一次远了一些。

sentences.en: Anna’s decoy had worked!
sentences.zh: 安娜的诱饵奏效了！

sentences.en: She spun around and ran.
sentences.zh: 她猛地转身跑了起来。

sentences.en: The snow fell faster, the thick flakes clumping on her eyelashes and making it hard to see. “Elsa!” The name ripped from her throat. “Elsaaaa!
sentences.zh: 雪下得更急，厚厚的雪片黏在她的睫毛上，让她几乎看不清。“艾莎！”这个名字从她喉咙里撕裂而出。“艾莎——

sentences.en: El—” She choked on the word.
sentences.zh: 艾——”这个字卡在了她喉咙里。

sentences.en: There, standing in front of her, wasn’t her sister, but the wolf.
sentences.zh: 站在她面前的，不是姐姐，而是那只狼。

sentences.en: Once more, its fierce yellow eyes were fixed right on her.
sentences.zh: 那双凶猛的黄眼睛再次死死盯住她。

sentences.en: How had it gotten ahead of her?
sentences.zh: 它是怎么跑到她前头的？

sentences.en: There was no time to think—only to run.
sentences.zh: 没时间思考了——只能跑。

sentences.en: Anna pumped her legs, sending snow flying up around her.
sentences.zh: 安娜拼命蹬动双腿，雪沫在她四周飞溅。

sentences.en: She couldn’t stop.
sentences.zh: 她停不下来。

sentences.en: Her entire world was snow and fear and cold, and then suddenly—endless sky!
sentences.zh: 她的整个世界都是雪、恐惧和寒冷，然后忽然——无垠的天空！

sentences.en: Anna stumbled to a halt.
sentences.zh: 安娜踉跄着停住脚步。

sentences.en: She was at the edge of a cliff.
sentences.zh: 她站到了悬崖边。

sentences.en: An inky expanse of nothingness lay before her, but she knew whatever she found lurking behind her would be far worse.
sentences.zh: 眼前是一片墨黑虚无，可她知道，身后潜伏着的东西只会更可怕。

sentences.en: Hot breath.
sentences.zh: 炽热的呼吸。

sentences.en: Sharp claws.
sentences.zh: 锐利的爪子。

sentences.en: Sharper teeth. “ELSA!” she yelled again.
sentences.zh: 更锐利的牙齿。“艾莎！”她再次大喊。

sentences.en: But Elsa did not appear.
sentences.zh: 可艾莎没有出现。

sentences.en: If her sister wasn’t here by now, something horrible must have happened.
sentences.zh: 如果姐姐到现在还不在这里，那一定发生了可怕的事。

sentences.en: Pain seared itself across Anna’s shoulder blades.
sentences.zh: 一阵剧痛灼过安娜的肩胛骨。

sentences.en: She had hesitated for too long.
sentences.zh: 她犹豫得太久了。

sentences.en: The wolf’s claws had connected with her back.
sentences.zh: 狼的爪子已经抓上了她的后背。

sentences.en: Anna stumbled forward.
sentences.zh: 安娜向前踉跄。

sentences.en: She plunged over the edge— And woke up.
sentences.zh: 她坠下悬崖——然后醒了过来。

sentences.en: A cool, comforting hand was on her forehead, and as she blinked, Anna saw her mother’s face sharpen into focus.
sentences.zh: 一只冰凉而安抚的手贴在她额头上，安娜眨着眼，看清了母亲的脸。

sentences.en: The queen’s blue-gray eyes shone with concern, and her chestnut brown hair cascaded down one shoulder, loose from its usual upsweep of braids and bangs.
sentences.zh: 王后那蓝灰色的眼睛满含关切，栗棕色的头发从平日盘起的辫子和刘海上散落下来，瀑布般垂在一侧肩头。

sentences.en: A large burgundy scarf, stitched with a multitude of snowflakes and complete with purple fringe, had been thrown over her shoulders and was covering up a lavender nightgown.
sentences.zh: 一条绣满雪花、缀着紫色流苏的大酒红色围巾搭在她肩上，盖住了一件淡紫色的睡袍。

sentences.en: Anna shot up. “Where’s Elsa?
sentences.zh: 安娜猛地坐起。“艾莎在哪儿？

sentences.en: Did the wolf get her?” “Anna, it’s all right.” Her mother sat and wrapped an arm around her. “All is well.” “There was snow,” Anna said, her heart still pounding. “And trees!
sentences.zh: 狼抓到她了吗？”“安娜，没事的。”母亲坐下，伸手搂住她。“一切都好。”“有雪，”安娜说，心还在狂跳。“还有树！

sentences.en: I was running, and then…I slipped!” She struggled to sit up against her pillows. “Elsa was there, and then she wasn’t.
sentences.zh: 我在跑，然后……我滑倒了！”她挣扎着靠在枕头上坐起来。“艾莎本来在，然后就不见了。

sentences.en: I was so worried!” Her father strode forward with a tray bearing mugs of hot chocolate. “You had a bad dream,” he said.
sentences.zh: 我好担心！”父亲端着一个托盘走过来，托盘上放着几杯热可可。“你做了个噩梦，”他说。

sentences.en: His ruddy blond hair, usually brushed back neatly, was tousled, as if he’d just come in from a midnight ride.
sentences.zh: 他那一头红润的金发平日总是整齐地向后梳，此刻却乱蓬蓬的，仿佛刚从午夜的骑马中归来。

sentences.en: For some reason, he was wearing his navy-blue uniform resplendent with badges and golden epaulets instead of a nightshirt.
sentences.zh: 不知为何，他穿的不是睡衣，而是那身缀满徽章、饰着金色肩章的海军蓝制服。

sentences.en: Bending, he placed the tray on the bedside table. “Elsa is in her room, asleep, as we all should be at this hour.” But that didn’t seem quite right.
sentences.zh: 他弯下腰，把托盘放到床头柜上。“艾莎在在自己的房间，睡着了，这个时辰我们都该如此。”可这话听着不太对劲。

sentences.en: The last thing Anna remembered was being awake in this same bed, watching the dancing sky through her window, wanting to wake Elsa up to…do something.
sentences.zh: 安娜最后记得的，是自己醒着躺在这张床上，透过窗户望着舞动的天空，想叫醒艾莎去……做点什么。

sentences.en: But what?
sentences.zh: 可是什么呢？

sentences.en: Anna squinted her eyes, trying to remember through the pounding in her head.
sentences.zh: 安娜眯起眼睛，想在一阵阵头痛中努力回忆。

sentences.en: Odd.
sentences.zh: 奇怪。

sentences.en: That’s all she could remember.
sentences.zh: 她能记起的就只有这些。

sentences.en: The only thing after that was the outline of her nightmare: a mountain, a wolf, and bitter cold.
sentences.zh: 那之后的唯一片段，就是她噩梦的轮廓：一座山，一只狼，和刺骨的寒冷。

sentences.en: Her father settled next to her mother and handed a warm mug to Anna. “Drink up,” he said.
sentences.zh: 父亲在母亲身旁坐下，把一杯温热的饮料递给安娜。“喝吧，”他说。

sentences.en: The steam uncurled from the mug, moving with the same effortless grace as the wolf.
sentences.zh: 热气从杯中袅袅升起，带着和那只狼一样从容的优雅。

sentences.en: Anna shivered, still a bit shaken, but she had never said no to hot chocolate.
sentences.zh: 安娜打了个寒颤，仍有些惊魂未定，但她从没对热可可说过“不”。

sentences.en: She took a sip, and as the liquid slipped down to her belly, it warmed her stomach.
sentences.zh: 她抿了一口，暖流顺着喉咙滑进肚子，暖了她的胃。

sentences.en: Her mother patted her knee. “You know, when I have a bad dream, I always imagine crumpling up the nightmare and tossing it out the window so that Frigg has something else to fish for besides the moon and the sun.
sentences.zh: 母亲拍拍她的膝盖。“你知道，每当我做噩梦，我总想象把噩梦揉成一团，从窗口扔出去，好让弗丽格除了月亮和太阳，还能钓点别的东西。

sentences.en: You remember the old story I used to tell you about Frigg the Fisherman, right?” Anna did, but she shook her head.
sentences.zh: 你还记得我以前讲给你听的渔夫弗丽格的老故事吧？”安娜记得，却摇了摇头。

sentences.en: She wanted her mother to keep talking.
sentences.zh: 她想让母亲继续讲下去。

sentences.en: She leaned back as her mother began the tale of the boastful fisherman who kept casting his nets for bigger prizes and accidentally found himself stuck in a nighttime ocean of stars.
sentences.zh: 她向后靠去，听母亲讲起那个爱吹牛的渔夫——他不断撒网，想要更大的收获，却意外困在了夜晚的星海里。

sentences.en: Anna soaked in the comforting presence of her mother, who always smelled like calming lavender.
sentences.zh: 安娜沉浸于母亲令人安心的陪伴中，母亲身上总有股宁静的薰衣草香。

sentences.en: The memory of the nightmare faded, replaced by what was real: her cozy bedroom decorated with pink wallpaper, thick ornate rugs, an oval painting of Arendelle Castle that she loved to admire, a tapestry of queens, and flickering candles in the sconces on the walls.
sentences.zh: 噩梦的记忆淡去了，取而代之的是真实的一切：她那贴着粉色壁纸、铺着厚实华丽地毯的舒适卧室，一幅她最爱欣赏的阿伦黛尔城堡椭圆画，一幅历代王后的挂毯，还有壁灯里摇曳的烛火。

sentences.en: Though no flames burned in the fireplace, a few embers still glowed like dropped jewels.
sentences.zh: 壁炉里虽已没有火苗，几颗余烬却仍像散落的宝石般发着光。

sentences.en: And her parents there beside her were the coziest details of all.
sentences.zh: 而陪伴在身旁的父母，是所有温馨细节里最暖的。

sentences.en: Anna’s eyes grew heavy. “Feeling better?” her father whispered when her mother finished her tale.
sentences.zh: 安娜的眼皮沉了下来。“好些了吗？”母亲讲完故事时，父亲轻声问。

sentences.en: Anna nodded, and he smiled. “Everything is always better with hot chocolate,” he said. “We should wake Elsa up.” Anna’s eyes fluttered as she held up her empty mug. “She’d like this.” She almost missed her mother and father exchange a fleeting glance at her words.
sentences.zh: 安娜点点头，他笑了。“有了热可可，什么事都会好起来，”他说。“咱们该叫醒艾莎。”安娜举起空杯子，眼皮直眨。“她会喜欢这个的。”她差点没注意到，父母在自己这句话后交换了一个匆匆的眼神。

sentences.en: There was a shift in the room, as if a cloud had drifted past the window. “Elsa needs her sleep,” her mother said. “And you should try to get some rest, too.
sentences.zh: 屋里的气氛变了，仿佛一片云从窗外飘过。“艾莎需要睡觉，”母亲说。“你也应该试着休息一下。

sentences.en: Agnarr, can you please hand me that extra pillow?” Anna’s father stood and walked over to the white-painted chair that had been dragged from its place by the wall and now stood between Anna and the fireplace.
sentences.zh: 阿格瑞，能把那额外的枕头递给我吗？”安娜的父亲站起身，走向那把白漆椅子——它被人从靠墙的位置拖了过来，此刻立在安娜和壁炉之间。

sentences.en: Another pillow and a crumpled pile of blankets lay on the floor around it, as if it were a makeshift bed.
sentences.zh: 椅子周围的地板上还放着另一个枕头和一摞皱巴巴的毯子，仿佛那是张临时搭的床。

sentences.en: Anna looked from the floor to her parents.
sentences.zh: 安娜把目光从地板移到父母身上。

sentences.en: They only stayed in her room if she was really ill….“Were you sleeping in here?” Anna asked. “Am I sick?” “You’re just fine,” her father said with a soft smile.
sentences.zh: 他们只在她真的病了时才会留宿她房间……“你们睡在这儿吗？”安娜问。“我生病了？”“你很好，”父亲温柔地笑着说道。

sentences.en: Picking up the pillow, he placed it under Anna’s head while her mother tucked the blankets tight.
sentences.zh: 他拿起枕头，垫在安娜头下，母亲则把毯子掖得紧紧的。

sentences.en: Anna wiggled her toes to loosen the covers just a bit as her parents extinguished the lights and headed for the door. “Sweet dreams, Anna,” her mother whispered from the doorway, the light from the hallway outlining her and Anna’s father. “Sweet dreams…” Anna murmured back, sinking deeper into her pillow.
sentences.zh: 父母熄了灯，朝门口走去，安娜动了动脚趾，把被子松了松。“好梦，安娜，”母亲在门口轻声说，走廊的光勾出她和安娜父亲的轮廓。“好梦……”安娜喃喃回应，更深地陷进枕头里。

sentences.en: The patch of light grew smaller and smaller, until, at last, it vanished as the door clicked shut.
sentences.zh: 那片光亮越来越小，终于，随着门咔嗒一声关上，彻底消失了。

sentences.en: Anna listened to the sound of her parents’ footsteps recede before she turned her cheek to stare out her window.
sentences.zh: 安娜听着父母的脚步声渐渐远去，才侧过脸，凝望窗外。

sentences.en: The sky was asleep now, the ribbons of color from the northern lights tucked beneath a patchwork quilt of clouds.
sentences.zh: 此刻天空睡了，北极光那一条条彩带被藏进了一床拼布云的被子下。

sentences.en: But the moon stayed bright.
sentences.zh: 可月亮依旧明亮。

sentences.en: It glared down at her like one of the wolf’s yellow eyes.
sentences.zh: 它像狼的一只黄眼睛那样，瞪着她。

sentences.en: Watching.
sentences.zh: 注视着。

sentences.en: And waiting.
sentences.zh: 等待着。

sentences.en: But for what?
sentences.zh: 可是在等什么？

sentences.en: Cold again, Anna pulled the covers over her head, but sleep never came.
sentences.zh: 寒意又起，安娜把被子拉过头顶，却始终无法入睡。

chapters.title: 第1章
chapters.en:
ANNA FLEW DOWN the carpeted castle stairs of the second great hall, taking them two at a time.

She nearly tripped on the landing, but she didn’t bother to slow down. The clock tower had already tolled ten in the morning, and she’d promised Elsa she wouldn’t be late. For a second, she thought about sliding down the banister. It really was the fastest way to get around, but at twenty-one she was too old for such things…right? Right. But…

Anna’s feet slowed. The white wood of the banister gleamed with a recent polish and the promise of speed. And her new riding boots with heels—a gift from a dignitary from Zaria—hadn’t been broken in yet and weren’t exactly the best for running. She glanced over her shoulder. No one was around. Decision made, she hauled the skirt of her dress into her arms, slung a leg over the banister, and slid the rest of the way down, landing with ease as she reached the first-floor landing. She flew through the castle doors and raced outside, toward the stables.

“Elsa! I’m here!” Anna whisper-called as she moved through the barn doors and entered the quiet world of sweet hay and softly munching horses. She smoothed down the back of her black dress and checked to make sure that her long chestnut brown hair was still pinned in place by a double braid. “I’m not late! Well,” she amended, “not that late. But I was having the most fascinating dream where…” She trailed off, and looked around.

Her only audience was the alert ears of the castle horses and the litter of barn kittens that came stumbling toward the stables’ entrance whenever someone entered. But there was no sign of Elsa. Anna brushed her bangs off her forehead, confused. Somehow, even though she’d overslept, she had managed to beat Elsa. Which was odd. Very, very odd. Elsa was always on time; it was one of the many reasons she was such a great queen, beloved by all of Arendelle.

Picking up a purring gray kitten that had begun to bat at her bootlaces, Anna took a step toward the livery. Maybe Elsa had gotten here so early that she’d decided to inspect the recent delivery of apples. Careful to keep her voice low so as not to startle the horses, Anna called out again. “Elsa?”

“You’re looking in the wrong place,” a friendly voice called from the far end of the stables, and a second later, Kristoff Bjorgman’s head popped over a stall door, a pitchfork in his hand and a bit of straw in his hair.

Anna grinned. She always did whenever she was around Kristoff—she couldn’t help it. When Kristoff had first started to visit the castle frequently three years before, Gerda, one of the people who had known the girls since they were young, and who also helped them schedule their time, had remarked to the sisters that he resembled the mountains from which he harvested ice: broad and solid. Elsa had whispered back that he seemed “nice.” When Anna had pushed her for a little bit more, Elsa had added “blond.” All of which was true, but to Anna, Kristoff wasn’t just a mountain man or “nice” or “blond,” he was her best friend—and definitely something more, even if he did sometimes smell like a reindeer. Which was completely understandable, given his other best friend, Sven, was a reindeer.

Sven’s head popped over the stall door to look at Anna, and he twitched his ears in a friendly hello. Though Anna had invited both Sven and Kristoff multiple times to take up residence in one of the many spare rooms of the castle, they both preferred to stay in the stables. Anna suspected they enjoyed the less confined living space of the barn after spending the summer months in the mountains harvesting ice for the kingdom.

“She’s not here?” Anna asked, bending to set the kitten down gently. It scampered away to join the others.

Kristoff moved his hand under Sven’s lower lip and began to wiggle it as he said in Sven’s voice, “Someone’s not listening.”

Anna smiled at Kristoff’s “Sven Talk”—he was always dialoguing for his reindeer friend. It was silly, but she loved it, and so she took “Sven’s” advice and listened to her surroundings. At first, all she could make out was the occasional swish of a horse’s tail flicking flies away and the mewling of the kittens tumbling around one of the water troughs, but eventually, beneath the usual sounds, she heard an odd buzz that sounded like…

“Oh!” Anna’s eyes widened and she hurried to the far end of the stables, where there was a little window. Peering through it, she saw just what she had suspected: a small crowd of villagers gathered in the courtyard. And though Anna couldn’t see exactly what they were surrounding, she knew exactly who it would be: Elsa.

Wherever Elsa went, people seemed to follow. They were there in the morning, asking her questions about what should be done in the afternoon, asking what they should be doing in the evening, asking what they should do tomorrow. Elsa’s table in the council chambers was always heaped with papers, and more often than not, Anna only caught a glimpse of her sister as Gerda ushered her from one appointment to another, always tapping the comically large calendar like a metronome to keep Elsa on the day’s beat.

And Elsa’s frantic schedule had only gotten busier over the last month, because at the end of this week, she would at last follow the tradition started by their grandfather King Runeard: setting off on a grand tour of the world. In five days, Elsa would leave from the Arenfjord, the body of water on which Arendelle was built, sailing past Weselton and the Southern Isles before heading east to explore lands like Zaria, Royaume, Chatho, Tikaani, Eldora, Torres, and Corona, to name a few. Elsa would meet everyone: dignitaries and dancers, scientists, painters, and prized mountain goats. And she would be going without Anna.

When Kai, the castle’s old steward, had first mentioned it was time for Elsa to start planning for her grand tour, Anna had assumed she would be going with her older sister. But as the months dwindled down to weeks and then to days, Elsa still hadn’t invited her. And it wasn’t as though Anna hadn’t given Elsa plenty of chances to ask her. Only last week, Anna had oh-so-casually mentioned that it had always been a dream of hers to see the Chathoan ballet—and she’d said so in Chathoanese. She’d spent days perfecting her accent. Before that, she’d performed Tikaani’s national anthem for everyone at the castle, with an accompaniment by Olaf, the snowman whom Elsa had created three years ago with her magical ice powers, on a carrot-nose flute. So far, though, none of Anna’s efforts had worked.

But that was going to change today.

Or so she had planned.

Still peering through the window, Anna frowned as even more villagers in brightly colored shawls and jackets entered through the castle gates and hurried to join the crowd around Elsa.

Anna had been racking her mind all week and had finally decided that the perfect time would be this morning, during their last scheduled sisterly ride through the woods before Elsa’s departure. Anna knew that Elsa found the quiet of the forest peaceful, and she hoped that it would lead to the perfect moment to ask Elsa if she could go on the grand tour with her. A ride was also a good opportunity to prove that Anna could be a useful traveling companion. That she was helpful and wouldn’t get in the way. But that was part of the trouble. Elsa didn’t seem to need any help.

Though Elsa had only been crowned queen three years before, Anna already knew her older sister would be remembered as one of the great rulers of Arendelle, like the ones who appeared on the tapestry that hung across from Anna’s bed. Her sister appeared to always have everything under control—even her magical powers—with a regal presence that all respected. Whenever Elsa listened to Anna, she made Anna feel special and important, and at twenty-four years old, Elsa carried herself the same way she seemed to do everything: effortlessly.

“It’s been like that since she got here,” Kristoff said, coming to stand next to Anna and look out the stables’ window. “Which,” he said, giving her a teasing look, “was half an hour ago.”

Anna made a face. “I know, I know—I overslept…again.” She needed to find some way to pull Elsa out of the crowd for their horseback ride. Before Elsa left her.

Something tugged on Anna’s foot, and she looked down to see that the tiny gray kitten had returned, determined, it seemed, to catch those devious laces.

“Hey, Kristoff?” Anna said slowly, still watching the persistent kitten, only the size her palm, take on her large boot. “I think I have an idea. Do you have a minute?”

“For you?” Kristoff winked. “Always.”

Anna grinned as she wrenched the kitten off her laces and placed it into Kristoff’s arms. “Perfect! So, here’s the plan….”

A few minutes later, Anna left the stables and hurried out to the friendly crowd in the courtyard. As she got closer, she could hear their questions piling up all around Elsa.

“Your Majesty, the chimney in our forge has cracks, and I’m worried it won’t be mended in time for the winter,” called Ada Diaz, a woman with curly brown hair standing next to her wife, Tuva Diaz, who had even curlier brown hair. They were the best blacksmiths on the continent and were known for making the luckiest horseshoes, though it seemed even an abundance of lucky horseshoes weren’t as helpful as their queen’s collected wisdom.

“I was here first,” another familiar-looking villager sniped at Ada before turning in Elsa’s direction and bowing. “Your Majesty, you promised that the rocks in my garden would be removed by the beginning of autumn, and look—” He held up a red oak leaf. “It’s autumn!”

“Ah-hem,” yet another said. “The Village Crown is waiting for you to announce who the judges will be for the harvest festival this year, Your Majesty. Do you have the names?” Though Anna couldn’t see this particular person in the crowd, she knew, just by hearing his voice and grating, know-it-all cough, that it was Wael, the self-proclaimed reporter for the village, whose slick black hair always matched his ink-stained hands.

Sidling toward Elsa, Anna counted down silently. Three…two…one…Then she signaled for Kristoff.

“Oh, my goodness, Sven!” Kristoff proclaimed loudly from the stables’ entrance. “Look at these adorable kittens!”

“They’re cuter than you!” he said in Sven’s voice.

And during the brief second that everyone in the crowd turned to look at the kittens frolicking in the far corner of the courtyard, Anna darted into the throng, grabbed Elsa’s hand, and pulled her around the back of the stables and inside.

“Anna!” Elsa gasped as they ducked around a corner, where the fully saddled Havski and Fjøra, the swiftest horses in the stables, stood waiting for them. “What are you doing?”

Anna grinned. “Breaking you free!”

“But…” Elsa protested, sweeping a loose tendril of ice-blond hair off her forehead, “the villagers, they need my help—”

“I know!” Anna nodded. “But Kai and Gerda can handle their requests, and it’s important for you to ride out one last time before you set sail—just to make sure everything is in order. Don’t you agree? Besides,” she added, beaming even wider, “don’t you want to spend some time with me?”

Even though she’d been handling complaints all morning, Elsa still seemed regal and calm. The wind blew though an open door and buffeted her diaphanous blue split cape and coat, and tugged at the fishtail braid hanging over her left shoulder. For a moment, she looked like a timeless, valiant queen from one of Anna’s history books. But the next second, she flashed a grin at Anna, and it was like it had been before—when they were just two children sneaking out of their bedrooms for a nighttime adventure.

“I suppose I could let Kai and Gerda take care of things—just this once,” Elsa said.

Anna let out a whoop of joy. She swung up onto Havski’s back while Elsa took a moment to clamber on top of Fjøra, a beautiful horse with a black-and-white striped tail. Finally, after a few attempts, Elsa mounted. Together, they trotted out of the stables and left the courtyard, with Anna waving to Kristoff, who smiled from under a pile of kittens batting at his face.

The sisters crossed the Bridge of Arches and took in the wild, fresh autumn air. Behind them, nestled in the shadow of soaring mountains, the castle sparkled and shone with the decorative touches of Elsa’s ice magic. Anna kicked her horse into a canter, and Elsa did the same.

Arendelle was a kingdom of wilderness, of rugged coasts, deep blue waters, and towering ships. Lots and lots of ships. They came from everywhere, bringing people from all over the world who were happy to settle down in the picturesque kingdom—people who were happy to answer Anna’s invitation to share memories of their own countries so she could learn about their customs. Memories that could help Anna prepare Elsa for the grand tour…if only Elsa would let her. Because while ships brought people to the kingdom, they also left with people. The royal ship currently sat in the harbor, loaded with goods and waiting for Elsa to board.

As they rode past the expanding village and people waving excitedly at them, a delighted fizziness filled Anna’s body. This was the best part of opening the kingdom gates three years ago—all the new people and new ideas that had trickled in. Although the village was more populous than ever before, with more and more people having moved there, Arendelle would always be Anna’s heart and home. That was one thing that would never change.

As they moved beyond the houses and shops, the forest of Arendelle flourished around them, showing off in bright yellows, deep reds, and burnt oranges that reminded Anna of bonfires and melted caramels. A happy sigh slipped from Anna. The autumn leaves had just begun to turn and change, and the living things of the forest seemed to be settling into themselves, the same way Elsa had settled into being queen. Anna didn’t particularly like change. She always wanted things to stay the same. These days, Anna barely got to see Elsa, who was constantly cooped up in the council chambers poring over paperwork, or else leading important meetings that Anna also attended. But she was happy watching Elsa come into her own, even if it meant their relationship was evolving as a side effect of it.

The horses slowed, picking up an easy trot side by side. Wondering if now was the moment, Anna glanced over at Elsa. Her sister wore a far-off and pensive look on her face.

“What are you thinking about?” Anna asked.

“Oh.” Elsa looked up from her reins. “Nothing…just, you know, work.”

“Want to tell me?” Anna said, trying to keep her eagerness down to about a level eight, instead of her usual level ten. “You remember what Father always said, right?”

Elsa tilted her head. “What, that ‘burdens should be shared’?”

Something scraped in Anna, like a rough crumb caught in her throat. Because…well, her family’s burdens and secrets hadn’t been for everyone. Or at least, they hadn’t been for Anna. Her father had let a mountain troll bundle away Anna’s memories of Elsa’s ice magic, and he, her mother, and Elsa had all worked together to keep it a secret from Anna.

And it had stayed a very, very big secret, until Elsa’s coronation day, when Anna had pushed the new queen a little too far and Elsa had lost control of her temper—and her ice powers. Which, at the time, had seemed as terrible as the vast and eternal winter that had taken root in the kingdom, but in hindsight had been the best thing to ever happen to Anna. Not only had it marked the beginning of a new era with her sister, but Anna had also narrowly managed to avoid a very…hasty…marriage with a prince who had deceived her.

“Nope! Not that one!” Anna shook her head, wishing she could shake away the uncomfortable feeling. “The other saying—the one about ‘many hands make light work.’”

“Oh.” Elsa laughed. “He had a lot of sayings, didn’t he?”

Anna waited for Elsa to keep talking, but she seemed to have forgotten Anna was there again even though she was trotting alongside her.

“Hey, Elsa?” she tried again.

“Hmm?”

“Bet I can beat you to the clearing!”

“What?”

But Anna had already kicked Havski back into a gallop. Havski surged forward, setting Anna’s heart free. Riding the gray horse was like riding an avalanche: fast, thrilling, and powerful. Adrenaline rushed through her, and without thinking, she let go of the reins.

“What are you doing?” Elsa shouted from behind her.

“Flying!” Anna shouted back. She flung out her arms. Cool wind flowed over her face, and it seemed to blow away that tight feeling that had settled on her chest since Elsa had announced she was leaving. Elsa yelled something, but the wind swept her words away.

“What?” Anna glanced over her shoulder.

“BRANCH!” Elsa yelled again.

Anna swung forward just in time to duck beneath a birch tree’s low-hanging branch. Giggling, she hugged Havski’s neck and the horse snorted in response, never missing a stride. And why should he? They’d grown up together, and for a long time, he’d been the closest thing Anna had had to a best friend. They’d dodged thicker branches and jumped across wider rivers together. Picking up the reins again, she kept them loose and let Havski settle into a breathless canter.

Gradually, his strides shortened and he transitioned into an easy trot before reaching a mossy clearing. There was a crunch and the sound of twigs snapping, and Anna twisted in her saddle just in time to see Elsa and Fjøra blunder into the clearing. A single scarlet leaf had snagged on Elsa’s hair, and it looked almost as though the forest had crowned her its autumn queen.

Anna grinned. “Isn’t this fun?”

Sweeping away loose strands of her blond hair, Elsa plucked the leaf off her head, looked at it, and began to laugh. “It is,” she agreed.

Anna felt like a miniature sun had ignited in her chest.

Eventually, they neared the tamed, bountiful farmlands, and Anna, sneaking glances at Elsa, saw that her sister had finally settled into her saddle and was looking around the landscape with curious eyes. She seemed at ease. She seemed relaxed. Maybe it was time for Anna to finally ask her burning question. As they turned left, they passed a beautiful orchard with bright red apples and autumn leaves so orange that the world looked like it had been set aflame. Apples. Perfect.

Anna pointed at them. “Did you know that there’s an apple on the royal flag of Zaria?” she said oh-so-casually. “And that’s because it’s always customary for a guest to present an apple to the host.” A worry pricked Anna’s thoughts. “Your ship does have apples on board, right?”

Elsa shook her head. “Yes, Anna—you’ve made sure of it! If I have any more barrels of gifts you’ve suggested for everyone, my ship will be too heavy to leave the harbor!”

Anna swept her bangs out of her eyes and laughed. “What would you do without me?” She tugged on the reins, gently pulling Havski to a halt. “Elsa, I wanted to ask you something. I was wondering if I could join—” But before she could finish, Havski’s ears flattened as a rustling came from nearby.

A villager burst from the underbrush, panting heavily as she lifted her green skirts high so she could run.

It took Anna a moment to place her—there were so many new villagers in Arendelle these days—but then she recognized SoYun Lim, a girl Anna’s own age who’d recently started to herd cattle on a farm not far from there. Anna had talked to her over the summer, during one of the castle’s hosted bonfire nights, and had asked her about her native country of Chatho. Research, of course, for the grand tour. In fact, SoYun had been the one to help Anna perfect her Chathoanese accent.

But that girl always seemed as calm as a lake on a windless morning, her quiet nature soothing the animals she tended. The girl standing in front of her now was disheveled. Her jet-black braid, which usually hung as straight and tidy as a clothesline, was a series of escaping loops, and she had on two different boots—the left foot was clad in a tall black boot, while the right foot wore a soft brown leather one. But it wasn’t the strange state of her clothes or hair that sent warning bells tolling through Anna. It was the girl’s expression—wide-eyed, as though she’d seen a ghost—and the frantic way in which she flailed her arms to catch their attention.

“Your Majesty!” SoYun bobbed her head toward Elsa in a slight bow. “Thank goodness I caught up with you—something terrible has happened!”
chapters.zh:
安娜飞奔下第二大厅铺着地毯的城堡阶梯，一步跨两级。

她在楼梯平台上差点绊倒，却懒得放慢脚步。

钟楼早已敲过上午十点，而她向艾莎保证过不会迟到。

有那么一瞬，她想顺着扶手滑下去。

那确实是最快的移动方式，可二十一岁的她，对这样的事来说是不是太老了……对吧？

对。

可是……安娜的脚步慢了下来。

那白木扶手刚打过蜡，泛着光，仿佛在许诺着速度。

而她那双带跟的新马靴——是扎利亚一位使节送的礼物——还没穿顺脚，跑起来实在不太方便。

她回头瞥了一眼。

四下无人。

下定决心，她一把提起裙摆，一条腿跨上扶手，顺势滑下剩下的路程，到一楼平台时稳稳落地。

她冲过城堡大门，朝马厩飞奔而去。“艾莎！

我来了！”安娜压低声音喊着，穿过马厩门，走进那个满是干草清香、马儿轻轻咀嚼的安静世界。

她抚平黑裙的后摆，确认自己那条栗棕色长发仍被双辫固定得好好的。“我没迟到！

嗯，”她改口道，“不算太迟。

不过我刚才做了个特别有意思的梦，梦见……”她声音渐低，环顾四周。

她唯一的听众，是城堡里那些竖着耳朵的马，以及每次有人进门就跌跌撞撞涌向马厩门口的一窝小马崽。

可没有艾莎的踪影。

安娜把刘海从额头拨开，满心困惑。

不知怎的，尽管她睡过了头，竟还是比艾莎先到。

这可真奇怪。

非常、非常奇怪。

艾莎向来守时；这正是她如此杰出、深得全体阿伦黛尔人爱戴的诸多原因之一。

安娜抱起一只开始拍她鞋带、呼噜呼噜叫的灰猫崽，朝马具房迈了一步。

也许艾莎来得太早，决定去检查刚送来的苹果了。

安娜小心压低声音，免得惊了马，又喊了一声。“艾莎？”“你找错地方了，”一个友好的声音从马厩那头传来，一秒钟后，克斯托夫·比约格曼的脑袋从马栏门上探了出来，手里拿着干草叉，头发上沾着点稻草。

安娜咧嘴笑了。

每次在克斯托夫身边，她总会这样——她忍不住。

三年前克斯托夫刚开始频繁造访城堡时，格尔达——一个从小认识姐妹俩、还帮她们安排日程的人——曾对姐妹俩说，他像他采冰的那些山：宽厚而结实。

艾莎低声回说，他好像“人挺好”。安娜再追问，艾莎又加了个“金发”。这些都说得对，但在安娜眼里，克斯托夫不只是一个山里人，也不只是“人好”或“金发”，他是她最好的朋友——而且显然还不止于此，哪怕他有时确实带着股驯鹿味儿。

这完全说得通，毕竟他的另一个好朋友斯文就是头驯鹿。

斯文的脑袋也从马栏门上探出来看安娜，友好的抖了抖耳朵打招呼。

尽管安娜多次邀请斯文和克斯托夫搬进城堡里某间空房，他们俩却更愿待在马厩。

安娜猜想，他们夏天在山里为王国采了几个月冰，大概更享受马厩里这份不那么局促的空间。“她不在这儿？”安娜弯下腰，把猫崽轻轻放下，问道。

它小跑着去和别的猫崽会合了。

克斯托夫把手伸到斯文的下唇下，开始轻轻摆动，用斯文的嗓音说：“有人没在听。”安娜冲克斯托夫的“斯文代言”笑了——他总替驯鹿朋友说话。

这很傻，可她爱极了，于是她听从“斯文”的建议，留意起四周。

起初，她只辨得出马尾巴偶尔甩走苍蝇的嗖嗖声，还有小猫崽在饮水槽边翻滚的喵喵叫，但终于，在那些寻常声响之下，她听见一阵奇怪的嗡嗡声，像是……“噢！”安娜睁大眼睛，急忙奔向马厩那头的小窗。

她透过窗望去，正看见自己料到的一幕：一小群村民聚集在庭院里。

虽然安娜看不清他们围着的是什么，她却清楚那准是谁：艾莎。

艾莎走到哪儿，人们似乎就跟到哪儿。

早晨他们在那儿，问她下午该做什么；问晚上该做什么；问明天该做什么。

议事厅里艾莎的桌子总是堆满文件，安娜往往只能瞥见姐姐匆匆一眼——格尔达领着她赶一场接一场的约见，总像节拍器似的敲着那本大得滑稽的日历，好让艾莎踩准一天的节奏。

而艾莎那疯狂的日程在过去一个月里愈发忙碌，因为本周末，她终于要遵从祖父鲁内尔德国王定下的传统：启程进行一场环球大巡游。

五天后，艾莎将从阿伦峡湾——阿伦黛尔就建在这片水域上——启航，驶过维塞尔顿和南方群岛，然后向东去探索扎利亚、罗亚姆、查索、提卡尼、埃尔多拉、托雷斯、科罗纳等诸国。

艾莎将见到所有人：使节与舞者、科学家、画家，还有备受珍视的山羊。

而她这一去，没有安娜相伴。

当城堡老管家凯伊第一次提起，该让艾莎开始筹划环球巡游时，安娜以为自己会跟姐姐一起去。

可随着月份缩成星期、又缩成天数，艾莎仍未邀请她。

而且安娜并非没给艾莎很多开口邀请她的机会。

就在上周，安娜还煞有介事地随口提起，能看一场查索芭蕾一直是她的梦想——而且她是用查索语说的。

她花了好几天打磨自己的口音。

在那之前，她还为大家表演了提卡尼的国歌，由三年前艾莎用魔法冰力造出的雪人奥拉夫用胡萝卜鼻笛伴奏。

不过到目前为止，安娜的努力全都没奏效。

但今天，一切都会改变。

至少她是这样计划的。

安娜仍望着窗外，眉头皱了起来——更多披着鲜亮披肩、穿着鲜艳外套的村民从城堡大门进来，匆匆挤进围着艾莎的人堆。

安娜苦想了整整一周，终于认定最佳的时机就是今天早上——在艾莎出发前，姐妹俩最后一次按计划进行的林间骑行。

安娜知道，艾莎觉得森林的静谧令人安宁，她希望这能带来完美的时机，好开口问艾莎能否带她一起去巡游。

这趟骑行也是个好机会，能证明安娜会是个有用的旅伴。

证明她帮得上忙，不会碍事。

可这正是麻烦的一部分。

艾莎似乎不需要任何帮忙。

尽管艾莎三年前才加冕，安娜已经知道姐姐会被铭记为阿伦黛尔的伟君之一，就像挂在安娜床对面的挂毯上的那些君王。

姐姐似乎总能掌控一切——连她的魔法也一样——带着一种人人敬重的王者气度。

每当艾莎听安娜说话，总让安娜觉得自己特别又重要；二十四岁的艾莎举手投足间，和她做每件事一样：从容不迫。“她来了之后一直这样，”克斯托夫走过来站在安娜身边，望着马厩的窗外说道。“也就是，”他调侃地看了她一眼，“半小时前的事。”安娜做了个鬼脸。“我知道，我知道——我又睡过头了。”她得想个法子把艾莎从人堆里拽出来，好去骑马。

在艾莎撇下她之前。

有什么东西拽了拽安娜的脚，她低头一看，那只小灰猫崽又回来了，看样子铁了心要逮住那些狡猾的鞋带。“嘿，克斯托夫？”安娜慢吞吞地说，仍看着那只只有她掌心大、却锲而不舍地缠着她大靴子的猫崽。“我有点主意了。

你有空吗？”“为你？”克斯托夫眨眨眼。“随时奉陪。”安娜笑着把猫崽从鞋带上扯下来，塞进克斯托夫怀里。“太好了！

那么，计划是这样的……”几分钟后，安娜离开马厩，匆匆走向庭院里那群和善的村民。

越靠近，她越能听见人们的问题在艾莎周围越堆越高。“陛下，我们锻炉的烟囱裂了，我担心赶不上冬天前修好，”阿达·迪亚兹喊道——这是个棕色卷发的女人，站在她妻子图娃·迪亚兹身旁，而图娃的棕发卷得更厉害。

他们是大陆上最好的铁匠，以打造最幸运的马掌闻名，不过看来，再多的幸运马掌也不如女王沉稳的智慧管用。“我先来的，”另一个面熟的村民抢白阿达，转而朝艾莎鞠了一躬。“陛下，您答应过我，花园里的石头会在初秋前搬走，您看——”他举起一片红橡树叶。“秋天到了！”“咳咳，”又一人说。“村冠奖正等着您宣布今年丰收节由谁当评委呢，陛下。

名单有了吗？”尽管安娜在人群里看不见这个人，可光听那嗓音和那副自以为了不起、叫人刺耳的咳嗽，她就认出那是韦尔——村里自封的记者，那一头油亮黑发总和他沾满墨迹的手相配。

安娜侧身滑向艾莎，在心里默默倒数。

三……二……一……然后她给克斯托夫使了个眼色。“噢，天哪，斯文！”克斯托夫在马厩门口大声宣布。“快看这些可爱的小猫崽！”“它们比你还可爱！”他用斯文的嗓音说。

趁着人群那一瞬全部转头去看在庭院远角嬉戏的小猫崽，安娜窜进人堆，一把抓住艾莎的手，把她拽到马厩后头拉了进去。“安娜！”拐过角落时艾莎倒吸一口气，那里备好鞍的哈夫斯基和弗约拉——马厩里最快的两匹马——正等着她们。“你在干什么？”安娜咧嘴一笑。“把你救出来！”“可是……”艾莎一边把额前一缕散落的冰金色头发拨开，一边抗议，“村民们，他们需要我帮忙——”“我知道！”安娜点头。“可凯伊和格尔达能应付他们的请求，而且出发前最后骑一次马对你很重要——就为确保一切无误。

你不同意吗？

再说了，”她笑得更灿烂了，“你不想跟我待一会儿吗？”尽管整个上午都在处理抱怨，艾莎却依旧从容而威严。

风从敞开的门吹入，鼓起她那半透明的蓝色分体披风和外套，扯动着垂在左肩的鱼尾辫。

有那么一刻，她像极了安娜历史书里那位永垂不朽、英勇无畏的女王。

可下一秒，她冲安娜绽开笑容，仿佛回到了从前——那时她们还只是两个溜出卧室去夜探的两个孩子。“我想，我可以让凯伊和格尔达料理——就这一次，”艾莎说。

安娜开心地欢呼一声。

她翻身上了哈夫斯基的背，艾莎则花了点工夫爬上弗约拉——一匹尾巴黑白条纹相间的骏马。

试了几下，艾莎终于骑稳了。

她们一同小跑出马厩，离开庭院，安娜朝克斯托夫挥手，他正埋在一堆扑他脸的小猫崽下笑着。

姐妹俩越过拱桥，呼吸着旷野里清新的秋日空气。

身后，城堡依偎在高耸群山的阴影里，因艾莎冰魔法的点缀而熠熠生辉。

安娜催马小跑，艾莎也照做。

阿伦黛尔是个荒野之国，有崎岖的海岸、深蓝的海水，和高耸的船舶。

许许多多的船。

它们来自四方，带来世界各地乐意在这如画王国定居的人——这些人也乐意响应安娜的邀请，分享祖国的记忆，好让她了解各地的风土人情。

这些记忆能帮安娜为巡游给艾莎做准备……只要艾莎肯让她来。

因为船既把人送来王国，也载着人离开。

那艘皇家船如今停在港湾，装满了货物，等着艾莎登船。

她们骑马经过不断扩张的村庄，人们兴奋地向她们挥手，安娜浑身涌起一股雀跃的酥痒感。

这是三年前敞开王国大门最棒的部分——所有新人和新思想如细流般涌入。

尽管村庄比以往任何时候都更热闹，搬来的人越来越多，阿伦黛尔永远是安娜的心之所系与家园。

这是永不会变的一点。

她们越过房舍与店铺，阿伦黛尔的森林在四周繁茂生长，炫耀着明黄、深红与焦橙，让安娜想起篝火和融化的焦糖。

安娜轻轻舒了口气，满是欢喜。

秋叶刚开始变幻颜色，森林里的生灵似乎也安顿下来，正如艾莎安顿于女王之位。

安娜并不怎么喜欢变化。

她总希望一切如常。

这些日子，安娜几乎见不到艾莎，她不是成天闷在议事厅里钻研文件，就是主持安娜也参加的重要会议。

可她乐于看艾莎找到自我，即便这意味着她们的关系正随之悄然改变。

马儿慢下来，并肩踏起轻快的小步。

安娜想着此刻是不是时机，瞥了一眼艾莎。

姐姐脸上浮着一种出神而若有所思的神情。“你在想什么？”安娜问。“哦。”艾莎从缰绳上抬起眼。“没什么……就是，你知道的，公事。”“想跟我说说吗？”安娜说，努力把热切压到八分，而不是平素的十分。“你记得父亲总说的话吧？”艾莎偏了偏头。“什么，‘重担应当共担’？”安娜心里咯噔一下，像有颗粗粝的面包屑卡在喉咙。

因为……嗯，家里的重担和秘密，并非人尽可知。

至少，对安娜就不是。

父亲曾让一只山地地精把安娜关于艾莎冰魔法的记忆一并卷走，而他、母亲和艾莎齐心合力，对安娜瞒下了这个秘密。

这个秘密一直藏得很深很深，直到艾莎加冕那天，安娜把新女王逼得太过，艾莎才失控了脾气——也失控了冰力。

当时看来，这就像在王国扎根的无垠永冬一样可怕，可事后想来，却是发生在安娜身上最好的事。

它不光标志了与姐姐新纪元的开端，安娜还险险避开了与一位骗了她王子的、极其……仓促……的婚姻。“不！

不是那句！”安娜摇头，恨不得把那股不舒服的感觉也甩掉。“是另一句——‘众人拾柴火焰高’那句。”“哦。”艾莎笑了。“他的格言可真多，是不是？”安娜等着艾莎接着说，可她似乎又把安娜忘了，尽管正并肩小跑着。“嘿，艾莎？”她又试了一次。“嗯？”“打赌我能比你先到空地！”“什么？”可安娜早已催动哈夫斯基重新飞奔起来。

哈夫斯基向前一窜，安娜的心也自由了。

骑这匹灰马，就像骑着一场雪崩：飞快、刺激而有力。

肾上腺素在她体内奔涌，她想都没想就松开了缰绳。“你在干什么？”艾莎在身后喊。“飞！”安娜喊回去。

她张开双臂。

凉风拂过她的脸，仿佛吹散了自艾莎宣布离开以来压在她胸口的那种紧绷感。

艾莎喊了句什么，却被风卷走了。“什么？”安娜回头瞥了一眼。“树枝！”艾莎又喊。

安娜及时向前一伏，从一棵桦树低垂的枝下闪过。

她咯咯笑着搂住哈夫斯基的脖子，马儿喷了喷鼻息回应，步子丝毫没乱。

他何必乱呢？

他们一起长大，很长一段时间里，他几乎是安娜最亲近的“最好朋友”。

他们一起闪过更密的枝，一起跃过更宽的河。

她重新拾起缰绳，松松握着，让哈夫斯基转入一阵畅快的奔驰。

渐渐地，他的步幅缩短，在进入一片长满青苔的空地前转为轻快的小跑。

一阵嘎吱声和细枝折断的脆响传来，安娜在鞍上扭身，正好看见艾莎和弗约拉跌跌撞撞冲进空地。

一片猩红的叶子挂在了艾莎发间，看起来几乎像森林为她加冕，封她为秋之女王。

安娜咧嘴一笑。“这不好玩吗？”艾莎拂开散落的金发，把那片叶子从头上摘下，看了看，笑了起来。“好玩，”她表示赞同。

安娜觉得胸口里点亮了一颗小小的太阳。

终于，她们接近了被驯服而丰饶的农田，安娜偷瞄艾莎，见姐姐终于安稳坐进鞍里，好奇地环顾四周景色。

她显得自在。

她显得放松。

也许是时候，让安娜终于问出那个憋了很久的问题了。

她们向左转，经过一座美丽的果园，红艳艳的苹果和橙得发亮的秋叶，让世界仿佛着了火。

苹果。

完美。

安娜指向它们。“你知道扎利亚的皇家旗帜上有一只苹果吗？”她故作随意地说。“那是因为客人向来要给主人献一只苹果，这是惯例。”一丝担忧刺进安娜的心思。“你的船上备了苹果吧，对吧？”艾莎摇摇头。“备了，安娜——这可是你盯着的！

要是再装上你给每个人都建议的成桶礼物，我的船怕是重得开不出港湾了！”安娜把刘海从眼前拨开，笑了。“没我你怎么办？”她轻拉缰绳，缓缓让哈夫斯基停下。“艾莎，我想问你点事。

我在想我能不能一起——”可没等她说完，附近一阵窸窣声让哈夫斯基的耳朵向后贴平。

一个村民从灌木丛里冲出来，气喘吁吁，高高提起绿裙以便奔跑。

安娜愣了一下才认出她——如今阿伦黛尔的新村民太多了——但随即她认出了林小允，一个和安娜同龄的姑娘，最近开始在附近一座农场放牛。

安娜夏天曾在城堡举办的一场篝火夜谈上和她聊过，问起她的故国查索。

当然是为其巡游做准备的研究。

事实上，正是小允帮安娜打磨了查索口音。

可那姑娘向来像无风清晨的湖面般平静，她安静的性子安抚着照料的动物。

此刻站在她面前的姑娘却是一副狼狈相。

她那乌黑的辫子平时直挺挺、整齐得像晾衣绳，此刻却散成一串乱环，而且她穿了两只不一样的靴子——左脚是只高筒黑靴，右脚却是只柔软的棕色皮靴。

可让安娜警铃大作的，不是她衣衫或头发这副怪相。

而是那姑娘的表情——瞪大双眼，仿佛见了鬼——以及她拼命挥臂、想引起她们注意的慌张模样。“陛下！”小允朝艾莎微微低头行礼。“谢天谢地追上您了——出大事了！”

sentences.en: ANNA FLEW DOWN the carpeted castle stairs of the second great hall, taking them two at a time.
sentences.zh: 安娜飞奔下第二大厅铺着地毯的城堡阶梯，一步跨两级。

sentences.en: She nearly tripped on the landing, but she didn’t bother to slow down.
sentences.zh: 她在楼梯平台上差点绊倒，却懒得放慢脚步。

sentences.en: The clock tower had already tolled ten in the morning, and she’d promised Elsa she wouldn’t be late.
sentences.zh: 钟楼早已敲过上午十点，而她向艾莎保证过不会迟到。

sentences.en: For a second, she thought about sliding down the banister.
sentences.zh: 有那么一瞬，她想顺着扶手滑下去。

sentences.en: It really was the fastest way to get around, but at twenty-one she was too old for such things…right?
sentences.zh: 那确实是最快的移动方式，可二十一岁的她，对这样的事来说是不是太老了……对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But… Anna’s feet slowed.
sentences.zh: 可是……安娜的脚步慢了下来。

sentences.en: The white wood of the banister gleamed with a recent polish and the promise of speed.
sentences.zh: 那白木扶手刚打过蜡，泛着光，仿佛在许诺着速度。

sentences.en: And her new riding boots with heels—a gift from a dignitary from Zaria—hadn’t been broken in yet and weren’t exactly the best for running.
sentences.zh: 而她那双带跟的新马靴——是扎利亚一位使节送的礼物——还没穿顺脚，跑起来实在不太方便。

sentences.en: She glanced over her shoulder.
sentences.zh: 她回头瞥了一眼。

sentences.en: No one was around.
sentences.zh: 四下无人。

sentences.en: Decision made, she hauled the skirt of her dress into her arms, slung a leg over the banister, and slid the rest of the way down, landing with ease as she reached the first-floor landing.
sentences.zh: 下定决心，她一把提起裙摆，一条腿跨上扶手，顺势滑下剩下的路程，到一楼平台时稳稳落地。

sentences.en: She flew through the castle doors and raced outside, toward the stables. “Elsa!
sentences.zh: 她冲过城堡大门，朝马厩飞奔而去。“艾莎！

sentences.en: I’m here!” Anna whisper-called as she moved through the barn doors and entered the quiet world of sweet hay and softly munching horses.
sentences.zh: 我来了！”安娜压低声音喊着，穿过马厩门，走进那个满是干草清香、马儿轻轻咀嚼的安静世界。

sentences.en: She smoothed down the back of her black dress and checked to make sure that her long chestnut brown hair was still pinned in place by a double braid. “I’m not late!
sentences.zh: 她抚平黑裙的后摆，确认自己那条栗棕色长发仍被双辫固定得好好的。“我没迟到！

sentences.en: Well,” she amended, “not that late.
sentences.zh: 嗯，”她改口道，“不算太迟。

sentences.en: But I was having the most fascinating dream where…” She trailed off, and looked around.
sentences.zh: 不过我刚才做了个特别有意思的梦，梦见……”她声音渐低，环顾四周。

sentences.en: Her only audience was the alert ears of the castle horses and the litter of barn kittens that came stumbling toward the stables’ entrance whenever someone entered.
sentences.zh: 她唯一的听众，是城堡里那些竖着耳朵的马，以及每次有人进门就跌跌撞撞涌向马厩门口的一窝小马崽。

sentences.en: But there was no sign of Elsa.
sentences.zh: 可没有艾莎的踪影。

sentences.en: Anna brushed her bangs off her forehead, confused.
sentences.zh: 安娜把刘海从额头拨开，满心困惑。

sentences.en: Somehow, even though she’d overslept, she had managed to beat Elsa.
sentences.zh: 不知怎的，尽管她睡过了头，竟还是比艾莎先到。

sentences.en: Which was odd.
sentences.zh: 这可真奇怪。

sentences.en: Very, very odd.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常奇怪。

sentences.en: Elsa was always on time; it was one of the many reasons she was such a great queen, beloved by all of Arendelle.
sentences.zh: 艾莎向来守时；这正是她如此杰出、深得全体阿伦黛尔人爱戴的诸多原因之一。

sentences.en: Picking up a purring gray kitten that had begun to bat at her bootlaces, Anna took a step toward the livery.
sentences.zh: 安娜抱起一只开始拍她鞋带、呼噜呼噜叫的灰猫崽，朝马具房迈了一步。

sentences.en: Maybe Elsa had gotten here so early that she’d decided to inspect the recent delivery of apples.
sentences.zh: 也许艾莎来得太早，决定去检查刚送来的苹果了。

sentences.en: Careful to keep her voice low so as not to startle the horses, Anna called out again. “Elsa?” “You’re looking in the wrong place,” a friendly voice called from the far end of the stables, and a second later, Kristoff Bjorgman’s head popped over a stall door, a pitchfork in his hand and a bit of straw in his hair.
sentences.zh: 安娜小心压低声音，免得惊了马，又喊了一声。“艾莎？”“你找错地方了，”一个友好的声音从马厩那头传来，一秒钟后，克斯托夫·比约格曼的脑袋从马栏门上探了出来，手里拿着干草叉，头发上沾着点稻草。

sentences.en: Anna grinned.
sentences.zh: 安娜咧嘴笑了。

sentences.en: She always did whenever she was around Kristoff—she couldn’t help it.
sentences.zh: 每次在克斯托夫身边，她总会这样——她忍不住。

sentences.en: When Kristoff had first started to visit the castle frequently three years before, Gerda, one of the people who had known the girls since they were young, and who also helped them schedule their time, had remarked to the sisters that he resembled the mountains from which he harvested ice: broad and solid.
sentences.zh: 三年前克斯托夫刚开始频繁造访城堡时，格尔达——一个从小认识姐妹俩、还帮她们安排日程的人——曾对姐妹俩说，他像他采冰的那些山：宽厚而结实。

sentences.en: Elsa had whispered back that he seemed “nice.” When Anna had pushed her for a little bit more, Elsa had added “blond.” All of which was true, but to Anna, Kristoff wasn’t just a mountain man or “nice” or “blond,” he was her best friend—and definitely something more , even if he did sometimes smell like a reindeer.
sentences.zh: 艾莎低声回说，他好像“人挺好”。安娜再追问，艾莎又加了个“金发”。这些都说得对，但在安娜眼里，克斯托夫不只是一个山里人，也不只是“人好”或“金发”，他是她最好的朋友——而且显然还不止于此，哪怕他有时确实带着股驯鹿味儿。

sentences.en: Which was completely understandable, given his other best friend, Sven, was a reindeer.
sentences.zh: 这完全说得通，毕竟他的另一个好朋友斯文就是头驯鹿。

sentences.en: Sven’s head popped over the stall door to look at Anna, and he twitched his ears in a friendly hello.
sentences.zh: 斯文的脑袋也从马栏门上探出来看安娜，友好的抖了抖耳朵打招呼。

sentences.en: Though Anna had invited both Sven and Kristoff multiple times to take up residence in one of the many spare rooms of the castle, they both preferred to stay in the stables.
sentences.zh: 尽管安娜多次邀请斯文和克斯托夫搬进城堡里某间空房，他们俩却更愿待在马厩。

sentences.en: Anna suspected they enjoyed the less confined living space of the barn after spending the summer months in the mountains harvesting ice for the kingdom. “She’s not here?” Anna asked, bending to set the kitten down gently.
sentences.zh: 安娜猜想，他们夏天在山里为王国采了几个月冰，大概更享受马厩里这份不那么局促的空间。“她不在这儿？”安娜弯下腰，把猫崽轻轻放下，问道。

sentences.en: It scampered away to join the others.
sentences.zh: 它小跑着去和别的猫崽会合了。

sentences.en: Kristoff moved his hand under Sven’s lower lip and began to wiggle it as he said in Sven’s voice, “Someone’s not listening .” Anna smiled at Kristoff’s “Sven Talk”—he was always dialoguing for his reindeer friend.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫把手伸到斯文的下唇下，开始轻轻摆动，用斯文的嗓音说：“有人没在听。”安娜冲克斯托夫的“斯文代言”笑了——他总替驯鹿朋友说话。

sentences.en: It was silly, but she loved it, and so she took “Sven’s” advice and listened to her surroundings.
sentences.zh: 这很傻，可她爱极了，于是她听从“斯文”的建议，留意起四周。

sentences.en: At first, all she could make out was the occasional swish of a horse’s tail flicking flies away and the mewling of the kittens tumbling around one of the water troughs, but eventually, beneath the usual sounds, she heard an odd buzz that sounded like… “Oh!” Anna’s eyes widened and she hurried to the far end of the stables, where there was a little window.
sentences.zh: 起初，她只辨得出马尾巴偶尔甩走苍蝇的嗖嗖声，还有小猫崽在饮水槽边翻滚的喵喵叫，但终于，在那些寻常声响之下，她听见一阵奇怪的嗡嗡声，像是……“噢！”安娜睁大眼睛，急忙奔向马厩那头的小窗。

sentences.en: Peering through it, she saw just what she had suspected: a small crowd of villagers gathered in the courtyard.
sentences.zh: 她透过窗望去，正看见自己料到的一幕：一小群村民聚集在庭院里。

sentences.en: And though Anna couldn’t see exactly what they were surrounding, she knew exactly who it would be: Elsa.
sentences.zh: 虽然安娜看不清他们围着的是什么，她却清楚那准是谁：艾莎。

sentences.en: Wherever Elsa went, people seemed to follow.
sentences.zh: 艾莎走到哪儿，人们似乎就跟到哪儿。

sentences.en: They were there in the morning, asking her questions about what should be done in the afternoon, asking what they should be doing in the evening, asking what they should do tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 早晨他们在那儿，问她下午该做什么；问晚上该做什么；问明天该做什么。

sentences.en: Elsa’s table in the council chambers was always heaped with papers, and more often than not, Anna only caught a glimpse of her sister as Gerda ushered her from one appointment to another, always tapping the comically large calendar like a metronome to keep Elsa on the day’s beat.
sentences.zh: 议事厅里艾莎的桌子总是堆满文件，安娜往往只能瞥见姐姐匆匆一眼——格尔达领着她赶一场接一场的约见，总像节拍器似的敲着那本大得滑稽的日历，好让艾莎踩准一天的节奏。

sentences.en: And Elsa’s frantic schedule had only gotten busier over the last month, because at the end of this week, she would at last follow the tradition started by their grandfather King Runeard: setting off on a grand tour of the world.
sentences.zh: 而艾莎那疯狂的日程在过去一个月里愈发忙碌，因为本周末，她终于要遵从祖父鲁内尔德国王定下的传统：启程进行一场环球大巡游。

sentences.en: In five days, Elsa would leave from the Arenfjord, the body of water on which Arendelle was built, sailing past Weselton and the Southern Isles before heading east to explore lands like Zaria, Royaume, Chatho, Tikaani, Eldora, Torres, and Corona, to name a few.
sentences.zh: 五天后，艾莎将从阿伦峡湾——阿伦黛尔就建在这片水域上——启航，驶过维塞尔顿和南方群岛，然后向东去探索扎利亚、罗亚姆、查索、提卡尼、埃尔多拉、托雷斯、科罗纳等诸国。

sentences.en: Elsa would meet everyone : dignitaries and dancers, scientists, painters, and prized mountain goats.
sentences.zh: 艾莎将见到所有人：使节与舞者、科学家、画家，还有备受珍视的山羊。

sentences.en: And she would be going without Anna.
sentences.zh: 而她这一去，没有安娜相伴。

sentences.en: When Kai, the castle’s old steward, had first mentioned it was time for Elsa to start planning for her grand tour, Anna had assumed she would be going with her older sister.
sentences.zh: 当城堡老管家凯伊第一次提起，该让艾莎开始筹划环球巡游时，安娜以为自己会跟姐姐一起去。

sentences.en: But as the months dwindled down to weeks and then to days, Elsa still hadn’t invited her.
sentences.zh: 可随着月份缩成星期、又缩成天数，艾莎仍未邀请她。

sentences.en: And it wasn’t as though Anna hadn’t given Elsa plenty of chances to ask her.
sentences.zh: 而且安娜并非没给艾莎很多开口邀请她的机会。

sentences.en: Only last week, Anna had oh-so-casually mentioned that it had always been a dream of hers to see the Chathoan ballet—and she’d said so in Chathoanese.
sentences.zh: 就在上周，安娜还煞有介事地随口提起，能看一场查索芭蕾一直是她的梦想——而且她是用查索语说的。

sentences.en: She’d spent days perfecting her accent.
sentences.zh: 她花了好几天打磨自己的口音。

sentences.en: Before that, she’d performed Tikaani’s national anthem for everyone at the castle, with an accompaniment by Olaf, the snowman whom Elsa had created three years ago with her magical ice powers, on a carrot-nose flute.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，她还为大家表演了提卡尼的国歌，由三年前艾莎用魔法冰力造出的雪人奥拉夫用胡萝卜鼻笛伴奏。

sentences.en: So far, though, none of Anna’s efforts had worked.
sentences.zh: 不过到目前为止，安娜的努力全都没奏效。

sentences.en: But that was going to change today.
sentences.zh: 但今天，一切都会改变。

sentences.en: Or so she had planned.
sentences.zh: 至少她是这样计划的。

sentences.en: Still peering through the window, Anna frowned as even more villagers in brightly colored shawls and jackets entered through the castle gates and hurried to join the crowd around Elsa.
sentences.zh: 安娜仍望着窗外，眉头皱了起来——更多披着鲜亮披肩、穿着鲜艳外套的村民从城堡大门进来，匆匆挤进围着艾莎的人堆。

sentences.en: Anna had been racking her mind all week and had finally decided that the perfect time would be this morning, during their last scheduled sisterly ride through the woods before Elsa’s departure.
sentences.zh: 安娜苦想了整整一周，终于认定最佳的时机就是今天早上——在艾莎出发前，姐妹俩最后一次按计划进行的林间骑行。

sentences.en: Anna knew that Elsa found the quiet of the forest peaceful, and she hoped that it would lead to the perfect moment to ask Elsa if she could go on the grand tour with her.
sentences.zh: 安娜知道，艾莎觉得森林的静谧令人安宁，她希望这能带来完美的时机，好开口问艾莎能否带她一起去巡游。

sentences.en: A ride was also a good opportunity to prove that Anna could be a useful traveling companion.
sentences.zh: 这趟骑行也是个好机会，能证明安娜会是个有用的旅伴。

sentences.en: That she was helpful and wouldn’t get in the way.
sentences.zh: 证明她帮得上忙，不会碍事。

sentences.en: But that was part of the trouble.
sentences.zh: 可这正是麻烦的一部分。

sentences.en: Elsa didn’t seem to need any help.
sentences.zh: 艾莎似乎不需要任何帮忙。

sentences.en: Though Elsa had only been crowned queen three years before, Anna already knew her older sister would be remembered as one of the great rulers of Arendelle, like the ones who appeared on the tapestry that hung across from Anna’s bed.
sentences.zh: 尽管艾莎三年前才加冕，安娜已经知道姐姐会被铭记为阿伦黛尔的伟君之一，就像挂在安娜床对面的挂毯上的那些君王。

sentences.en: Her sister appeared to always have everything under control—even her magical powers—with a regal presence that all respected.
sentences.zh: 姐姐似乎总能掌控一切——连她的魔法也一样——带着一种人人敬重的王者气度。

sentences.en: Whenever Elsa listened to Anna, she made Anna feel special and important, and at twenty-four years old, Elsa carried herself the same way she seemed to do everything: effortlessly. “It’s been like that since she got here,” Kristoff said, coming to stand next to Anna and look out the stables’ window. “Which,” he said, giving her a teasing look, “was half an hour ago.” Anna made a face. “I know, I know—I overslept…again.” She needed to find some way to pull Elsa out of the crowd for their horseback ride.
sentences.zh: 每当艾莎听安娜说话，总让安娜觉得自己特别又重要；二十四岁的艾莎举手投足间，和她做每件事一样：从容不迫。“她来了之后一直这样，”克斯托夫走过来站在安娜身边，望着马厩的窗外说道。“也就是，”他调侃地看了她一眼，“半小时前的事。”安娜做了个鬼脸。“我知道，我知道——我又睡过头了。”她得想个法子把艾莎从人堆里拽出来，好去骑马。

sentences.en: Before Elsa left her.
sentences.zh: 在艾莎撇下她之前。

sentences.en: Something tugged on Anna’s foot, and she looked down to see that the tiny gray kitten had returned, determined, it seemed, to catch those devious laces. “Hey, Kristoff?” Anna said slowly, still watching the persistent kitten, only the size her palm, take on her large boot. “I think I have an idea.
sentences.zh: 有什么东西拽了拽安娜的脚，她低头一看，那只小灰猫崽又回来了，看样子铁了心要逮住那些狡猾的鞋带。“嘿，克斯托夫？”安娜慢吞吞地说，仍看着那只只有她掌心大、却锲而不舍地缠着她大靴子的猫崽。“我有点主意了。

sentences.en: Do you have a minute?” “For you?” Kristoff winked. “Always.” Anna grinned as she wrenched the kitten off her laces and placed it into Kristoff’s arms. “Perfect!
sentences.zh: 你有空吗？”“为你？”克斯托夫眨眨眼。“随时奉陪。”安娜笑着把猫崽从鞋带上扯下来，塞进克斯托夫怀里。“太好了！

sentences.en: So, here’s the plan….” A few minutes later, Anna left the stables and hurried out to the friendly crowd in the courtyard.
sentences.zh: 那么，计划是这样的……”几分钟后，安娜离开马厩，匆匆走向庭院里那群和善的村民。

sentences.en: As she got closer, she could hear their questions piling up all around Elsa. “Your Majesty, the chimney in our forge has cracks, and I’m worried it won’t be mended in time for the winter,” called Ada Diaz, a woman with curly brown hair standing next to her wife, Tuva Diaz, who had even curlier brown hair.
sentences.zh: 越靠近，她越能听见人们的问题在艾莎周围越堆越高。“陛下，我们锻炉的烟囱裂了，我担心赶不上冬天前修好，”阿达·迪亚兹喊道——这是个棕色卷发的女人，站在她妻子图娃·迪亚兹身旁，而图娃的棕发卷得更厉害。

sentences.en: They were the best blacksmiths on the continent and were known for making the luckiest horseshoes, though it seemed even an abundance of lucky horseshoes weren’t as helpful as their queen’s collected wisdom. “I was here first,” another familiar-looking villager sniped at Ada before turning in Elsa’s direction and bowing. “Your Majesty, you promised that the rocks in my garden would be removed by the beginning of autumn, and look—” He held up a red oak leaf. “It’s autumn!” “Ah-hem,” yet another said. “The Village Crown is waiting for you to announce who the judges will be for the harvest festival this year, Your Majesty.
sentences.zh: 他们是大陆上最好的铁匠，以打造最幸运的马掌闻名，不过看来，再多的幸运马掌也不如女王沉稳的智慧管用。“我先来的，”另一个面熟的村民抢白阿达，转而朝艾莎鞠了一躬。“陛下，您答应过我，花园里的石头会在初秋前搬走，您看——”他举起一片红橡树叶。“秋天到了！”“咳咳，”又一人说。“村冠奖正等着您宣布今年丰收节由谁当评委呢，陛下。

sentences.en: Do you have the names?” Though Anna couldn’t see this particular person in the crowd, she knew, just by hearing his voice and grating, know-it-all cough, that it was Wael, the self-proclaimed reporter for the village, whose slick black hair always matched his ink-stained hands.
sentences.zh: 名单有了吗？”尽管安娜在人群里看不见这个人，可光听那嗓音和那副自以为了不起、叫人刺耳的咳嗽，她就认出那是韦尔——村里自封的记者，那一头油亮黑发总和他沾满墨迹的手相配。

sentences.en: Sidling toward Elsa, Anna counted down silently.
sentences.zh: 安娜侧身滑向艾莎，在心里默默倒数。

sentences.en: Three…two…one …Then she signaled for Kristoff. “Oh, my goodness, Sven!” Kristoff proclaimed loudly from the stables’ entrance. “Look at these adorable kittens!” “They’re cuter than you!” he said in Sven’s voice.
sentences.zh: 三……二……一……然后她给克斯托夫使了个眼色。“噢，天哪，斯文！”克斯托夫在马厩门口大声宣布。“快看这些可爱的小猫崽！”“它们比你还可爱！”他用斯文的嗓音说。

sentences.en: And during the brief second that everyone in the crowd turned to look at the kittens frolicking in the far corner of the courtyard, Anna darted into the throng, grabbed Elsa’s hand, and pulled her around the back of the stables and inside. “Anna!” Elsa gasped as they ducked around a corner, where the fully saddled Havski and Fjøra, the swiftest horses in the stables, stood waiting for them. “What are you doing?” Anna grinned. “Breaking you free!” “But…” Elsa protested, sweeping a loose tendril of ice-blond hair off her forehead, “the villagers, they need my help—” “I know!” Anna nodded. “But Kai and Gerda can handle their requests, and it’s important for you to ride out one last time before you set sail—just to make sure everything is in order.
sentences.zh: 趁着人群那一瞬全部转头去看在庭院远角嬉戏的小猫崽，安娜窜进人堆，一把抓住艾莎的手，把她拽到马厩后头拉了进去。“安娜！”拐过角落时艾莎倒吸一口气，那里备好鞍的哈夫斯基和弗约拉——马厩里最快的两匹马——正等着她们。“你在干什么？”安娜咧嘴一笑。“把你救出来！”“可是……”艾莎一边把额前一缕散落的冰金色头发拨开，一边抗议，“村民们，他们需要我帮忙——”“我知道！”安娜点头。“可凯伊和格尔达能应付他们的请求，而且出发前最后骑一次马对你很重要——就为确保一切无误。

sentences.en: Don’t you agree?
sentences.zh: 你不同意吗？

sentences.en: Besides,” she added, beaming even wider, “don’t you want to spend some time with me?” Even though she’d been handling complaints all morning, Elsa still seemed regal and calm.
sentences.zh: 再说了，”她笑得更灿烂了，“你不想跟我待一会儿吗？”尽管整个上午都在处理抱怨，艾莎却依旧从容而威严。

sentences.en: The wind blew though an open door and buffeted her diaphanous blue split cape and coat, and tugged at the fishtail braid hanging over her left shoulder.
sentences.zh: 风从敞开的门吹入，鼓起她那半透明的蓝色分体披风和外套，扯动着垂在左肩的鱼尾辫。

sentences.en: For a moment, she looked like a timeless, valiant queen from one of Anna’s history books.
sentences.zh: 有那么一刻，她像极了安娜历史书里那位永垂不朽、英勇无畏的女王。

sentences.en: But the next second, she flashed a grin at Anna, and it was like it had been before—when they were just two children sneaking out of their bedrooms for a nighttime adventure. “I suppose I could let Kai and Gerda take care of things—just this once,” Elsa said.
sentences.zh: 可下一秒，她冲安娜绽开笑容，仿佛回到了从前——那时她们还只是两个溜出卧室去夜探的两个孩子。“我想，我可以让凯伊和格尔达料理——就这一次，”艾莎说。

sentences.en: Anna let out a whoop of joy.
sentences.zh: 安娜开心地欢呼一声。

sentences.en: She swung up onto Havski’s back while Elsa took a moment to clamber on top of Fjøra, a beautiful horse with a black-and-white striped tail.
sentences.zh: 她翻身上了哈夫斯基的背，艾莎则花了点工夫爬上弗约拉——一匹尾巴黑白条纹相间的骏马。
