“Kristoff?” Anna interrupted, furrowing her eyebrows. “What about Kristoff?”

Elsa closed her eyes and rubbed her temples, just as Anna had suspected Elsa had wanted to do earlier. “He’s not here. I thought he’d be back by now, but…”

Worry zipped through Anna, but she forced herself to shrug. “I’m sure he’s fine,” she said. “You know how happy Bulda is whenever he visits.” She smiled, thinking of the mountain troll who’d raised Kristoff as her own. “I bet you he’s delayed because he’s so full of mushroom stew that he’s too heavy for Sven to carry, and they have to walk.”

But it seemed Elsa couldn’t be distracted from her worry, not even with the funny image. Elsa shook her head. “It’s so much pressure. I don’t know what I can do.”

“You mean, what we can do…with a secret book full of magic!” Anna said.

Elsa groaned. “Oh, Anna!” She shook her head. “I know you want it to be, but I don’t think magic is the answer to all of our problems.”

“Okay, I hear you, but look.” Anna held out Secrets of the Magic Makers. “There is so much information in here.” She flipped through the pages until she found the one she was looking for. “See? This one grants your dreams.”

Elsa sighed. “Anna, I told you not to go back in the secret room.”

“I didn’t go back into it. I grabbed this book before I left the first time. Look at it!”

Reluctantly, Elsa glanced down at the page that had been pushed under her nose, but before she had a chance to skim, Gerda pulled back the tapestry, wearing her signature green skirt, jacket, and cap, and holding Elsa’s great big calendar.

“Your Majesty, I’m sorry,” the woman said, and Anna could hear the sympathy in her voice, “but even with the grand tour postponed, this fiasco with the sickness has put us behind schedule. And now you must write explanations to all the different dignitaries and heads of countries to explain why you can’t make it.”

Elsa took a deep breath. “Yes, of course, Gerda, you’re right. The work of a queen is never complete.” She glanced over at Anna, who held her breath. “Here. Let me have that book. Maybe you’re right. I promise I’ll look at it as soon as I have a spare minute.”

“Of—of course,” Anna said, happy to share. But she would have been even happier if Elsa had told Gerda that Anna had found something important. That they were working on discovering a solution together.

“I’d like to meet with an animal expert now to get their opinion,” Elsa said, and Anna noticed again that she was tugging on her fingers. “And a botanist. I’m not sure what should be done first….”

“If you need someone to write letters, I can help with that,” Anna offered. “I’ve read up on all the different etiquettes of each country.”

“That should be just fine, dear,” Gerda said, her pencil already flying over the calendar to adjust it. “Just make sure Elsa signs them before you mail them.”

“I will!” Anna promised, happy to help Elsa and happy to have something to do while she waited for Kristoff to return to the castle. She had so many things she wanted to ask him, starting with, How do the trolls say we can cure the Blight? and leading to, Do you know how to read the mysterious ancient runes in my mother’s book?

“Thanks, Anna,” Elsa said as Gerda hurried away to arrange everything. “If that’s all taken care of, then I need to get going. I’ll make sure I visit you before I go to bed, okay?”

But she turned before Anna could even nod.

And though Anna stood in the middle of a crowded castle still bursting to the brim with villagers, the sight of Elsa walking away from her had never made Anna feel more alone.
chapters.zh:
安娜听见城堡某处传来钟鸣与脚步声。

黎明已破，温煦的秋日阳光洒在她脸上。

安娜闭着眼伸了个懒腰，享受被子的温暖与枕头的柔软。

再眯几分钟。

在去找艾莎、多问韦斯顿家山羊、并把昨晚在母亲书里的发现告诉她之前，她等得起。

毕竟，她太舒服了，破窝而起简直是罪过，而且——她的思绪戛然而止。

《魔法创造者之秘》。

那本有咒语的书。

那本可能治愈动物的书。

安娜猛地弹起，眼睛睁大——却被刺盲的不是晨光，而是正午般的金色阳光。

她又睡过头了！

比斯文啃根胡萝卜还快，安娜还没从被子里挣脱就滚下了床。

她抓起《魔法创造者之秘》，被子在身后拍打着，冲过更衣室奔下楼。

她懒得敲门，一把推开父母旧卧室的门。

床铺得齐整，壁炉里的灰已冷。

当然——这会儿姐姐早起来了好几个钟头。

艾莎，出于某种奇怪的原因，喜欢早晨。

她说早晨让她如新雪般清新，却让安娜如鸡粪般“清新”。

一阵头痛在太阳穴处敲击。

尽管她多睡了几小时，却睡得不安稳，因为童年噩梦回来后，她花了很久才放松。

想想。

这会儿艾莎会在哪儿？

安娜从卧室一转，跑过走廊从敞开的门里窥看。

艾莎不在图书馆，也不在议事厅。

也许在画像廊？

安娜飞下楼，在楼梯平台急转——撞上什么温暖而结实的东西。

安娜向后飞出，瘫倒在地。

一阵钝痛窜过她的屁股，所幸跌落大部被地毯缓冲。

哎哟。“嘿！”那面温暖的“墙”在上方抱怨。“看路！”“你才看路！”安娜回嘴，旋即后悔。

想当巡游皇家使节的人不该这么说。“对不起，”她补了一句，抬头看见埃妮奥拉夫人那张布满皱纹的老脸正俯视她。“安娜！”埃妮奥拉夫人仓促行了个屈膝礼，她棕色长裙与臂中那束白“缎带”形成对比。“抱歉，我没认出你这身……”她的目光上下扫过。“被子？”安娜龇牙。

皇家使节大概也该记得执行重要任务前穿上得体的衣服——还要梳头。

她的头发不像头发，倒像鸟窝。“没关系的。”安娜爬起身。“我本该专心些。”一如往常。

她把被子裹紧，但愿它比自己皱巴巴的浅绿睡衣和光脚看着体面些。

安娜知道埃妮奥拉是从提卡尼迁来阿伦黛尔的新村民之一，确切说，是教过安娜提卡尼国歌的那位。

埃妮奥拉住在农地外围一间舒适的农舍。

安娜抬着下巴问：“您来城堡有何事，埃妮奥拉夫人？”埃妮奥拉叹气，她脸上的皱纹本就比阿格瑞国王的旧航海图上的线还多，此刻一皱眉仿佛又增了十倍。“我来见女王。”她抿起嘴。“我们都是。”安娜挑起眉。“我们？”埃妮奥拉退后，露出大 hall外排成一队、正盯着安娜的更多村民。

她认出许多朋友——制糖人、农夫、点灯人、磨坊主、两位铁匠，还有许多。

许许多多。

安娜睁大眼，只见村民的队伍从通往大 hall的双扇门，一路穿过第二大厅，直到画像廊。

安娜口干舌燥，清了清嗓子。“你们为何要见艾莎？

呃，艾莎女王？”她问。

埃妮奥拉伸出那束“缎带”，安娜这才看清它们根本不是缎带。

它们是麦秆，却不是安娜从塔窗看惯的长长金秆，这些麦秆又短又斑白——从头烂到尾，只有顶端的麦穗还能认出。

安娜正盯着，几粒种子已碎成白尘。

先是动物，然后是庄稼。

怎么回事？“我们今早醒来，”埃妮奥拉说，“全都这样了——一切！”村民在她身后嘟囔着附和。

安娜得把这些村民的事告诉艾莎——马上。“失陪。”安娜把目光从埃妮奥拉夫人臂中那可怜的束上扯开，朝大 hall方向匆匆下楼。“借过，借过！”队伍挪动让安娜挤过，她看见每人都拿着与埃妮奥拉相似的白束：南瓜本是落日色，如今溅满难看的大斑；苹果本红润、圆实、脆生，此刻却像生面团般软塌。

队伍上下，安娜看见干枯的玉米皮、斑白的土豆，和苍白如奶油的胡萝卜。

安娜能想到的每种庄稼、每种蔬菜、每种谷物，都毁了。

腐烂。

枯萎病。

安娜加快脚步。

挤过一个神色慌张的女人，她终于穿门而入大 hall。

大 hall，顾名思义，正是：大。

它是城堡最大的房间，有高窗与闪亮的水晶灯，能同时容纳上百风度翩翩的贵族与旋转的淑女、艾莎的宝座，以及一座巨大的巧克力喷泉。

有一次，当晚冬风暴威胁年度冰舞赛时，它甚至容下过一整座溜冰场。

可此刻，在安娜记忆里头一回，大 hall显得小了。

穿过画像廊的单行队伍，没让她准备好面对挤满大 hall的人潮。

即便在记载中最繁忙的市集日——艾莎加冕后不久，人人都来见新魔法君主时——也没这么多人。

或许有过，但欢乐占的空间远不及恐惧。

恐惧填满大厅，如母亲故事里的大地巨人般庞大而真切。

安娜四周的声音绷得紧紧，仿佛随时会断。“全完了！

都毁了！”“我的牛！

叫不醒！”“我这辈子从没！

仿佛大地都乱了套！”“你觉得这和北地人有关吗？”“不，”有人咕哝。“鲁内尔德国王，愿他安息，早确保他们再不会来烦阿伦黛尔。”“还有动物……”安娜听见外面传来怪声。

那声音像学琴的孩子与动物园声响的混合。

安娜从窗里窥看，倒吸一口气。

庭院和大 hall一样满，挤满了农夫与动物。

羊儿挣脱了牧人，平时那么谨慎的牧羊犬似乎分了神，追着空中别人看不见的东西。

所有动物都像行走的鬼，皮毛是同一种病态的黄白。

安娜正看着，一头牛和两匹马跪倒在地，眼睛如煤块般又大又黑，嘴张着、舌垂着，直到忽然，它们睡着了。

安娜胃里翻腾。“借过，”她一遍遍说，想挤过厅前，奔向艾莎必在的宝座。

嘟囔的人跟在她身后，她在人群中穿进穿出，不止一次得从某人靴下拽回被子。

最后一推，她挤到宝座前，看见艾莎立在那里，如释重负——恰在此时，当地记者韦尔喊道：“那可救不了我们！”“韦尔，”艾莎说，“请你只——”“咳咳！

冬天快到了。”韦尔沾墨的手指疯狂比划。“我们将无食可吃！

我们该有答案——而你作为女王，有责任给我们答案、照顾你的子民！

我们的粮食撑不过一周！”他的话让大 hall一片肃静。

艾莎高高站着，毫不退让，可安娜了解姐姐。

她看得见姐姐眼中那过亮的光泽。

能在水晶灯下闪烁的不只是冰。

泪也可以。

明亮而炽热的怒火扫过安娜。“别那样对我姐姐说话！”她冲到艾莎身边脱口而出。“安娜，”艾莎低声说，“我应付得来，没事——”安娜瞪着韦尔。“不，不是！”那人也回瞪。“艾莎已尽全力，”安娜继续，语速又快又烈。“她有方案！

她会在巡游前把一切修好！”身侧，她听见艾莎倒吸一口气。“安娜——”“就剩三天了，”一个面露倦容的村民说，怀里抱着安娜原以为该是翡翠色西葫芦、此刻却更像大白蛞蝓的东西。“女王真能——”“安娜——”艾莎又试。

可安娜没听。

她要为姐姐撑腰。

艾莎或许能立在那儿听人质疑，可安娜绝不答应。“艾莎当然能！”安娜说，攥着她们发光的秘密、那本神秘书的承诺。“安娜。”艾莎甩出手。

曾几何时，冰矛会从地面冒出，可如今艾莎已能掌控魔力。

如今那不再是危险的尖冰矛，只是个手势——提醒妹妹说话小心。“我替妹妹道歉，”艾莎对大 hall众人说。

她抬下巴的样子，和安娜记得父亲在特殊典礼上、想显出最王者风范时一模一样。

安娜张嘴想抗议，可瞥一眼艾莎的神情，就把剩下的话全压了回去。

她脸颊发烫。

燃烧的怒火化成了燃烧的尴尬。

她都做了什么？“我理解你们的担忧，”艾莎继续，声音平稳而冷静。“我也同此心。

我一直在说的是，为表明我解决庄稼毁坏与动物生病之问题的决心，我将推迟巡游，直到理清这眼前的麻烦。”“什么？”安娜没忍住倒吸一口气，震惊姐姐竟会取消巡游。

她不懂艾莎怎么想——若推迟让各国使节与百姓以为阿伦黛尔并非敞开大门、而是再次关闭，怎么办？

从韦尔震惊的脸与人群的低语，安娜知道自己并非唯一对这宣告吃惊的人。

若不是立在一大群焦虑村民前，安娜想，艾莎这会儿定在揉太阳穴、叹气。

可他们立在一大群焦虑村民前，姐姐从未辜负众望：她是女王，威严而镇定。“因为，”艾莎说，声音大到人尽可闻，“皇家船满载口粮：苹果、小麦、干菜、奶酪、腌鲱鱼罐头与香肠。

我们需分享盈余，否则染上枯萎病的农场村民将更受苦。”艾莎又一次想出完美方案——简单得安娜奇怪自己怎没想到。

艾莎那么擅见大局，安娜却总被眼前晃的线头分神。“那些食物最多撑我们三天，”韦尔抗议。“您凭什么认为船上的食物没坏，陛下？”他那种万事通的态度，让安娜想放出棉花糖——艾莎那危险的巨型雪人、奥拉夫的弟弟——去对付他。

可既然不行——棉花糖如今是北山冰宫的管家——她便满足于瞪韦尔。“我会清查这儿的厨房，”艾莎提议。

她身旁，凯伊在大幅羊皮纸上疾书，而棕发和善、负责监管厨房人员的奥丽娜，则十指交握、陷入深思。

没什么能逃过奥丽娜审慎的眼，安娜知道她大概已在心中列起厨房能供的食材清单。“万一那些食物也坏了呢？”人群中一声喊。

众人盯着艾莎，安娜屏息。

可艾莎只看着一人：奥丽娜。

那女人微微摇头：厨房尚好。

安娜舒气，庆幸至少这消息不糟。“作为你们的女王，”艾莎大声说，声音有力，“我必确保你们有食。”人群低语，可安娜听出语气变了。

她身边的交谈不再如绷太紧的弦般颤栗。

相反，话语松了，交谈放松了，村民思量艾莎的提议。“我觉得是好主意，”图娃喊。“我和妻子接受。”两位铁匠点头同意。“我也接受，”埃妮奥拉喊，不久其他村民也纷纷赞同。

除韦尔外都同意，他只不情愿地点头，却不忘加一句：“行——但村冠奖会确保你们守住安娜的承诺，三天内找出解法。”安娜满心骄傲，看凯伊领着不满的村民出城堡、朝港湾去取皇家船的物资。

她想欢呼，却只轻轻尖叫一声，对艾莎耳语：“太妙了。”可艾莎没回笑。

相反，她走向大 hall一处更隐秘的侧门，被挂毯遮住。“安娜，”她背身说，“我们能谈一分钟吗？”安娜的笑消失，跟着姐姐。

她或许不知农畜为何沉睡、毛为何变白、王国食物为何化尘成灰，可她确知一件事：她绝对、完全、百分之百有麻烦了。“三天？！”挂毯一落放回原位、遮住她们，艾莎就转向安娜。“阿伦黛尔的安娜，我到底怎么能在这么快修好这烂摊子？”尽管艾莎没提高嗓门，安娜却听出她压抑的挫败。“这事加上克斯托夫——”“克斯托夫？”安娜皱眉打断。“克斯托夫怎么了？”艾莎闭眼揉太阳穴，正如安娜早先猜她想做的。“他不在这儿。

我以为他这会儿该回来了，可……”担忧窜过安娜，她却强迫自己耸肩。“我肯定他没事，”她说。“你知道布尔达每次见他多开心。”她笑着想起那位把克斯托夫当自己孩子养大的山地地精。“我打赌他耽搁是因为蘑菇炖菜吃太撑，重得斯文驮不动，只好走回来。”可艾莎似乎无法被这滑稽画面分心。

艾莎摇头。“压力太大了。

我不知道能做什么。”“你是说，我们能做什么……用那本满是魔法的秘密书！”安娜说。

艾莎呻吟。“噢，安娜！”她摇头。“我知道你希望如此，可我不觉得魔法能解答我们所有问题。”“好，我听到了，可你看。”安娜举起《魔法创造者之秘》。“这里面信息多着呢。”她翻到要找的那页。“看？

这一条能成全你的梦。”艾莎叹气。“安娜，我让你别回密室。”“我没回去。

我第一次离开前就拿了这本书。

看这个！”艾莎不情愿地低头瞥了下顶到鼻尖的那页，可还没来得及略读，格尔达就拉开挂毯，穿着她标志性的绿裙、绿外套、绿帽，拿着艾莎那本大日历。“陛下，抱歉，”那女人说，安娜听得出她声里的同情，“可即便巡游推迟，这场病乱子还是让我们落后了日程。

现在您得给各国使节与元首写说明，解释为何去不成。”艾莎深吸一口气。“对，当然，格尔达，你说得对。

女王的工作永无止境。”她瞥了眼屏息的安娜。“给。

把那本书给我。

也许你是对的。

我保证一有空就翻。”“当——当然，”安娜说，乐意分享。

可若艾莎告诉格尔达安娜发现了重要东西，她会更开心。

说他们正一起寻找解法。“我想现在见位动物专家，听听意见，”艾莎说，安娜再次注意到她在拽手指。“还有植物学家。

我不确定该先做什么……”“若需要人写信，我能帮忙，”安娜提议。“我读过各国不同的礼仪。”“那就好，亲爱的，”格尔达说，铅笔已在日历上飞快调整。“只要确保艾莎签名后再寄。”“我会的！”安娜承诺，既高兴能帮艾莎，也高兴有事可做、等着克斯托夫回城堡。

她有太多想问他，先是“地精说我们怎么治枯萎病？”再到“你认得我母亲书里那些神秘古如尼文吗？”“谢了，安娜，”格尔达匆匆去安排时艾莎说。“若都安排好了，我得走了。

我睡前一定来看你，好吗？”可她转身时安娜还没来得及点头。

尽管安娜站在挤满村民、仍满到溢出的城堡中央，看着艾莎离自己而去，她从未感到如此孤独。

sentences.en: ANNA HEARD THE SOUND of chimes and footsteps from somewhere in the castle.
sentences.zh: 安娜听见城堡某处传来钟鸣与脚步声。

sentences.en: Dawn had broken, spilling warm autumn sunlight across her face.
sentences.zh: 黎明已破，温煦的秋日阳光洒在她脸上。

sentences.en: Keeping her eyes closed, Anna stretched, enjoying the coziness of her quilt and the softness of her pillow.
sentences.zh: 安娜闭着眼伸了个懒腰，享受被子的温暖与枕头的柔软。

sentences.en: Just a few more minutes.
sentences.zh: 再眯几分钟。

sentences.en: She could afford to wait before she found Elsa, asked more about the Westens’ goats, and told her about what she’d found last night in their mother’s book.
sentences.zh: 在去找艾莎、多问韦斯顿家山羊、并把昨晚在母亲书里的发现告诉她之前，她等得起。

sentences.en: After all, she was so comfortable that it would be a crime to untuck herself, and— Her thoughts screeched to a halt.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，她太舒服了，破窝而起简直是罪过，而且——她的思绪戛然而止。

sentences.en: Secrets of the Magic Makers .
sentences.zh: 《魔法创造者之秘》。

sentences.en: The book with spells in it.
sentences.zh: 那本有咒语的书。

sentences.en: The book with a potential cure for the animals.
sentences.zh: 那本可能治愈动物的书。

sentences.en: Anna lurched up, eyes flying open—only to be blinded not by the light of dawn, but by golden mid-morning sun.
sentences.zh: 安娜猛地弹起，眼睛睁大——却被刺盲的不是晨光，而是正午般的金色阳光。

sentences.en: She’d overslept again!
sentences.zh: 她又睡过头了！

sentences.en: Faster than Sven could chomp a carrot, Anna tumbled out of bed before she could even untwist herself from her quilt.
sentences.zh: 比斯文啃根胡萝卜还快，安娜还没从被子里挣脱就滚下了床。

sentences.en: She grabbed Secrets of the Magic Makers , and with her blanket flapping behind her, she sprinted through the dressing room and downstairs.
sentences.zh: 她抓起《魔法创造者之秘》，被子在身后拍打着，冲过更衣室奔下楼。

sentences.en: Not bothering to knock, she flung open the door to her parents’ old bedroom.
sentences.zh: 她懒得敲门，一把推开父母旧卧室的门。

sentences.en: The bed was neatly made, the ashes cold in their hearth.
sentences.zh: 床铺得齐整，壁炉里的灰已冷。

sentences.en: Of course—her sister would have been up for hours at this point.
sentences.zh: 当然——这会儿姐姐早起来了好几个钟头。

sentences.en: Elsa, for some strange reason, enjoyed mornings.
sentences.zh: 艾莎，出于某种奇怪的原因，喜欢早晨。

sentences.en: She said they made her feel fresh as new snow, while they made Anna feel as fresh as chicken droppings.
sentences.zh: 她说早晨让她如新雪般清新，却让安娜如鸡粪般“清新”。

sentences.en: A headache pounded at her temples.
sentences.zh: 一阵头痛在太阳穴处敲击。

sentences.en: Even though she’d overslept by hours, it had been a restless sleep, as it had taken her long hours to relax after the return of the childhood nightmare.
sentences.zh: 尽管她多睡了几小时，却睡得不安稳，因为童年噩梦回来后，她花了很久才放松。

sentences.en: Think.
sentences.zh: 想想。

sentences.en: Where would Elsa be at this time of day?
sentences.zh: 这会儿艾莎会在哪儿？

sentences.en: Whirling from the bedchamber, Anna ran down the hallway to peer through open doors.
sentences.zh: 安娜从卧室一转，跑过走廊从敞开的门里窥看。

sentences.en: Elsa wasn’t in the library or council chambers.
sentences.zh: 艾莎不在图书馆，也不在议事厅。

sentences.en: Maybe the portrait gallery?
sentences.zh: 也许在画像廊？

sentences.en: Anna flew downstairs and made a sharp turn on the landing—and barreled into something warm and solid.
sentences.zh: 安娜飞下楼，在楼梯平台急转——撞上什么温暖而结实的东西。

sentences.en: Anna flew backward, sprawling onto the ground.
sentences.zh: 安娜向后飞出，瘫倒在地。

sentences.en: A dull pain rattled through her backside, but thankfully, the majority of her fall had been cushioned by the carpet.
sentences.zh: 一阵钝痛窜过她的屁股，所幸跌落大部被地毯缓冲。

sentences.en: Ow. “Hey!” the warm wall grumbled from above. “Watch where you’re going!” “You watch where you’re going!” Anna replied, and instantly regretted it.
sentences.zh: 哎哟。“嘿！”那面温暖的“墙”在上方抱怨。“看路！”“你才看路！”安娜回嘴，旋即后悔。

sentences.en: That’s not what someone hoping to be a royal ambassador on a grand tour should say. “I’m sorry,” she added, looking up to see the old, wrinkled face of Madam Eniola staring down at her. “Anna!” Madam Eniola bobbed a curtsy, her long brown skirt contrasting with the bundle of white ribbons she held in her arms. “My apologies, I didn’t recognize you in your…” Her eyes swept up and down. “Quilt?” Anna winced.
sentences.zh: 想当巡游皇家使节的人不该这么说。“对不起，”她补了一句，抬头看见埃妮奥拉夫人那张布满皱纹的老脸正俯视她。“安娜！”埃妮奥拉夫人仓促行了个屈膝礼，她棕色长裙与臂中那束白“缎带”形成对比。“抱歉，我没认出你这身……”她的目光上下扫过。“被子？”安娜龇牙。

sentences.en: Royal ambassadors should also probably remember to put on proper clothes before carrying out their important missions—and to comb their hair, too.
sentences.zh: 皇家使节大概也该记得执行重要任务前穿上得体的衣服——还要梳头。

sentences.en: Her hair didn’t look so much like hair as it resembled a bird’s nest. “That’s all right.” Anna clambered to her feet. “I should have been paying attention.” Like always.
sentences.zh: 她的头发不像头发，倒像鸟窝。“没关系的。”安娜爬起身。“我本该专心些。”一如往常。

sentences.en: She pulled her quilt tighter around her and hoped it looked more dignified than her ruffled pale green nightgown and bare feet.
sentences.zh: 她把被子裹紧，但愿它比自己皱巴巴的浅绿睡衣和光脚看着体面些。

sentences.en: Anna knew Eniola as one of the new villagers who’d moved to Arendelle from Tikaani, and specifically as the one who had taught Tikaani’s national anthem to Anna.
sentences.zh: 安娜知道埃妮奥拉是从提卡尼迁来阿伦黛尔的新村民之一，确切说，是教过安娜提卡尼国歌的那位。

sentences.en: Eniola lived in a cozy cottage on the outskirts of the farmlands.
sentences.zh: 埃妮奥拉住在农地外围一间舒适的农舍。

sentences.en: Holding her chin up, Anna asked, “What brings you to the castle, Madam Eniola?” Eniola sighed, and the creases on her face, which already held more lines than King Agnarr’s old sailing charts, seemed to increase tenfold as she frowned. “I’m here to speak to the queen.” She pursed her lips. “We all are.” Anna arched an eyebrow. “We?” Eniola stepped back to reveal more villagers lined up outside the Great Hall, staring at Anna.
sentences.zh: 安娜抬着下巴问：“您来城堡有何事，埃妮奥拉夫人？”埃妮奥拉叹气，她脸上的皱纹本就比阿格瑞国王的旧航海图上的线还多，此刻一皱眉仿佛又增了十倍。“我来见女王。”她抿起嘴。“我们都是。”安娜挑起眉。“我们？”埃妮奥拉退后，露出大 hall外排成一队、正盯着安娜的更多村民。

sentences.en: She recognized many of her friends—the candymaker, the farmer, the gas lamp lighter, the miller, the two blacksmiths, and many more.
sentences.zh: 她认出许多朋友——制糖人、农夫、点灯人、磨坊主、两位铁匠，还有许多。

sentences.en: Many, many more.
sentences.zh: 许许多多。

sentences.en: Anna’s eyes widened as she saw that the line of villagers extended from the double doors that led into the Great Hall all the way through the second great hall and into the portrait gallery.
sentences.zh: 安娜睁大眼，只见村民的队伍从通往大 hall的双扇门，一路穿过第二大厅，直到画像廊。

sentences.en: Anna’s mouth went dry, and she cleared her throat. “Why do you need to see Elsa?
sentences.zh: 安娜口干舌燥，清了清嗓子。“你们为何要见艾莎？

sentences.en: Erm, Queen Elsa?” she asked.
sentences.zh: 呃，艾莎女王？”她问。

sentences.en: Eniola held out her bundle of ribbons, which Anna saw now were not actually ribbons at all.
sentences.zh: 埃妮奥拉伸出那束“缎带”，安娜这才看清它们根本不是缎带。

sentences.en: They were strands of wheat, but instead of the long golden straws Anna was used to seeing from the tower window, these strands were short and mottled white—moldy and rotten all the way through and recognizable only by the heads of grains at the tops.
sentences.zh: 它们是麦秆，却不是安娜从塔窗看惯的长长金秆，这些麦秆又短又斑白——从头烂到尾，只有顶端的麦穗还能认出。

sentences.en: Even as Anna stared, a few seeds crumbled off into white dust.
sentences.zh: 安娜正盯着，几粒种子已碎成白尘。

sentences.en: First the animals, then the crops.
sentences.zh: 先是动物，然后是庄稼。

sentences.en: What was going on? “We woke this morning,” Eniola said, “and it’s all like this—everything!” The villagers grumbled in agreement behind her.
sentences.zh: 怎么回事？“我们今早醒来，”埃妮奥拉说，“全都这样了——一切！”村民在她身后嘟囔着附和。

sentences.en: Anna needed to tell Elsa about all these villagers— now . “Excuse me.” Anna tore her eyes away from the pitiful bundle in Madam Eniola’s arms and hurried downstairs in the direction of the Great Hall. “Pardon me, coming through!” The line shifted to allow Anna to wiggle by, and as she did, she saw that each and every person held white bundles similar to the one that Madam Eniola held: the pumpkins, usually the color of the sunset, had large unsightly splotches splashed across them, while the apples, usually red, round, and crisp, seemed to have the same consistency as raw dough.
sentences.zh: 安娜得把这些村民的事告诉艾莎——马上。“失陪。”安娜把目光从埃妮奥拉夫人臂中那可怜的束上扯开，朝大 hall方向匆匆下楼。“借过，借过！”队伍挪动让安娜挤过，她看见每人都拿着与埃妮奥拉相似的白束：南瓜本是落日色，如今溅满难看的大斑；苹果本红润、圆实、脆生，此刻却像生面团般软塌。

sentences.en: Up and down the line, Anna saw dried corn husks, white-mottled potatoes, and carrots as pale as cream.
sentences.zh: 队伍上下，安娜看见干枯的玉米皮、斑白的土豆，和苍白如奶油的胡萝卜。

sentences.en: Every crop, every vegetable, every grain Anna could think of, was destroyed.
sentences.zh: 安娜能想到的每种庄稼、每种蔬菜、每种谷物，都毁了。

sentences.en: Rotten.
sentences.zh: 腐烂。

sentences.en: The Blight.
sentences.zh: 枯萎病。

sentences.en: Anna picked up the pace.
sentences.zh: 安娜加快脚步。

sentences.en: Squeezing past a harried-looking woman, she at last made it through the doors and into the Great Hall.
sentences.zh: 挤过一个神色慌张的女人，她终于穿门而入大 hall。

sentences.en: The Great Hall, as its name suggested, was exactly that: great .
sentences.zh: 大 hall，顾名思义，正是：大。

sentences.en: It was the largest room in the castle, with tall windows and a gleaming chandelier, capable of fitting a hundred dashing lords and twirling ladies, Elsa’s throne, and a massive chocolate fountain all at the same time.
sentences.zh: 它是城堡最大的房间，有高窗与闪亮的水晶灯，能同时容纳上百风度翩翩的贵族与旋转的淑女、艾莎的宝座，以及一座巨大的巧克力喷泉。

sentences.en: Once, it had even hosted an entire ice skating rink when a late winter storm had threatened the annual ice dance competition.
sentences.zh: 有一次，当晚冬风暴威胁年度冰舞赛时，它甚至容下过一整座溜冰场。

sentences.en: But now, for the first time Anna could remember, the Great Hall felt small.
sentences.zh: 可此刻，在安娜记忆里头一回，大 hall显得小了。

sentences.en: The single file line cutting through the portrait gallery hadn’t prepared her for the absolute crush of people that filled the Great Hall.
sentences.zh: 穿过画像廊的单行队伍，没让她准备好面对挤满大 hall的人潮。

sentences.en: Even on the busiest market day on record—shortly after Elsa’s coronation, when everyone had come to see their new magical sovereign—there had not been this many people.
sentences.zh: 即便在记载中最繁忙的市集日——艾莎加冕后不久，人人都来见新魔法君主时——也没这么多人。

sentences.en: Or maybe there had been, but joy didn’t take up nearly as much room as fear.
sentences.zh: 或许有过，但欢乐占的空间远不及恐惧。

sentences.en: Fear filled the hall, as large and present as one of the Earth Giants in her mother’s tales.
sentences.zh: 恐惧填满大厅，如母亲故事里的大地巨人般庞大而真切。

sentences.en: The voices all around Anna were pulled tight, sounding as if they would break at any moment. “Everything is gone!
sentences.zh: 安娜四周的声音绷得紧紧，仿佛随时会断。“全完了！

sentences.en: It’s been ruined!” “My cattle!
sentences.zh: 都毁了！”“我的牛！

sentences.en: They won’t wake up!” “Never in all my days!
sentences.zh: 叫不醒！”“我这辈子从没！

sentences.en: It’s as if the very earth has gone awry!” “Do you think this has to do with the Northuldra?” “No,” someone grunted. “King Runeard, may he rest in greatest peace, made sure they would never trouble Arendelle again.” “And the animals…” Anna heard a strange noise from outside.
sentences.zh: 仿佛大地都乱了套！”“你觉得这和北地人有关吗？”“不，”有人咕哝。“鲁内尔德国王，愿他安息，早确保他们再不会来烦阿伦黛尔。”“还有动物……”安娜听见外面传来怪声。

sentences.en: It sounded like a mix of children learning how to play the violin crossed with the sounds of a zoo.
sentences.zh: 那声音像学琴的孩子与动物园声响的混合。

sentences.en: Peering through the window, Anna gasped.
sentences.zh: 安娜从窗里窥看，倒吸一口气。

sentences.en: The courtyard was just as full as the Great Hall, filled to the brim with farmers and animals.
sentences.zh: 庭院和大 hall一样满，挤满了农夫与动物。

sentences.en: Sheep had broken loose from their shepherds, and the herding dogs, usually so careful, seemed distracted, following something in the air that no one else could see.
sentences.zh: 羊儿挣脱了牧人，平时那么谨慎的牧羊犬似乎分了神，追着空中别人看不见的东西。

sentences.en: All the animals looked like walking ghosts, their fur and hides the same sickly yellow-white.
sentences.zh: 所有动物都像行走的鬼，皮毛是同一种病态的黄白。

sentences.en: And even as Anna watched, a cow and two horses knelt to the ground, their eyes as large and black as lumps of coal, their mouths open and tongues lolling out until, suddenly, they fell asleep.
sentences.zh: 安娜正看着，一头牛和两匹马跪倒在地，眼睛如煤块般又大又黑，嘴张着、舌垂着，直到忽然，它们睡着了。

sentences.en: Anna’s stomach turned. “Excuse me,” she said over and over again as she tried to wade her way to the front of the hall, toward the throne where Elsa must be.
sentences.zh: 安娜胃里翻腾。“借过，”她一遍遍说，想挤过厅前，奔向艾莎必在的宝座。

sentences.en: Grumbling people followed in her wake as she wove in and out of the crowd, and more than once, she had to tug her quilt from beneath someone’s boot.
sentences.zh: 嘟囔的人跟在她身后，她在人群中穿进穿出，不止一次得从某人靴下拽回被子。

sentences.en: But with one last push, she made it to the throne, relief washing over her as she found Elsa standing there, just as Wael, the local journalist, yelled out, “That’s not going to help us!” “Wael,” Elsa said, “if you would please only just—” “ Ah-hem!
sentences.zh: 最后一推，她挤到宝座前，看见艾莎立在那里，如释重负——恰在此时，当地记者韦尔喊道：“那可救不了我们！”“韦尔，”艾莎说，“请你只——”“咳咳！

sentences.en: Winter is fast approaching.” Wael’s ink-stained fingers gestured wildly. “We will have nothing to eat!
sentences.zh: 冬天快到了。”韦尔沾墨的手指疯狂比划。“我们将无食可吃！

sentences.en: We deserve answers—and it’s your responsibility as queen to give us answers and take care of your people!
sentences.zh: 我们该有答案——而你作为女王，有责任给我们答案、照顾你的子民！

sentences.en: We don’t have enough food to last the week!” A hush fell over the Great Hall at his words.
sentences.zh: 我们的粮食撑不过一周！”他的话让大 hall一片肃静。

sentences.en: Elsa stood tall, not backing down, but Anna knew her sister.
sentences.zh: 艾莎高高站着，毫不退让，可安娜了解姐姐。

sentences.en: She could see the overbright sheen of her eyes.
sentences.zh: 她看得见姐姐眼中那过亮的光泽。

sentences.en: It wasn’t just ice that could sparkle in chandelier light.
sentences.zh: 能在水晶灯下闪烁的不只是冰。

sentences.en: Tears could, too.
sentences.zh: 泪也可以。

sentences.en: Anger, bright and hot, swept through Anna. “Don’t speak to my sister that way!” she burst out as she reached Elsa’s side. “Anna,” Elsa said, her voice low, “I’ve got this, it’s fine—” Anna glared at Wael. “No, it’s not!” The man glared right back. “Elsa is doing her best,” Anna plowed on, her words coming fast and furious. “She has a plan!
sentences.zh: 明亮而炽热的怒火扫过安娜。“别那样对我姐姐说话！”她冲到艾莎身边脱口而出。“安娜，”艾莎低声说，“我应付得来，没事——”安娜瞪着韦尔。“不，不是！”那人也回瞪。“艾莎已尽全力，”安娜继续，语速又快又烈。“她有方案！

sentences.en: She’ll fix everything before she leaves on the grand tour!” Next to her, she heard Elsa’s breath catch. “Anna—” “That’s in just three days,” a tired-looking villager said, her arms full of what Anna thought was supposed to be emerald zucchini but now looked more like great white slugs. “Can the queen really—” “Anna—” Elsa tried again.
sentences.zh: 她会在巡游前把一切修好！”身侧，她听见艾莎倒吸一口气。“安娜——”“就剩三天了，”一个面露倦容的村民说，怀里抱着安娜原以为该是翡翠色西葫芦、此刻却更像大白蛞蝓的东西。“女王真能——”“安娜——”艾莎又试。

sentences.en: But Anna didn’t listen.
sentences.zh: 可安娜没听。

sentences.en: She was going to stick up for her sister.
sentences.zh: 她要为姐姐撑腰。

sentences.en: Elsa might be able to stand there and listen to people doubt her, but Anna wasn’t going to have any of it. “Of course Elsa can!” Anna said, holding on to their glowing secret, the promise of the mysterious book. “ANNA.” Elsa flung out her hand.
sentences.zh: 艾莎或许能立在那儿听人质疑，可安娜绝不答应。“艾莎当然能！”安娜说，攥着她们发光的秘密、那本神秘书的承诺。“安娜。”艾莎甩出手。

sentences.en: There was a time when icy spears would have sprouted from the floor, but Elsa had control of her magical powers now.
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，冰矛会从地面冒出，可如今艾莎已能掌控魔力。

sentences.en: Instead of a dangerously pointed ice spear, it was now just a gesture—to remind her sister to watch what she said. “I apologize for my sister,” Elsa said to the Great Hall at large.
sentences.zh: 如今那不再是危险的尖冰矛，只是个手势——提醒妹妹说话小心。“我替妹妹道歉，”艾莎对大 hall众人说。

sentences.en: Her chin had lifted in the exact same way Anna remembered her father lifting his during special ceremonies, when he was trying to be his most regal.
sentences.zh: 她抬下巴的样子，和安娜记得父亲在特殊典礼上、想显出最王者风范时一模一样。

sentences.en: Anna opened her mouth to protest, but one glance at Elsa’s expression squashed any words she had left.
sentences.zh: 安娜张嘴想抗议，可瞥一眼艾莎的神情，就把剩下的话全压了回去。

sentences.en: Her cheeks flushed.
sentences.zh: 她脸颊发烫。

sentences.en: Burning anger transformed into burning embarrassment.
sentences.zh: 燃烧的怒火化成了燃烧的尴尬。

sentences.en: What had she done? “I understand your concern,” Elsa continued, her voice steady and cool. “And I share it.
sentences.zh: 她都做了什么？“我理解你们的担忧，”艾莎继续，声音平稳而冷静。“我也同此心。

sentences.en: What I’ve been trying to say is, to show my commitment to solving the problem of the ruined crops and sick animals, I’m postponing my grand tour until I can sort out this troubling matter at hand.” “What?” Anna gasped before she could stop herself, shocked her sister would cancel her grand tour.
sentences.zh: 我一直在说的是，为表明我解决庄稼毁坏与动物生病之问题的决心，我将推迟巡游，直到理清这眼前的麻烦。”“什么？”安娜没忍住倒吸一口气，震惊姐姐竟会取消巡游。

sentences.en: She didn’t understand what Elsa was thinking—what if postponement convinced the dignitaries and people from other lands that Arendelle wasn’t, in fact, opening its gates, but closing them once again?
sentences.zh: 她不懂艾莎怎么想——若推迟让各国使节与百姓以为阿伦黛尔并非敞开大门、而是再次关闭，怎么办？

sentences.en: And from the shocked look on Wael’s face and the murmur of the crowd, Anna knew she wasn’t the only one surprised by this announcement.
sentences.zh: 从韦尔震惊的脸与人群的低语，安娜知道自己并非唯一对这宣告吃惊的人。

sentences.en: If they hadn’t been standing in front of a large crowd of stressed villagers, Anna imagined Elsa would be rubbing her temples and sighing right about now.
sentences.zh: 若不是立在一大群焦虑村民前，安娜想，艾莎这会儿定在揉太阳穴、叹气。

sentences.en: But they were standing in front of stressed villagers, and her sister never failed to live up to what was expected of her: she was queen, regal and unflappable. “Because,” Elsa said, speaking loud enough for all to hear, “the royal ship is loaded with rations of food, apples, wheat, dried vegetables, cheeses, cans of pickled herring, and sausages.
sentences.zh: 可他们立在一大群焦虑村民前，姐姐从未辜负众望：她是女王，威严而镇定。“因为，”艾莎说，声音大到人尽可闻，“皇家船满载口粮：苹果、小麦、干菜、奶酪、腌鲱鱼罐头与香肠。

sentences.en: We need to share our surplus, or else the villagers with Blight-stricken farms will suffer further.” Once again, Elsa had come up with the perfect solution—one so obvious Anna wondered why she hadn’t thought of it herself.
sentences.zh: 我们需分享盈余，否则染上枯萎病的农场村民将更受苦。”艾莎又一次想出完美方案——简单得安娜奇怪自己怎没想到。

sentences.en: Elsa was so good at seeing the larger tapestry, while Anna let herself get distracted by whatever thread was dangling in front of her at that very moment. “That amount of food will only last us all three days at the most ,” Wael protested. “And what makes you think the food on your ship hasn’t soured, Your Majesty ?” There was something about his all-knowing attitude that made Anna want to release Marshmallow, Elsa’s dangerous giant snowman—and Olaf’s little brother—on him.
sentences.zh: 艾莎那么擅见大局，安娜却总被眼前晃的线头分神。“那些食物最多撑我们三天，”韦尔抗议。“您凭什么认为船上的食物没坏，陛下？”他那种万事通的态度，让安娜想放出棉花糖——艾莎那危险的巨型雪人、奥拉夫的弟弟——去对付他。

sentences.en: But seeing as that wasn’t an option, since Marshmallow was currently the housekeeper for the ice palace on top of the North Mountain, she’d settle for glaring at Wael instead. “I’ll scour our kitchen here,” Elsa offered.
sentences.zh: 可既然不行——棉花糖如今是北山冰宫的管家——她便满足于瞪韦尔。“我会清查这儿的厨房，”艾莎提议。

sentences.en: Beside her, Kai scribbled a note onto a ream of parchment, while brown-haired and kind Olina, in charge of overseeing the kitchen staff, clasped her gloved hands together in deep thought.
sentences.zh: 她身旁，凯伊在大幅羊皮纸上疾书，而棕发和善、负责监管厨房人员的奥丽娜，则十指交握、陷入深思。

sentences.en: Nothing ever missed Olina’s careful eye, and Anna knew that she was probably already running through a mental list of food the castle kitchen could provide. “What if that food’s gone bad, too?” cried a voice from the crowd.
sentences.zh: 没什么能逃过奥丽娜审慎的眼，安娜知道她大概已在心中列起厨房能供的食材清单。“万一那些食物也坏了呢？”人群中一声喊。

sentences.en: Anna held her breath while everyone stared at Elsa.
sentences.zh: 众人盯着艾莎，安娜屏息。

sentences.en: Elsa, however, looked at only one person: Olina.
sentences.zh: 可艾莎只看着一人：奥丽娜。

sentences.en: The woman gave a slight shake of her head: the kitchen was still fine.
sentences.zh: 那女人微微摇头：厨房尚好。

sentences.en: Anna exhaled, thankful that at least this one piece of news wasn’t terrible. “As your queen,” Elsa said loudly, her voice strong, “I will see to it that you have food.” The crowd murmured, but Anna could hear the shift in tone.
sentences.zh: 安娜舒气，庆幸至少这消息不糟。“作为你们的女王，”艾莎大声说，声音有力，“我必确保你们有食。”人群低语，可安娜听出语气变了。

sentences.en: The conversation around her no longer vibrated with the intensity of a string pulled too tight.
sentences.zh: 她身边的交谈不再如绷太紧的弦般颤栗。

sentences.en: Instead, the words loosened and the conversation relaxed as the villagers considered Elsa’s proposal. “I think it’s a good idea,” Tuva called out. “My wife and I accept.” And the two blacksmiths nodded in agreement. “I accept, too,” Eniola called out, and soon other villagers voiced their agreement as well.
sentences.zh: 相反，话语松了，交谈放松了，村民思量艾莎的提议。“我觉得是好主意，”图娃喊。“我和妻子接受。”两位铁匠点头同意。“我也接受，”埃妮奥拉喊，不久其他村民也纷纷赞同。

sentences.en: All except for Wael, who only reluctantly nodded, but not before adding, “Fine—but the Village Crown will make sure that you keep Anna’s promise that the solution will be found before three days are up.” Pride filled Anna as Kai led the disgruntled villagers back out of the castle and toward the harbor to collect the supplies from the royal ship.
sentences.zh: 除韦尔外都同意，他只不情愿地点头，却不忘加一句：“行——但村冠奖会确保你们守住安娜的承诺，三天内找出解法。”安娜满心骄傲，看凯伊领着不满的村民出城堡、朝港湾去取皇家船的物资。

sentences.en: She felt like cheering, but instead she settled on a quiet squeal, and whispered to Elsa, “That was brilliant .” But Elsa didn’t smile back.
sentences.zh: 她想欢呼，却只轻轻尖叫一声，对艾莎耳语：“太妙了。”可艾莎没回笑。

sentences.en: Instead, she walked to one of the more secretive side entrances to the Great Hall, hidden from view by a tapestry. “Anna,” she said without turning around, “can we talk for a minute, please?” Anna’s smile slipped away as she followed her older sister.
sentences.zh: 相反，她走向大 hall一处更隐秘的侧门，被挂毯遮住。“安娜，”她背身说，“我们能谈一分钟吗？”安娜的笑消失，跟着姐姐。

sentences.en: She might not know why the farm animals were sleeping or why their fur was turning white, or why the kingdom’s food seemed to be turning to dust and ash, but she did know one thing: she was absolutely, completely, 100 percent in trouble. “Three days?!” Elsa whirled on Anna as soon as the tapestry fell back in place, obscuring them from view. “Anna of Arendelle, how on earth can I fix this mess, and so soon?” Even though Elsa didn’t raise her voice, Anna could hear her frustration boiling underneath. “Between this and Kristoff—” “Kristoff?” Anna interrupted, furrowing her eyebrows. “What about Kristoff?” Elsa closed her eyes and rubbed her temples, just as Anna had suspected Elsa had wanted to do earlier. “He’s not here.
sentences.zh: 她或许不知农畜为何沉睡、毛为何变白、王国食物为何化尘成灰，可她确知一件事：她绝对、完全、百分之百有麻烦了。“三天？！”挂毯一落放回原位、遮住她们，艾莎就转向安娜。“阿伦黛尔的安娜，我到底怎么能在这么快修好这烂摊子？”尽管艾莎没提高嗓门，安娜却听出她压抑的挫败。“这事加上克斯托夫——”“克斯托夫？”安娜皱眉打断。“克斯托夫怎么了？”艾莎闭眼揉太阳穴，正如安娜早先猜她想做的。“他不在这儿。

sentences.en: I thought he’d be back by now, but…” Worry zipped through Anna, but she forced herself to shrug. “I’m sure he’s fine,” she said. “You know how happy Bulda is whenever he visits.” She smiled, thinking of the mountain troll who’d raised Kristoff as her own. “I bet you he’s delayed because he’s so full of mushroom stew that he’s too heavy for Sven to carry, and they have to walk.” But it seemed Elsa couldn’t be distracted from her worry, not even with the funny image.
sentences.zh: 我以为他这会儿该回来了，可……”担忧窜过安娜，她却强迫自己耸肩。“我肯定他没事，”她说。“你知道布尔达每次见他多开心。”她笑着想起那位把克斯托夫当自己孩子养大的山地地精。“我打赌他耽搁是因为蘑菇炖菜吃太撑，重得斯文驮不动，只好走回来。”可艾莎似乎无法被这滑稽画面分心。

sentences.en: Elsa shook her head. “It’s so much pressure.
sentences.zh: 艾莎摇头。“压力太大了。

sentences.en: I don’t know what I can do.” “You mean, what we can do…with a secret book full of magic!” Anna said.
sentences.zh: 我不知道能做什么。”“你是说，我们能做什么……用那本满是魔法的秘密书！”安娜说。

sentences.en: Elsa groaned. “ Oh , Anna!” She shook her head. “I know you want it to be, but I don’t think magic is the answer to all of our problems.” “Okay, I hear you, but look .” Anna held out Secrets of the Magic Makers . “There is so much information in here.” She flipped through the pages until she found the one she was looking for. “See?
sentences.zh: 艾莎呻吟。“噢，安娜！”她摇头。“我知道你希望如此，可我不觉得魔法能解答我们所有问题。”“好，我听到了，可你看。”安娜举起《魔法创造者之秘》。“这里面信息多着呢。”她翻到要找的那页。“看？

sentences.en: This one grants your dreams .” Elsa sighed. “Anna, I told you not to go back in the secret room.” “I didn’t go back into it.
sentences.zh: 这一条能成全你的梦。”艾莎叹气。“安娜，我让你别回密室。”“我没回去。

sentences.en: I grabbed this book before I left the first time.
sentences.zh: 我第一次离开前就拿了这本书。

sentences.en: Look at it!” Reluctantly, Elsa glanced down at the page that had been pushed under her nose, but before she had a chance to skim, Gerda pulled back the tapestry, wearing her signature green skirt, jacket, and cap, and holding Elsa’s great big calendar. “Your Majesty, I’m sorry,” the woman said, and Anna could hear the sympathy in her voice, “but even with the grand tour postponed, this fiasco with the sickness has put us behind schedule.
sentences.zh: 看这个！”艾莎不情愿地低头瞥了下顶到鼻尖的那页，可还没来得及略读，格尔达就拉开挂毯，穿着她标志性的绿裙、绿外套、绿帽，拿着艾莎那本大日历。“陛下，抱歉，”那女人说，安娜听得出她声里的同情，“可即便巡游推迟，这场病乱子还是让我们落后了日程。

sentences.en: And now you must write explanations to all the different dignitaries and heads of countries to explain why you can’t make it.” Elsa took a deep breath. “Yes, of course, Gerda, you’re right.
sentences.zh: 现在您得给各国使节与元首写说明，解释为何去不成。”艾莎深吸一口气。“对，当然，格尔达，你说得对。

sentences.en: The work of a queen is never complete.” She glanced over at Anna, who held her breath. “Here.
sentences.zh: 女王的工作永无止境。”她瞥了眼屏息的安娜。“给。

sentences.en: Let me have that book.
sentences.zh: 把那本书给我。

sentences.en: Maybe you’re right.
sentences.zh: 也许你是对的。

sentences.en: I promise I’ll look at it as soon as I have a spare minute.” “Of—of course,” Anna said, happy to share.
sentences.zh: 我保证一有空就翻。”“当——当然，”安娜说，乐意分享。

sentences.en: But she would have been even happier if Elsa had told Gerda that Anna had found something important.
sentences.zh: 可若艾莎告诉格尔达安娜发现了重要东西，她会更开心。

sentences.en: That they were working on discovering a solution together . “I’d like to meet with an animal expert now to get their opinion,” Elsa said, and Anna noticed again that she was tugging on her fingers. “And a botanist.
sentences.zh: 说他们正一起寻找解法。“我想现在见位动物专家，听听意见，”艾莎说，安娜再次注意到她在拽手指。“还有植物学家。

sentences.en: I’m not sure what should be done first….” “If you need someone to write letters, I can help with that,” Anna offered. “I’ve read up on all the different etiquettes of each country.” “That should be just fine, dear,” Gerda said, her pencil already flying over the calendar to adjust it. “Just make sure Elsa signs them before you mail them.” “I will!” Anna promised, happy to help Elsa and happy to have something to do while she waited for Kristoff to return to the castle.
sentences.zh: 我不确定该先做什么……”“若需要人写信，我能帮忙，”安娜提议。“我读过各国不同的礼仪。”“那就好，亲爱的，”格尔达说，铅笔已在日历上飞快调整。“只要确保艾莎签名后再寄。”“我会的！”安娜承诺，既高兴能帮艾莎，也高兴有事可做、等着克斯托夫回城堡。

sentences.en: She had so many things she wanted to ask him, starting with, How do the trolls say we can cure the Blight? and leading to, Do you know how to read the mysterious ancient runes in my mother’s book? “Thanks, Anna,” Elsa said as Gerda hurried away to arrange everything. “If that’s all taken care of, then I need to get going.
sentences.zh: 她有太多想问他，先是“地精说我们怎么治枯萎病？”再到“你认得我母亲书里那些神秘古如尼文吗？”“谢了，安娜，”格尔达匆匆去安排时艾莎说。“若都安排好了，我得走了。

sentences.en: I’ll make sure I visit you before I go to bed, okay?” But she turned before Anna could even nod.
sentences.zh: 我睡前一定来看你，好吗？”可她转身时安娜还没来得及点头。

sentences.en: And though Anna stood in the middle of a crowded castle still bursting to the brim with villagers, the sight of Elsa walking away from her had never made Anna feel more alone.
sentences.zh: 尽管安娜站在挤满村民、仍满到溢出的城堡中央，看着艾莎离自己而去，她从未感到如此孤独。

chapters.title: 第7章
chapters.en:
THROUGH HER BEDROOM WINDOW, Anna watched the exodus of the castle staff trailing over the Bridge of Arches and into the darkening village.

That afternoon, Elsa had given the staff the option of taking off from work with pay so that they could go help their nearby relatives whose animals and crops were suffering from the Blight. After she had written the letters, Anna had changed into her travel cloak and spent the rest of the day helping unload food from the royal ship and handing it out to the villagers amidst the groaning of sick animals.

She’d wanted to cover her ears, but then she thought that would be the cowardly thing to do. She couldn’t just ignore the ugly things in the world around her. If people did that, no one would ever help at all, and nothing would become well again. And so Anna had gone to help the farmers dab white fur with wet washcloths to try to keep their livestock alert. She’d stroked a sad little foal’s fuzzy ears as it curled up next to the sleeping form of its mother, who did not so much as stir at the foal’s pitiful nickers.

Anna turned away from the window and paced, still in her travel cloak from earlier. Just as she’d thought, Elsa hadn’t come to see her. She knew her sister was busy, but…Anna glanced out the window again, and made up her mind. Lighting an oil lamp, she quickly made her way through the now empty halls of the castle to Elsa’s council chambers.

As Anna approached the doors, she was surprised to see no yellow light trickling out from beneath. Her breath quickened. Maybe something else had gone wrong in the village, something so bad that it had pulled Elsa away from the signing of the dignitaries’ letters.

Anna knocked, and when there was no answer, she let herself in.

Elsa was nowhere to be found.

But—Anna felt her mouth tighten.

There, lying unopened on the desk, was Secrets of the Magic Makers. It was clear Elsa hadn’t touched it. But she needed to! Anna knew people said she was too optimistic, naïve about the way the world worked, and maybe that was true, but she had faith in stories. And she had faith that there was a solution to any problem, just as long as one kept looking. She just needed to get Elsa to listen to her.

Anna hurried back through the castle, gripping Secrets of the Magic Makers. She looked everywhere for her sister, until her eyes grew heavy with sleep as the sky continued to darken outside the castle. Maybe Elsa wasn’t in the castle at all. Reluctantly, Anna trudged back to her room.

And then…

Voices.

Voices coming from Elsa’s bedroom. Anna pressed her ear to the bedroom door, and though she couldn’t make out the words, she recognized the low timbre of Kai’s voice as well as Gerda’s northern cadence.

Anna staggered from the door. Elsa was having a meeting without her! There was a time when Anna knew Elsa would have invited her to each and every single meeting, would have sought out her advice, but now…now it seemed Elsa no longer had any need for her little sister at all. Elsa had chosen to shut her out once more.

With all the dignity she could muster, Anna walked slowly away from the door, but as soon as she was out of sight from Elsa’s bedroom, she broke into a run, trying to escape the emotion that threatened to overwhelm her. Rushing into the sanctuary of her own bedroom, Anna slammed the door shut and sat cross-legged on her shaggy pink rug, Secrets of the Magic Makers spread open in front of her. She studied the book, which blurred slightly in her gaze from unshed tears. Anna flipped through it again, and a loose page fell out, one that looked like it was ripped from another book.

Reaching for it, Anna was reminded of the same loose page that had given her so much hope the previous night. The page with a spell to make your dreams come true. Her tears dried up, and Anna felt her sadness replaced by another rising emotion, one growing so fast and so big that it seemed to take on a life of its own. For a moment, she thought she understood what Elsa experienced when she used her magic. Anna had to let this wild, untamed hope free—even if Elsa didn’t think it would work, there could be no downside to trying. And if it worked, maybe the doors to council meetings would reopen to Anna. Maybe the strained tension between Anna and Elsa would disappear. Because that was her dearest dream: Anna hoped she could help the people of Arendelle, working together with Elsa to find a solution that would make everything right again. And in the process, Anna hoped Elsa would realize she needed her sister, just the same way that Anna needed Elsa.

Tugging out the loose page, Anna whispered the words out loud:

“Wild, awake!

Wind and snow!

Plant the seed

And watch it grow!

Say this spell,

And you shall see

All your dreams

Come to be!”

A beat of silence. Anna felt foolish. What had she thought would happen after she read the spell? That her sister would materialize in front of her? Come racing in with open arms and lead her back to the secret room? Without her wild hope tugging her forward, Anna deflated. She crumpled up the dream spell page and put it in her cloak pocket, not wanting to look at it anymore.

From the dressing room, Anna suddenly heard footsteps followed by voices.

“Poor thing, there is so much on her mind,” a voice floated through the door. Anna recognized it as Gerda’s.

“She bears so much,” Kai agreed, his voice loud and clear as they passed right by her door.

The council meeting must be over by now. Which meant that at any second, there would be a knock on her door, and Elsa would ask to come in. Any second now, she’d tell Anna how sorry she was that it took her so long to listen to Anna’s suggestion and that Anna was right, they needed to look at the books in the secret room. Then Anna would show her Secrets of the Magic Makers and the loose page with the spell, and they would fix everything. They would do it together. After all, they were sisters.

Anna sat up straighter on her rug and waited…and waited. The knock never came.

——

Anna’s dreams were nightmare-tossed yet again. She dreamed of dark shadows in treetops, Earth Giants destroying the village, and a shipwreck on a stormy sea. And then—ice. Anna had told Elsa she did not remember the moments during which she’d turned to ice. But that was a lie. She would never forget the horror of warm flesh turning cold, then all sensation fleeing as her warm blood frosted into stone-cold crystal. She would never forget the last bit of heat escaping through her final breath, would never forget seeing her sister sob, and the unique pain of not being able to do absolutely anything at all. Tonight, Anna’s nightmares would not let her forget. And so Anna’s dream morphed….

She was a girl of ice, standing outside the castle, only able to peer into the window and never enter through the doors. Inside, she could see Elsa reading aloud to a girl, whose glossy white hair was pulled back in two braids. Anna didn’t recognize the girl—her back was to the window—but she did recognize the girl’s dress, a soft green one with sunflowers embroidered on the hem. Anna’s birthday dress. She could see Kristoff entering the room, strumming his guitar and smiling at the girl.

Who are you? Anna wanted to yell at the ivory-haired girl. Turn around! But her frozen lips could not speak, and Anna had to wait, impatiently and horribly, until, at last, the girl turned around to reveal…Anna’s eyes. Anna’s nose. Anna’s smile. The white-haired girl was Anna—but she wasn’t. Anna had been replaced. By this other person. And no one in the room, not Kristoff, Olaf, Kai, Gerda—not even her own sister—realized it. Or maybe they did and they simply did not care. A high howl pierced the air, and the ice shattered. It broke away from Anna like a suit of armor, revealing her true self beneath. Suddenly, she could run, but the castle had shifted into a wide white tundra, and there was no place to hide before the wolf appeared. Because it was already there.

Without turning around, Anna felt the yellow eyes of the wolf fixed on her back. She ran. Yet, no matter how hard she pumped her legs or how fast her heart beat, nothing seemed to change. There was just a flat expanse of gray snow below her and even grayer sky above. The world was colorless and bleak and without hope, and then—

An explosion of red pain burst through her vision as the wolf’s claws raked and sank into her back.

Anna expected to wake up—she always woke up.

But this time, she didn’t.

Instead, the wolf flipped her over onto her back, opened its huge jaws, and swallowed her whole.

Anna’s eyes flew open. Sweat sheened her skin and she felt hollow, as if her insides had been scooped out, like a gutted pumpkin. Something prodded her back.

“Troll’s toes!” Anna exclaimed to nobody as she pulled the book out from beneath her. Sometime in the night, she must have dozed off on the floor and rolled onto the book, its thick spine digging into her own, explaining the sharp pain of the wolf’s claws in her nightmare. Anna let her head sink back onto the floor and flung her hand over her eyes.

“This is getting ridiculous,” she muttered, hoping the sound of her voice would chase away the lingering fear. “You’re too old for this kind of stuff.” Though, she didn’t feel old. In fact, that was kind of the problem. These last two days, she had felt oh so very young indeed. And that ache that always lurked just beneath the sea of her thoughts surfaced, sending a ripple of sadness through her.

How she missed her parents. Her mother would have fixed everything with a story or two about silly and magical things, like shaggy goats outwitting trolls, or an empress who forgot her clothes. And her father, he would have chased away any lingering fear with a candle that crackled and emitted a sweet, soothing scent, or a warm mug of hot chocolate.

Mmmm…hot chocolate…with marshmallows.

“Come on, Anna.” She spoke out loud again, trying to shake the loneliness. “They’re not here, but you can definitely get your own mug of hot chocolate. It’s not like the wolf is hiding beneath the bed or something.” She let out a soft little “Ha!” for good measure. The sound wasn’t very convincing, but there was no one she had to convince but herself. And so, she got off the floor, and the terrible, awful nightmare that had ended differently than it ever had before—with the wolf finally winning—slipped from her tired mind.

Anna realized she was still in her travel cloak, but she didn’t care. She could change into her pajamas once she got back. Taking a flickering candle from her bedside table, Anna was her own source of light in a castle of darkness. The flame was weak, yet just bright enough for her to make her way through the familiar halls and down to the kitchen. And—wait. What was that?

Lifting the candle up a little higher, Anna paused on the stairs. She thought she’d seen a bit of movement, a skim of white. But as she strained her eyes to peer beyond the candle’s light, Anna didn’t see anything unusual or out of place or snarling with fangs.…

“You’re being silly,” she chided herself. “Keep going. Remember: marshmallows!” Still, the memory of the nightmare resurfaced and trailed her through the corridors, down the stairs, and into the kitchen.

The kitchen was the beating heart of the castle, the cheery red-glow of its stoves producing delicious banquets and even more delicious heat that cut through the autumn’s creeping damp.

Tonight, though, the kitchen felt oddly empty and quiet. The pots and pans, instead of being clanged around by busy cooks, were hanging quietly on their hooks in neat lines next to colorful garlands of garlic, dried peppers, and herbs that draped from the ceiling, dropping down to tickle the lids of jams, beets, and pickled herring. Usually, at least one cook remained to keep an eye on the fire stoves, but Elsa had dismissed the cook staff, too, including Olina—which meant only Anna, Elsa, Olaf, Gerda, and Kai were sleeping in the castle that night. Which explained why it felt particularly quiet, dark, and empty.

That—and the fact that Sven and Kristoff still weren’t back yet. At least, Anna didn’t think they were back yet—she didn’t know for sure. Usually, outings to the Valley of the Living Rock didn’t last this long, and since he knew things weren’t going too well with the villagers, he’d know not to linger. He was a mountain man; he could take care of himself. But still, Anna began to worry and hoped they had made it back. Despite her optimism, she always worried for those she loved. It was what made Anna…Anna.

She sighed, heart heavy, and shuffled over to the stove. Making hot chocolate was simple, and while she wasn’t great with cooking that required twenty different detailed steps and ingredients and lots of fine chopping, she was adept at mixing delicious chocolate powder with milk and setting it on the stovetop. But as Anna stirred the pot of warming milk to stop a skin from forming, she heard a soft clatter.

She stopped stirring. “Hello?” she called hopefully. “Kristoff, is that you?”

No response.

She thought she heard the sound of footsteps fading away, but from the other side of the kitchen leading toward the stairs. Maybe Kristoff was wearing his earmuffs and hadn’t been able to hear her through the fluff. Typical Kristoff. Or maybe it was Olaf. Perhaps he was up for a night of reading a gripping passage about existentialism or a book on another -ism.

Quickly, Anna turned off the stove and removed the milk. The hot chocolate would have to wait. The footsteps were too intriguing. If it was Olaf, she’d leave it alone. But if it was Kristoff, she had to know what the trolls had said about the Blight. Still…it wasn’t really cold enough yet for Kristoff to be wearing his earmuffs. Like Elsa, the cold didn’t seem to bother him as much as it did the non-mountain folk. After all, he’d grown up in the cold. Taking the candle, Anna followed the footsteps up the stairs to the rest of the castle.

“Kristoff? Is that you?” she asked.

It sounded like the person was walking through the portrait gallery, then the second great hall, and finally, the Great Hall. She stood in the doorway, lifting her candle as high as she could. It only shed light on the polished wooden floor. She hadn’t heard the footsteps leave the Great Hall, which meant Kristoff, if it was him, was still there in the dark room with Anna. She stepped inside, peering behind each column that lined the wall of the cavernous room. She yanked at curtains and moved from one to the next.

“Kristoff?” Anna called. Her candle’s flame danced this way and that. Nothing, nothing, nothing, two yellow eyes, nothing, nothing—Anna stopped breathing.

Two yellow eyes.

She brought the candle back around and saw the form of a wolf.

White and massive, exactly like the one in her nightmare.

Except this time, it was different.

Because Anna was awake.
chapters.zh:
安娜透过卧室窗，望着城堡仆从的队伍过拱桥、没入渐暗的村庄。

那天下午，艾莎给了仆从带薪休假的选择，好去帮附近染上枯萎病的牲口与庄稼的亲戚。

写完信后，安娜换上旅行斗篷，用那天余下的时间帮忙从皇家船卸粮、在病畜的呻吟中分发给村民。

她曾想捂住耳朵，却又想那太懦弱。

她不能对周遭丑陋之事视而不见。

若人人如此，便无人会帮忙，一切也永无好转。

于是安娜去帮农夫用湿布轻拭白毛，试图让牲口保持清醒。

她抚过一匹伤心小马驹毛茸茸的耳，它蜷在沉睡的母亲身旁，母亲对马驹可怜的嘶鸣动也不动。

安娜转离窗，踱起步，仍穿着早先的旅行斗篷。

正如所料，艾莎没来看她。

她知姐姐忙，可……安娜又瞥向窗外，下了决心。

点起油灯，她快步穿过如今空荡的城堡长廊，去艾莎的议事厅。

安娜走近门，惊讶地发现门下没有黄光漏出。

她呼吸加快。

也许村里又出了岔子，严重到把艾莎从使节信的签署中拉走。

安娜敲门，无人应，便自己进去。

哪儿都没有艾莎。

可——安娜感到嘴绷紧。

桌上，未打开地躺着《魔法创造者之秘》。

显然艾莎没碰过它。

可她必须碰！

安娜知道人们说她太乐观、对世界运作太天真，也许没错，可她相信故事。

她也相信任何问题都有解法，只要不断寻找。

她只需让艾莎听她。

安娜攥着《魔法创造者之秘》匆匆穿回城堡。

她到处找姐姐，直到城堡外天色愈暗、眼皮愈沉。

也许艾莎根本不在城堡。

安娜不情愿地拖步回房。

然后……人声。

从艾莎卧室传来的声音。

安娜把耳贴门，虽听不清字句，却认出凯伊低沉的嗓音与格尔达的北方腔调。

安娜从门边踉跄退开。

艾莎在开会，没叫她！

曾几何时，安娜知道艾莎会邀她参加每场会、征求她的意见，可现在……现在艾莎似乎再不需要小妹妹。

艾莎再次选择把她关在门外。

安娜用尽所能的尊严，缓缓走离门，可一离开艾莎卧室的视线，便拔腿狂奔，想逃开那要将她淹没的情绪。

冲进自己卧室这方避难所，安娜砰地关上门，盘腿坐在毛茸茸的粉毯上，《魔法创造者之秘》摊在面前。

她研究着书，书在她含泪的视线里微微模糊。

安娜又翻，一页散页掉出，像是从别处撕来的。

她伸手去拿，想起昨夜给过她莫大希望的那张散页。

那是张让梦想成真的咒语页。

她的泪干了，安娜感到悲伤被另一种升起的情绪取代，它涨得又快又大，仿佛有了自己的生命。

有那么一刻，她以为自己懂了艾莎用魔法时的感受。

安娜必须释放这狂野不羁的希望——即便艾莎觉得没用，试一试也无妨。

若成了，也许议事厅的门会重向安娜敞开。

也许安娜与艾莎间的紧绷会消散。

因为那是她最深的梦：安娜希望帮阿伦黛尔百姓，与艾莎并肩找到让一切复原的解法。

而在此过程中，安娜希望艾莎明白她需要妹妹，正如安娜需要艾莎。

安娜抽出散页，轻声念出那些字：“荒野，醒吧！

风与雪！

种下种子，看它生长！

念此咒语，你将看见，所有梦想，皆会成真！”片刻寂静。

安娜觉得自己傻。

她念完咒语后，以为会发生什么？

姐姐会凭空出现在面前？

张开双臂冲进来，领她回密室？

没了那股狂野希望牵引，安娜泄了气。

她把梦境咒语页揉成一团，塞进斗篷口袋，不愿再看。

从更衣室，安娜忽然听见脚步声伴着人声。“可怜的孩子，她心事太多了，”一个声音飘过门。

安娜认出是格尔达的。“她负担太重，”凯伊附和，声音洪亮清晰，正从她门外经过。

议事会这会儿该结束了。

也就是说，随时会有敲门声，艾莎会请求进来。

随时，她会告诉安娜，她花了那么久才听进建议、很抱歉，是安娜对了，他们该看密室里的书。

然后安娜会给她看《魔法创造者之秘》和带咒语的散页，一起修好一切。

他们会一起做。

毕竟，她们是姐妹。

安娜在毯上坐直，等……等。

敲门声始终没来。——安娜的梦又被噩梦翻搅。

她梦见树梢的黑影、大地巨人摧毁村庄、风暴海上的沉船。

然后——冰。

安娜曾告诉艾莎，她不记得自己变成冰那几刻。

可那是谎。

她永忘不了温热血肉转冷、所有知觉逃逸、温血冻成冰冷水晶的恐惧。

她永忘不了最后一丝热气随终息逃逸，永忘不了看姐姐啜泣，以及那种全然无能为力的独特痛楚。

今夜，安娜的噩梦不让她忘。

于是安娜的梦变了……

她成了冰女孩，立在城堡外，只能从窗窥看，却进不了门。

里面，她看见艾莎给一个女孩朗诵，那女孩油亮白发梳成两条辫。

安娜认不出那女孩——她背对窗——却认得她的裙子，一条柔绿、裙摆绣着向日葵的裙。

安娜的生日裙。

她看见克斯托夫进屋，弹着吉他冲女孩笑。

你是谁？

安娜想朝那象牙发女孩喊。

转过来！

可她冻住的唇发不出声，安娜只能不耐又可怕地等，直到那女孩终于转身，露出……安娜的眼睛。

安娜的鼻。

安娜的微笑。

那白发的女孩是安娜——又不是。

安娜被取代了。

被这另一个人。

屋里没人——克斯托夫、奥拉夫、凯伊、格尔达——连她亲姐姐——都没察觉。

或许察觉了，却根本不在乎。

一声高嗥刺破空气，冰碎了。

它如铠甲般从安娜身上脱落，露出底下真实的她。

忽然她能跑了，可城堡已变成辽阔白原，狼出现前无处可藏。

因它已在那。

不用回头，安娜感到狼的黄眼钉在她背上。

她跑。

可无论她蹬得多狠、心跳多快，一切似乎不变。

脚下只是灰雪的平阔，头顶是更灰的天。

世界无色、荒凉、无望，然后——狼爪划过、扎进她背，一阵赤红剧痛在视野中炸开。

安娜以为会醒来——她总会醒来。

可这次，她没有。

相反，狼把她掀翻仰面，张开巨口，将她整个吞下。

安娜猛睁眼。

汗覆皮肤，她感到空虚，像五脏六腑被掏空，如挖空的南瓜。

有东西戳她背。“地精的脚趾！”安娜对着空处惊叫，从身下抽出书。

夜里某时，她定是在地上打盹、滚到书上，厚书脊硌着自己背，解释了梦中狼爪的剧痛。

安娜把头沉回地板，抬手遮眼。“这太荒唐了，”她嘟囔，盼自己的声音赶走余惧。“你太大了，不该这样。”可她不觉得自己老。

事实上，那正是问题。

这两天，她确觉得自己太小了。

那总潜于思绪之海下的痛楚浮起，送一阵悲伤的涟漪过她。

她多想父母。

母亲会用一两个关于傻气魔法之物的故事搞定一切，比如笨山羊智胜地精，或忘了穿衣的皇后。

父亲会用一支噼啪、散发甜润安神的蜡烛，或一杯温热可可，赶走余惧。

嗯……热可可……加棉花糖。“加油，安娜。”她又出声，想甩掉孤独。“他们不在，可你绝对能给自己弄杯可可。

又不是狼藏在床下。”她为壮胆轻轻“哈！”一声。

那声音不太有说服力，可她只需说服自己。

于是她离了地，那场结局前所未有的可怕噩梦——狼终于赢了——从疲惫的心头滑走。

安娜发现自己还穿着旅行斗篷，却不在意。

回来再换睡衣也行。

从床头柜取了支摇曳的蜡烛，安娜成了黑暗城堡中自己的光源。

火苗弱，却恰好够她穿过熟悉的长廊、下到厨房。

然后——等等。

那是什么？

安娜在楼梯上停步，把蜡烛举高些。

她以为瞥见一点动静、一抹白。

可当她眯眼望向烛光之外，安娜没见任何异常、错位或龇牙之物……“你真傻，”她责自己。“继续走。

记住：棉花糖！”然而噩梦的记忆复现，随她穿廊、下楼、进厨房。

厨房是城堡的跳动之心，炉子欢快的红光照出美味宴席，更美的热气刺穿秋日潜入的潮。

可今夜，厨房怪异地空而静。

锅碗不再被忙碌的厨子敲响，而是静静挂在钩上排成行，旁是天花垂下的彩绳蒜串、干椒与香草，垂下来轻拂果酱、甜菜与腌鲱鱼的盖。

通常至少留一名厨子看炉，可艾莎也遣散了厨役，包括奥丽娜——也就是说那夜城堡里只睡安娜、艾莎、奥拉夫、格尔达与凯伊。

这解释了为何格外静、暗、空。

还有——斯文与克斯托夫仍未回来。

至少，安娜觉得他们没回——她不确定。

通常去活石谷不会这么久，而且他知村民处境不妙，该知不可久留。

他是山里人；能照顾自己。

可安娜仍忧心，盼他们已回。

尽管乐观，她总为所爱担忧。

这正是安娜之为安娜。

她叹气，心沉，拖步走向炉。

做热可可简单，她虽不擅长需二十道精细步骤与配料、大量细切的烹饪，却擅于把美味可可粉与奶混匀、放上炉。

可安娜搅着温奶防结皮时，听见一声轻响。

她停搅。“你好？”她满怀希望地喊。“克斯托夫，是你吗？”无人应。

她以为听见脚步声渐远，却是从厨房另一侧、朝楼梯方向。

也许克斯托夫戴了耳罩，隔着毛绒听不见她。

典型的克斯托夫。

也许是奥拉夫。

或许他正打算夜读一段existentialism（存在主义）的扣人心弦段落，或一本别的“主义”书。

安娜迅速关炉、移开奶。

热可可得等等。

那脚步太引人好奇。

若是奥拉夫，她便不管。

可若是克斯托夫，她必知地精对枯萎病说了什么。

不过……天还没冷到克斯托夫戴耳罩。

像艾莎，寒冷似乎不像烦扰非山民那样烦他。

毕竟他在寒冷中长大。

安娜持烛，随脚步上楼去城堡其余处。“克斯托夫？

是你吗？”她问。

听来那人走过画像廊，再第二大厅，最后大 hall。

她立门口，把烛举到最高。

它只照亮擦亮的木地板。

她没听见脚步离大 hall，也就是说若是克斯托夫，仍在那暗室与安娜同在。

她步入，窥看空旷房间壁列每根柱后。

她拽开帘，从一处移到下一处。“克斯托夫？”安娜喊。

她的烛焰四舞。

没有、没有、没有、两只黄眼、没有、没有——安娜屏息。

两只黄眼。

她把烛转回，看见狼的身形。

白而巨大，正如噩梦里的那只。

可这次，不同。

因为安娜是醒着的。

sentences.en: THROUGH HER BEDROOM WINDOW, Anna watched the exodus of the castle staff trailing over the Bridge of Arches and into the darkening village.
sentences.zh: 安娜透过卧室窗，望着城堡仆从的队伍过拱桥、没入渐暗的村庄。

sentences.en: That afternoon, Elsa had given the staff the option of taking off from work with pay so that they could go help their nearby relatives whose animals and crops were suffering from the Blight.
sentences.zh: 那天下午，艾莎给了仆从带薪休假的选择，好去帮附近染上枯萎病的牲口与庄稼的亲戚。

sentences.en: After she had written the letters, Anna had changed into her travel cloak and spent the rest of the day helping unload food from the royal ship and handing it out to the villagers amidst the groaning of sick animals.
sentences.zh: 写完信后，安娜换上旅行斗篷，用那天余下的时间帮忙从皇家船卸粮、在病畜的呻吟中分发给村民。

sentences.en: She’d wanted to cover her ears, but then she thought that would be the cowardly thing to do.
sentences.zh: 她曾想捂住耳朵，却又想那太懦弱。

sentences.en: She couldn’t just ignore the ugly things in the world around her.
sentences.zh: 她不能对周遭丑陋之事视而不见。

sentences.en: If people did that, no one would ever help at all, and nothing would become well again.
sentences.zh: 若人人如此，便无人会帮忙，一切也永无好转。

sentences.en: And so Anna had gone to help the farmers dab white fur with wet washcloths to try to keep their livestock alert.
sentences.zh: 于是安娜去帮农夫用湿布轻拭白毛，试图让牲口保持清醒。

sentences.en: She’d stroked a sad little foal’s fuzzy ears as it curled up next to the sleeping form of its mother, who did not so much as stir at the foal’s pitiful nickers.
sentences.zh: 她抚过一匹伤心小马驹毛茸茸的耳，它蜷在沉睡的母亲身旁，母亲对马驹可怜的嘶鸣动也不动。

sentences.en: Anna turned away from the window and paced, still in her travel cloak from earlier.
sentences.zh: 安娜转离窗，踱起步，仍穿着早先的旅行斗篷。

sentences.en: Just as she’d thought, Elsa hadn’t come to see her.
sentences.zh: 正如所料，艾莎没来看她。

sentences.en: She knew her sister was busy, but…Anna glanced out the window again, and made up her mind.
sentences.zh: 她知姐姐忙，可……安娜又瞥向窗外，下了决心。

sentences.en: Lighting an oil lamp, she quickly made her way through the now empty halls of the castle to Elsa’s council chambers.
sentences.zh: 点起油灯，她快步穿过如今空荡的城堡长廊，去艾莎的议事厅。

sentences.en: As Anna approached the doors, she was surprised to see no yellow light trickling out from beneath.
sentences.zh: 安娜走近门，惊讶地发现门下没有黄光漏出。

sentences.en: Her breath quickened.
sentences.zh: 她呼吸加快。

sentences.en: Maybe something else had gone wrong in the village, something so bad that it had pulled Elsa away from the signing of the dignitaries’ letters.
sentences.zh: 也许村里又出了岔子，严重到把艾莎从使节信的签署中拉走。

sentences.en: Anna knocked, and when there was no answer, she let herself in.
sentences.zh: 安娜敲门，无人应，便自己进去。

sentences.en: Elsa was nowhere to be found.
sentences.zh: 哪儿都没有艾莎。

sentences.en: But—Anna felt her mouth tighten.
sentences.zh: 可——安娜感到嘴绷紧。

sentences.en: There, lying unopened on the desk, was Secrets of the Magic Makers .
sentences.zh: 桌上，未打开地躺着《魔法创造者之秘》。

sentences.en: It was clear Elsa hadn’t touched it.
sentences.zh: 显然艾莎没碰过它。

sentences.en: But she needed to!
sentences.zh: 可她必须碰！

sentences.en: Anna knew people said she was too optimistic, naïve about the way the world worked, and maybe that was true, but she had faith in stories.
sentences.zh: 安娜知道人们说她太乐观、对世界运作太天真，也许没错，可她相信故事。

sentences.en: And she had faith that there was a solution to any problem, just as long as one kept looking.
sentences.zh: 她也相信任何问题都有解法，只要不断寻找。

sentences.en: She just needed to get Elsa to listen to her.
sentences.zh: 她只需让艾莎听她。

sentences.en: Anna hurried back through the castle, gripping Secrets of the Magic Makers .
sentences.zh: 安娜攥着《魔法创造者之秘》匆匆穿回城堡。

sentences.en: She looked everywhere for her sister, until her eyes grew heavy with sleep as the sky continued to darken outside the castle.
sentences.zh: 她到处找姐姐，直到城堡外天色愈暗、眼皮愈沉。

sentences.en: Maybe Elsa wasn’t in the castle at all.
sentences.zh: 也许艾莎根本不在城堡。

sentences.en: Reluctantly, Anna trudged back to her room.
sentences.zh: 安娜不情愿地拖步回房。

sentences.en: And then… Voices.
sentences.zh: 然后……人声。

sentences.en: Voices coming from Elsa’s bedroom.
sentences.zh: 从艾莎卧室传来的声音。

sentences.en: Anna pressed her ear to the bedroom door, and though she couldn’t make out the words, she recognized the low timbre of Kai’s voice as well as Gerda’s northern cadence.
sentences.zh: 安娜把耳贴门，虽听不清字句，却认出凯伊低沉的嗓音与格尔达的北方腔调。

sentences.en: Anna staggered from the door.
sentences.zh: 安娜从门边踉跄退开。

sentences.en: Elsa was having a meeting without her!
sentences.zh: 艾莎在开会，没叫她！

sentences.en: There was a time when Anna knew Elsa would have invited her to each and every single meeting, would have sought out her advice, but now…now it seemed Elsa no longer had any need for her little sister at all.
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，安娜知道艾莎会邀她参加每场会、征求她的意见，可现在……现在艾莎似乎再不需要小妹妹。

sentences.en: Elsa had chosen to shut her out once more.
sentences.zh: 艾莎再次选择把她关在门外。

sentences.en: With all the dignity she could muster, Anna walked slowly away from the door, but as soon as she was out of sight from Elsa’s bedroom, she broke into a run, trying to escape the emotion that threatened to overwhelm her.
sentences.zh: 安娜用尽所能的尊严，缓缓走离门，可一离开艾莎卧室的视线，便拔腿狂奔，想逃开那要将她淹没的情绪。

sentences.en: Rushing into the sanctuary of her own bedroom, Anna slammed the door shut and sat cross-legged on her shaggy pink rug, Secrets of the Magic Makers spread open in front of her.
sentences.zh: 冲进自己卧室这方避难所，安娜砰地关上门，盘腿坐在毛茸茸的粉毯上，《魔法创造者之秘》摊在面前。

sentences.en: She studied the book, which blurred slightly in her gaze from unshed tears.
sentences.zh: 她研究着书，书在她含泪的视线里微微模糊。

sentences.en: Anna flipped through it again, and a loose page fell out, one that looked like it was ripped from another book.
sentences.zh: 安娜又翻，一页散页掉出，像是从别处撕来的。

sentences.en: Reaching for it, Anna was reminded of the same loose page that had given her so much hope the previous night.
sentences.zh: 她伸手去拿，想起昨夜给过她莫大希望的那张散页。

sentences.en: The page with a spell to make your dreams come true.
sentences.zh: 那是张让梦想成真的咒语页。

sentences.en: Her tears dried up, and Anna felt her sadness replaced by another rising emotion, one growing so fast and so big that it seemed to take on a life of its own.
sentences.zh: 她的泪干了，安娜感到悲伤被另一种升起的情绪取代，它涨得又快又大，仿佛有了自己的生命。

sentences.en: For a moment, she thought she understood what Elsa experienced when she used her magic.
sentences.zh: 有那么一刻，她以为自己懂了艾莎用魔法时的感受。

sentences.en: Anna had to let this wild, untamed hope free—even if Elsa didn’t think it would work, there could be no downside to trying.
sentences.zh: 安娜必须释放这狂野不羁的希望——即便艾莎觉得没用，试一试也无妨。

sentences.en: And if it worked, maybe the doors to council meetings would reopen to Anna.
sentences.zh: 若成了，也许议事厅的门会重向安娜敞开。

sentences.en: Maybe the strained tension between Anna and Elsa would disappear.
sentences.zh: 也许安娜与艾莎间的紧绷会消散。

sentences.en: Because that was her dearest dream: Anna hoped she could help the people of Arendelle, working together with Elsa to find a solution that would make everything right again.
sentences.zh: 因为那是她最深的梦：安娜希望帮阿伦黛尔百姓，与艾莎并肩找到让一切复原的解法。

sentences.en: And in the process, Anna hoped Elsa would realize she needed her sister, just the same way that Anna needed Elsa.
sentences.zh: 而在此过程中，安娜希望艾莎明白她需要妹妹，正如安娜需要艾莎。

sentences.en: Tugging out the loose page, Anna whispered the words out loud: “Wild, awake!
sentences.zh: 安娜抽出散页，轻声念出那些字：“荒野，醒吧！

sentences.en: Wind and snow!
sentences.zh: 风与雪！

sentences.en: Plant the seed And watch it grow!
sentences.zh: 种下种子，看它生长！

sentences.en: Say this spell, And you shall see All your dreams Come to be!” A beat of silence.
sentences.zh: 念此咒语，你将看见，所有梦想，皆会成真！”片刻寂静。

sentences.en: Anna felt foolish.
sentences.zh: 安娜觉得自己傻。

sentences.en: What had she thought would happen after she read the spell?
sentences.zh: 她念完咒语后，以为会发生什么？

sentences.en: That her sister would materialize in front of her?
sentences.zh: 姐姐会凭空出现在面前？

sentences.en: Come racing in with open arms and lead her back to the secret room?
sentences.zh: 张开双臂冲进来，领她回密室？

sentences.en: Without her wild hope tugging her forward, Anna deflated.
sentences.zh: 没了那股狂野希望牵引，安娜泄了气。

sentences.en: She crumpled up the dream spell page and put it in her cloak pocket, not wanting to look at it anymore.
sentences.zh: 她把梦境咒语页揉成一团，塞进斗篷口袋，不愿再看。

sentences.en: From the dressing room, Anna suddenly heard footsteps followed by voices. “Poor thing, there is so much on her mind,” a voice floated through the door.
sentences.zh: 从更衣室，安娜忽然听见脚步声伴着人声。“可怜的孩子，她心事太多了，”一个声音飘过门。

sentences.en: Anna recognized it as Gerda’s. “She bears so much,” Kai agreed, his voice loud and clear as they passed right by her door.
sentences.zh: 安娜认出是格尔达的。“她负担太重，”凯伊附和，声音洪亮清晰，正从她门外经过。

sentences.en: The council meeting must be over by now.
sentences.zh: 议事会这会儿该结束了。

sentences.en: Which meant that at any second, there would be a knock on her door, and Elsa would ask to come in.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，随时会有敲门声，艾莎会请求进来。

sentences.en: Any second now, she’d tell Anna how sorry she was that it took her so long to listen to Anna’s suggestion and that Anna was right, they needed to look at the books in the secret room.
sentences.zh: 随时，她会告诉安娜，她花了那么久才听进建议、很抱歉，是安娜对了，他们该看密室里的书。

sentences.en: Then Anna would show her Secrets of the Magic Makers and the loose page with the spell, and they would fix everything.
sentences.zh: 然后安娜会给她看《魔法创造者之秘》和带咒语的散页，一起修好一切。

sentences.en: They would do it together.
sentences.zh: 他们会一起做。

sentences.en: After all, they were sisters.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，她们是姐妹。

sentences.en: Anna sat up straighter on her rug and waited…and waited.
sentences.zh: 安娜在毯上坐直，等……等。

sentences.en: The knock never came. —— Anna’s dreams were nightmare-tossed yet again.
sentences.zh: 敲门声始终没来。——安娜的梦又被噩梦翻搅。

sentences.en: She dreamed of dark shadows in treetops, Earth Giants destroying the village, and a shipwreck on a stormy sea.
sentences.zh: 她梦见树梢的黑影、大地巨人摧毁村庄、风暴海上的沉船。

sentences.en: And then—ice.
sentences.zh: 然后——冰。

sentences.en: Anna had told Elsa she did not remember the moments during which she’d turned to ice.
sentences.zh: 安娜曾告诉艾莎，她不记得自己变成冰那几刻。

sentences.en: But that was a lie.
sentences.zh: 可那是谎。

sentences.en: She would never forget the horror of warm flesh turning cold, then all sensation fleeing as her warm blood frosted into stone-cold crystal.
sentences.zh: 她永忘不了温热血肉转冷、所有知觉逃逸、温血冻成冰冷水晶的恐惧。

sentences.en: She would never forget the last bit of heat escaping through her final breath, would never forget seeing her sister sob, and the unique pain of not being able to do absolutely anything at all.
sentences.zh: 她永忘不了最后一丝热气随终息逃逸，永忘不了看姐姐啜泣，以及那种全然无能为力的独特痛楚。

sentences.en: Tonight, Anna’s nightmares would not let her forget.
sentences.zh: 今夜，安娜的噩梦不让她忘。

sentences.en: And so Anna’s dream morphed….
sentences.zh: 于是安娜的梦变了……

sentences.en: She was a girl of ice, standing outside the castle, only able to peer into the window and never enter through the doors.
sentences.zh: 她成了冰女孩，立在城堡外，只能从窗窥看，却进不了门。

sentences.en: Inside, she could see Elsa reading aloud to a girl, whose glossy white hair was pulled back in two braids.
sentences.zh: 里面，她看见艾莎给一个女孩朗诵，那女孩油亮白发梳成两条辫。

sentences.en: Anna didn’t recognize the girl—her back was to the window—but she did recognize the girl’s dress, a soft green one with sunflowers embroidered on the hem.
sentences.zh: 安娜认不出那女孩——她背对窗——却认得她的裙子，一条柔绿、裙摆绣着向日葵的裙。

sentences.en: Anna’s birthday dress.
sentences.zh: 安娜的生日裙。

sentences.en: She could see Kristoff entering the room, strumming his guitar and smiling at the girl.
sentences.zh: 她看见克斯托夫进屋，弹着吉他冲女孩笑。

sentences.en: Who are you?
sentences.zh: 你是谁？

sentences.en: Anna wanted to yell at the ivory-haired girl.
sentences.zh: 安娜想朝那象牙发女孩喊。

sentences.en: Turn around!
sentences.zh: 转过来！

sentences.en: But her frozen lips could not speak, and Anna had to wait, impatiently and horribly, until, at last, the girl turned around to reveal…Anna’s eyes.
sentences.zh: 可她冻住的唇发不出声，安娜只能不耐又可怕地等，直到那女孩终于转身，露出……安娜的眼睛。

sentences.en: Anna’s nose.
sentences.zh: 安娜的鼻。

sentences.en: Anna’s smile.
sentences.zh: 安娜的微笑。

sentences.en: The white-haired girl was Anna—but she wasn’t.
sentences.zh: 那白发的女孩是安娜——又不是。

sentences.en: Anna had been replaced.
sentences.zh: 安娜被取代了。

sentences.en: By this other person.
sentences.zh: 被这另一个人。

sentences.en: And no one in the room, not Kristoff, Olaf, Kai, Gerda—not even her own sister—realized it.
sentences.zh: 屋里没人——克斯托夫、奥拉夫、凯伊、格尔达——连她亲姐姐——都没察觉。

sentences.en: Or maybe they did and they simply did not care.
sentences.zh: 或许察觉了，却根本不在乎。

sentences.en: A high howl pierced the air, and the ice shattered.
sentences.zh: 一声高嗥刺破空气，冰碎了。

sentences.en: It broke away from Anna like a suit of armor, revealing her true self beneath.
sentences.zh: 它如铠甲般从安娜身上脱落，露出底下真实的她。

sentences.en: Suddenly, she could run, but the castle had shifted into a wide white tundra, and there was no place to hide before the wolf appeared.
sentences.zh: 忽然她能跑了，可城堡已变成辽阔白原，狼出现前无处可藏。

sentences.en: Because it was already there.
sentences.zh: 因它已在那。

sentences.en: Without turning around, Anna felt the yellow eyes of the wolf fixed on her back.
sentences.zh: 不用回头，安娜感到狼的黄眼钉在她背上。

sentences.en: She ran.
sentences.zh: 她跑。

sentences.en: Yet, no matter how hard she pumped her legs or how fast her heart beat, nothing seemed to change.
sentences.zh: 可无论她蹬得多狠、心跳多快，一切似乎不变。

sentences.en: There was just a flat expanse of gray snow below her and even grayer sky above.
sentences.zh: 脚下只是灰雪的平阔，头顶是更灰的天。

sentences.en: The world was colorless and bleak and without hope, and then— An explosion of red pain burst through her vision as the wolf’s claws raked and sank into her back.
sentences.zh: 世界无色、荒凉、无望，然后——狼爪划过、扎进她背，一阵赤红剧痛在视野中炸开。

sentences.en: Anna expected to wake up—she always woke up.
sentences.zh: 安娜以为会醒来——她总会醒来。

sentences.en: But this time, she didn’t.
sentences.zh: 可这次，她没有。

sentences.en: Instead, the wolf flipped her over onto her back, opened its huge jaws, and swallowed her whole.
sentences.zh: 相反，狼把她掀翻仰面，张开巨口，将她整个吞下。

sentences.en: Anna’s eyes flew open.
sentences.zh: 安娜猛睁眼。

sentences.en: Sweat sheened her skin and she felt hollow, as if her insides had been scooped out, like a gutted pumpkin.
sentences.zh: 汗覆皮肤，她感到空虚，像五脏六腑被掏空，如挖空的南瓜。

sentences.en: Something prodded her back. “Troll’s toes!” Anna exclaimed to nobody as she pulled the book out from beneath her.
sentences.zh: 有东西戳她背。“地精的脚趾！”安娜对着空处惊叫，从身下抽出书。

sentences.en: Sometime in the night, she must have dozed off on the floor and rolled onto the book, its thick spine digging into her own, explaining the sharp pain of the wolf’s claws in her nightmare.
sentences.zh: 夜里某时，她定是在地上打盹、滚到书上，厚书脊硌着自己背，解释了梦中狼爪的剧痛。

sentences.en: Anna let her head sink back onto the floor and flung her hand over her eyes. “This is getting ridiculous,” she muttered, hoping the sound of her voice would chase away the lingering fear. “You’re too old for this kind of stuff.” Though, she didn’t feel old.
sentences.zh: 安娜把头沉回地板，抬手遮眼。“这太荒唐了，”她嘟囔，盼自己的声音赶走余惧。“你太大了，不该这样。”可她不觉得自己老。

sentences.en: In fact, that was kind of the problem.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那正是问题。

sentences.en: These last two days, she had felt oh so very young indeed.
sentences.zh: 这两天，她确觉得自己太小了。

sentences.en: And that ache that always lurked just beneath the sea of her thoughts surfaced, sending a ripple of sadness through her.
sentences.zh: 那总潜于思绪之海下的痛楚浮起，送一阵悲伤的涟漪过她。

sentences.en: How she missed her parents.
sentences.zh: 她多想父母。

sentences.en: Her mother would have fixed everything with a story or two about silly and magical things, like shaggy goats outwitting trolls, or an empress who forgot her clothes.
sentences.zh: 母亲会用一两个关于傻气魔法之物的故事搞定一切，比如笨山羊智胜地精，或忘了穿衣的皇后。

sentences.en: And her father, he would have chased away any lingering fear with a candle that crackled and emitted a sweet, soothing scent, or a warm mug of hot chocolate.
sentences.zh: 父亲会用一支噼啪、散发甜润安神的蜡烛，或一杯温热可可，赶走余惧。

sentences.en: Mmmm…hot chocolate…with marshmallows. “Come on, Anna.” She spoke out loud again, trying to shake the loneliness. “They’re not here, but you can definitely get your own mug of hot chocolate.
sentences.zh: 嗯……热可可……加棉花糖。“加油，安娜。”她又出声，想甩掉孤独。“他们不在，可你绝对能给自己弄杯可可。

sentences.en: It’s not like the wolf is hiding beneath the bed or something.” She let out a soft little “Ha!” for good measure.
sentences.zh: 又不是狼藏在床下。”她为壮胆轻轻“哈！”一声。

sentences.en: The sound wasn’t very convincing, but there was no one she had to convince but herself.
sentences.zh: 那声音不太有说服力，可她只需说服自己。

sentences.en: And so, she got off the floor, and the terrible, awful nightmare that had ended differently than it ever had before—with the wolf finally winning—slipped from her tired mind.
sentences.zh: 于是她离了地，那场结局前所未有的可怕噩梦——狼终于赢了——从疲惫的心头滑走。

sentences.en: Anna realized she was still in her travel cloak, but she didn’t care.
sentences.zh: 安娜发现自己还穿着旅行斗篷，却不在意。

sentences.en: She could change into her pajamas once she got back.
sentences.zh: 回来再换睡衣也行。

sentences.en: Taking a flickering candle from her bedside table, Anna was her own source of light in a castle of darkness.
sentences.zh: 从床头柜取了支摇曳的蜡烛，安娜成了黑暗城堡中自己的光源。

sentences.en: The flame was weak, yet just bright enough for her to make her way through the familiar halls and down to the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 火苗弱，却恰好够她穿过熟悉的长廊、下到厨房。

sentences.en: And—wait.
sentences.zh: 然后——等等。

sentences.en: What was that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: Lifting the candle up a little higher, Anna paused on the stairs.
sentences.zh: 安娜在楼梯上停步，把蜡烛举高些。

sentences.en: She thought she’d seen a bit of movement, a skim of white.
sentences.zh: 她以为瞥见一点动静、一抹白。

sentences.en: But as she strained her eyes to peer beyond the candle’s light, Anna didn’t see anything unusual or out of place or snarling with fangs.… “You’re being silly,” she chided herself. “Keep going.
sentences.zh: 可当她眯眼望向烛光之外，安娜没见任何异常、错位或龇牙之物……“你真傻，”她责自己。“继续走。

sentences.en: Remember: marshmallows!” Still, the memory of the nightmare resurfaced and trailed her through the corridors, down the stairs, and into the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 记住：棉花糖！”然而噩梦的记忆复现，随她穿廊、下楼、进厨房。

sentences.en: The kitchen was the beating heart of the castle, the cheery red-glow of its stoves producing delicious banquets and even more delicious heat that cut through the autumn’s creeping damp.
sentences.zh: 厨房是城堡的跳动之心，炉子欢快的红光照出美味宴席，更美的热气刺穿秋日潜入的潮。

sentences.en: Tonight, though, the kitchen felt oddly empty and quiet.
sentences.zh: 可今夜，厨房怪异地空而静。

sentences.en: The pots and pans, instead of being clanged around by busy cooks, were hanging quietly on their hooks in neat lines next to colorful garlands of garlic, dried peppers, and herbs that draped from the ceiling, dropping down to tickle the lids of jams, beets, and pickled herring.
sentences.zh: 锅碗不再被忙碌的厨子敲响，而是静静挂在钩上排成行，旁是天花垂下的彩绳蒜串、干椒与香草，垂下来轻拂果酱、甜菜与腌鲱鱼的盖。

sentences.en: Usually, at least one cook remained to keep an eye on the fire stoves, but Elsa had dismissed the cook staff, too, including Olina—which meant only Anna, Elsa, Olaf, Gerda, and Kai were sleeping in the castle that night.
sentences.zh: 通常至少留一名厨子看炉，可艾莎也遣散了厨役，包括奥丽娜——也就是说那夜城堡里只睡安娜、艾莎、奥拉夫、格尔达与凯伊。

sentences.en: Which explained why it felt particularly quiet, dark, and empty.
sentences.zh: 这解释了为何格外静、暗、空。

sentences.en: That—and the fact that Sven and Kristoff still weren’t back yet.
sentences.zh: 还有——斯文与克斯托夫仍未回来。

sentences.en: At least, Anna didn’t think they were back yet—she didn’t know for sure.
sentences.zh: 至少，安娜觉得他们没回——她不确定。

sentences.en: Usually, outings to the Valley of the Living Rock didn’t last this long, and since he knew things weren’t going too well with the villagers, he’d know not to linger.
sentences.zh: 通常去活石谷不会这么久，而且他知村民处境不妙，该知不可久留。

sentences.en: He was a mountain man; he could take care of himself.
sentences.zh: 他是山里人；能照顾自己。

sentences.en: But still, Anna began to worry and hoped they had made it back.
sentences.zh: 可安娜仍忧心，盼他们已回。

sentences.en: Despite her optimism, she always worried for those she loved.
sentences.zh: 尽管乐观，她总为所爱担忧。

sentences.en: It was what made Anna…Anna.
sentences.zh: 这正是安娜之为安娜。

sentences.en: She sighed, heart heavy, and shuffled over to the stove.
sentences.zh: 她叹气，心沉，拖步走向炉。

sentences.en: Making hot chocolate was simple, and while she wasn’t great with cooking that required twenty different detailed steps and ingredients and lots of fine chopping, she was adept at mixing delicious chocolate powder with milk and setting it on the stovetop.
sentences.zh: 做热可可简单，她虽不擅长需二十道精细步骤与配料、大量细切的烹饪，却擅于把美味可可粉与奶混匀、放上炉。

sentences.en: But as Anna stirred the pot of warming milk to stop a skin from forming, she heard a soft clatter.
sentences.zh: 可安娜搅着温奶防结皮时，听见一声轻响。

sentences.en: She stopped stirring. “Hello?” she called hopefully. “Kristoff, is that you?” No response.
sentences.zh: 她停搅。“你好？”她满怀希望地喊。“克斯托夫，是你吗？”无人应。

sentences.en: She thought she heard the sound of footsteps fading away, but from the other side of the kitchen leading toward the stairs.
sentences.zh: 她以为听见脚步声渐远，却是从厨房另一侧、朝楼梯方向。

sentences.en: Maybe Kristoff was wearing his earmuffs and hadn’t been able to hear her through the fluff.
sentences.zh: 也许克斯托夫戴了耳罩，隔着毛绒听不见她。

sentences.en: Typical Kristoff.
sentences.zh: 典型的克斯托夫。

sentences.en: Or maybe it was Olaf.
sentences.zh: 也许是奥拉夫。

sentences.en: Perhaps he was up for a night of reading a gripping passage about existentialism or a book on another -ism.
sentences.zh: 或许他正打算夜读一段existentialism（存在主义）的扣人心弦段落，或一本别的“主义”书。

sentences.en: Quickly, Anna turned off the stove and removed the milk.
sentences.zh: 安娜迅速关炉、移开奶。

sentences.en: The hot chocolate would have to wait.
sentences.zh: 热可可得等等。

sentences.en: The footsteps were too intriguing.
sentences.zh: 那脚步太引人好奇。

sentences.en: If it was Olaf, she’d leave it alone.
sentences.zh: 若是奥拉夫，她便不管。

sentences.en: But if it was Kristoff, she had to know what the trolls had said about the Blight.
sentences.zh: 可若是克斯托夫，她必知地精对枯萎病说了什么。

sentences.en: Still…it wasn’t really cold enough yet for Kristoff to be wearing his earmuffs.
sentences.zh: 不过……天还没冷到克斯托夫戴耳罩。

sentences.en: Like Elsa, the cold didn’t seem to bother him as much as it did the non-mountain folk.
sentences.zh: 像艾莎，寒冷似乎不像烦扰非山民那样烦他。

sentences.en: After all, he’d grown up in the cold.
sentences.zh: 毕竟他在寒冷中长大。

sentences.en: Taking the candle, Anna followed the footsteps up the stairs to the rest of the castle. “Kristoff?
sentences.zh: 安娜持烛，随脚步上楼去城堡其余处。“克斯托夫？

sentences.en: Is that you?” she asked.
sentences.zh: 是你吗？”她问。

sentences.en: It sounded like the person was walking through the portrait gallery, then the second great hall, and finally, the Great Hall.
sentences.zh: 听来那人走过画像廊，再第二大厅，最后大 hall。

sentences.en: She stood in the doorway, lifting her candle as high as she could.
sentences.zh: 她立门口，把烛举到最高。

sentences.en: It only shed light on the polished wooden floor.
sentences.zh: 它只照亮擦亮的木地板。

sentences.en: She hadn’t heard the footsteps leave the Great Hall, which meant Kristoff, if it was him, was still there in the dark room with Anna.
sentences.zh: 她没听见脚步离大 hall，也就是说若是克斯托夫，仍在那暗室与安娜同在。

sentences.en: She stepped inside, peering behind each column that lined the wall of the cavernous room.
sentences.zh: 她步入，窥看空旷房间壁列每根柱后。

sentences.en: She yanked at curtains and moved from one to the next. “Kristoff?” Anna called.
sentences.zh: 她拽开帘，从一处移到下一处。“克斯托夫？”安娜喊。

sentences.en: Her candle’s flame danced this way and that.
sentences.zh: 她的烛焰四舞。

sentences.en: Nothing, nothing, nothing, two yellow eyes, nothing, nothing—Anna stopped breathing.
sentences.zh: 没有、没有、没有、两只黄眼、没有、没有——安娜屏息。

sentences.en: Two yellow eyes.
sentences.zh: 两只黄眼。

sentences.en: She brought the candle back around and saw the form of a wolf.
sentences.zh: 她把烛转回，看见狼的身形。

sentences.en: White and massive, exactly like the one in her nightmare.
sentences.zh: 白而巨大，正如噩梦里的那只。

sentences.en: Except this time, it was different.
