"斯文！"克斯托夫喊着，托住他的朋友，那颗脑袋垂得极低，鹿角都快扫到结霜的草地上。

斯文发出一声低沉的呻吟，那声音把安娜肺里的气都挤了出来。

不——不是斯文。

他一个小时前还好好的！"薄荷，"艾莎有气无力地说，安娜转头看姐姐，发现艾莎和自己一样神色慌乱。"SoYun说过薄荷对赫伯特有用，我前两天见过的那些山羊用了也有效。""那个草药师的铺子！"安娜说，把目光从克斯托夫那张失神的脸上移开，望向脚下的村庄。"加布里埃拉的店里一向备着薄荷！

要是不管用，还有面包师布洛杰特——""会管用的，"艾莎斩钉截铁地打断，"我之前去过那儿问草药方子，可没人在家，"她补充道，"这会儿她总该回来了。"说完，他们顺着小路冲向村庄，克斯托夫一路上手都没离开过斯文，安娜的眼睛则死死盯着前方的房屋和店铺。

越早把村民撤走，就能越早想出办法，同时对付枯萎病和那只狼。

一个王国怎么会一下子摊上这么多倒霉事？

可情况本可能更糟。

安娜心里清楚。

毕竟，斯文还处在枯萎病的初期。

他本可能痛得直不起腰，本可能一头栽倒，陷进那种怎么都醒不过来的沉睡，再也跑不过狼的利齿。

那只狼。

它和枯萎病有什么关系吗？

安娜想起斯文在厨房里僵立不动、任由狼逼近的模样，仿佛那双黄眼睛把他钉在了原地。

可这说不通。

枯萎病出现在狼之前，但也许狼把斯文吓得太狠——把他这头驯鹿从头到脚都吓得乱了套——以至于他身体的防御被撼动，让枯萎病得以趁虚而入，像一团带刺又顽强的野草，在斯文体内悄悄蔓延。

但起码斯文还能动。

他还有力气小跑，背上驮着奥拉夫，雪人把自个儿的胡萝卜鼻子用绳子吊在驯鹿口鼻前，好让斯文保持清醒和干劲。

安娜真希望自己也有那么简单的东西——比如一根胡萝卜——能让克斯托夫打起精神。

她刚认识克斯托夫时，还以为他天生就是个爱皱眉的闷葫芦，可相处久了才发现，他其实爱笑，笑起来毫不费力。

可此刻，她眼看着那个独来独往的山地汉子又慢慢回来了。

忧心在他脸上刻出道道纹路，嘴角也往下拉着。

安娜放慢脚步走起来，把他的手拢进自己掌心。"嘿。

会没事的。

我答应过三天内把这团乱子收拾好，我们就一定做到。

连狼一起。"克斯托夫摇摇头，棕色的眼睛里满是忧虑。"我就是想不明白到底发生了什么。

先有枯萎病，然后我又找不到地精，接着——""等等，什么？"安娜倒吸一口气。"你说找不到地精是什么意思？""他们不在活石谷，也没留下任何口信，"克斯托夫解释道。

他无所谓地耸耸肩，可安娜看得出他宽阔的肩膀里绷着一股劲。"他们是神秘的家伙，我懂，但他们好歹通常会给我留个'蜗牛信'。"安娜凭经验知道，蜗牛信就是借友好的森林蜗牛帮忙，在树叶背面写下的字条。

那些字条向来有点难认，而且黏糊糊的。"他们以前这样过吗？"安娜问，可克斯托夫还没来得及答，斯文的头猛地一抬，耳朵向前竖了起来。

克斯托夫松开安娜的手。"怎么了，老伙计？"可安娜觉得自己猜到了——一阵轻柔、远远的呜咽飘进他们耳朵。

那声音几乎像风，哀怨又诡异，可那音调让安娜手臂上顿时起了一层鸡皮疙瘩。

因为那不是风。

这是完完全全属于人的声音——而且是从村庄里传来的。"不，"艾莎轻声呢喃，安娜又觉得一阵恶心。

剩下的路他们一路狂奔。

阿伦黛尔的村庄沿着海港弯成一道弧，像一群围着浴盆边缘的小鸟，在港湾边稳住身形。

安娜一向以村里那些鲜艳的屋子为傲，每栋都刷着明快的色彩，缀着精致的装饰。

许多村民喜欢加上贴合自家个性的小点缀——这里的每一户，安娜都认识，也都喜爱。

过去三年里，没有哪一周她不是往村里跑的，哪怕有些日子艾莎抽不开身。

平常的早晨，村民起得早，买来新鲜的面包当早饭，顺便聊聊头一天的新闻。

比起城堡，安娜更喜欢村庄，也喜欢有朋友在身边。

比如面包师布洛杰特，总备着一篮黄油饼干分给孩子们——偶尔也分给她。

还有阿kim，那个针线活灵巧、给安娜织了顶猫耳帽的裁缝。

还有三姐妹——苏普丽雅、迪帕和贾亚，她们每周都盼着见安娜，讨论刚读过的书，再把书改成戏来演。

平常的早晨就该是那样。

可今天不是平常的早晨。

完全不是。

鹅卵石铺的街道上空无一人，却满是他们尖叫的回声。

狼进城堡之前，一定先袭击了村庄。"不——"安娜刚要喊，艾莎伸手捂住她的嘴，把叫声堵了回去。"嘘。"艾莎指了指一扇窗。

安娜凑近往里看，只见埃尼奥拉夫人睡得正沉，睡帽歪在灰白的头发上。

她眼睛闭着，嘴却张着，发出一声令人毛骨悚然的尖叫。

安娜打骨子里知道，若埃尼奥拉夫人睁开眼，那双眼睛一定会和狼的一样，亮得发黄。

就像凯和格尔达那样。"要是惊动了他们，"艾莎低声说，"我想他们会攻击我们。"安娜点点头，觉得姐姐说得对。"咱们只管给斯文弄点薄荷叶，"她小声说，"然后就走。""我们不分头行动，"艾莎说，挨个看了他们一眼，牵起奥拉夫的手，"我们在一起，不出声，一直往前走。"说得真像个真正的领袖。

他们穿过鹅卵石小道，朝集市走去。

每转过一个弯，安娜都打了个寒颤。

街上虽空无一人，她却总觉得自己被什么盯着——仿佛所有的窗户都是盯着他们的眼睛。

又仿佛阴影里藏着一只狼，正等着扑上来。

不过，安娜安慰自己，艾莎已经封住了城堡。

她梦里的那只狼，被关在了里面，在安娜想出更好的办法之前，跑不出来。

等给累坏了的斯文——他现在抬起每只蹄子都像搬着块大石头——找到帮手，安娜就会想办法溜回城堡，把密室里的每本书一页页翻遍，找出破解的咒语。

一定有这么一道，哪怕她不记得见过。

要是破解咒语的符文还没被译出来……那她就只好去琢磨怎么破译那种文字，哪怕要花上二十年。

忧心啃着她的胃。

她知道自己没有二十年。

一天都未必有。

狼还会用它的噩梦蛊惑谁？

到头来他们大家都会怎样？

他们走到草药师铺子那扇森绿色的门前，艾莎转向同伴们。"你跟着安娜，"她对克斯托夫说，安娜还没来得及拦住姐姐、或者跟上去，艾莎已经进了加布里埃拉的铺子。

安娜要跟进去。

克斯托夫带着温和的笑，挡在她前面。"艾莎说了留下，"他说，"我不能让她一个人进去！""我看她应付得来，"克斯托夫说着，把肩上的镐摘了下来，"她是女王。""她首先是我的姐姐。"安娜看了看奥拉夫。"你守着斯文，别让他睡着了。"奥拉夫在她进门时敬了个礼，克斯托夫就跟在她身后。

铺子里回荡着一声哀嚎，那声音又响又清楚又凄惨，安娜真想把挂着的哪一束干草药塞进耳朵，好把声音盖过去。

接着——尖叫停了。

片刻之后，艾莎从楼梯上飞奔下来。"走！"艾莎说，声音里满是惊恐，"我们得立刻离开！"他们慌忙出来，砰地关上门，艾莎又用冰把门缝封死，以防万一。"我不小心吵醒了草药师，"艾莎喘着气说。

果然，安娜能听见加布里埃拉在里头走动的脚步声。"你拿到薄荷了吗？"克斯托夫问。

艾莎伸出手，在斯文鼻尖下亮出一点绿叶子。

斯文的头猛地抬起，安娜宽慰地发现，他吸进那股刺鼻气味时，瞳孔微微收缩了一点点。"那还等什么？"安娜说，"走吧。"可她还没转过身，眼角的余光瞥见一道动静。

克斯托夫把镐举过了头顶。"安静，"他低声说，眼睛不离大路，"有什么东西来了。"一道影子顺着鹅卵石朝他们移来。

安娜屏住了呼吸。

一个身影出现在视野里。

高高的，动作飞快。

艾莎举起双手，接着……"嗬嗬，"一个声音轻声说，"姑娘们，是你们吗？""奥肯，"安娜轻声说。

果然是奥肯，一个高大壮实的汉子，肩膀宽得像只划艇，腿粗得像树干。

尽管个子惊人，奥肯的圆脸蛋却红扑扑的，像瓷娃娃，他的赤褐色胡子和帽檐下翘出的卷发，与他身上那件安娜知道是他奶奶织的绿色羊毛针织衫，形成了一种喜感的反差。

奥肯竖起一根手指抵在唇上。

然后他十指交叉握在一起。

他看起来比安娜上星期去他的商栈时老了十岁。

疲惫污浊了他的脸，头上的帽子也歪着。

他眨着蓝莹莹的大眼，褐色的络腮胡跟着抽动。

他招了招手。

他们一起安静却飞快地穿过空荡的街道，沿着安娜认得的一条土路，走向一片银桦环绕、草木葱茏的山谷。

可尽管安娜对这条路熟得很，一切都变了样。

本该像老朋友一样亲切的树，成了狼可能藏身的又一处理所当然的地方。

它逃出城堡的封锁了吗？

他们刚一出村，艾莎就转过身，再次挥动双手，把一股寒气和一阵飞冰覆在村庄上。

片刻之后，村庄也被罩进一座冰穹里，呜咽的哭声被闷在了里头。

艾莎没说什么，赶紧追上来与大家会合，可安娜读懂了姐姐脸上的神情：我必须这么做。

为了他们好。

也为了我们。

安娜知道姐姐是对的。

万一狼出了城堡，正觉得饿呢？

万一那些梦游的人稀里糊涂走出村庄、往城堡去，把狼放出来呢？

艾莎做的事是对的。

终于，他们可以开口说话了。"谢天谢地你们没事，"奥肯说，"我们看到城堡被冰封住，还盼着你们平安。""我们？"艾莎又惊又喜地重复，显然想到了一处，"这么说，不是所有人都睡着？"奥肯点点头。"我们几个设法逃到了我的'流浪奥肯商栈'——""还有桑拿房！"奥拉夫插嘴，"哦，我真想进你的桑拿房！""还有桑拿房，对，"奥肯点头，"我们现在就去那儿。"奥肯是个什么都卖一点的店主，从胡萝卜到雪铲，再到疗伤药水，应有尽有。

他要说最有名的，还得是他的桑拿房——一间杉木与蒸汽的屋子，连最冷的冬夜都能让人觉得像丛林里温暖的傍晚。

他的铺子坐落在森林深处的一小块空地上，离汇入大河的小溪不远，也在通往北山和那座闪闪发光的冰宫的小路上——那是三年前艾莎初探魔力时亲手造的。

那座小木屋造得用心至极，原木上刻着几何花纹，高窗镶着菱形玻璃。

奥肯对他的铺子十分自豪。

他曾向安娜承认，从前想过当设计师，后来才发现自己真正的快乐在于照料别人，确保他们能以公道的价格从他这儿得到所需的一切。

克斯托夫对最后那句可不敢苟同。

奥肯的商栈昼夜营业，疲惫的旅人总能在那儿找到桑拿房和一堆蓬松的毛巾，暖暖地等着他们。

可当他们走近铺子，安娜看见三年来头一回，窗帘拉上了，窗上挂着一块手绘的小牌子：打烊。"这边，"奥肯轻声说，领着他们绕到后门，那是安娜只见过、从没进去过的。

他敲了敲门：一下长敲，接着三下轻敲。

没动静，接着安娜瞥见窗帘后面微微一颤。"暗号，谢谢？"一个男人的声音传来。"盈余，"奥肯轻声说。

一阵脚步声过后，是几声咔哒和金属碰撞的响动，门吱呀开了。"快，快，"奥肯轻声说。

他把安娜、艾莎、克斯托夫、斯文和奥拉夫都扫进屋，自己才进屋，拧了拧门把手确认锁好。

对自己的手艺满意了，他转身面对他们，神色担忧。"四条腿的动物平时是不许进'流浪奥肯商栈兼桑拿房'的。

这次破例，对吧？""他可懂规矩了，"安娜替斯文说，"我保证他不惹事。"奥肯神色变了变，点了点头。

总算，他们都安全了。

奥肯又拉上几道插销，挂了不下七把挂锁，金属再次吱呀作响。

这店主可不愿冒险让狼进屋、弄乱他整洁的铺子。

安娜环顾四周。

好吧，那是他曾经整洁的铺子。"哦，天哪，"艾莎低声说。

奥肯的货架向来摆着五花八门的东西——花盆压在书上，旁边是耙子和装着糖炒栗子的桶——平时在铺子里排得整整齐齐。

可现在，货架和上面的货全被推到了边上。

安娜猜，是用来加固窗户的。

万一有人——或某只狼——想破门而入。

整间木屋像在为一大战做准备，而且不光是屋子准备好了。

她四下张望，看见储藏室里有两个村民。

铁匠图娃，腰间工具带上挂着锤子，守在前门；柜台边，韦尔正往旧收据上飞快地写着什么。

一见是他，安娜心里一阵尴尬，又是一阵更强烈的恼火。

要是那记者昨天没激她，也许她就不会向所有人夸口说艾莎能在三天内解决一切，也许艾莎也就不会背着她开那场议事会。

也许安娜就不会不小心把狼从噩梦里念出来。"别人都去哪儿了？"奥拉夫从斯文背上跳下来，走到房间中央，往翻倒的书架后面张望，问道，"他们都在桑拿房里吗？"图娃摇摇头。"就我们这些了。

我们是仅剩的人。"安娜僵住了。

她原以为至少能再挤进三四十个村民。

而不只是两个。

她看向艾莎，可这位姐姐若早料到屋里人这么少，脸上也没露出来。

艾莎点点头。"好吧。

既然就这些人，那就这些人吧。"虽说声音平静，安娜却看见她捏着母亲围巾的流苏。"谁能跟我说说到底怎么回事？""我来。"韦尔举起一张纸。"我在把一切都记下来。"艾莎、奥肯和图娃朝柜台走去，安娜却走到角落——奥肯在那儿丢了一堆厚羊毛毯，克斯托夫正把毯子团成一个软窝，围在斯文身边。"我不明白，"克斯托夫摇着头，"我们去找地精的时候他还好好的，就连回到城堡，他也看着挺精神。

我是说，饿，但还行。"他摇摇头，"我知道听着荒唐，可就好像他只是看了狼一眼，就染上了枯萎病。

从那以后他就一直不对劲！""没错。"安娜凑近斯文，把薄荷叶在他鼻尖下晃了晃。"快，别睡着！"她说。

可驯鹿的眼睛还是耷拉下来。

和SoYun描述的一模一样。

枯萎病来得又急又凶。

克斯托夫一遍遍轻轻晃着他的口鼻。

他们什么也做不了。"这时候，我们得找个秘术师，"安娜说，想到了传说中那些通晓魔法的智者。"安娜？

克斯托夫？

你们过来一下？"艾莎喊道。

安娜和克斯托夫赶紧过去。

走近时，韦尔把杯子递给他们。"谁都不想睡着，以防万一。""以防什么？"安娜抿了一口。

她差点呛着。

那是她喝过最浓的咖啡，咖啡顺着喉咙下去，她几乎觉得发梢都跟着打了卷。

看克斯托夫通红的脸颊和艾莎发颤的手，安娜猜他们也被这猛劲儿惊到了。"狼跑过镇子时还醒着的人，都一直醒着，"图娃说，向来开朗的脸上此刻一片凝重，"只有熬夜到深夜的人才躲过了它的沉睡诅咒，"她继续道，"所以我们才把咖啡煮得这么浓。

谁知道睡着了会怎样？"这念头可怕极了，而一阵突然袭来的疲惫更让它雪上加霜，安娜浑身都涌起困意。

她只想蜷起来睡一觉。"我那会儿醒着，可格尔达和凯，嗯，他们一定睡着了，因为，我是说，他们绝不会……"艾莎说到一半，不知怎么接。"他们不是攻击我们了吗？"奥拉夫问。"哎呀，他们不知道那是我们！"安娜赶忙替朋友们辩解，"而且他们也根本不像自己……我想他们是把我们当成了噩梦的一部分。"说到他们，安娜只盼凯和格尔达平安，盼狼没再伤害他们。

图娃点点头。"我妻子也是一模一样。

艾达攻击我，一边还尖叫着叫我快去救她。

而我什么也做不了。"图娃脸上的神情让安娜心都碎了。

她太明白那种无助的滋味了。

图娃定了定神，继续说。"我把她留在了家里。

她就一直尖叫，尖叫……""安娜，你说我们需要秘术师，对吧？"奥肯十指指尖相对，敲着问道，"也许索伦森能帮上忙！""索……什么？"奥拉夫问。"索伦森，"奥肯说，"你们管他叫神话与传说的专家。

他是矿工山上的秘术师。""那座山上除了熊和猞猁，根本没人住，"克斯托夫说。

这咖啡实在太浓了。

安娜简直能发誓，自己刚听见奥肯说有个神话与传说的专家——一位秘术师——住在矿工山上。

艾莎偏了偏头。"什么？"奥肯刚要再说什么，安娜却分了神，没听进去。

秘术师根本不存在。

他们不过是安娜和艾莎小时候，母亲睡前讲给她们的故事里的角色。

传说秘术师会摆弄药水、符咒和厉害的咒语——可这种人根本不存在，至少安娜一直是这么以为的。

可要说谁能逆转一道念错的咒语，那一定非秘术师莫属。

忽然间，去找索伦森，比回到密室更有盼头。

安娜摇摇头。

要是一周前有人告诉她，她会认真考虑去寻一位秘术师，她准会笑出声。

可话说回来，她当初怎么也料不到，会有一只噩梦里的狼在王国里游荡。"我们以前怎么从没听说过索伦森？"艾莎追问。"他独居在一座高塔里，"奥肯解释，"可要是这是诅咒，他能帮忙！""他是不是……"艾莎挥了挥手指，让雪花在屋里打着转，"像我一样？""嗐，不是，"奥肯摇头，"没人像你。""我们得去找他！"安娜转向姐姐，可姐姐一脸将信将疑。

安娜猛地转向克斯托夫，想拉个盟友，问他："你不同意吗？"可克斯托夫像没听见。

他正望着斯文的方向，喃喃道："为什么会这样？"他手一抖，咖啡从杯里溅出来——是担心，还是咖啡的劲，安娜分不清。"它是从哪儿来的？""魔法，"奥肯说，"只能是魔法。"这话像把屋里的空气都抽走了，安娜瞥了眼艾莎，只见姐姐同时像缩进自己心里、又像僵成了直挺挺的一具——像枚鹦鹉螺的壳。"是你干的？"韦尔问艾莎。

安娜的头痛以雷霆之势卷土重来。"艾莎绝不会——""她当然不会！"图娃说，"也没人说她会。

可烂掉的庄稼、沉睡的走兽和人，再加上现在这只狼——除了诅咒或某种咒语，还能是什么？"铁匠的话音未落，一阵愧疚涌上安娜心头。

是时候坦白了。"艾莎？"她试探着叫。

一屋子人都看向她，她缩了缩脖子。

她的声音变得尖细。"呃……我能……跟你单独说一会儿吗？

就我们俩？""这地方也不算大啊，"艾莎说。"你说什么？"奥肯打断，"你刚才说什么？"艾莎张着嘴。"我是说，我不是——这地方挺好，但你知道，也不是最——"借着艾莎慌神，安娜把姐姐拉离众人，蹲到柜台后面。"我们得去见索伦森，"安娜低声说，在旅行斗篷口袋里摸索那页从《魔法制造者之秘》撕下的散页。

艾莎仰头看了看天花板，叹了口气。"安娜，我都说了，魔法不是——""我知道，我知道，"安娜点头，"它不是解决办法。

但它也许是原因。""什么？"艾莎问，"安娜，你到底想说什么？""现在，别生气，"安娜说，"就是——你看，我听见你背着我在开议事会，这倒没事，但不知怎么的，它让我难受。

我拿回《魔法制造者之秘》随便翻翻，你知道，因为母亲以前总在晚上给我们讲故事。

那个……我找到了一首歌，说是一首诗更确切，嗯，也许那是个咒语，结果呢，也许、大概、可能——它真的——""安娜。"艾莎叹了口气，把脸埋进手里。"重点是……"安娜深吸一口气，把书里撕下的那页递了出去。"阿伦黛尔被诅咒了……而且……可能就是我下的诅咒。"

sentences.en: “SVEN!” KRISTOFF CRIED, holding up his friend, whose head lolled so low to the ground that his antlers skimmed the frost-covered grass.
sentences.zh: "斯文！"克斯托夫喊着，托住他的朋友，那颗脑袋垂得极低，鹿角都快扫到结霜的草地上。

sentences.en: Sven let out a rumbling groan, and the sound squeezed the breath out of Anna’s lungs.
sentences.zh: 斯文发出一声低沉的呻吟，那声音把安娜肺里的气都挤了出来。

sentences.en: No—not Sven.
sentences.zh: 不——不是斯文。

sentences.en: He’d been fine only an hour ago! “Mint,” Elsa said faintly, and when Anna turned to look at her sister, she saw that Elsa looked as shaken as she herself felt. “SoYun said that mint helped Hebert, and it was effective with the goats I saw the other day, too.” “The botanist’s shop!” Anna said, tearing her eyes away from Kristoff’s devastated expression and looking out at the village below them. “Gabriella always has mint in her shop!
sentences.zh: 他一个小时前还好好的！"薄荷，"艾莎有气无力地说，安娜转头看姐姐，发现艾莎和自己一样神色慌乱。"SoYun说过薄荷对赫伯特有用，我前两天见过的那些山羊用了也有效。""那个草药师的铺子！"安娜说，把目光从克斯托夫那张失神的脸上移开，望向脚下的村庄。"加布里埃拉的店里一向备着薄荷！

sentences.en: And if that doesn’t work, Baker Blodget—” “It’ll work,” Elsa said, cutting in firmly. “I was there earlier to ask about herbal remedies, but no one was home,” she added. “She must be back by now.” With that, they ran down the path to the village, Kristoff keeping a hand on Sven the entire time while Anna’s eyes remained fixed on the homes and shops ahead.
sentences.zh: 要是不管用，还有面包师布洛杰特——""会管用的，"艾莎斩钉截铁地打断，"我之前去过那儿问草药方子，可没人在家，"她补充道，"这会儿她总该回来了。"说完，他们顺着小路冲向村庄，克斯托夫一路上手都没离开过斯文，安娜的眼睛则死死盯着前方的房屋和店铺。

sentences.en: The sooner they could evacuate the villagers, the sooner they could come up with a plan for how to defeat both the Blight and the wolf.
sentences.zh: 越早把村民撤走，就能越早想出办法，同时对付枯萎病和那只狼。

sentences.en: How much bad luck could a single kingdom have at once?
sentences.zh: 一个王国怎么会一下子摊上这么多倒霉事？

sentences.en: But it could be far worse.
sentences.zh: 可情况本可能更糟。

sentences.en: Anna knew that.
sentences.zh: 安娜心里清楚。

sentences.en: Sven was still in the early stages of the Blight, after all.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，斯文还处在枯萎病的初期。

sentences.en: He could be doubling over in pain, he could be falling over, plunging into that unshakable sleep that would leave him unable to run from the wolf’s teeth.
sentences.zh: 他本可能痛得直不起腰，本可能一头栽倒，陷进那种怎么都醒不过来的沉睡，再也跑不过狼的利齿。

sentences.en: The wolf.
sentences.zh: 那只狼。

sentences.en: Did it have anything to do with the Blight?
sentences.zh: 它和枯萎病有什么关系吗？

sentences.en: Anna remembered the way Sven had stood still in the kitchen as the wolf stalked toward him, as if those yellow eyes had pinned him in place.
sentences.zh: 安娜想起斯文在厨房里僵立不动、任由狼逼近的模样，仿佛那双黄眼睛把他钉在了原地。

sentences.en: But that didn’t make sense.
sentences.zh: 可这说不通。

sentences.en: The Blight came before the wolf, but maybe the wolf had so terrified Sven—had so rattled him to his reindeer core—that his body’s defenses had been jostled enough for the Blight to settle in and begin to creep through Sven like a thorny, resilient weed.
sentences.zh: 枯萎病出现在狼之前，但也许狼把斯文吓得太狠——把他这头驯鹿从头到脚都吓得乱了套——以至于他身体的防御被撼动，让枯萎病得以趁虚而入，像一团带刺又顽强的野草，在斯文体内悄悄蔓延。

sentences.en: But at least Sven was moving.
sentences.zh: 但起码斯文还能动。

sentences.en: He was still strong enough to trot, and he carried Olaf on his back, the snowman holding his own carrot nose in front of the reindeer’s muzzle on a string to keep Sven awake and motivated.
sentences.zh: 他还有力气小跑，背上驮着奥拉夫，雪人把自个儿的胡萝卜鼻子用绳子吊在驯鹿口鼻前，好让斯文保持清醒和干劲。

sentences.en: Anna wished that she had something as simple as a carrot to cheer up Kristoff.
sentences.zh: 安娜真希望自己也有那么简单的东西——比如一根胡萝卜——能让克斯托夫打起精神。

sentences.en: When she’d first met Kristoff, she’d thought he was just a perpetual grump, but as she spent more time with him, she realized that he was someone who loved to laugh and wore a smile easily.
sentences.zh: 她刚认识克斯托夫时，还以为他天生就是个爱皱眉的闷葫芦，可相处久了才发现，他其实爱笑，笑起来毫不费力。

sentences.en: Now, though, she could see the solitary mountain man slowly returning.
sentences.zh: 可此刻，她眼看着那个独来独往的山地汉子又慢慢回来了。

sentences.en: Worry carved lines into his face and his mouth tugged down.
sentences.zh: 忧心在他脸上刻出道道纹路，嘴角也往下拉着。

sentences.en: Anna slowed to a walk and slipped her hand into his. “Hey.
sentences.zh: 安娜放慢脚步走起来，把他的手拢进自己掌心。"嘿。

sentences.en: It’ll be okay.
sentences.zh: 会没事的。

sentences.en: I promised we’d fix this mess in three days, and we will.
sentences.zh: 我答应过三天内把这团乱子收拾好，我们就一定做到。

sentences.en: Wolf and all.” Kristoff shook his head, brown eyes troubled. “I just don’t understand what’s happening.
sentences.zh: 连狼一起。"克斯托夫摇摇头，棕色的眼睛里满是忧虑。"我就是想不明白到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: First the Blight, and then I couldn’t find the trolls, and then—” “Wait, what?” Anna gasped. “What do you mean, you couldn’t find the trolls?” “They weren’t in the Valley of the Living Rock, and they didn’t leave behind any message,” Kristoff explained.
sentences.zh: 先有枯萎病，然后我又找不到地精，接着——""等等，什么？"安娜倒吸一口气。"你说找不到地精是什么意思？""他们不在活石谷，也没留下任何口信，"克斯托夫解释道。

sentences.en: He shrugged carelessly, but Anna could see the tension in his broad shoulders. “They’re mysterious creatures, I get it, but they usually at least leave me snail mail.” Snail mail, as Anna knew from experience, was notes written on the bottom of leaves with the help of friendly forest snails.
sentences.zh: 他无所谓地耸耸肩，可安娜看得出他宽阔的肩膀里绷着一股劲。"他们是神秘的家伙，我懂，但他们好歹通常会给我留个'蜗牛信'。"安娜凭经验知道，蜗牛信就是借友好的森林蜗牛帮忙，在树叶背面写下的字条。

sentences.en: They tended to be a bit difficult to read, and very, very sticky. “Have they ever done that before?” Anna asked, but before Kristoff could answer, Sven’s head jerked up, his ears swiveling forward.
sentences.zh: 那些字条向来有点难认，而且黏糊糊的。"他们以前这样过吗？"安娜问，可克斯托夫还没来得及答，斯文的头猛地一抬，耳朵向前竖了起来。

sentences.en: Kristoff dropped Anna’s hand. “What is it, boy?” But Anna thought she knew, as a soft, far-off wailing met their ears.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫松开安娜的手。"怎么了，老伙计？"可安娜觉得自己猜到了——一阵轻柔、远远的呜咽飘进他们耳朵。

sentences.en: It almost sounded like the wind, mournful and ghostly, but the pitch of it sent a rush of goosebumps cascading across Anna’s arms.
sentences.zh: 那声音几乎像风，哀怨又诡异，可那音调让安娜手臂上顿时起了一层鸡皮疙瘩。

sentences.en: Because it was not the wind.
sentences.zh: 因为那不是风。

sentences.en: This was an utterly human sound—and it was coming from the village. “ No ,” Elsa breathed, and Anna felt sick again.
sentences.zh: 这是完完全全属于人的声音——而且是从村庄里传来的。"不，"艾莎轻声呢喃，安娜又觉得一阵恶心。

sentences.en: They sprinted the rest of the way.
sentences.zh: 剩下的路他们一路狂奔。

sentences.en: The village of Arendelle curved around the harbor, balancing along the bay like a flock of birds ringing the edge of a birdbath.
sentences.zh: 阿伦黛尔的村庄沿着海港弯成一道弧，像一群围着浴盆边缘的小鸟，在港湾边稳住身形。

sentences.en: Anna had always taken pride in the village’s vibrant homes, painted with bright splashes of color and trimmed with exquisite detail.
sentences.zh: 安娜一向以村里那些鲜艳的屋子为傲，每栋都刷着明快的色彩，缀着精致的装饰。

sentences.en: Many villagers liked to add personal touches that matched the personality of those living inside—and Anna knew and loved each and every one of them.
sentences.zh: 许多村民喜欢加上贴合自家个性的小点缀——这里的每一户，安娜都认识，也都喜爱。

sentences.en: There hadn’t been one week in the last three years that she hadn’t made a trip into the village, even on the days when Elsa wasn’t able to join her.
sentences.zh: 过去三年里，没有哪一周她不是往村里跑的，哪怕有些日子艾莎抽不开身。

sentences.en: On a usual morning, the villagers woke early, gathering fresh loaves of bread for breakfast and exchanging news from the previous day.
sentences.zh: 平常的早晨，村民起得早，买来新鲜的面包当早饭，顺便聊聊头一天的新闻。

sentences.en: Anna much preferred the village to the castle, and she loved having friends.
sentences.zh: 比起城堡，安娜更喜欢村庄，也喜欢有朋友在身边。

sentences.en: Friends like Baker Blodget, who always had a spare basket of fresh butter biscuits to share with the children—and, occasionally, Anna.
sentences.zh: 比如面包师布洛杰特，总备着一篮黄油饼干分给孩子们——偶尔也分给她。

sentences.en: Or Akim, the seamster who was deft with the knitting needles and had made Anna her very own hat with cat ears.
sentences.zh: 还有阿kim，那个针线活灵巧、给安娜织了顶猫耳帽的裁缝。

sentences.en: And then there were the three sisters, Supriya, Deepa, and Jaya, who couldn’t wait to see Anna every week to discuss the latest books they’d read and turned into a play.
sentences.zh: 还有三姐妹——苏普丽雅、迪帕和贾亚，她们每周都盼着见安娜，讨论刚读过的书，再把书改成戏来演。

sentences.en: That was how a usual morning looked.
sentences.zh: 平常的早晨就该是那样。

sentences.en: But this was not a usual morning.
sentences.zh: 可今天不是平常的早晨。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 完全不是。

sentences.en: The cobblestoned streets were empty of people, but full of their screams.
sentences.zh: 鹅卵石铺的街道上空无一人，却满是他们尖叫的回声。

sentences.en: Before the wolf had entered the castle, it must have attacked the village. “NO—” Anna began to yell, but Elsa put a hand over her mouth, stifling her cry. “Shhh.” Elsa pointed to a window.
sentences.zh: 狼进城堡之前，一定先袭击了村庄。"不——"安娜刚要喊，艾莎伸手捂住她的嘴，把叫声堵了回去。"嘘。"艾莎指了指一扇窗。

sentences.en: Peering inside, Anna saw Madam Eniola fast asleep, her nightcap askew on her gray hair.
sentences.zh: 安娜凑近往里看，只见埃尼奥拉夫人睡得正沉，睡帽歪在灰白的头发上。

sentences.en: Her eyes were closed, but her mouth was open in a bloodcurdling scream.
sentences.zh: 她眼睛闭着，嘴却张着，发出一声令人毛骨悚然的尖叫。

sentences.en: And Anna knew deep in her bones that if Madam Eniola’s eyes were to flutter open, they would be as bright yellow as the wolf’s.
sentences.zh: 安娜打骨子里知道，若埃尼奥拉夫人睁开眼，那双眼睛一定会和狼的一样，亮得发黄。

sentences.en: Like what happened to Kai and Gerda. “If we provoke them,” Elsa whispered, “I think they’ll attack us.” Anna nodded, sensing that her sister was right. “We just need to get some mint leaves for Sven,” she whispered. “Then we can go.” “We don’t split up,” Elsa said, looking each of them in the eye and taking Olaf’s hand. “We stay together, we stay silent, and we keep moving.” Spoken like a true leader.
sentences.zh: 就像凯和格尔达那样。"要是惊动了他们，"艾莎低声说，"我想他们会攻击我们。"安娜点点头，觉得姐姐说得对。"咱们只管给斯文弄点薄荷叶，"她小声说，"然后就走。""我们不分头行动，"艾莎说，挨个看了他们一眼，牵起奥拉夫的手，"我们在一起，不出声，一直往前走。"说得真像个真正的领袖。

sentences.en: They moved through the cobblestoned paths toward the market.
sentences.zh: 他们穿过鹅卵石小道，朝集市走去。

sentences.en: Anna shuddered as they rounded every corner.
sentences.zh: 每转过一个弯，安娜都打了个寒颤。

sentences.en: Though there was no one in the streets, she had the constant feeling that someone was watching—as if all the windows were eyes staring at them.
sentences.zh: 街上虽空无一人，她却总觉得自己被什么盯着——仿佛所有的窗户都是盯着他们的眼睛。

sentences.en: Or as though a wolf were in the shadows, just waiting to pounce.
sentences.zh: 又仿佛阴影里藏着一只狼，正等着扑上来。

sentences.en: But, Anna assured herself, Elsa had sealed off the castle.
sentences.zh: 不过，安娜安慰自己，艾莎已经封住了城堡。

sentences.en: The wolf, her nightmare wolf, was trapped inside, contained until Anna could figure out a better plan.
sentences.zh: 她梦里的那只狼，被关在了里面，在安娜想出更好的办法之前，跑不出来。

sentences.en: Once they got help for the exhausted Sven—who now lifted each hoof as though it were heavy as a boulder—Anna would figure out a way to sneak back into the castle and read through each and every book in the hidden room, page by page, searching for a counter spell.
sentences.zh: 等给累坏了的斯文——他现在抬起每只蹄子都像搬着块大石头——找到帮手，安娜就会想办法溜回城堡，把密室里的每本书一页页翻遍，找出破解的咒语。

sentences.en: There had to be one, even if she couldn’t remember having seen one.
sentences.zh: 一定有这么一道，哪怕她不记得见过。

sentences.en: And if the counter spell’s runes hadn’t yet been translated…well, then she would just have to figure out how to decode the language, even if it took her twenty years.
sentences.zh: 要是破解咒语的符文还没被译出来……那她就只好去琢磨怎么破译那种文字，哪怕要花上二十年。

sentences.en: Worry gnawed at her stomach.
sentences.zh: 忧心啃着她的胃。

sentences.en: She knew she did not have twenty years.
sentences.zh: 她知道自己没有二十年。

sentences.en: She might not even have a day.
sentences.zh: 一天都未必有。

sentences.en: Who else would the wolf enchant with its nightmare bewitchment?
sentences.zh: 狼还会用它的噩梦蛊惑谁？

sentences.en: What would happen to all of them in the end?
sentences.zh: 到头来他们大家都会怎样？

sentences.en: They reached the forest-green doors of the botanist’s shop, and Elsa turned toward her companions. “Stay with Anna,” she instructed Kristoff, and before Anna could stop her sister, or join her, Elsa was inside Gabriella’s shop.
sentences.zh: 他们走到草药师铺子那扇森绿色的门前，艾莎转向同伴们。"你跟着安娜，"她对克斯托夫说，安娜还没来得及拦住姐姐、或者跟上去，艾莎已经进了加布里埃拉的铺子。

sentences.en: Anna made to follow her.
sentences.zh: 安娜要跟进去。

sentences.en: Kristoff stepped in front of her with a gentle smile. “Elsa said to stay,” he said. “I can’t let her go in there alone!” “I think she’s got it covered,” Kristoff said, even as he unhooked his pickax from across his shoulder. “She is queen.” “She’s my sister first.” Anna looked at Olaf. “Please stay with Sven and make sure he doesn’t fall asleep.” Olaf saluted her as she went through the doorway, Kristoff just behind her.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫带着温和的笑，挡在她前面。"艾莎说了留下，"他说，"我不能让她一个人进去！""我看她应付得来，"克斯托夫说着，把肩上的镐摘了下来，"她是女王。""她首先是我的姐姐。"安娜看了看奥拉夫。"你守着斯文，别让他睡着了。"奥拉夫在她进门时敬了个礼，克斯托夫就跟在她身后。

sentences.en: Inside the shop, a wailing scream reverberated, a sound so loud and clear and sad that Anna wished she could stick one of the many bunches of dried herbs in her ears to drown it out.
sentences.zh: 铺子里回荡着一声哀嚎，那声音又响又清楚又凄惨，安娜真想把挂着的哪一束干草药塞进耳朵，好把声音盖过去。

sentences.en: Then—the screaming stopped.
sentences.zh: 接着——尖叫停了。

sentences.en: A moment later, Elsa came flying down the staircase. “Go!” Elsa said, her voice wild with fear. “We need to leave now!” They hurried out and slammed the door, and then Elsa sealed its seams with ice, for good measure. “I accidentally woke the botanist,” Elsa said, panting.
sentences.zh: 片刻之后，艾莎从楼梯上飞奔下来。"走！"艾莎说，声音里满是惊恐，"我们得立刻离开！"他们慌忙出来，砰地关上门，艾莎又用冰把门缝封死，以防万一。"我不小心吵醒了草药师，"艾莎喘着气说。

sentences.en: And indeed, Anna could hear footsteps as Gabriella moved inside. “Did you get the mint?” Kristoff asked.
sentences.zh: 果然，安娜能听见加布里埃拉在里头走动的脚步声。"你拿到薄荷了吗？"克斯托夫问。

sentences.en: Elsa held out her hand, flashing a bit of green leaf under Sven’s nose.
sentences.zh: 艾莎伸出手，在斯文鼻尖下亮出一点绿叶子。

sentences.en: Sven’s head jerked up, and Anna noticed with relief that his pupils contracted, ever so slightly as he inhaled the sharp scent. “Then what are we waiting for?” Anna said. “Let’s go .” But before she could turn around, there was a flash of movement out of the corner of her eye.
sentences.zh: 斯文的头猛地抬起，安娜宽慰地发现，他吸进那股刺鼻气味时，瞳孔微微收缩了一点点。"那还等什么？"安娜说，"走吧。"可她还没转过身，眼角的余光瞥见一道动静。

sentences.en: Kristoff had raised his pickax over his head. “Quiet,” he whispered, not taking his eyes from the road. “Something’s coming.” A shadow moved toward them across the cobblestones.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫把镐举过了头顶。"安静，"他低声说，眼睛不离大路，"有什么东西来了。"一道影子顺着鹅卵石朝他们移来。

sentences.en: Anna held her breath.
sentences.zh: 安娜屏住了呼吸。

sentences.en: A figure came into view.
sentences.zh: 一个身影出现在视野里。

sentences.en: Tall, and quick.
sentences.zh: 高高的，动作飞快。

sentences.en: Elsa raised her hands, and then… “Hoo-hoo,” a voice whispered. “Girls, is that you?” “Oaken,” Anna whispered.
sentences.zh: 艾莎举起双手，接着……"嗬嗬，"一个声音轻声说，"姑娘们，是你们吗？""奥肯，"安娜轻声说。

sentences.en: Sure enough, there stood Oaken, a large, powerfully built man with shoulders as wide as a rowboat and legs as thick as tree trunks.
sentences.zh: 果然是奥肯，一个高大壮实的汉子，肩膀宽得像只划艇，腿粗得像树干。

sentences.en: But despite his rather formidable height, Oaken’s round cheeks were as rosy as a porcelain doll’s, and his auburn beard and the frizz poking out from under his cap clashed gloriously with the green wool knit sweater that Anna knew his nan had made for him.
sentences.zh: 尽管个子惊人，奥肯的圆脸蛋却红扑扑的，像瓷娃娃，他的赤褐色胡子和帽檐下翘出的卷发，与他身上那件安娜知道是他奶奶织的绿色羊毛针织衫，形成了一种喜感的反差。

sentences.en: Oaken lifted a finger to his lips.
sentences.zh: 奥肯竖起一根手指抵在唇上。

sentences.en: Then he clasped his fingers together.
sentences.zh: 然后他十指交叉握在一起。

sentences.en: He looked as though he’d aged ten years since Anna had seen him just the other week during a visit to his trading post.
sentences.zh: 他看起来比安娜上星期去他的商栈时老了十岁。

sentences.en: Exhaustion sullied his face, and the cap on his head was askew.
sentences.zh: 疲惫污浊了他的脸，头上的帽子也歪着。

sentences.en: His ruddy muttonchops twitched as he blinked wide blue eyes.
sentences.zh: 他眨着蓝莹莹的大眼，褐色的络腮胡跟着抽动。

sentences.en: He beckoned.
sentences.zh: 他招了招手。

sentences.en: Together, they walked quietly but quickly through the empty streets, following the dirt path that Anna knew would take them down into a grassy valley surrounded by silver birch trees.
sentences.zh: 他们一起安静却飞快地穿过空荡的街道，沿着安娜认得的一条土路，走向一片银桦环绕、草木葱茏的山谷。

sentences.en: But even though Anna knew the path well, everything seemed different.
sentences.zh: 可尽管安娜对这条路熟得很，一切都变了样。

sentences.en: Trees that should have felt as familiar as old friends became just another potential place for a wolf to hide.
sentences.zh: 本该像老朋友一样亲切的树，成了狼可能藏身的又一处理所当然的地方。

sentences.en: Had it escaped the hold of the castle?
sentences.zh: 它逃出城堡的封锁了吗？

sentences.en: As soon as they stepped out of the village, Elsa turned around, and again waved her hands, directing a rush of cold and a flurry of ice over the village.
sentences.zh: 他们刚一出村，艾莎就转过身，再次挥动双手，把一股寒气和一阵飞冰覆在村庄上。

sentences.en: A minute later, the village, too, was encased in an ice dome, the screaming sobs muffled.
sentences.zh: 片刻之后，村庄也被罩进一座冰穹里，呜咽的哭声被闷在了里头。

sentences.en: Elsa didn’t say anything as she hurried to catch up with the group, but Anna could read the expression on her sister’s face clear enough: I had to.
sentences.zh: 艾莎没说什么，赶紧追上来与大家会合，可安娜读懂了姐姐脸上的神情：我必须这么做。

sentences.en: For their own good.
sentences.zh: 为了他们好。

sentences.en: And for ours.
sentences.zh: 也为了我们。

sentences.en: And Anna knew her sister was right.
sentences.zh: 安娜知道姐姐是对的。

sentences.en: What if the wolf got out of the castle, and was feeling hungry?
sentences.zh: 万一狼出了城堡，正觉得饿呢？

sentences.en: What if the sleepwalkers accidentally wandered out of the village toward the castle and freed the wolf?
sentences.zh: 万一那些梦游的人稀里糊涂走出村庄、往城堡去，把狼放出来呢？

sentences.en: What Elsa had done was the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 艾莎做的事是对的。

sentences.en: Finally, it was safe for them to speak. “Thank the glaciers you’re all right,” Oaken said. “We hoped you were okay when we saw the ice encase the castle.” Anna’s hope, which had been slipping away from her since Gabriella’s shop, caught on his word. “We?” Elsa repeated excitedly, clearly thinking along similar lines. “So, not everyone is asleep?” Oaken nodded. “A handful of us managed to flee to my Wandering Oaken’s Trading Post—” “And Sauna!” Olaf inserted. “Oh, I’d like to go into your sauna!” “And Sauna, yes.” Oaken nodded. “That’s where we’re going now.” Oaken was a shopkeeper who sold a little bit of this and a little bit of that, from carrots to snow shovels to healing draughts and more.
sentences.zh: 终于，他们可以开口说话了。"谢天谢地你们没事，"奥肯说，"我们看到城堡被冰封住，还盼着你们平安。""我们？"艾莎又惊又喜地重复，显然想到了一处，"这么说，不是所有人都睡着？"奥肯点点头。"我们几个设法逃到了我的'流浪奥肯商栈'——""还有桑拿房！"奥拉夫插嘴，"哦，我真想进你的桑拿房！""还有桑拿房，对，"奥肯点头，"我们现在就去那儿。"奥肯是个什么都卖一点的店主，从胡萝卜到雪铲，再到疗伤药水，应有尽有。

sentences.en: But most famous of all was his sauna, a room of cedarwood and steam that could make even the coldest winter nights feel like a balmy evening in the jungle.
sentences.zh: 他要说最有名的，还得是他的桑拿房——一间杉木与蒸汽的屋子，连最冷的冬夜都能让人觉得像丛林里温暖的傍晚。

sentences.en: His shop sat in a small pocket in the forest, a little way off from a small creek that fed into a larger river and on the path that led to the North Mountain and the sparkling ice palace Elsa had crafted when she’d first experimented with her powers three years before.
sentences.zh: 他的铺子坐落在森林深处的一小块空地上，离汇入大河的小溪不远，也在通往北山和那座闪闪发光的冰宫的小路上——那是三年前艾莎初探魔力时亲手造的。

sentences.en: The little wooden cabin had been built with loving attention to detail, with geometric patterns carved into its logs, and tall windows fitted with diamond-paned glass.
sentences.zh: 那座小木屋造得用心至极，原木上刻着几何花纹，高窗镶着菱形玻璃。

sentences.en: Oaken took great pride in his shop.
sentences.zh: 奥肯对他的铺子十分自豪。

sentences.en: He’d once admitted to Anna that he used to think about becoming a designer before figuring out his real joy in life came from taking care of people and making sure they could get whatever they needed from him—for a fair price.
sentences.zh: 他曾向安娜承认，从前想过当设计师，后来才发现自己真正的快乐在于照料别人，确保他们能以公道的价格从他这儿得到所需的一切。

sentences.en: Kristoff would disagree with that last part.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫对最后那句可不敢苟同。

sentences.en: Oaken’s trading post was open around the clock, and weary travelers could always find the sauna and a pile of fluffy towels ready and waiting to warm them.
sentences.zh: 奥肯的商栈昼夜营业，疲惫的旅人总能在那儿找到桑拿房和一堆蓬松的毛巾，暖暖地等着他们。

sentences.en: But as they neared the shop, Anna saw that for the first time in three years, the curtains were drawn, and a little painted sign hung in the window: CLOSED. “This way,” Oaken whispered, leading them around to a back entrance that Anna had only seen but never entered.
sentences.zh: 可当他们走近铺子，安娜看见三年来头一回，窗帘拉上了，窗上挂着一块手绘的小牌子：打烊。"这边，"奥肯轻声说，领着他们绕到后门，那是安娜只见过、从没进去过的。

sentences.en: He knocked on the door: one long tap, followed by three quick ones.
sentences.zh: 他敲了敲门：一下长敲，接着三下轻敲。

sentences.en: Nothing happened, and then Anna spotted a tiny quiver behind the curtains. “Password, please?” came a man’s voice. “Surplus,” Oaken whispered.
sentences.zh: 没动静，接着安娜瞥见窗帘后面微微一颤。"暗号，谢谢？"一个男人的声音传来。"盈余，"奥肯轻声说。

sentences.en: There was the sound of footsteps, then several clicks and a jangle of metal before the door creaked open. “Hurry, hurry,” Oaken whispered.
sentences.zh: 一阵脚步声过后，是几声咔哒和金属碰撞的响动，门吱呀开了。"快，快，"奥肯轻声说。

sentences.en: He swept Anna, Elsa, Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf inside, then stepped into the cabin himself, twisting the doorknob to make sure it was locked.
sentences.zh: 他把安娜、艾莎、克斯托夫、斯文和奥拉夫都扫进屋，自己才进屋，拧了拧门把手确认锁好。

sentences.en: Satisfied with his work, he turned to face them, looking concerned. “Four-footed animals aren’t usually allowed inside Wandering Oaken’s Trading Post and Sauna.
sentences.zh: 对自己的手艺满意了，他转身面对他们，神色担忧。"四条腿的动物平时是不许进'流浪奥肯商栈兼桑拿房'的。

sentences.en: This is an exception, ja ?” “He’s very well-behaved,” Anna said of Sven. “I promise he won’t be a problem.” Oaken’s expression shifted, and he nodded.
sentences.zh: 这次破例，对吧？""他可懂规矩了，"安娜替斯文说，"我保证他不惹事。"奥肯神色变了变，点了点头。

sentences.en: At last, they were all safe.
sentences.zh: 总算，他们都安全了。

sentences.en: Metal screeched again as Oaken slid several bolts shut and clicked no less than seven padlocks.
sentences.zh: 奥肯又拉上几道插销，挂了不下七把挂锁，金属再次吱呀作响。

sentences.en: The shopkeeper wasn’t taking any chances of letting a wolf enter his cabin and mess up his tidy shop.
sentences.zh: 这店主可不愿冒险让狼进屋、弄乱他整洁的铺子。

sentences.en: Anna looked around.
sentences.zh: 安娜环顾四周。

sentences.en: Well, what used to be his tidy shop. “Oh, dear,” Elsa murmured.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那是他曾经整洁的铺子。"哦，天哪，"艾莎低声说。

sentences.en: Oaken’s shelves, stuffed with an odd assortment of goods—flowerpots sitting on top of books, next to a corner of rakes and barrels of candied nuts—usually marched in straight lines throughout the shop.
sentences.zh: 奥肯的货架向来摆着五花八门的东西——花盆压在书上，旁边是耙子和装着糖炒栗子的桶——平时在铺子里排得整整齐齐。

sentences.en: But now, the shelves and all their wares had been pushed to the edges.
sentences.zh: 可现在，货架和上面的货全被推到了边上。

sentences.en: Reinforcements for the windows, Anna guessed.
sentences.zh: 安娜猜，是用来加固窗户的。

sentences.en: In case someone—or some wolf —tried to break in.
sentences.zh: 万一有人——或某只狼——想破门而入。

sentences.en: It looked as though the cabin itself were preparing for a great war, and it wasn’t just the cabin that was ready for a fight.
sentences.zh: 整间木屋像在为一大战做准备，而且不光是屋子准备好了。

sentences.en: Looking around, she spotted two villagers in the storeroom.
sentences.zh: 她四下张望，看见储藏室里有两个村民。

sentences.en: Tuva the blacksmith, her hammer dangling from a tool belt, stood guard at the front door, and at the counter, scribbling across old receipts, was Wael.
sentences.zh: 铁匠图娃，腰间工具带上挂着锤子，守在前门；柜台边，韦尔正往旧收据上飞快地写着什么。

sentences.en: At the sight of him, Anna felt a twinge of embarrassment and an even stronger pinch of annoyance.
sentences.zh: 一见是他，安娜心里一阵尴尬，又是一阵更强烈的恼火。

sentences.en: If the journalist hadn’t goaded her yesterday, maybe she wouldn’t have promised everyone that Elsa could fix everything in three days, and then maybe Elsa wouldn’t have had a council meeting without her.
sentences.zh: 要是那记者昨天没激她，也许她就不会向所有人夸口说艾莎能在三天内解决一切，也许艾莎也就不会背着她开那场议事会。

sentences.en: And then maybe Anna wouldn’t have accidentally spelled the wolf out of her nightmare. “Where is everyone else?” Olaf asked as he hopped off Sven, made his way into the center of the room, and peered behind overturned bookshelves. “Are they all in the sauna?” Tuva shook her head. “This is all of us.
sentences.zh: 也许安娜就不会不小心把狼从噩梦里念出来。"别人都去哪儿了？"奥拉夫从斯文背上跳下来，走到房间中央，往翻倒的书架后面张望，问道，"他们都在桑拿房里吗？"图娃摇摇头。"就我们这些了。

sentences.en: We’re the only ones left.” Anna froze.
sentences.zh: 我们是仅剩的人。"安娜僵住了。

sentences.en: Earlier, she had assumed she’d find at least thirty or forty other villagers crammed inside.
sentences.zh: 她原以为至少能再挤进三四十个村民。

sentences.en: Not just two .
sentences.zh: 而不只是两个。

sentences.en: She looked over at Elsa, but if her older sister had been expecting to find more villagers in there, her expression didn’t show it.
sentences.zh: 她看向艾莎，可这位姐姐若早料到屋里人这么少，脸上也没露出来。

sentences.en: Elsa nodded. “Okay.
sentences.zh: 艾莎点点头。"好吧。

sentences.en: If this is what we have, this is what we have.” And though her voice was calm, Anna saw that she played with the tassels of their mother’s scarf. “Can someone please tell me exactly what happened?” “I can.” Wael held up a piece of paper. “I’m writing everything down.” Elsa, Oaken, and Tuva moved toward the countertop, but Anna made her way to the corner, where Oaken had dropped off a pile of thick wool blankets that Kristoff was now crunching into a soft nest around Sven. “I don’t understand.” Kristoff shook his head. “He was fine when we were looking for the trolls, and even when we got back to the castle, he seemed good.
sentences.zh: 既然就这些人，那就这些人吧。"虽说声音平静，安娜却看见她捏着母亲围巾的流苏。"谁能跟我说说到底怎么回事？""我来。"韦尔举起一张纸。"我在把一切都记下来。"艾莎、奥肯和图娃朝柜台走去，安娜却走到角落——奥肯在那儿丢了一堆厚羊毛毯，克斯托夫正把毯子团成一个软窝，围在斯文身边。"我不明白，"克斯托夫摇着头，"我们去找地精的时候他还好好的，就连回到城堡，他也看着挺精神。

sentences.en: I mean, hungry, but good.” He shook his head. “I know it sounds ridiculous, but it’s like he got the Blight by just looking at the wolf.
sentences.zh: 我是说，饿，但还行。"他摇摇头，"我知道听着荒唐，可就好像他只是看了狼一眼，就染上了枯萎病。

sentences.en: He’s been out of sorts ever since!” “True.” Anna leaned close to Sven and waved the mint leaves under his nose. “Come on, don’t fall asleep!” she said.
sentences.zh: 从那以后他就一直不对劲！""没错。"安娜凑近斯文，把薄荷叶在他鼻尖下晃了晃。"快，别睡着！"她说。

sentences.en: But the reindeer’s eyes drooped.
sentences.zh: 可驯鹿的眼睛还是耷拉下来。

sentences.en: It was exactly as SoYun had described.
sentences.zh: 和SoYun描述的一模一样。

sentences.en: The Blight was coming on quickly and horribly.
sentences.zh: 枯萎病来得又急又凶。

sentences.en: Kristoff gently shook his muzzle again and again.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫一遍遍轻轻晃着他的口鼻。

sentences.en: There was nothing they could do. “At this point, we need a mystic,” Anna said, thinking of the magically inclined wise-folk who existed in legends. “Anna?
sentences.zh: 他们什么也做不了。"这时候，我们得找个秘术师，"安娜说，想到了传说中那些通晓魔法的智者。"安娜？

sentences.en: Kristoff?
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫？

sentences.en: Can you come here?” Elsa called.
sentences.zh: 你们过来一下？"艾莎喊道。

sentences.en: Anna and Kristoff hurried over.
sentences.zh: 安娜和克斯托夫赶紧过去。

sentences.en: As they neared, Wael held out mugs to them. “No one wants to fall asleep, just in case.” “Just in case what ?” Anna took a sip.
sentences.zh: 走近时，韦尔把杯子递给他们。"谁都不想睡着，以防万一。""以防什么？"安娜抿了一口。

sentences.en: She almost choked.
sentences.zh: 她差点呛着。

sentences.en: It was the strongest cup of coffee she’d ever tasted, and she could practically feel the tips of her hair twist up as the coffee coursed through her.
sentences.zh: 那是她喝过最浓的咖啡，咖啡顺着喉咙下去，她几乎觉得发梢都跟着打了卷。

sentences.en: Based on Kristoff’s now red cheeks and the tremor of Elsa’s hand, Anna suspected that they, too, had not been ready for the jolt. “Everyone who was asleep when the wolf ran through town has stayed asleep,” Tuva said, her usually cheerful face somber. “Only the people who were up late at night avoided falling under its sleeping curse,” she continued. “That’s why we made the coffee so strong.
sentences.zh: 看克斯托夫通红的脸颊和艾莎发颤的手，安娜猜他们也被这猛劲儿惊到了。"狼跑过镇子时还醒着的人，都一直醒着，"图娃说，向来开朗的脸上此刻一片凝重，"只有熬夜到深夜的人才躲过了它的沉睡诅咒，"她继续道，"所以我们才把咖啡煮得这么浓。

sentences.en: Who knows what will happen if we fall asleep?” It was a terrible thought, made all the more terrible by the sudden exhaustion that washed over Anna.
sentences.zh: 谁知道睡着了会怎样？"这念头可怕极了，而一阵突然袭来的疲惫更让它雪上加霜，安娜浑身都涌起困意。

sentences.en: All she wanted to do was curl up and sleep. “I was awake, but Gerda and Kai, well, they must have been asleep, because, I mean, they would never…” Elsa trailed off, at a loss. “Didn’t they attack us?” Olaf asked. “Well, they didn’t know it was us!” Anna rushed to clear her friends’ names. “And they weren’t exactly themselves….I think they thought we were part of their nightmares.” Speaking about them, Anna hoped Kai and Gerda were okay, and that the wolf hadn’t hurt them any more than it already had.
sentences.zh: 她只想蜷起来睡一觉。"我那会儿醒着，可格尔达和凯，嗯，他们一定睡着了，因为，我是说，他们绝不会……"艾莎说到一半，不知怎么接。"他们不是攻击我们了吗？"奥拉夫问。"哎呀，他们不知道那是我们！"安娜赶忙替朋友们辩解，"而且他们也根本不像自己……我想他们是把我们当成了噩梦的一部分。"说到他们，安娜只盼凯和格尔达平安，盼狼没再伤害他们。

sentences.en: Tuva nodded. “Exactly the same with my wife.
sentences.zh: 图娃点点头。"我妻子也是一模一样。

sentences.en: Ada attacked me, all the while screaming for me to come help her.
sentences.zh: 艾达攻击我，一边还尖叫着叫我快去救她。

sentences.en: And there was absolutely nothing I could do.” The expression on Tuva’s face broke Anna’s heart.
sentences.zh: 而我什么也做不了。"图娃脸上的神情让安娜心都碎了。

sentences.en: She knew only too well what it was like to feel helpless.
sentences.zh: 她太明白那种无助的滋味了。

sentences.en: Tuva collected herself and continued. “I left her at home.
sentences.zh: 图娃定了定神，继续说。"我把她留在了家里。

sentences.en: She just kept screaming and screaming.…” “Anna, you said we need a mystic, ja ?” asked Oaken, tapping the tips of his fingers together. “Maybe Sorenson can help!” “Sore-what?” Olaf asked. “Sorenson,” said Oaken. “He’s what you’d call an expert in myths and lore.
sentences.zh: 她就一直尖叫，尖叫……""安娜，你说我们需要秘术师，对吧？"奥肯十指指尖相对，敲着问道，"也许索伦森能帮上忙！""索……什么？"奥拉夫问。"索伦森，"奥肯说，"你们管他叫神话与传说的专家。

sentences.en: He’s the mystic of Miner’s Mountain.” “No one lives on that mountain but bears and lynx,” Kristoff said.
sentences.zh: 他是矿工山上的秘术师。""那座山上除了熊和猞猁，根本没人住，"克斯托夫说。

sentences.en: The coffee was way too strong.
sentences.zh: 这咖啡实在太浓了。

sentences.en: Anna could have sworn she’d just heard Oaken say that an expert in myths and lore—a mystic —lived on Miner’s Mountain.
sentences.zh: 安娜简直能发誓，自己刚听见奥肯说有个神话与传说的专家——一位秘术师——住在矿工山上。

sentences.en: Elsa tilted her head. “What?” Oaken started to say something else, but Anna was too distracted to pay attention.
sentences.zh: 艾莎偏了偏头。"什么？"奥肯刚要再说什么，安娜却分了神，没听进去。

sentences.en: Mystics didn’t exist.
sentences.zh: 秘术师根本不存在。

sentences.en: They were just characters in stories Anna and Elsa’s mother would tell them before bed as young girls.
sentences.zh: 他们不过是安娜和艾莎小时候，母亲睡前讲给她们的故事里的角色。

sentences.en: Mystics were rumored to dabble in potions, enchantments, and powerful spells—but such people simply didn’t exist, or so Anna had thought.
sentences.zh: 传说秘术师会摆弄药水、符咒和厉害的咒语——可这种人根本不存在，至少安娜一直是这么以为的。

sentences.en: But if anyone would know how to reverse an accidental spell, it would be a mystic.
sentences.zh: 可要说谁能逆转一道念错的咒语，那一定非秘术师莫属。

sentences.en: Suddenly, finding Sorenson seemed more promising than returning to the secret room.
sentences.zh: 忽然间，去找索伦森，比回到密室更有盼头。

sentences.en: Anna shook her head.
sentences.zh: 安娜摇摇头。

sentences.en: If anyone had told her a week ago that she would be seriously considering seeking out a mystic, she would have laughed.
sentences.zh: 要是一周前有人告诉她，她会认真考虑去寻一位秘术师，她准会笑出声。

sentences.en: But then again, she never would have believed that a nightmare wolf would be stalking the kingdom. “Why haven’t we heard about Sorenson before?” Elsa demanded. “He keeps to himself in a tall tower,” Oaken explained. “But if this is a curse, he could help!” “Is he…” Elsa waved her fingers, sending a dance of snowflakes twirling through the room. “Like me?” “Why, no.” Oaken shook his head. “No one is like you.” “We need to get to him!” Anna said, turning to her sister, who looked less than convinced.

chapters.title: 第11章
chapters.en:
ANNA HELD HER BREATH as Elsa took the page, her eyes wide, scanning it line by line.

“Anna—did you see the small note at the bottom?”

“No,” Anna said, turning red. “Why? What’s it say?”

Elsa moved the paper in front of her, along with a magnifying glass made of ice that she’d crafted.

Peering through the ice, Anna read:

*SPELL NOT GUARANTEED TO BE EXACTLY WHAT YOU WISHED FOR.

**IF NOT REVERSED, SPELL SHALL TAKE ROOT PERMANENTLY ON ITS THIRD SUNRISE.

“Oh,” Anna said. “Yeah, I…definitely didn’t see that.”

Elsa bit her lip, and her eyes shimmered.

“I’m sorry.” Anna shook her head, all the while hoping she could shake away the words. “I was only trying to help.”

Elsa sighed. “I know. I can’t be upset at you for that.”

There was something about Elsa’s words that made Anna want to curl up and cry. She almost would rather have had Elsa yell at her than sigh like she had. If Elsa had yelled at her, it would have meant that she thought of Anna as someone who had the ability to shape the kingdom’s future, but that sigh…it was the same sound her parents had made when a five-year-old Anna accidentally broke a clay figurine of a salamander over the mantel. “I thought it was a dragon,” a sorry Anna had told them. “I thought that it could fly!”

It’s okay, they had said. You didn’t know any better.

“Anna!”

Kristoff’s yell cut through Anna’s thought spiral. She shot to her feet. Kristoff never yelled like that. Not even the time Anna had set fire to his sleigh to save them from a pack of normal wolves, of the animal—not magical—variety.

“What’s wrong?” she called. Because something had to be wrong for him to sound like that.

“Sven.” Kristoff’s eyes and hair were wild. “He fell asleep. He won’t wake up.”

Anna ran out from behind the counter, aware of Elsa following close behind. Sure enough, Sven’s eyes were shut and his sides heaved with ragged, labored breath.

Kristoff rubbed Sven’s cheek with the back of his hand.

What to do, what to do, what to do!

But there was nothing Anna could do, except…“Elsa!” She whirled around to see her sister. “We have to meet this Sorenson person—he may be Sven’s only chance!”

“But—”

“We can ask him about, you know.” Anna bumped a little against the word spell, not wanting to admit to everyone just yet who exactly was responsible for the wolf. “And we can see if he knows how to cure the Blight!”

At least the Blight wasn’t her fault. It had happened before Anna had said her spell, but still…it was rather curious that both the Blight and wolf shared similar symptoms: a strange kind of sleep and color-changing eyes. Anna felt like she was looking at a puzzle with a shifting picture. They could be related, but Anna wasn’t sure how.

“Oaken, where exactly in the mountain does Sorenson live?” Elsa asked as Anna hurried back over to the counter.

Oaken pulled out a map and spread it smooth in front of the register, then traced a path east, to Miner’s Mountain. He tapped his finger at the base of the mountain. “Follow the Roaring River past the Black Mountains until you see the signs for the abandoned mines. Beware. They’re dangerous.”

Kristoff leaned forward to get a closer look. “Dangerous how?”

“They’re known for awful cave-ins and terrible landslides,” Oaken said.

“And the Huldrefólk who live in the heart of the mountain,” Tuva added. “They’re tricky. Sometimes, they help. Other times, they lure humans off the safest paths.”

Wael rolled his eyes. “The Huldrefólk aren’t real, you know. They’re just bedtime stories, an excuse for people who can’t follow directions and a scapegoat for when things go missing.”

“The Huldrefólk are dangerous,” Tuva continued, ignoring Wael. “You know the stories. They like to hide in the shadows. They’re thieves—they steal things.” The blacksmith dragged her eyes back to Elsa. “I think it would be wiser if you fled, Your Majesty. Maybe another country will have the answer, and they can bring help.”

Anna was too stunned to speak. She couldn’t believe Tuva was suggesting they leave their home when it needed them most. And from the look on Elsa’s face, she knew her sister felt the same way.

“Thank you for your advice.” Elsa stood up to pick up her cloak. “I appreciate it. But it’s my job to remain in Arendelle with everybody, and to find a solution, Huldrefólk or no. I’ll leave now.”

Anna shot up. “Don’t you mean we’ll leave now?”

With a flourish, Elsa swirled her cloak onto her shoulders. “No, Anna. You heard them. It’s too dangerous. I think it would be best if you all left on the royal ship, at least until things are back to normal. I can protect myself.”

Anna could hardly believe her ears. She couldn’t leave Arendelle in such a state of danger. “It’s not about protection,” she said, her thoughts flying fast, trying to come up with a winning argument that could convince Elsa. “It’s about…about…” She looked down at the mug in her hand. “It’s about keeping you awake!” she finished. “You need at least one person with you who can keep you awake—”

“And another who knows the way of the mountains,” Kristoff added. Anna noted with gratitude that he’d already shouldered his traveler’s pack and added a coil of rope to his belt, even though he did cast a worried look at his sleeping reindeer friend. Anna knew how it must feel to volunteer to be separated from a sick and sleeping Sven, but she also knew that it would be even harder for Kristoff to not at least try to help. It was the way she felt, too, and part of the reason why she loved him so much.

Olaf popped up from Sven’s blanket nest. “And a snowman who likes warm hugs!”

For a moment, Elsa stood still, as though she’d been carved from ice. Anna had already started planning how she would sneak away from the royal ship if her sister ordered her aboard, but finally, Elsa raised her hands in surrender. “All right. Anna and Kristoff will come with me. Oaken,” she said, turning to him, “would you please lead the others to the royal ship? Set sail south as fast as you can, and stay there until you hear word from me.”

“And if we don’t hear back?” Wael asked.

Anna stuck her chin up. “I promise you—you will.”

Oaken lifted a thick finger and pointed out the window. “Then I suggest you leave now. The morning is almost over, and you’ll want to reach Sorenson’s before nightfall. And remember: beware the Huldrefólk!”

As Elsa and Kristoff did a final check of their supplies, Anna fidgeted with the crumpled spell in her cloak pocket. It might have caused trouble, but it was something her mother had touched, and the thought comforted her. Fastening her cloak, Anna went over to Olaf, who was shoveling a few more carrots into his own traveler’s pack.

“I’m coming, too. I’m a snowman adventurer! A snoventurer!”

Anna smiled and placed a hand on Olaf’s back. At least bravery existed in her snow friend, even if it was lacking in others. “I know you are, but Olaf…I need to ask you to stay here.”

Olaf’s grin slid off his face. “You—you don’t want me to come?”

“I do,” Anna said, and it was the truth. Olaf might be silly, and he could occasionally lose his head, but he was wise in ways of the heart and he knew how to bring warmth to cold places. And Anna had a feeling that, soon, they would be in need of hugs more than ever. In fact, she could use one herself now. But the people standing before her could use him even more. She picked up his carrot nose and set it back in place. “Kristoff needs you here to keep an eye on Sven, and Elsa and I need you here to help the villagers stay awake as they carry Sven and head to the ship.” Anna ruffled his twiggy hair.

“Oh, I already have tons of ideas to keep them awake!” Olaf assured her, brightening. “The question is: How will I choose which idea?” He began to tick off his repertoire on his fingers. “I could sing soothing lullabies, do an interpretive dance of falling autumn leaves, recite the names of all the best beaches in the world in alphabetical order—”

“Remember,” Kristoff interrupted as he came over, his traveler’s pack heaped with the added supplies from Oaken, “you’re trying to stop them from sleeping. Not put them to sleep.”

Anna nudged Kristoff’s boot with her toe. “Hush,” she whispered.

“I’ll start a rousing game of charades. Or, no. What about jokes?” Olaf said. “Everybody loves jokes. They’ll be laughing too hard to sleep. Ahem.” He straightened his top coal button. “What do snowmen eat for lunch?”

“What?” Oaken asked.

“I’m not really sure. Snowmen really don’t eat anything, which is a bit perplexing. There was the time I tried eating fruitcake, but it kind of went right through me.”

Kristoff cocked an eyebrow while Anna giggled.

“Perfect. See, Olaf? You’ll be great!” Anna said. But as she followed Elsa and Kristoff to the door, the laughter within her faded. Dangerous things lurked outside these doors, and in the mountains. Dangerous things lurked within books, too. Dangerous power, it seemed, also lurked somewhere within Anna.

But here was her chance to fix things. Here was her chance to prove herself to Arendelle. To prove herself to Elsa. And if she didn’t, if she couldn’t, the nightmare would be complete.

The wolf would swallow the world, starting with everyone she loved.

安娜屏住了呼吸，艾莎接过那页纸，睁大眼睛一行行地扫。"安娜——你看见底下那行小字了吗？""没，"安娜说，脸红了，"怎么了？

上面说什么？"艾莎把纸移到面前，还拿出一面她用冰做的放大镜。

透过冰镜，安娜读到：本咒语不保证恰好如你所愿。若不加逆转，咒语将在第三个日出时永久扎根。"哦，"安娜说，"是啊，我……确实没看见。"艾莎咬了咬嘴唇，眼里泛起水光。"对不起。"安娜摇着头，只盼能把那些字摇出脑海。"我只是想帮忙。""我知道。

我不会为这个生你的气。"艾莎的话里有种东西，让安娜想缩成一团哭出来。

她宁可艾莎冲她吼，也不愿她这样叹气。

要是艾莎吼她，至少说明艾莎还把她当成能左右王国未来的人；可那一声叹气……和父母当年一模一样——五岁的安娜不小心把壁炉台上那只蝾螈泥像摔碎时，父母就是这么叹的。"我还以为它是条龙呢，"小安娜对他们说，"我以为它能飞！"没关系的，他们说过。

你那时候还不懂事。"安娜！"克斯托夫一声大喊，打断了安娜越想越乱的思绪。

她猛地站起身。

克斯托夫从不会那样喊。

连那次安娜为了把他们从一群普通野狼（是动物——不是魔法——那种）嘴里救出来、把他雪橇点着了的时候，他都没这样过。"怎么了？"她喊。

因为他这样喊，一定出了事。"斯文，"克斯托夫的头发和眼睛都乱了，"他睡着了。

叫不醒。"安娜从柜台后跑出来，知道艾莎紧跟在后。

果不其然，斯文眼睛闭着，身体两侧随着艰难粗重的呼吸一起一伏。

克斯托夫用手背蹭了蹭斯文的脸颊。

怎么办，怎么办，怎么办！

可安娜什么也做不了，只能——"艾莎！"她猛地转向姐姐，"我们得去见那个索伦森——他也许是斯文唯一的希望！""可是——""我们可以问问他关于，那个东西的事，"安娜对"咒语"两个字轻轻一撞，还不想当众承认狼到底是谁招来的，"我们也可以看他知不知道怎么治枯萎病！"起码枯萎病不是她的错。

它发生在安娜念咒之前，可还是……枯萎病和狼症状如此相似，实在蹊跷：一种奇异的沉睡，和变色的眼睛。

安娜觉得自己像在看一幅图案不断变换的拼图。

它们可能有关联，可安娜不确定怎么连。"奥肯，索伦森到底住在山里什么地方？"安娜赶紧回到柜台边，艾莎问道。

奥肯抽出一张地图，在收银台前摊平，手指顺着一条路向东，指向矿工山。

他在山脚敲了敲。"顺着咆哮河，过了黑山，直到看见废弃矿井的牌子。

小心。

那里很危险。"克斯托夫凑近细看。"怎么个危险法？""那是出了名的塌方和山体滑坡，"奥肯说，"还有住在山心里的胡尔德精灵，"图娃补充，"他们狡猾。

有时帮忙。

有时又把人从最安全的路上诱开。"韦尔翻了个白眼。"胡尔德精灵根本不存在，你知道的。

不过是哄小孩睡觉的故事，是给那些认不得路的人找的借口，也是东西丢了时的替罪羊。""胡尔德精灵很危险，"图娃不理韦尔，继续说，"你也知道那些故事。

他们爱躲在阴影里。

他们是贼——偷东西。"铁匠把目光移回艾莎身上。"陛下，我想您还是撤走更明智。

也许别的国家会有答案，能带人来帮忙。"安娜惊得说不出话。

她不敢相信图娃竟建议在王国最需要时离开。

看艾莎的表情，她知道姐姐也是一样想的。"谢谢你的建议，"艾莎站起身拿起斗篷，"我很感激。

但留下来和所有人一起、找出办法，是我的职责，不管有没有胡尔德精灵。

我现在就走。"安娜腾地站起。"你不是说'我们一起走'吗？"艾莎潇洒地把斗篷一甩搭上肩。"不，安娜。

你听见他们说了。

太危险了。

我想最好你们都坐皇家船离开，至少等到一切恢复正常。

我能保护自己。"安娜简直不敢相信自己的耳朵。

她不能在这种危险的关头丢下阿伦黛尔。"这不是保护的问题，"她说，脑子飞快转动，想找出能说服艾莎的理由，"这是关于……关于……"她低头看着手里的杯子，"是要让你保持清醒！"她脱口而出，"你至少需要一个能陪着你、让你不睡着的人——""还有一个认得山路的人，"克斯托夫补了一句。

安娜感激地注意到，他已经把行囊背上肩，腰里还多了卷绳子，尽管他忧心忡忡地看了眼熟睡的驯鹿朋友。

安娜明白，自愿和病中沉睡的斯文分开是什么滋味，可她也知道，对克斯托夫来说，连试都不试一下，会更难受。

她自己也是这种感觉，而这正是她那么爱他的部分原因。

奥拉夫从斯文的毯子窝里冒出头。"还有个爱暖抱抱的雪人！"有那么一刻，艾莎站着不动，像是用冰雕出来的一般。

安娜已经盘算好，要是姐姐命令她上船，她要怎么从皇家船溜走；可终于，艾莎举起双手，做了个投降的姿势。"好吧。

安娜和克斯托夫跟我来。

奥肯，"她转向他，"请你带其他人去皇家船好吗？

全速向南开，待在那儿，直到收到我的消息。""要是我们没回音呢？"韦尔问。

安娜抬起下巴。"我向你们保证——你们会的。"奥肯竖起粗手指指向窗外。"那我建议你们现在就走。

早晨快过去了，你们得在天黑前赶到索伦森那儿。

记住：当心胡尔德精灵！"艾莎和克斯托夫最后检查了一遍装备，安娜则摆弄着斗篷口袋里那张揉皱的咒语。

它也许惹了祸，可那是母亲碰过的东西，想到这，她心里安稳了些。

安娜系好斗篷，走到奥拉夫身边，他正往自己的行囊里塞几根胡萝卜。"我也去。

我是个雪人探险家！

雪险家！"安娜笑着把手搭在奥拉夫背上。

起码她的雪人朋友有勇气，哪怕别人没有。"我知道你是，可奥拉夫……我要你留在这儿。"奥拉夫的笑容一下子垮了。"你——你不想让我去？""我想的，"安娜说，这是真心话。

奥拉夫也许傻乎乎，偶尔还会把脑袋弄丢，可他在心意上很通透，懂得怎么给冷的地方带去温暖。

安娜有种预感，很快他们就会比任何时候都更需要拥抱。

其实，她现在自己就想要一个。

可眼前这些人，比她更需要他。

她把他的胡萝卜鼻子摆回原位。"克斯托夫需要你在这儿看着斯文，而艾莎和我需要你在这儿，帮村民们把斯文抬到船上时保持清醒。"安娜揉了揉他树枝般的头发。"哦，我已经有好多主意能让他们清醒了！"奥拉夫来了精神，"问题是：我该怎么选哪个主意？"他掰着手指头数起来："我可以唱助眠的摇篮曲，跳一支落叶飘零的即兴舞，按字母顺序报出全世界最好的海滩名字——""记住，"克斯托夫走过来打断，他的行囊里又塞满了奥肯给的物资，"你是想阻止他们睡着。

不是哄他们睡。"安娜用脚尖碰了碰克斯托夫的靴子。"嘘，"她低声说，"我来发起一场热闹的猜词游戏。

或者，不。

讲笑话怎么样？"奥拉夫说，"大家都爱听笑话。

他们笑得喘不过气，就睡不着了。

咳嗯。"他正了正顶上的煤块扣子，"雪人中午吃什么？""什么？"奥肯问，"我真说不准。

雪人其实什么都不吃，有点费解。

有一次我试着吃水果蛋糕，结果它直接从我身上穿过去了。"克斯托夫挑起眉毛，安娜咯咯笑。"完美。

你看，奥拉夫？

你会很棒的！"安娜说。

可她跟着艾莎和克斯托夫走到门口时，心里的笑意淡了。

门外的山林里，藏着危险的东西。

书里也藏着危险的东西。

而危险的力量，似乎也藏在安娜身体里的某处。

可这是她弥补的机会。

这是她向阿伦黛尔证明自己的机会。

向艾莎证明自己的机会。

而要是她做不到、若她无力做到，这场噩梦就圆满了。

狼会吞下整个世界，从她所爱的人开始。

chapters.title: 第12章
chapters.en:
THE SUN SHONE with intensity in the sky, a bright flat disk that sparked the colorful splendor of autumn leaves.

Usually, Anna loved nothing more than sunny fall days, those afternoons when the sky was as blue as could be and everything around her was golden. Usually. Today, though, the sun was too bright. It showed too many things: their footprints on the path, their shadows creeping across the ground, the bright gleam of Elsa’s hair. All were as visible as could possibly be. Beacons for the wolf that might as well have screamed DELICIOUS MEALS WENT THAT WAY.

Even though they had all guessed that the wolf would not move during the day, and that it was still trapped in the castle, there was no real way to be sure. So they stayed away from the cleared wagon path that followed the Roaring River, and instead stuck to the interior of the forest, picking their way over fallen logs and stumbling against rocks hidden by piles of leaves. Anna tripped more than a few times over wayward roots. Sneaking through the woods while imagining a wolf chasing her was all too familiar to Anna.

After a little while, an embarrassed Anna admitted to Kristoff what she had done. And instead of being upset at her, he hugged her. He understood that all she had wanted to do was help, and he was optimistic about their plan to save Sven.

“I don’t get it,” Anna said, trying to keep her voice quiet enough not to attract attention, but loud enough for Kristoff and Elsa to hear her over the crunching of leaves. “I have good dreams all the time. I’ve dreamed about flying, and living in a castle made of chocolate, and unicorn quests, and—”

“And me, obviously,” Kristoff suggested with a cheeky grin.

Anna nudged his arm. “Focus,” she said, trying to sound stern, though she knew her cheeks were turning pink.

“I’m just glad you didn’t dream of something really scary—like a land-walking shark,” he said.

Anna smiled. “Is that your most terrifying nightmare?”

“No.” Kristoff shook his head. “When I was little, I used to have nightmares about Bulda trying to spoon-feed me mushroom soup.”

Anna paused to unhook her cloak from a thorny bush. “That’s not scary at all.”

Kristoff adjusted his traveler’s pack. “Have you ever had a troll try to spoon-feed you?”

Anna giggled and turned to Elsa, trying to invite her to the conversation, but Elsa didn’t so much as crack a smile. She’d been practically silent since they’d left Oaken’s trading post, and Anna had the sinking suspicion her sister was upset with her.

“H-how about you, Elsa?” Anna tried to keep her tone light and airy. “What’s your worst nightmare?”

Elsa pushed back a branch. “I don’t have nightmares.”

From out of the corner of her eye, Anna saw Kristoff pick up the pace. He always liked to avoid spats whenever he could. And he, like Anna, could detect one brewing.

“Come on, Elsa.” Anna took a quick side step to avoid the branch whipping back toward her as Elsa released it. “Everyone has nightmares. I’m your sister. You can tell me. You all know my nightmare now—a massive, girl-stalking wolf.”

Elsa flung their mother’s scarf over her shoulder. “I don’t know what to tell you, Anna, except that I don’t have nightmares.”

Anna’s sinking suspicion was no longer sinking. It had hit rock bottom, and anchored in the pit of her stomach. Elsa was definitely upset with her, and the worst part—the absolute worst part—was that Anna didn’t blame her. Anna was a little furious at herself.

Snowflakes drifted in the shafts of sunlight that trickled down through the trees. Anna looked up. The sky remained as blue as ever, which meant there could only be one other source of snow.

“Elsa, why are you making flurries?” Anna held out a finger to capture a miniscule ice crystal. “We can’t have snow. We’ll leave footprints. More than the ones we’re already leaving in the mud.”

Elsa stopped and looked at her. “It’s not me.”

“Then what do you call this?” Anna held out her finger.

Elsa inspected the flake, and her pale cheeks grew even paler. “That’s not snow.”

“Anna! Elsa!” Kristoff yelled from ahead. He stood on top of a wooded knoll, looking down at something on the other side. “Come quick!”

They stopped caring who—or what—might hear them, and ran, coming to a halt beside Kristoff. Anna gasped. The forest ended on top of the knoll, and a red farmhouse sat before them, cradled by fields of wheat; wheat that was all white, translucent even, in the sun’s sharp light. As Anna looked, a breeze rippled through the field, dislodging the grains and sending up billows of what looked like ash.

The Blight was spreading.

“We can’t keep tiptoeing around,” Kristoff said, and Anna could tell he was thinking of Sven’s white coat that matched the terrible white powder. “All this darting and dodging is taking way too long. We have to move way faster!” He was right. But Anna didn’t know what to do.

Even from this distance, she could spot little white huddles among the fields. Cows that had fallen asleep. Horses that had dropped in their tracks. Any animal that could take them farther or faster had fallen sick. The only thing that looked normal in the bleached autumn landscape was the navy thread of the Roaring River that wound its way to the base of Miner’s Mountain in the distance.

“Can you freeze the river?” Anna asked Elsa. “Then maybe we could cross it.”

“Huh.” Elsa tilted her head. “That’s an idea! Maybe these will help, too.”

Elsa waved her hands, and Anna felt like she’d grown three inches. Looking down at her feet, she realized why: Elsa had transformed Anna’s walking boots into a pair of ice skates. Anna wobbled, but Kristoff grabbed her elbow, keeping her upright.

Elsa nodded at the rushing river. “We can ice-skate.”

That was not what Anna had had in mind. She gulped. It was a good idea, but Elsa was the skater, not Anna. And when Anna did skate, she preferred to skate on smooth, solid ground. On a river, there was always the chance the ice could break, pitching her into icy water. “We’ll be exposed on the open river,” Anna said slowly. “We won’t be able to hide.”

“Luckily,” Elsa said as she made her way down the knoll and to the river’s edge, “you’re traveling with an expert in ice. I can make the ice just thin enough that it’ll support our weight, but anything heavier—like a giant wolf—will crash right through it.” And with that, she stepped out onto the water.

As the toe of Elsa’s skate touched the surface, a bloom of ice crystals appeared on the river. The crystal blossoms doubled, then quadrupled, then further multiplied, until the entire surface of the river had transformed into a sheet of wild ice blossoms refracting over and over and over again in the blinding midday sun.

It was, Anna admitted to herself, another one of Elsa’s great ideas and magical creations. But just not one she really cared for all that much. She trusted her sister, though, and so she moved to the river’s edge. The ice was so thin she could see straight through it, as though it were the delicate pane of her bedroom window.

“Come on, Anna,” Kristoff said, “we’re losing time!” He jumped out onto the river with his own ice skates. The sheet of ice jounced like a trampoline beneath him, but it held, just as Elsa promised it would.

“I won’t let anything happen to you, Anna,” Elsa said, reading her sister’s worried expression. “This is our best chance, and we don’t have much time to fix this nightmare.”

Elsa was right. Anna had gotten them into this mess. And now she needed to fix it. Taking a breath, she stepped out onto the ice. Elsa led in front, each stroke of her feet scattering ice crystals across the surface.

Lined on either side by trees in their autumn splendor, the river looked like a diamond necklace set against a cushion of red. And as Anna got her feet under her, she felt her heart lighten, just a bit. The rattling, windswept leaves sounded like applause. She took courage in the sound. It was as though Arendelle were cheering for her, wanting her to succeed. And she would. She wouldn’t stop until Arendelle was safe.

Hours passed. Wind snarled Anna’s hair, and the constant rush of cold wind meant her nose had started to drip. Her feet were beginning to ache. Elsa’s magical skates usually fit just right, but today they squeezed a bit too tight, as though Elsa had forgotten Anna had grown up. Disheartened by the thought, she tried to shake away her melancholy. Anna hit a divot—and tripped. Before she could smash her nose into the ice, a hand caught her arm.

“You okay there, Twinkle Toes?” Kristoff asked.

“Totally,” Anna said. “I meant to do that.” Even though her ice-skating had much improved since her first lesson with Elsa, she wasn’t winning a competition anytime soon.

“Sorry,” Kristoff said. “I didn’t mean to ruin the Anna Axel.”

Putting her nose in the air, Anna sniffed. “I guess I can forgive you.”

Kristoff grinned, his hand slipping into hers. “Are you sure?” And then he was off, skating backward as fast as he could, pulling Anna after him. The world around them blurred as he whirled her around, as confident on the ice as he was on solid ground. Faster and faster they skated, balancing on a thin edge between control and out-of-control. Ahead of them, Elsa cruised with ease, not noticing them tilting, slipping, flying, until—

“Look out!” Anna shouted as the river took an unexpected bend. But the warning came too late. Kristoff didn’t have time to pull them to a new course, and they skidded off the river and into a tall pile of maple leaves. Lying back, Anna watched as a swirl of golden leaves fell around them.

“I meant to do that,” Kristoff said.

“Mm-hmm. The same way I meant to do the Anna Axel?” she asked.

He nodded. “Exactly.”

“ANNA!” Elsa’s voice tore through the air.

“I’m here!” Anna stood up and shook out her travel cloak to send leaves skittering to the ground. “We had a bit of a misstep. Er, mis-skate.”

Elsa’s blade sent a spray of powder over them as she came to an abrupt stop in front of them. “This isn’t a time for game-playing!”

The world as Anna knew it slowed, then froze. And though Elsa hadn’t done any magic—there had been no twirl of her hand, no blast of her ice, no ice shard burrowing its way into Anna’s heart—Elsa’s words froze something deep within Anna. Her hope. And things that are frozen…shatter. Anna could feel the splinters of her broken hope tumbling through her like smashed glass, making every breath, every blink, painful as she looked at her sister, queen of Arendelle, who no longer had any place for her sister’s silly antics.

“I know it’s not a game,” Anna retorted.

“I don’t think you do,” Elsa said, her voice carefully controlled. Anna wanted to shake her perfect sister, to see some sort of crack, to show her that she saw her as an equal. But that tone—that disappointed tone—revealed all too well exactly what Elsa thought of Anna. And then Anna was no longer hurt, no longer numb, no longer frozen. She boiled.

“I’m not a child,” Anna said. She was grateful that the ice skates’ blades made her taller than she usually was. “Do you think I don’t know?” With each word, her voice got louder and louder until she practically shouted. “Do you think I haven’t been trying?”

And before she could hear Elsa’s reply, Anna flung herself out onto the ice.

Digging the blades in deep, she pushed and pushed, going faster and faster. Anna felt too much. She was too much. That was the trouble. She was too distracted. Too carefree. Too ridiculous for anyone—even for her sister—to see how she could be helpful to the kingdom.

The wind whipped her cloak behind her, but she leaned into it, wanting to feel the fresh iciness against her hot, angry skin. For a moment, she thought she heard Elsa calling out to her, but she didn’t stop. She wanted to skate away from it all. Away from that disappointed note in Elsa’s voice, away from Kristoff’s undeserved gentle kindness, and away from her own messy, tangled emotions.

Away from her giant, cursed mistake.

The ice groaned beneath her weight, her blades scratching out a mournful note that Anna couldn’t escape. Faster, faster, faster! If only she could skate as quick as the wind, maybe she’d melt into it and be swept away from all that she’d done.

And that’s when the ice cracked.
