黑沙从门缝渗进塔屋，黑暗黏腻的念头像油一样黏在安娜身上。

像虫子爬进耳朵的念头，牙齿腐烂脱落，黑色的浪淹没人，还有一扇门。

一扇白色大门，紫花一遍遍重复，每朵都在对她说：你不够好，你不受欢迎，你被关在门外。

念头一阵阵砸来，像暴风雨的海，安娜觉得喘不过气。

她的心一紧，像有什么压在胸口。

那重量让她难开口，可她必须——得警告朋友们。"你、你们，"安娜低声说，想让嘴动起来。

可就在这宝贵的几秒，沙已漫进屋，汇成一汪黑水洼。

沙粒升起、打着旋飞到空中，仿佛每粒都有自己的小翅膀、自己的脑子，接着它们成群结队，勾出一道影子的轮廓。

一只狼的影子。

恐惧给了她力气。"纳特玛拉！"安娜喊。

沙凝成了那只巨大的白狼。

此刻这怪物有一面墙那么长。

头几乎刮到画着的天花板。

仿佛慢动作，安娜看见其他人转过身。

克斯托夫张大了嘴，艾莎惊恐地瞪圆了眼。

可最先反应的，是索伦森——那位相信科学与神话纠缠的老科学家。"闭眼！"他弹起身，抓向身边的某个玻璃瓶。

安娜闭了眼。

一秒后，即便闭着眼，也有一道强光闪过，接着是狼的一声嚎叫。

不。

不是狼，安娜纠正自己。

是纳特玛拉。"楼上！"索伦森喊，"跑！"尽管她为那光闭了眼，黑点仍斑斑点点缀在视野里，她站起，和克斯托夫朝楼梯跑去。

他们一步两级，她听见尖叫和像磨刀的声音。

回头一瞥，她看见索伦森在楼梯底，他身旁艾莎一遍遍射出冰矛，刺向狼。

可那些冰矛，又尖又致命，造成的伤害却像把牙签插进水里。

艾莎每放一支冰矛，它便飞向目标——可从不命中。

纳特玛拉似乎不是由毛、骨或肉组成。

也不是任何实在的东西。

因为冰矛快钉住它的爪时，狼爪一碰就化开，像沙一样变形——安娜意识到，像沙。

正如索伦森所说。

纳特玛拉能化成任何形。

从任何门缝渗过。

钻进人心最脆弱的缝。

它以恐惧为食，可他们怎能不怕它？

它就是恐惧。

一点黑沙飘向安娜，她又屏住呼吸。

黏腻的念头涌回脑中：是她干的。

她什么都对不了。

她从来不行。

她让艾莎失望了。"安娜！"克斯托夫行囊挂在肩头，拽着她的胳膊，"继续走！"他声音里的担忧与关切，把安娜猛地唤回自己。

她跟着他跑，一口气冲上那令人眩晕的紧螺旋阶梯，直到冲进索伦森观测台寒冷开阔的空中。

换作别时，她知道自己会愿意待在上头。

山间空气清冽，头顶的星星亮得直跳。

头顶的圆月又圆又熟，简直让人想从天上摘下，塞进口袋，当块甜点留着以后吃。

圆形平台中央，立着一架铜望远镜，像初生的小马驹，细腿打着晃，闪闪发亮。

它指向苍穹，是台帮人在天体之舞里寻答案的仪器。

一切陌生、迷人又美丽。

却是个死胡同。

正如安娜的噩梦，无路可逃。

狼还在身后塔梯上，把她逼到了死角——这次是在木台上，离地几百尺，唯一的出路——跳——对他们谁都没好处。

他们被困住了！

索伦森的肩撞上她，他从她身边冲到台边。

他探身越过简朴的木栏，抓住夜里的空气，又缩回手。

满月的光里，安娜辨出他掌心一点银光：一根钢丝缆——细得离塔一尺就似乎消失。"抓住桌布！"他指向望远镜旁那张长木工作台。

台上满是烧杯、温度计、气压计、铅笔鹅毛笔、算盘、尺子、长颈瓶，还有一页页演算。

索伦森毕生的心血，似乎都摆在一条绣着番红花的淡紫小桌布上。

若扯了桌布，那些心血——积年累月的——会砸在台上，永远丢失。

安娜犹豫了。"动手！"索伦森冲她吼。

可安娜做不到，她就是做不到。

那是一桌答案，是一生搜集信息的成果。

于是克斯托夫伸手到她身后，把桌布抽了出来。

随着一声巨响，那些美丽奇异的器具摔在地上，声音像心碎。"现在把布撕了！"索伦森命令。

狼凶狠的吠叫和冰的刮擦声充斥空气。

艾莎已上到观测台，站在入口，一遍遍甩手。

每弹一下腕，门口就填满冰——新冰，刚结的冰，没有裂缝的冰。

反正就那一会儿。

因为接着纳特玛拉会撞上去，裂纹便爬满表面，每次都有更多黑沙从缝里钻过。

平滑的冰。

碎裂的冰。

平滑。

碎裂。

艾莎挡着纳特玛拉和它的沙爪，可就连艾莎——勇敢、强壮、睿智、有魔法的艾莎——也撑不了永远。

安娜已能看见她肩头塌下的疲惫。

她弹腕的力道一次比一次松。

哧啦——！

安娜转头，看见克斯托夫正听索伦森的命令，把桌布撕成宽条，可安娜没去帮忙。

她的心被别的事占了。

每次艾莎甩腕、用冰填满门口，安娜都觉得纳特玛拉大了些。

平滑的冰。

碎裂的冰。

平滑的冰。

是的，安娜现在确定了。

每当艾莎朝这神话之兽射出魔法冰，它的爪就扩张，牙就磨尖，力气翻倍。"艾莎！"安娜喊，"艾莎，停下！

你的魔法！

它在让它更强！"可在纳特玛拉的咆哮、扯布的声响、冰一遍遍碎裂里，艾莎听不见。

此刻他们唯一的生路是逃。"快！"索伦森喊，"拿一些！"安娜从克斯托夫手里接过一段桌布，踉跄走向科学家。

索伦森抓住布条，在细钢丝上绕了个U形。"手，"他哼道。

安娜照做，伸出手腕，他把布条垂下的两端在安娜腋下打了个简易吊带。

索伦森拍拍摇摇欲坠的木栏。"爬上去。"安娜照做。

直到她稳在最高一根栏杆上，面朝脚下远处的山坡，索伦森的打算才真正明白。"等一下，"安娜扭身面对他，"你不是认真的。""抓稳了！"索伦森使劲一推。

安娜一声尖叫，在风与星中冲下观测台。

她喊。

顺着山几乎像飞，但绝对像掉。

缆绳在她速降时一弹一跳。

她把桌布缠在腕上，死命抓着，腿在身下晃荡。

头顶某处，她听见艾莎、克斯托夫和索伦森在她身后嗖嗖滑下的喊声。

谢天谢地他们安全！

安娜几乎笑出来——可地面正朝她冲来，快得过头。

她眯眼对抗黑夜，顺着起伏缆绳的去向看；它在山脚一棵树杈里消失，靠近矿井入口。

这点好。

可不好的是她冲向那结实的树干有多快。

这速度撞上树，准断几根肋骨，算她走运。

她得慢下来。"雪！"她回头朝艾莎喊，"雪！

雪雪雪雪！"她好像听见艾莎回喊，可安娜分不清。

风夺走了姐姐唇边任何的话。

她只能盼望并相信姐姐知道怎么做，像她一向那样。

离树十尺。

现在五尺。

现在两尺。

安娜松开桌布，让自己自由。

她在黑空气里翻滚，像过了一年，其实不过一瞬，接着——噗！

一阵冰凉的刺痒裹住安娜，像奥肯客栈卖的那种冒泡饮料一样清新舒坦。

柔软蓬松的雪花 cushion 了她的坠落。

艾莎又做到了。

可没时间喘气。

安娜滚开，艾莎、克斯托夫和索伦森像熟透的苹果从树上掉进雪堆。

安娜跳起。"大家都没事？

它在哪儿？"众人点头，克斯托夫指了指。

安娜转身。

暗里看不清，可她勉强辨出一片影子，像黑雪的雪崩般冲下山：纳特玛拉。

还在追。"矿井！"安娜说，"快！""那儿不安全！"索伦森说，"塌方和毒气——""还有胡尔德精灵！"安娜说，"艾莎，记得那神话吗！"艾莎倒吸一口气。"'胡尔德精灵总能寻回失物。'阿伦的剑！""那也许是我们唯一的机会！"安娜说，"我们得找到他们，问回旋之刃在哪儿！""可——"索伦森的抗议被一声长嚎切断，那嚎声越拔越高，直到整个王国的空气都成了尖叫，安娜被它的重量压得踉跄。

安娜双手捂耳，冲过警告牌，扯下钉在入口的木板，一头扎进矿口大张的嘴。

朋友们跟着。

嚎声连这儿都追来，克斯托夫在手忙脚乱的行囊里点提灯，可终于他们能看见了。

四周都是通道：细的、宽的、窄的，上上下下，绕来绕去。

可哪条是死路？

哪条通有毒气的洞室，或插着尖棍的坑，或冬眠的熊？

最重要的是，哪条通胡尔德精灵？"走哪条，索伦森？"安娜问。

可老科学家一脸茫然。

他的银长胡子朝四面支棱，像也糊涂了。

安娜身旁的克斯托夫甩了甩提灯，光弧在墙地间荡漾。

岩石里有什么一闪，安娜低头看。

她站在一条又长又金属的东西上：矿车的轨道！"这边！"安娜说，循着轨道撒腿就跑。

一秒后，他们来到一间大洞室，最里头安然坐着一辆木矿车，像早等好了他们。

克斯托夫夸张地示意。"当当！

您的座驾候着了，女士。""哎呀，谢谢您，好心的先生！"安娜爬进去，艾莎和索伦森跟在身后。

克斯托夫推车，想让生锈的轮子往前。

车滚了滚又停了，安娜看见原因。

一根绳子捆在车一头，把它拴在一块突出的巨石上。"可以吗？"她问他，伸手要提灯。

他递给她。"可以。"安娜把提灯火焰凑向绳子。

纳特玛拉的嚎声更响了，响得不可能，隧道都在震。

它到了。

它巨爪的每一步，都让大地一颤。

安娜看得出自己的猜测没错——艾莎每用一次魔法，纳特玛拉就更可怕几分。

它立在洞口，遮了月光，黑沙绕身打转，眼睛黄光闪闪。

安娜手里的绳子焦了——发黑，变细。

终于，它断了。

可车不动。"我们怎么不动？"艾莎叫，"我们太重了，"安娜绝望地转着念头，"也许晃一晃——""不用，"索伦森打断，"什么意思？"安娜急了。

可科学家只一笑——接着纵身跳出车。

他朝矿口——朝纳特玛拉——冲去。"不——！"安娜喊，尽管在纳特玛拉嚎声的海洋里，她听不见自己。

可索伦森得手了。

他一走，车轻了，轮子往前滚，起初慢，然后越来越快——接着车猛地一沉，安娜不得不扔了克斯托夫的提灯。

它砸在车底，可光没灭。

粗木刮着她的手，她死命抓着车边。

车顺着轨道冲，在颠簸的弯和急转里吱叫，每个弯都像要把他们甩出去。"太快了！"艾莎喊，"慢点！""刹车失灵了！"克斯托夫举着提灯伸到前方，回喊，"转向杆卡住了！"安娜惊恐地张嘴，拼命想对策。"往右靠！"克斯托夫吼。

安娜和艾莎把身子往右甩，车在轨上偏移，顺着弯走。

克斯托夫不停喊指令。

就这样——克斯托夫喊，安娜和艾莎左倾右斜——他们能操控车子，之字形滑向山心，而不是直直坠下。

他们总会在某处停下。

不是吗？

忽然，前头有光。

一个出口！"那是什么？"艾莎喊，"离早晨还早！"她没错，安娜的眼睛饮着光，发现那光泛着奇异的碧绿。

她还没来得及多想光从哪来，克斯托夫喊："湖！"哗啦！

在一声温水的炸响里，他们栽进一个地下湖。

车在水波里往前滚，然后停了，出乎意料浅的水结束了这场狂奔。

克斯托夫的提灯灭了，烟袅袅升空气。

安娜让自己静下来。

感受肺里的空气，听地下世界的安静。

可并非全然寂静。

远非如此。

四周是轻柔的泼溅声，石笋滴进映着奇异光的湖里。

安娜低头看水，又惊奇地抬头。

她终于知道光的来处。

洞顶垂着百万只小萤虫，每只都发出淡蓝冰色般的柔光。

它们映在湖面，仿佛他们泡在一个星空下的浴缸里。

这是个由声、水、光组成的隐秘世界，既安抚又辉煌。"大家都没事？"安娜问。

克斯托夫微微龇牙，却还算开朗："嗯！""没事，"艾莎说，"但愿索伦森没事。"安娜也但愿，可她不想让姐姐担心。"他肯定没事，"安娜尽量打起精神，"那科学家袖里藏的把戏，比您日程里的约会还多。"她慢慢站起。"等我们有了剑破除纳特玛拉的诅咒，大家就都好了。"她小心站稳，踮起脚看一只萤虫。"哇，"她轻叹。

每只萤虫像串珠项链，又像冰柱垂着，美得完美。

一阵水声。

安娜看去，艾莎已爬出矿车，走进湖里。

水浅，只到姐姐腰。

她懒得把斗篷拎出水面，任它浮起环绕，几乎像长出一片闪亮的鱼尾。

美人鱼是安娜希望成真的事物。

也许，只是也许，它们是真的。

艾莎蹚到石岸。"你去哪儿？"安娜问。

艾莎停下，抬头望他们刚冲下的陡轨。"我听不见任何声音，"艾莎低声说，像她们又变回小女孩，在礼拜堂玩捉迷藏，等父母来找，"那是好事，对吧？"克斯托夫声音也压低，"纳特玛拉追不上我们。

我们快得不可能，轨道那么多，它分不清我们走哪条。""抬头看，"艾莎阴沉地说。

安娜顺着姐姐的目光。

萤虫的光里，她辨出上方十几条通道，每条都通某处。

通许多某处。

安娜绷紧了。

他们甩掉了纳特玛拉。

他们失去了索伦森。

而现在，他们也迷路了。

sentences.en: AS THE BLACK SAND trickled into the tower room from beneath the door, thoughts, dark and sticky, clung to Anna like oil.
sentences.zh: 黑沙从门缝渗进塔屋，黑暗黏腻的念头像油一样黏在安娜身上。

sentences.en: Thoughts like bugs crawling into ears, teeth rotting and falling out, waves black and drowning, and a door.
sentences.zh: 像虫子爬进耳朵的念头，牙齿腐烂脱落，黑色的浪淹没人，还有一扇门。

sentences.en: A large white door with purple flowers repeating over and over again, each one telling her that she was not good enough, that she was not wanted, that she was shut out.
sentences.zh: 一扇白色大门，紫花一遍遍重复，每朵都在对她说：你不够好，你不受欢迎，你被关在门外。

sentences.en: And as the thoughts hit her, pounding as relentlessly as a stormy sea, Anna felt it hard to breathe.
sentences.zh: 念头一阵阵砸来，像暴风雨的海，安娜觉得喘不过气。

sentences.en: Her heart tightened as if something was pressing on her chest.
sentences.zh: 她的心一紧，像有什么压在胸口。

sentences.en: The weight made it hard to speak, but she must—she had to warn her friends. “Y-you guys,” Anna whispered, trying to get her mouth to work.
sentences.zh: 那重量让她难开口，可她必须——得警告朋友们。"你、你们，"安娜低声说，想让嘴动起来。

sentences.en: But in those few precious seconds, the sand had spilled into the room, forming a dark puddle.
sentences.zh: 可就在这宝贵的几秒，沙已漫进屋，汇成一汪黑水洼。

sentences.en: The grains lifted and swirled into the air, as if each grain had its own pair of miniature wings, its own brain, and then they swarmed, creating the outline of a shadow.
sentences.zh: 沙粒升起、打着旋飞到空中，仿佛每粒都有自己的小翅膀、自己的脑子，接着它们成群结队，勾出一道影子的轮廓。

sentences.en: A wolf’s shadow.
sentences.zh: 一只狼的影子。

sentences.en: Fear gave her strength. “Nattmara!” Anna yelled.
sentences.zh: 恐惧给了她力气。"纳特玛拉！"安娜喊。

sentences.en: The sand solidified into the great white wolf.
sentences.zh: 沙凝成了那只巨大的白狼。

sentences.en: Now the creature was as big as the length of wall.
sentences.zh: 此刻这怪物有一面墙那么长。

sentences.en: Its head practically scraped the painted ceiling.
sentences.zh: 头几乎刮到画着的天花板。

sentences.en: As if in slow motion, Anna saw the others turn.
sentences.zh: 仿佛慢动作，安娜看见其他人转过身。

sentences.en: Kristoff’s mouth dropped open, while Elsa’s eyes widened in horror.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫张大了嘴，艾莎惊恐地瞪圆了眼。

sentences.en: But it was Sorenson—the old scientist who believed in the entanglement of science and myth, myth and science—who reacted first. “Close your eyes!” He bolted up and grabbed for one of the many glass vials near him.
sentences.zh: 可最先反应的，是索伦森——那位相信科学与神话纠缠的老科学家。"闭眼！"他弹起身，抓向身边的某个玻璃瓶。

sentences.en: Anna shut her eyes.
sentences.zh: 安娜闭了眼。

sentences.en: A second later, there was a bright flash even through her closed eyelids, followed by the yelp of the wolf.
sentences.zh: 一秒后，即便闭着眼，也有一道强光闪过，接着是狼的一声嚎叫。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Not a wolf , Anna corrected herself.
sentences.zh: 不是狼，安娜纠正自己。

sentences.en: Nattmara. “Upstairs!” Sorenson yelled. “Run!” And even though she had closed her eyes to the flash, black dots still spotted her vision as she stood and ran with Kristoff toward the steps.
sentences.zh: 是纳特玛拉。"楼上！"索伦森喊，"跑！"尽管她为那光闭了眼，黑点仍斑斑点点缀在视野里，她站起，和克斯托夫朝楼梯跑去。

sentences.en: Taking them two at a time, she was aware of screaming and a noise that sounded like sharpening knives.
sentences.zh: 他们一步两级，她听见尖叫和像磨刀的声音。

sentences.en: Glancing backward, she saw Sorenson at the bottom of the stairs, and beside him, Elsa, shooting ice javelins at the wolf again and again and again.
sentences.zh: 回头一瞥，她看见索伦森在楼梯底，他身旁艾莎一遍遍射出冰矛，刺向狼。

sentences.en: But the ice javelins, sharp and lethal, seemed to do as much harm as a toothpick plunged into water.
sentences.zh: 可那些冰矛，又尖又致命，造成的伤害却像把牙签插进水里。

sentences.en: Each time Elsa let loose an ice javelin, it soared through the air toward its target—but it never hit its target.
sentences.zh: 艾莎每放一支冰矛，它便飞向目标——可从不命中。

sentences.en: The Nattmara didn’t seem to be made of fur or bone or muscle.
sentences.zh: 纳特玛拉似乎不是由毛、骨或肉组成。

sentences.en: Or anything solid, really.
sentences.zh: 也不是任何实在的东西。

sentences.en: Because as ice javelins were about to pin its paws down in place, the wolf’s paws dissolved at their touch, shifting and morphing its shape like— like sand , Anna realized.
sentences.zh: 因为冰矛快钉住它的爪时，狼爪一碰就化开，像沙一样变形——安娜意识到，像沙。

sentences.en: It was as Sorenson had said.
sentences.zh: 正如索伦森所说。

sentences.en: The Nattmara could take any form.
sentences.zh: 纳特玛拉能化成任何形。

sentences.en: Seep through the cracks in any door.
sentences.zh: 从任何门缝渗过。

sentences.en: Slip into the fragile spots of a person’s heart.
sentences.zh: 钻进人心最脆弱的缝。

sentences.en: It fed on fear, but how could they not be afraid of it?
sentences.zh: 它以恐惧为食，可他们怎能不怕它？

sentences.en: It was fear.
sentences.zh: 它就是恐惧。

sentences.en: A bit of black sand floated toward Anna, and her breath caught again.
sentences.zh: 一点黑沙飘向安娜，她又屏住呼吸。

sentences.en: The sticky thoughts rushed back into her mind: She’d done this.
sentences.zh: 黏腻的念头涌回脑中：是她干的。

sentences.en: She couldn’t do anything right.
sentences.zh: 她什么都对不了。

sentences.en: She never could.
sentences.zh: 她从来不行。

sentences.en: She’d failed Elsa. “ANNA!” Kristoff, his traveler’s pack dangling from his shoulder, pulled her arm. “KEEP GOING!” The sound of his voice—full of worry and care—snapped Anna back into herself.
sentences.zh: 她让艾莎失望了。"安娜！"克斯托夫行囊挂在肩头，拽着她的胳膊，"继续走！"他声音里的担忧与关切，把安娜猛地唤回自己。

sentences.en: She ran with him, and didn’t stop racing up the dizzying, tight spiral of steps until she exploded out into the cold, open air of Sorenson’s observation deck.
sentences.zh: 她跟着他跑，一口气冲上那令人眩晕的紧螺旋阶梯，直到冲进索伦森观测台寒冷开阔的空中。

sentences.en: Any other time, she knew she would have loved to stay up there.
sentences.zh: 换作别时，她知道自己会愿意待在上头。

sentences.en: The mountain air was so clear that the stars above pulsed bright.
sentences.zh: 山间空气清冽，头顶的星星亮得直跳。

sentences.en: The moon overhead was round and ripe, just begging to be plucked from the sky and put into her pocket as a sweet treat for later.
sentences.zh: 头顶的圆月又圆又熟，简直让人想从天上摘下，塞进口袋，当块甜点留着以后吃。

sentences.en: And in the center of the circular deck, standing like a newborn colt on spindly legs, gleamed a copper telescope.
sentences.zh: 圆形平台中央，立着一架铜望远镜，像初生的小马驹，细腿打着晃，闪闪发亮。

sentences.en: It pointed to the heavens, an instrument that helped seek answers in the celestial dance.
sentences.zh: 它指向苍穹，是台帮人在天体之舞里寻答案的仪器。

sentences.en: It was all strange, fascinating, and beautiful.
sentences.zh: 一切陌生、迷人又美丽。

sentences.en: And a dead end.
sentences.zh: 却是个死胡同。

sentences.en: Just like in Anna’s nightmare, there was no place to run.
sentences.zh: 正如安娜的噩梦，无路可逃。

sentences.en: The wolf, still behind them on the tower stairs, had cornered her, this time on a wooden deck, hundreds of feet in the air, and the only means of escape—jumping—definitely didn’t bode well for any of them.
sentences.zh: 狼还在身后塔梯上，把她逼到了死角——这次是在木台上，离地几百尺，唯一的出路——跳——对他们谁都没好处。

sentences.en: They were trapped!
sentences.zh: 他们被困住了！

sentences.en: Sorenson’s shoulder collided with hers as he shot past her to the edge of the deck.
sentences.zh: 索伦森的肩撞上她，他从她身边冲到台边。

sentences.en: Leaning over the simple wooden railing, he grasped at the night air and then pulled back.
sentences.zh: 他探身越过简朴的木栏，抓住夜里的空气，又缩回手。

sentences.en: In the light of the full moon, Anna could make out the silver glint of something in his palm: a wire cable—one so thin it seemed to vanish only a foot away from the tower. “Grab the tablecloth!” He gestured to the long wooden workbench that stood next to the telescope.
sentences.zh: 满月的光里，安娜辨出他掌心一点银光：一根钢丝缆——细得离塔一尺就似乎消失。"抓住桌布！"他指向望远镜旁那张长木工作台。

sentences.en: It was covered in beakers, thermometers and barometers, pencils and quills, abacuses, rulers, flasks, and pages of calculations.
sentences.zh: 台上满是烧杯、温度计、气压计、铅笔鹅毛笔、算盘、尺子、长颈瓶，还有一页页演算。

sentences.en: And seemingly all of Sorenson’s life’s work sat on a little lavender tablecloth neatly embroidered with a crocus.
sentences.zh: 索伦森毕生的心血，似乎都摆在一条绣着番红花的淡紫小桌布上。

sentences.en: If the tablecloth were pulled, all of that work—years and years of it—would smash onto the deck, lost forever.
sentences.zh: 若扯了桌布，那些心血——积年累月的——会砸在台上，永远丢失。

sentences.en: Anna hesitated. “Do it!” Sorenson roared at her.
sentences.zh: 安娜犹豫了。"动手！"索伦森冲她吼。

sentences.en: But Anna couldn’t, she just couldn’t.
sentences.zh: 可安娜做不到，她就是做不到。

sentences.en: It was a table of answers, the work of a lifetime of gathering information.
sentences.zh: 那是一桌答案，是一生搜集信息的成果。

sentences.en: So Kristoff reached behind her and tugged the tablecloth free.
sentences.zh: 于是克斯托夫伸手到她身后，把桌布抽了出来。

sentences.en: With a tremendous clash, the beautiful and strange devices fell to the floor, the sound something similar to the breaking of a heart. “Now tear the cloth!” Sorenson commanded.
sentences.zh: 随着一声巨响，那些美丽奇异的器具摔在地上，声音像心碎。"现在把布撕了！"索伦森命令。

sentences.en: The sound of the wolf’s vicious barks and the scrape of ice filled the air.
sentences.zh: 狼凶狠的吠叫和冰的刮擦声充斥空气。

sentences.en: Elsa had made it to the observation deck and stood at the entrance, flinging her hand out again and again and again.
sentences.zh: 艾莎已上到观测台，站在入口，一遍遍甩手。

sentences.en: With each flick of her wrist, the doorway filled to the brim with ice—fresh ice, new ice, ice without cracks.
sentences.zh: 每弹一下腕，门口就填满冰——新冰，刚结的冰，没有裂缝的冰。

sentences.en: For a moment, anyway.
sentences.zh: 反正就那一会儿。

sentences.en: Because then the Nattmara would slam itself against it, sending cracks scattering across the surface, and a little more black sand wisped through the cracks each time.
sentences.zh: 因为接着纳特玛拉会撞上去，裂纹便爬满表面，每次都有更多黑沙从缝里钻过。

sentences.en: Smooth ice.
sentences.zh: 平滑的冰。

sentences.en: Shattered ice.
sentences.zh: 碎裂的冰。

sentences.en: Smooth.
sentences.zh: 平滑。

sentences.en: Shattered.
sentences.zh: 碎裂。

sentences.en: Elsa was holding the Nattmara and its sandy paws at bay, but even Elsa—brave, strong, wise, magical Elsa—couldn’t keep at it forever.
sentences.zh: 艾莎挡着纳特玛拉和它的沙爪，可就连艾莎——勇敢、强壮、睿智、有魔法的艾莎——也撑不了永远。

sentences.en: Already, Anna could see the weariness in the slope of her shoulders.
sentences.zh: 安娜已能看见她肩头塌下的疲惫。

sentences.en: The snap of her wrist grew looser with each deft gesture.
sentences.zh: 她弹腕的力道一次比一次松。

sentences.en: Riiiiiiip!
sentences.zh: 哧啦——！

sentences.en: Anna turned to see Kristoff obeying Sorenson’s orders and tearing the tablecloth into thick strips, but Anna didn’t offer to help.
sentences.zh: 安娜转头，看见克斯托夫正听索伦森的命令，把桌布撕成宽条，可安娜没去帮忙。

sentences.en: Instead, her mind had become preoccupied by something else.
sentences.zh: 她的心被别的事占了。

sentences.en: Each time Elsa flung out her wrist and filled the doorway with ice, Anna thought the Nattmara grew a little bigger.
sentences.zh: 每次艾莎甩腕、用冰填满门口，安娜都觉得纳特玛拉大了些。

sentences.en: Smooth ice.
sentences.zh: 平滑的冰。

sentences.en: Shattered ice.
sentences.zh: 碎裂的冰。

sentences.en: Smooth ice.
sentences.zh: 平滑的冰。

sentences.en: Yes, Anna was sure of it now.
sentences.zh: 是的，安娜现在确定了。

sentences.en: Whenever Elsa shot a magical blast of ice at the creature of myth, its paws expanded, its teeth sharpened, and its strength doubled. “Elsa!” Anna cried. “Elsa, stop!
sentences.zh: 每当艾莎朝这神话之兽射出魔法冰，它的爪就扩张，牙就磨尖，力气翻倍。"艾莎！"安娜喊，"艾莎，停下！

sentences.en: Your magic!
sentences.zh: 你的魔法！

sentences.en: It’s making it stronger!” But between the snarling of the Nattmara, the tearing of the cloth, and the sound of ice cracking again and again and again, Elsa couldn’t hear her.
sentences.zh: 它在让它更强！"可在纳特玛拉的咆哮、扯布的声响、冰一遍遍碎裂里，艾莎听不见。

sentences.en: Their only way of surviving in this moment would be if they escaped. “Hurry!” Sorenson cried. “Take some!” Anna took a bit of tablecloth from Kristoff and stumbled toward the scientist.
sentences.zh: 此刻他们唯一的生路是逃。"快！"索伦森喊，"拿一些！"安娜从克斯托夫手里接过一段桌布，踉跄走向科学家。

sentences.en: Grabbing the strip, Sorenson looped the cloth over the thin wire, making a U with the fabric. “Hands,” he grunted.
sentences.zh: 索伦森抓住布条，在细钢丝上绕了个U形。"手，"他哼道。

sentences.en: Anna obliged, holding out her wrists as he tied the dangling ends of the cloth strip under Anna’s armpits to create a makeshift harness.
sentences.zh: 安娜照做，伸出手腕，他把布条垂下的两端在安娜腋下打了个简易吊带。

sentences.en: Sorenson patted the rickety wooden railing. “Climb up.” Anna did as she was told.
sentences.zh: 索伦森拍拍摇摇欲坠的木栏。"爬上去。"安娜照做。

sentences.en: Only when she was balanced on the topmost rail, facing the mountain slope far beneath her, did Sorenson’s plan truly sink in. “Wait a second,” Anna said, twisting to face him. “You can’t be serious.” “Hang on tight!” Sorenson pushed her—hard.
sentences.zh: 直到她稳在最高一根栏杆上，面朝脚下远处的山坡，索伦森的打算才真正明白。"等一下，"安娜扭身面对他，"你不是认真的。""抓稳了！"索伦森使劲一推。

sentences.en: With a squeal, Anna slipped off the observation deck in a rush of wind and stars.
sentences.zh: 安娜一声尖叫，在风与星中冲下观测台。

sentences.en: She screamed.
sentences.zh: 她喊。

sentences.en: Careening down the mountain nearly felt like flying, but definitely felt like falling.
sentences.zh: 顺着山几乎像飞，但绝对像掉。

sentences.en: The cable jounced and jiggled as she sped down the mountainside.
sentences.zh: 缆绳在她速降时一弹一跳。

sentences.en: Wrapping her wrists in the tablecloth, she held on for dear life as her legs swung beneath her.
sentences.zh: 她把桌布缠在腕上，死命抓着，腿在身下晃荡。

sentences.en: From somewhere above, she could hear Elsa and Kristoff and Sorenson shouting as they zipped down behind her.
sentences.zh: 头顶某处，她听见艾莎、克斯托夫和索伦森在她身后嗖嗖滑下的喊声。

sentences.en: Thank goodness they were safe!
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地他们安全！

sentences.en: Anna almost laughed—but the ground was rushing toward her, and coming up way too fast.
sentences.zh: 安娜几乎笑出来——可地面正朝她冲来，快得过头。

sentences.en: Straining her eyes against the dark night, Anna followed the path of the rippling cable; it disappeared into the branches of a tree at the foot of the mountain, near the entrance to the mines.
sentences.zh: 她眯眼对抗黑夜，顺着起伏缆绳的去向看；它在山脚一棵树杈里消失，靠近矿井入口。

sentences.en: That much was good.
sentences.zh: 这点好。

sentences.en: But what wasn’t good was how fast she was approaching the very solid trunk.
sentences.zh: 可不好的是她冲向那结实的树干有多快。

sentences.en: If she hit the tree at this pace, she would definitely break a few ribs, and that was if she was lucky.
sentences.zh: 这速度撞上树，准断几根肋骨，算她走运。

sentences.en: She needed to slow down. “SNOW!” she yelled back at Elsa. “SNOW!
sentences.zh: 她得慢下来。"雪！"她回头朝艾莎喊，"雪！

sentences.en: SNOW SNOW SNOW!” She thought she heard Elsa shout back, but Anna couldn’t tell.
sentences.zh: 雪雪雪雪！"她好像听见艾莎回喊，可安娜分不清。

sentences.en: The wind stole whatever words left her sister’s lips.
sentences.zh: 风夺走了姐姐唇边任何的话。

sentences.en: She just had to hope and trust that her sister would know what to do, the way she always did.
sentences.zh: 她只能盼望并相信姐姐知道怎么做，像她一向那样。

sentences.en: Ten feet away from the tree.
sentences.zh: 离树十尺。

sentences.en: Now five.
sentences.zh: 现在五尺。

sentences.en: Now two.
sentences.zh: 现在两尺。

sentences.en: Anna released the tablecloth and set herself free.
sentences.zh: 安娜松开桌布，让自己自由。

sentences.en: She tumbled through the dark air for what felt like a year but was likely only a moment, and then— WOMP!
sentences.zh: 她在黑空气里翻滚，像过了一年，其实不过一瞬，接着——噗！

sentences.en: A cold tingle enveloped Anna, as refreshing and comforting as one of the bubbly drinks Oaken sold at his lodge.
sentences.zh: 一阵冰凉的刺痒裹住安娜，像奥肯客栈卖的那种冒泡饮料一样清新舒坦。

sentences.en: Soft, pillowy snowflakes had cushioned her fall.
sentences.zh: 柔软蓬松的雪花 cushion 了她的坠落。

sentences.en: Elsa had done it again.
sentences.zh: 艾莎又做到了。

sentences.en: But there was no time to catch her breath.
sentences.zh: 可没时间喘气。

sentences.en: Instead, Anna rolled out of the way as Elsa, Kristoff, and Sorenson plopped into the snow pile like ripe apples falling from a tree.
sentences.zh: 安娜滚开，艾莎、克斯托夫和索伦森像熟透的苹果从树上掉进雪堆。

sentences.en: Anna shot up. “Everyone okay?
sentences.zh: 安娜跳起。"大家都没事？

sentences.en: Where is it?” Everyone nodded, then Kristoff pointed.
sentences.zh: 它在哪儿？"众人点头，克斯托夫指了指。

sentences.en: Anna turned.
sentences.zh: 安娜转身。

sentences.en: It was hard to see in the dark, but she could just make out a patch of shadow barreling down the mountain like an avalanche of black snow: the Nattmara.
sentences.zh: 暗里看不清，可她勉强辨出一片影子，像黑雪的雪崩般冲下山：纳特玛拉。

sentences.en: Still on the hunt. “The mines!” Anna said. “Hurry!” “They’re not safe!” Sorenson said. “Cave-ins and toxic air—” “And Huldrefólk!” Anna said. “Elsa, remember the myth!” Elsa gasped. “‘ Huldrefólk always find that which is lost .’ Aren’s sword!” “It may be our only chance!” Anna said. “We have to find them and ask where the Revolute Blade is!” “But—” Sorenson’s protest was cut off by a long howl, a howl that rose in pitch until the very air of the kingdom became a scream, and Anna staggered under its weight.
sentences.zh: 还在追。"矿井！"安娜说，"快！""那儿不安全！"索伦森说，"塌方和毒气——""还有胡尔德精灵！"安娜说，"艾莎，记得那神话吗！"艾莎倒吸一口气。"'胡尔德精灵总能寻回失物。'阿伦的剑！""那也许是我们唯一的机会！"安娜说，"我们得找到他们，问回旋之刃在哪儿！""可——"索伦森的抗议被一声长嚎切断，那嚎声越拔越高，直到整个王国的空气都成了尖叫，安娜被它的重量压得踉跄。

sentences.en: Clasping her hands over her ears, Anna ran past the warning posts, ripped back the wooden boards that had been nailed up over the entrance, and dove into the gaping mouth of the mines.
sentences.zh: 安娜双手捂耳，冲过警告牌，扯下钉在入口的木板，一头扎进矿口大张的嘴。

sentences.en: Her friends followed her.
sentences.zh: 朋友们跟着。

sentences.en: The howl reached them even there, and Kristoff struggled with his traveler’s pack to light his lantern, but at last they could see.
sentences.zh: 嚎声连这儿都追来，克斯托夫在手忙脚乱的行囊里点提灯，可终于他们能看见了。

sentences.en: All around, there were passages: thin ones, wide ones, narrow ones, up and down and around.
sentences.zh: 四周都是通道：细的、宽的、窄的，上上下下，绕来绕去。

sentences.en: But which led to a dead end?
sentences.zh: 可哪条是死路？

sentences.en: And which led to chambers of poisonous gases or pits with sharp sticks or sleeping bears?
sentences.zh: 哪条通有毒气的洞室，或插着尖棍的坑，或冬眠的熊？

sentences.en: Most importantly, which would take them to the Huldrefólk? “Which one, Sorenson?” Anna asked.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，哪条通胡尔德精灵？"走哪条，索伦森？"安娜问。

sentences.en: But the old scientist looked perplexed.
sentences.zh: 可老科学家一脸茫然。

sentences.en: His long silver beard tufted in all directions, as if it, too, were confused.
sentences.zh: 他的银长胡子朝四面支棱，像也糊涂了。

sentences.en: Standing beside Anna, Kristoff swung his lantern, sending arcs of light rippling across the walls and floor.
sentences.zh: 安娜身旁的克斯托夫甩了甩提灯，光弧在墙地间荡漾。

sentences.en: Something glinted in the rock, and Anna looked down.
sentences.zh: 岩石里有什么一闪，安娜低头看。

sentences.en: She was standing on something long and metal: the tracks for mine carts! “This way!” Anna said, taking off in a sprint as she followed the tracks.
sentences.zh: 她站在一条又长又金属的东西上：矿车的轨道！"这边！"安娜说，循着轨道撒腿就跑。

sentences.en: A second later, they arrived in a large chamber where, at the far end, sitting comfortably as if it had been waiting for them all along, was a wooden mine cart.
sentences.zh: 一秒后，他们来到一间大洞室，最里头安然坐着一辆木矿车，像早等好了他们。

sentences.en: Kristoff gestured to it theatrically. “Ta-da!
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫夸张地示意。"当当！

sentences.en: Your chariot awaits, m’lady.” “Why, thank you, kind sir!” Anna clambered in, with Elsa and Sorenson climbing in behind her.
sentences.zh: 您的座驾候着了，女士。""哎呀，谢谢您，好心的先生！"安娜爬进去，艾莎和索伦森跟在身后。

sentences.en: Kristoff pushed the cart, trying to get the rusty wheels to move forward.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫推车，想让生锈的轮子往前。

sentences.en: They rolled a bit then stopped, and Anna saw why.
sentences.zh: 车滚了滚又停了，安娜看见原因。

sentences.en: A rope had been tied around one end of the cart, anchoring it to a jutting boulder. “May I?” she asked him, reaching for his lantern.
sentences.zh: 一根绳子捆在车一头，把它拴在一块突出的巨石上。"可以吗？"她问他，伸手要提灯。

sentences.en: He handed it to her. “You may.” Anna held the lantern’s flame to the rope.
sentences.zh: 他递给她。"可以。"安娜把提灯火焰凑向绳子。

sentences.en: The Nattmara’s howl was even louder now, impossibly so, and the tunnel shook.
sentences.zh: 纳特玛拉的嚎声更响了，响得不可能，隧道都在震。

sentences.en: It had arrived.
sentences.zh: 它到了。

sentences.en: Each step of its giant paws sent a tremor through the earth.
sentences.zh: 它巨爪的每一步，都让大地一颤。

sentences.en: And Anna could see that her guess had been right—each time Elsa used her magic, the Nattmara seemed to have grown more fearsome and more horrible.
sentences.zh: 安娜看得出自己的猜测没错——艾莎每用一次魔法，纳特玛拉就更可怕几分。

sentences.en: It stood in the mouth of the cave, eclipsing the light of the moon, black sand sweeping around it as its eyes shone yellow.
sentences.zh: 它立在洞口，遮了月光，黑沙绕身打转，眼睛黄光闪闪。

sentences.en: In Anna’s hands, the rope charred—blackening, thinning.
sentences.zh: 安娜手里的绳子焦了——发黑，变细。

sentences.en: Finally, it snapped.
sentences.zh: 终于，它断了。

sentences.en: But the cart stayed put. “Why aren’t we moving?” Elsa cried out. “We’re too heavy for it,” Anna said, desperation whirling through her. “Maybe if we rock a bit—” “No need,” Sorenson interrupted. “What do you mean?” Anna demanded.
sentences.zh: 可车不动。"我们怎么不动？"艾莎叫，"我们太重了，"安娜绝望地转着念头，"也许晃一晃——""不用，"索伦森打断，"什么意思？"安娜急了。

sentences.en: But the scientist only smiled—and then launched himself out of the cart.
sentences.zh: 可科学家只一笑——接着纵身跳出车。

sentences.en: He sprinted toward the mouth of the mines…toward the Nattmara. “Noooooo!” Anna yelled, though she couldn’t hear herself in the ocean of the Nattmara’s howl.
sentences.zh: 他朝矿口——朝纳特玛拉——冲去。"不——！"安娜喊，尽管在纳特玛拉嚎声的海洋里，她听不见自己。

sentences.en: But Sorenson had done the trick.
sentences.zh: 可索伦森得手了。

sentences.en: With his weight gone, the cart rose and the wheels rolled forward, slow at first, then faster and faster—and then the cart plunged, forcing Anna to drop Kristoff’s lantern.
sentences.zh: 他一走，车轻了，轮子往前滚，起初慢，然后越来越快——接着车猛地一沉，安娜不得不扔了克斯托夫的提灯。

sentences.en: It crashed to the floor of the cart, but the light didn’t snuff out.
sentences.zh: 它砸在车底，可光没灭。

sentences.en: Rough wood cut into her hands as she clung to the sides of the cart for dear life.
sentences.zh: 粗木刮着她的手，她死命抓着车边。

sentences.en: It barreled down the tracks, screeching through jolting turns and sharp twists, threatening to buck them out at every turn. “We’re going too fast!” Elsa shouted. “Slow down!” “The brakes aren’t working!” Kristoff yelled back as he retrieved his lantern and held it out in front of them. “And the steering stick is stuck!” Anna felt her mouth open in horror as she frantically tried to think of a solution. “Lean right!” Kristoff bellowed.
sentences.zh: 车顺着轨道冲，在颠簸的弯和急转里吱叫，每个弯都像要把他们甩出去。"太快了！"艾莎喊，"慢点！""刹车失灵了！"克斯托夫举着提灯伸到前方，回喊，"转向杆卡住了！"安娜惊恐地张嘴，拼命想对策。"往右靠！"克斯托夫吼。

sentences.en: Anna and Elsa flung their weight to the right, and the cart shifted on the track, following the curve of the rail.
sentences.zh: 安娜和艾莎把身子往右甩，车在轨上偏移，顺着弯走。

sentences.en: Kristoff continued to yell instructions.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫不停喊指令。

sentences.en: In this way—with Kristoff calling out and Anna and Elsa leaning this way and that—they were able to direct the cart, zigzagging down into the mountain’s core instead of dropping vertically.
sentences.zh: 就这样——克斯托夫喊，安娜和艾莎左倾右斜——他们能操控车子，之字形滑向山心，而不是直直坠下。

sentences.en: They would roll to a stop at some point.
sentences.zh: 他们总会在某处停下。

sentences.en: Wouldn’t they?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: And then, suddenly, there was light up ahead.
sentences.zh: 忽然，前头有光。

sentences.en: An exit! “What is that?” Elsa shouted. “We’re nowhere near morning!” She was right, and as Anna’s eyes drank in the light, she realized it held a strange aqua glow.
sentences.zh: 一个出口！"那是什么？"艾莎喊，"离早晨还早！"她没错，安娜的眼睛饮着光，发现那光泛着奇异的碧绿。

sentences.en: Before she could wonder too much where it came from, Kristoff yelled, “LAKE!” SPLASH!
sentences.zh: 她还没来得及多想光从哪来，克斯托夫喊："湖！"哗啦！

sentences.en: In an explosion of lukewarm water, they careened into an underground lake.
sentences.zh: 在一声温水的炸响里，他们栽进一个地下湖。

sentences.en: The cart rolled forward in the rippling water, then stopped, the surprisingly shallow body of water bringing their wild ride to an end.
sentences.zh: 车在水波里往前滚，然后停了，出乎意料浅的水结束了这场狂奔。

sentences.en: Kristoff’s lantern went out, smoke snaking off into the air.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫的提灯灭了，烟袅袅升空气。

sentences.en: Anna allowed herself to be still.
sentences.zh: 安娜让自己静下来。

sentences.en: To feel the air in her lungs and hear the quiet of the subterranean world.
sentences.zh: 感受肺里的空气，听地下世界的安静。

sentences.en: But it wasn’t utter silence.
sentences.zh: 可并非全然寂静。

sentences.en: Far from it.
sentences.zh: 远非如此。

sentences.en: All around them was a soft splish-splash as stalactites dripped water into the reflective lake that was illuminated by the strange light.
sentences.zh: 四周是轻柔的泼溅声，石笋滴进映着奇异光的湖里。

sentences.en: Anna looked down at the water and then up in wonder.
sentences.zh: 安娜低头看水，又惊奇地抬头。

sentences.en: She finally knew the source of the light.
sentences.zh: 她终于知道光的来处。

sentences.en: Dangling from the cave ceiling were a million tiny glowworms, each one giving off a gentle light the color of the bluest ice.
sentences.zh: 洞顶垂着百万只小萤虫，每只都发出淡蓝冰色般的柔光。

sentences.en: They reflected onto the surface of the lake so that it looked they were in a bathtub under a galaxy of stars.
sentences.zh: 它们映在湖面，仿佛他们泡在一个星空下的浴缸里。

sentences.en: It was a secret world of sound and water and light, both comforting and glorious. “Is everyone okay?” Anna asked.
sentences.zh: 这是个由声、水、光组成的隐秘世界，既安抚又辉煌。"大家都没事？"安娜问。

sentences.en: Kristoff winced slightly, but said, more or less cheerfully, “Yep!” “Yes,” Elsa said. “I hope Sorenson is okay.” Anna hoped so, too, but she didn’t want her sister to worry. “I’m sure he’s fine,” Anna said, mustering as much enthusiasm as she could. “That scientist has more tricks up his sleeves than appointments in your schedule.” She stood up slowly. “And everyone will be okay once we have the sword to break the Nattmara’s curse.” Careful to keep her balance, she rose to her tiptoes and examined a glowworm. “Wow,” she breathed out.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫微微龇牙，却还算开朗："嗯！""没事，"艾莎说，"但愿索伦森没事。"安娜也但愿，可她不想让姐姐担心。"他肯定没事，"安娜尽量打起精神，"那科学家袖里藏的把戏，比您日程里的约会还多。"她慢慢站起。"等我们有了剑破除纳特玛拉的诅咒，大家就都好了。"她小心站稳，踮起脚看一只萤虫。"哇，"她轻叹。

sentences.en: Each glowworm looked like a beaded necklace and hung like an icicle, beautiful and perfect.
sentences.zh: 每只萤虫像串珠项链，又像冰柱垂着，美得完美。

sentences.en: There was the sound of swirling water.
sentences.zh: 一阵水声。

sentences.en: Anna looked over to see that Elsa had clambered out of the mine cart and stepped into the lake.
sentences.zh: 安娜看去，艾莎已爬出矿车，走进湖里。

sentences.en: It was shallow, only coming up to her sister’s waist.
sentences.zh: 水浅，只到姐姐腰。

sentences.en: She didn’t bother to lift her cloak out of the water, but instead let it float up around her, so that it almost looked like she’d grown a twinkling mermaid’s fin.
sentences.zh: 她懒得把斗篷拎出水面，任它浮起环绕，几乎像长出一片闪亮的鱼尾。

sentences.en: Now mermaids were something Anna wished were real.
sentences.zh: 美人鱼是安娜希望成真的事物。

sentences.en: And maybe, just maybe, they were.
sentences.zh: 也许，只是也许，它们是真的。

sentences.en: Elsa waded to the rocky banks. “Where are you going?” Anna asked.
sentences.zh: 艾莎蹚到石岸。"你去哪儿？"安娜问。

sentences.en: Elsa stopped to look up at the steep track they had careened down only moments before. “I can’t hear anything,” Elsa whispered, as though they were little girls again playing hide-and-find in the chapel and waiting for their parents to discover them. “That’s good, right?” Kristoff’s voice was hushed. “The Nattmara couldn’t have followed us.
sentences.zh: 艾莎停下，抬头望他们刚冲下的陡轨。"我听不见任何声音，"艾莎低声说，像她们又变回小女孩，在礼拜堂玩捉迷藏，等父母来找，"那是好事，对吧？"克斯托夫声音也压低，"纳特玛拉追不上我们。

sentences.en: We were going impossibly fast, and there were too many tracks for it to know which ones we chose.” “Look up,” Elsa said grimly.
sentences.zh: 我们快得不可能，轨道那么多，它分不清我们走哪条。""抬头看，"艾莎阴沉地说。

sentences.en: Anna followed her sister’s gaze.
sentences.zh: 安娜顺着姐姐的目光。

sentences.en: In the glowworms’ light, she could make out a dozen different passages above them, each one leading to somewhere.
sentences.zh: 萤虫的光里，她辨出上方十几条通道，每条都通某处。

sentences.en: To many somewheres.
sentences.zh: 通许多某处。

sentences.en: Anna tensed.
sentences.zh: 安娜绷紧了。

sentences.en: They had lost the Nattmara.
sentences.zh: 他们甩掉了纳特玛拉。

sentences.en: They had lost Sorenson.
sentences.zh: 他们失去了索伦森。

sentences.en: And now they were lost, too.
sentences.zh: 而现在，他们也迷路了。

chapters.title: Chapter Sixteen
chapters.en:
ANNA, ELSA, AND KRISTOFF couldn’t stay in the cave of crystal-clear water and glowworm light forever.

Because now, even the quiet was dangerous.

It had been nearly twenty-four hours since Anna had last slept, and judging from the dark bags under Elsa’s eyes, it had even been even longer for her. But it was Kristoff who was suffering from exhaustion the most. Looking for his troll family, he’d already done a hard day’s ride before arriving back at the castle, only to flee. He had been awake for too long. He needed sleep. They all did.

But if they slept, it might make it easier for the Nattmara to track them—and Anna knew it wouldn’t give up. That was the nature of a nightmare—one second, they were forgotten, and the next, they exploded into sharp memory. Anna, Elsa, and Kristoff had to keep moving through the mines. They had to keep their feet shuffling forward, their eyes open. If one of them slept, it could be the end of them all. They had so many people to save.

And so, after gathering strands of glowworms to hang around their necks and wrists, they decided on a tunnel—not because it was familiar, but because it seemed to go more up than the others. Using the skills he’d learned on the mountain, Kristoff had been able to help them all scale the wall with his rope to reach the highest passageway.

As they trudged forward, Anna tried to think about energizing things: sunrises, sledding, playing with the children in town, Olaf. But instead of making her feel excited and awake, they only made her feel sad and even more tired. She wondered if she would ever feel awake again. Kristoff stumbled beside her. Instead of catching himself as he normally would, he dropped to his knees and sank back onto his heels.

Anna stooped beside him and rested a hand on his back. “Are you okay, Kristoff? You have to get up!” She nudged him.

Kristoff mumbled in reply and laid his head on the ground. “This rock is so soft.”

Anna pulled on his arm, but instead of yanking him to his feet, she only succeeded in making herself more tired, and she, too, sank to the ground.

Kristoff was right. The rock was soft and still and it wanted her to lay her head down on it. It was warm, and from the depths of her sleep-addled mind, Anna remembered a lesson Gerda had taught her, about how the earth was a crust of dirt floating on top of hot magma, and that sometimes, little pockets of heat would spring warm water from the rocks underneath. Even though these carved tunnels within the mines had never seen the sun, they felt like a touch of summer—of lying on rocky beaches kissed by the sun. All Anna wanted to do was to stretch out her tired muscles and sleep there. Anna! From a long way away, she heard someone calling her name. Anna, get up!

“Just a few more minutes,” Anna mumbled.

A slap of cold air hit her. Anna jolted upright. “Hey!” She wiped away what seemed to be the remnants of a snowball from her cheek.

“What was that for?” Kristoff protested, snow also flecking his face.

“I’m saving your lives,” Elsa said. She conjured another snowball, which she juggled. “On your feet, or it’s more ice in your face. We have a deal?”

“Blargh!” Kristoff sputtered. “Just let us sleep!”

“Sorry, but I can’t do that.” Elsa shook head. “Anna! Oh, for goodness’ sake.”

Anna felt another slap of cold snow and jerked her head up. “Sorry, sorry,” she mumbled, her tongue feeling too thick for her mouth. Snow glistened at Elsa’s fingertips, and something niggled at Anna’s mind. It was something important. It had something to do with Elsa and her magic. But what was it?

As Elsa wound her arm, ready to pitch another snowball at either one of them, Anna remembered. She shot up tall and nearly jumped.

“Elsa, stop!”

Her sister dropped her snowball to the ground, where it landed with a small puff. “You promise to stay awake now? Because there’s more snow where that came from.”

But Anna was no longer sleepy. Far from it. “You can’t keep using your magic,” she said. “On the observation deck, I noticed that every time you did, the Nattmara grew.”

“Oh.” Elsa folded her arms across her chest. “Great.”

Anna rooted around in Kristoff’s pack and pulled out the book, flipping open its pages to confirm her theory. But they were soaked through from the lake, the ink indecipherable. She sighed.

SNORFFF!

The sisters looked down to see Kristoff’s eyes had closed again, a strangled snore escaping from him as his head drifted toward his chest.

“What are we going to do about him?” Elsa asked.

“Umm.” Anna cast about for an idea—any idea. Usually, they came sharp and sure, but lack of sleep was making her feel fuzzy. All she could really focus on were their shadows thrown by the glowworms onto the cave wall opposite them. Shadows. Shadows similar to the famous shadow puppets of Zaria. She’d read how the puppeteers were often as famous as singers, and could fill whole theaters with their performances. If they could ever defeat the Nattmara and make everything right again, maybe she would invite some of the puppeteers to come give a performance in Arendelle. Everyone had liked it so much last year when Kristoff had performed his musical….

“That’s it!” Anna shouted. That’s it, it, it. Her words echoed down the rocky corridor. Crouching down to be at the same level as Kristoff’s fluttering eyelashes, she began to sing: “‘Goblin toes are ugly, and Hulder tails are sweet—but you would never catch me, sweep one off his’…paw!”

It was a silly song that Kristoff had made up for the last spring festival. The children in the village had loved it, and had performed it for the kingdom under Kristoff’s encouraging eye. When Anna had first met the mountain man, he’d been snow-crusted and only grunted a few words to her. She never would have thought that underneath the rough exterior, and a dirt patch or two, his real language was song.

Kristoff had a gift for melody, and though he didn’t mind the odd soup stain on his shirt and didn’t care about the difference between a salad fork and a dessert fork, he was sensitive about song lyrics. Particularly to songs he had written.

“Huh?” Kristoff’s eyes flew open. “It’s supposed to be ‘sweep one off his feet!’”

Eyes sparkling, Elsa sang the next verse. “‘Goblins like to eat a lot, and Hulder like to sing—but you will never find one with a feathered’…nose!”

“No!” Kristoff surged to his feet. “That doesn’t rhyme! And what does a feathered nose even mean?”

“Now we got him,” Anna whispered to her sister, and she grabbed his hand. “Come on, Kristoff, sing it for us?”

And Kristoff—poor, tired, sorrowful Kristoff—sang.

Together, the three of them moved forward through the darkness, their voices echoing so that they sounded like an entire choir rather than just three fatigued friends hoping to survive, hoping to save the kingdom that Anna loved more than anything. She gave herself over to the sound, letting it sweep her along.

They sang about the Huldrefólk. They sang about Aren and his gallant sword. And then they sang a silly ballad about a goose who fell in love with a duck.

As they reached the end of the song, Anna thought about how beautiful Elsa’s voice sounded. She hadn’t known her sister could hit quite such high notes, or even sing harmonies. Anna stopped singing, wanting to listen closer. And that’s when she realized that Kristoff had stopped singing…and so had Elsa.

In fact, all three of them had fallen silent, and yet the song continued. It climbed around them, higher and higher.

It was as though the rocks themselves were singing. But that couldn’t be—could it?

Elsa pointed down a passage to their left. “It’s coming from there.”

Anna turned toward it.

“Hold on!” Elsa grabbed her. “What makes you think we’re going that way?”

“Why wouldn’t we?” Anna said. “We’re lost, and we need help. Besides, something so beautiful can’t possibly be dangerous!”

Elsa stared at her. “Did you learn nothing from your engagement with Prince—”

“Shh,” Kristoff interrupted. “The singing’s stopped.”

And so it had.

Anna whirled on Elsa. “We missed out on someone who could have helped us!”

“Or maybe we missed out on whatever could have eaten us,” Elsa said.

Kristoff gulped. “Or maybe they’re right behind you.”

“Very funny, Kristoff,” Anna told him.

“No,” he protested. “I’m…serious. Look.”

While Anna had been talking with Elsa, they had walked into a new portion of the mines.

Unlike the other passageways, this one had never seen the tip of a pickax. Because all around were crystals—and not just any crystals. Each one was taller than Kristoff and as wide as a tree trunk. They jutted from the walls and the ceiling, angled every which way to form a forest of sparkling rock. Each crystal was a shifting white, as though when the crystals had formed, they’d been filled with smoke.

But it wasn’t the crystals’ unusual size or color that made Anna gasp or caused Elsa to grip her so hard that Anna could feel Elsa’s fingernails digging into her shoulder. Sitting astride a crystal as large as a pony was a little child.

At least, Anna thought it might be a child, as the figure was definitely child-sized, about as big as a three-year-old human. In the dim light of the glowworm bracelet she’d put on, Anna could just make out the gleam of an eye, and soft-looking gray leggings that glimmered slightly as the child kicked out their legs.

The child began to sing again, though the melody had no words. Just clear, round notes.

With a gasp, Anna began to run toward the child, stubbing her toes and just missing occasional low-hanging rocks. But she didn’t care. All that mattered was that there was a child under the mountain who had been left alone. And Anna never wanted anyone to feel alone or left out—not ever. Not if she could help it.

Worry pulsed through her, followed by guilt. She hadn’t even heard of a child missing from the village. She knew she’d been distracted with Elsa’s impending grand tour, but she couldn’t have been so busy as to not have heard about a missing child. She wondered how long the child had been down there, where the guardians were, or—she realized with a lurch—maybe the question should be, what had happened to them? Did the Nattmara get them?

But before she could get more than a few feet from the child, she felt someone tug on the back of her cloak, yanking her.

“Anna,” Elsa whispered, voice as low as could be, “do you see the ears?”

Anna squinted, trying to see what Elsa saw. At first, she couldn’t, as the child’s curls bumped over where she expected the ears to be, except…

Anna squinted so hard now that she could see her own eyelashes.

And then, she saw them: the child’s ears rose to slender points, like the tips of a dragonfly’s wings.

Suddenly, Anna remembered a bedtime story from a long, long time ago, back when she and Elsa had shared a room. They are tall and strong, with sharp ears. And they’re sensitive. Which is why, little Elsa, Mother had said with a tug on the hem of Elsa’s pajama bottoms, if you ever see one, you must not mention their tail! It’s rude.

And if you do—a young Anna had popped up from behind her pillow fort, making a scary face and shaping her hands into claws—they might eat you!

Elsa had burst into giggles, which had only made Anna wrinkle her face more and add an extra growl.

All right, enough, Mother had said, scooping Anna up in one arm to plop her beside Elsa before she sat next to them on the bed. Cuddle close. Scooch in.

Anna had let her face fall back to normal, but she’d kept her fingers curled into claws as she cozied up next to her mother and sister and asked, Momma, what do their tails look like?

No one knows, Mother had said, and fixed a ribbon in Anna’s ponytail. They keep them hidden under skirts or keep their backs to the wall at all times.

But I wanna knoooow, Anna had whined, and her mother had kissed the top of her head and laughed.

Everyone is entitled to their secrets, she’d said. Especially the hidden people.

The hidden people.

Or, as the Arendellians called them…

“Huldrefólk,” Anna breathed. And as she spoke the name aloud, Oaken’s words came back to her, sharp as a stalactite.

Beware the Huldrefólk.

安娜、艾莎和克斯托夫不能永远待在这水晶清水与萤虫光亮的洞里。

因为现在，连安静都危险。

距安娜上次睡觉已快二十四小时，看艾莎眼底的乌青，她更久。

可最爱缺觉的是克斯托夫。

找他的地精家人，他早在回城堡前就骑了一整天，接着又逃离。

他醒得太久了。

他需要睡。

他们都需要。

可若他们睡了，纳特玛拉更易追踪他们——而安娜知道它不会放弃。

那是噩梦的本性——前一秒忘了，下一秒猛地炸成清晰的记忆。

安娜、艾莎和克斯托夫得在矿里继续走。

他们得让脚不停往前蹭，眼睛睁着。

只要一人睡着，就可能全员完蛋。

他们有太多人要救。

于是，捡了些萤虫串在脖子和手腕上后，他们选了一条通道——不是因为眼熟，而是它似乎比别的上坡多。

克斯托夫用山上学的本事，帮大家用绳子攀上墙，够到最高的通道。

他们拖着步往前，安娜试着想提神的事：日出、滑雪橇、和镇上孩子玩、奥拉夫。

可这些没让她兴奋清醒，反倒更难过、更累。

她怀疑自己还能不能再清醒过来。

克斯托夫在她身旁踉跄。

他没像平时那样稳住自己，而是跪倒，坐回脚跟。

安娜在他身边蹲下，手贴上他的背。"没事吧，克斯托夫？

你得起来！"她推了推他。

克斯托夫嘟囔着回应，头枕到地上。"这石头好软。"安娜拽他胳膊，没把他拉起，反而把自己累得更甚，也跟着坐倒。

克斯托夫说得对。

石头软软静静，想让她把头枕上去。

它暖暖的，安娜昏沉的脑里记起格尔达教过的一课：大地是浮在热岩浆上的土壳，有时小股热气会从底下岩里涌出温泉。

这些矿里的隧道虽从没见过太阳，却像夏日的余温——像躺在被太阳亲过的石滩上。

安娜只想舒展酸疼的筋骨，睡在那儿。

安娜！

远远地，她听见有人喊她名字。

安娜，起来！"再几分钟，"安娜嘟囔。

一阵冷气拍在脸上。

安娜猛地坐直。"嘿！"她抹掉颊上像是雪球残渣的东西，"你干吗？"克斯托夫也一脸雪沫，抗议。"我在救你们命，"艾莎说。

她变出另一个雪球，在手里掂着。"站起来，不然脸上再来冰。

成交？""呃啊！"克斯托夫喷着，"让我们睡吧！""抱歉，我不能，"艾莎摇头，"安娜！

哦，天哪。"安娜感到又一阵冷雪，猛抬起头。"抱歉抱歉，"她嘟囔，舌头在嘴里发胀。

雪在艾莎指尖发亮，安娜心里有什么被轻轻揪了一下。

是件重要的事。

和艾莎与她的魔法有关。

可是什么？

艾莎抡起胳膊，准备再朝他俩任一丢雪球，安娜想起来了。

她腾地站高，几乎跳起。"艾莎，停下！"姐姐把雪球丢到地上，噗一声轻响。"现在你保证清醒了？

因为雪还多的是。"可安娜不再困了。

远非如此。"你不能一直用魔法，"她说，"在观测台上，我注意到你每用一次，纳特玛拉就变大。"_oh."艾莎抱臂胸前，"好极了。"安娜在克斯托夫包里翻出书，翻开页想证实自己的判断。

可它们被湖水浸透，墨迹难辨。

她叹气。

呼噜！

姐妹俩低头，看见克斯托夫的眼睛又闭了，头歪向胸口，发出被掐住的鼾声。"我们拿他怎么办？"艾莎问。"嗯。"安娜四处找主意——任何主意。

平时主意来得又利又准，可缺觉让她昏昏的。

她只能盯着萤虫投在对面洞壁上的影子。

影子。

类似扎里亚有名的皮影。

她读过，那些艺人常和歌手一样有名，能凭表演坐满整座剧院。

若他们真能打败纳特玛拉、让一切复原，也许她会请些皮影艺人来阿伦黛尔表演。

去年克斯托夫演他的音乐剧时，大家都那么喜欢。"就是它！"安娜喊。

就是它，它，它。

她的话在岩石走廊里回荡。

她蹲到和克斯托夫扑闪的睫毛一般高，开始唱："'妖精的脚趾丑，胡尔德的尾巴甜——可你绝对抓不住我，扫走他一只'……爪！"那是克斯托夫为上个春庆编的傻歌。

村里的孩子爱死了，在克斯托夫鼓励下为王国演过。

安娜初遇这山地汉子时，他满身雪渣，只对她咕哝几个字。

她绝想不到，粗糙的外表下、一两块泥斑里，他真正的语言是歌。

克斯托夫有旋律的天赋，虽不介意衬衫上的汤渍，分不清餐叉和甜点叉，却对歌词敏感。

尤其对自己写的歌。"哈？"克斯托夫睁大眼，"应该是'扫走他一只脚'！"艾莎眨着眼，唱下一节："'妖精爱吃，胡尔德爱唱——可你绝找不到一只长着羽毛的'……鼻子！""不！"克斯托夫蹿起身，"那不押韵！

长羽毛的鼻子算什么？""这下抓住他了，"安娜对姐姐低语，抓住他的手，"来，克斯托夫，唱给我们听？"而克斯托夫——可怜、疲惫、忧伤的克斯托夫——唱了。

三人穿过黑暗往前，声音回荡，像一整支唱诗班，而非三个盼着活命、盼着救下安娜最爱的王国的疲惫朋友。

她把自己交给了声音，任它带着走。

他们唱胡尔德精灵。

他们唱阿伦和他英勇的剑。

接着唱了首傻乎乎的叙事歌，讲一只鹅爱上一只鸭。

唱到歌尾，安娜想着艾莎的嗓音多美。

她不知姐姐能唱这么高的音，甚至能和声。

安娜停了唱，想听更清。

就在这时她发觉克斯托夫停了……艾莎也停了。

其实三人全静了，可歌还在继续。

它绕着他们升，越来越高。

仿佛岩石自己在唱。

可那不可能——可能吗？

艾莎指向左边一条通道。"从那儿来的。""站住！"艾莎拽住她，"你凭什么认为我们走那边？""为什么不？"安娜说，"我们迷路了，需要帮忙。

再说，这么美的东西不可能危险！"艾莎盯着她。"你从和王子订婚那事上什么都没学到？——""嘘，"克斯托夫打断，"歌停了。"果然停了。

安娜猛地转向艾莎。"我们错过能帮忙的人了！""也许我们错过的是能吃掉我们的东西，"艾莎说。

克斯托夫咽口水。"也许它们就在你背后。""真逗，克斯托夫，"安娜说。"不，"他抗议，"我是……认真的。

看。"安娜和艾莎说话时，他们已走进矿里新的一段。

和其他通道不同，这段从没见过镐尖。

因为四周都是水晶——还不只是普通水晶。

每一株都比克斯托夫高，粗如树干。

它们从墙和顶上斜伸出来，朝各个方向，形成一片闪亮的岩石森林。

每株水晶是流动的白色，像成形时灌进了烟。

可让安娜倒吸一口气、让艾莎攥紧她的，不是水晶罕见的尺寸或颜色，而是——

骑在一株小马般大的水晶上的，是个小孩。

至少安娜想是个孩子，因为这身影确实孩子大小，约莫三岁小孩高。

在她戴上的萤虫手环微光里，安娜勉强辨出一只眼睛的反光，和柔软的灰色紧身裤，孩子蹬腿时微微发亮。

孩子又唱起来，只是旋律没有词。

只有清亮圆润的音。

安娜倒吸一口气，朝孩子跑去，脚趾撞得生疼，勉强躲过偶尔低垂的石头。

可她不在乎。

重要的是山下有个被独自留下的孩子。

而安娜从不愿任何人觉得孤单或被落下——绝不。

只要她帮得上。

担忧涌过她，接着是愧疚。

她连村里有个孩子失踪都没听说。

她知道自己在为艾莎即将开始的巡游分心，可再忙也不至于没听说孩子丢了。

她想知道孩子在这儿多久了， guardians 在哪儿，或者——她心里一沉——也许该问，他们出了什么事？

是纳特玛拉害了他们？

可她还没走到离孩子几尺远，就觉有人拽她斗篷后襟，猛地一拉。"安娜，"艾莎极低的声音，"你看见那耳朵了吗？"安娜眯眼，想看清艾莎所见。

起初她看不见，因为孩子的卷发盖住了她预期耳朵的位置，只是……安娜现在眯得连自己睫毛都看见。

接着，她看见了：孩子的耳朵尖尖竖起，像蜻蜓翅膀的尖端。

忽然，安娜记起很久很久以前，她和艾莎还同住一屋时的睡前故事。

他们高大强壮，耳朵尖尖。

而且敏感。

所以，小艾莎，母亲扯了扯艾莎睡裤脚边说，若你见到一个，绝不可提他们的尾巴！

那不礼貌。

要是你提了——小安娜从枕头堡垒后冒出来，做个鬼脸，手弯成爪——他们也许会吃了你！

艾莎咯咯笑，只让安娜皱脸更凶，又加一声吼。

好了好了，母亲把安娜一把捞起，搁到艾莎身边，自己坐上床。

挨紧点。

挤进来。

安娜把脸恢复正常，却还把手指弯成爪，依偎在母亲和姐姐间，问：妈妈，他们的尾巴什么样？

没人知道，母亲说，替安娜拢好马尾上的丝带。

他们把尾巴藏在裙下，或总是背贴墙。

可我想知——道，安娜哼唧，母亲亲了亲她头顶，笑了。

人人都有保密的权利，她说。

尤其是隐者。

隐者。

或者说，阿伦黛尔人叫他们……"胡尔德精灵，"安娜轻唤。

她念出这名字，奥肯的话像石笋一样尖利地回响。

当心胡尔德精灵。

sentences.en: ANNA, ELSA, AND KRISTOFF couldn’t stay in the cave of crystal-clear water and glowworm light forever.
sentences.zh: 安娜、艾莎和克斯托夫不能永远待在这水晶清水与萤虫光亮的洞里。

sentences.en: Because now, even the quiet was dangerous.
sentences.zh: 因为现在，连安静都危险。

sentences.en: It had been nearly twenty-four hours since Anna had last slept, and judging from the dark bags under Elsa’s eyes, it had even been even longer for her.
sentences.zh: 距安娜上次睡觉已快二十四小时，看艾莎眼底的乌青，她更久。

sentences.en: But it was Kristoff who was suffering from exhaustion the most.
sentences.zh: 可最爱缺觉的是克斯托夫。

sentences.en: Looking for his troll family, he’d already done a hard day’s ride before arriving back at the castle, only to flee.
sentences.zh: 找他的地精家人，他早在回城堡前就骑了一整天，接着又逃离。

sentences.en: He had been awake for too long.
sentences.zh: 他醒得太久了。

sentences.en: He needed sleep.
sentences.zh: 他需要睡。

sentences.en: They all did.
sentences.zh: 他们都需要。

sentences.en: But if they slept, it might make it easier for the Nattmara to track them—and Anna knew it wouldn’t give up.
sentences.zh: 可若他们睡了，纳特玛拉更易追踪他们——而安娜知道它不会放弃。

sentences.en: That was the nature of a nightmare—one second, they were forgotten, and the next, they exploded into sharp memory.
sentences.zh: 那是噩梦的本性——前一秒忘了，下一秒猛地炸成清晰的记忆。

sentences.en: Anna, Elsa, and Kristoff had to keep moving through the mines.
sentences.zh: 安娜、艾莎和克斯托夫得在矿里继续走。

sentences.en: They had to keep their feet shuffling forward, their eyes open.
sentences.zh: 他们得让脚不停往前蹭，眼睛睁着。

sentences.en: If one of them slept, it could be the end of them all.
sentences.zh: 只要一人睡着，就可能全员完蛋。

sentences.en: They had so many people to save.
sentences.zh: 他们有太多人要救。

sentences.en: And so, after gathering strands of glowworms to hang around their necks and wrists, they decided on a tunnel—not because it was familiar, but because it seemed to go more up than the others.
sentences.zh: 于是，捡了些萤虫串在脖子和手腕上后，他们选了一条通道——不是因为眼熟，而是它似乎比别的上坡多。

sentences.en: Using the skills he’d learned on the mountain, Kristoff had been able to help them all scale the wall with his rope to reach the highest passageway.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫用山上学的本事，帮大家用绳子攀上墙，够到最高的通道。

sentences.en: As they trudged forward, Anna tried to think about energizing things: sunrises, sledding, playing with the children in town, Olaf.
sentences.zh: 他们拖着步往前，安娜试着想提神的事：日出、滑雪橇、和镇上孩子玩、奥拉夫。

sentences.en: But instead of making her feel excited and awake, they only made her feel sad and even more tired.
sentences.zh: 可这些没让她兴奋清醒，反倒更难过、更累。

sentences.en: She wondered if she would ever feel awake again.
sentences.zh: 她怀疑自己还能不能再清醒过来。

sentences.en: Kristoff stumbled beside her.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫在她身旁踉跄。

sentences.en: Instead of catching himself as he normally would, he dropped to his knees and sank back onto his heels.
sentences.zh: 他没像平时那样稳住自己，而是跪倒，坐回脚跟。

sentences.en: Anna stooped beside him and rested a hand on his back. “Are you okay, Kristoff?
sentences.zh: 安娜在他身边蹲下，手贴上他的背。"没事吧，克斯托夫？

sentences.en: You have to get up!” She nudged him.
sentences.zh: 你得起来！"她推了推他。

sentences.en: Kristoff mumbled in reply and laid his head on the ground. “This rock is so soft.” Anna pulled on his arm, but instead of yanking him to his feet, she only succeeded in making herself more tired, and she, too, sank to the ground.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫嘟囔着回应，头枕到地上。"这石头好软。"安娜拽他胳膊，没把他拉起，反而把自己累得更甚，也跟着坐倒。

sentences.en: Kristoff was right.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫说得对。

sentences.en: The rock was soft and still and it wanted her to lay her head down on it.
sentences.zh: 石头软软静静，想让她把头枕上去。

sentences.en: It was warm, and from the depths of her sleep-addled mind, Anna remembered a lesson Gerda had taught her, about how the earth was a crust of dirt floating on top of hot magma, and that sometimes, little pockets of heat would spring warm water from the rocks underneath.
sentences.zh: 它暖暖的，安娜昏沉的脑里记起格尔达教过的一课：大地是浮在热岩浆上的土壳，有时小股热气会从底下岩里涌出温泉。

sentences.en: Even though these carved tunnels within the mines had never seen the sun, they felt like a touch of summer—of lying on rocky beaches kissed by the sun.
sentences.zh: 这些矿里的隧道虽从没见过太阳，却像夏日的余温——像躺在被太阳亲过的石滩上。

sentences.en: All Anna wanted to do was to stretch out her tired muscles and sleep there.
sentences.zh: 安娜只想舒展酸疼的筋骨，睡在那儿。

sentences.en: Anna!
sentences.zh: 安娜！

sentences.en: From a long way away, she heard someone calling her name.
sentences.zh: 远远地，她听见有人喊她名字。

sentences.en: Anna, get up! “Just a few more minutes,” Anna mumbled.
sentences.zh: 安娜，起来！"再几分钟，"安娜嘟囔。

sentences.en: A slap of cold air hit her.
sentences.zh: 一阵冷气拍在脸上。

sentences.en: Anna jolted upright. “Hey!” She wiped away what seemed to be the remnants of a snowball from her cheek. “What was that for?” Kristoff protested, snow also flecking his face. “I’m saving your lives,” Elsa said.
sentences.zh: 安娜猛地坐直。"嘿！"她抹掉颊上像是雪球残渣的东西，"你干吗？"克斯托夫也一脸雪沫，抗议。"我在救你们命，"艾莎说。

sentences.en: She conjured another snowball, which she juggled. “On your feet, or it’s more ice in your face.
sentences.zh: 她变出另一个雪球，在手里掂着。"站起来，不然脸上再来冰。

sentences.en: We have a deal?” “Blargh!” Kristoff sputtered. “Just let us sleep!” “Sorry, but I can’t do that.” Elsa shook head. “Anna!
sentences.zh: 成交？""呃啊！"克斯托夫喷着，"让我们睡吧！""抱歉，我不能，"艾莎摇头，"安娜！

sentences.en: Oh, for goodness’ sake.” Anna felt another slap of cold snow and jerked her head up. “Sorry, sorry,” she mumbled, her tongue feeling too thick for her mouth.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。"安娜感到又一阵冷雪，猛抬起头。"抱歉抱歉，"她嘟囔，舌头在嘴里发胀。

sentences.en: Snow glistened at Elsa’s fingertips, and something niggled at Anna’s mind.
sentences.zh: 雪在艾莎指尖发亮，安娜心里有什么被轻轻揪了一下。

sentences.en: It was something important.
sentences.zh: 是件重要的事。

sentences.en: It had something to do with Elsa and her magic.
sentences.zh: 和艾莎与她的魔法有关。

sentences.en: But what was it?
sentences.zh: 可是什么？

sentences.en: As Elsa wound her arm, ready to pitch another snowball at either one of them, Anna remembered.
sentences.zh: 艾莎抡起胳膊，准备再朝他俩任一丢雪球，安娜想起来了。

sentences.en: She shot up tall and nearly jumped. “Elsa, stop!” Her sister dropped her snowball to the ground, where it landed with a small puff . “You promise to stay awake now?
sentences.zh: 她腾地站高，几乎跳起。"艾莎，停下！"姐姐把雪球丢到地上，噗一声轻响。"现在你保证清醒了？

sentences.en: Because there’s more snow where that came from.” But Anna was no longer sleepy.
sentences.zh: 因为雪还多的是。"可安娜不再困了。

sentences.en: Far from it. “You can’t keep using your magic,” she said. “On the observation deck, I noticed that every time you did, the Nattmara grew.” “Oh.” Elsa folded her arms across her chest. “Great.” Anna rooted around in Kristoff’s pack and pulled out the book, flipping open its pages to confirm her theory.
sentences.zh: 远非如此。"你不能一直用魔法，"她说，"在观测台上，我注意到你每用一次，纳特玛拉就变大。"_oh."艾莎抱臂胸前，"好极了。"安娜在克斯托夫包里翻出书，翻开页想证实自己的判断。

sentences.en: But they were soaked through from the lake, the ink indecipherable.
sentences.zh: 可它们被湖水浸透，墨迹难辨。

sentences.en: She sighed.
sentences.zh: 她叹气。

sentences.en: SNORFFF!
sentences.zh: 呼噜！

sentences.en: The sisters looked down to see Kristoff’s eyes had closed again, a strangled snore escaping from him as his head drifted toward his chest. “What are we going to do about him?” Elsa asked. “Umm.” Anna cast about for an idea— any idea.
sentences.zh: 姐妹俩低头，看见克斯托夫的眼睛又闭了，头歪向胸口，发出被掐住的鼾声。"我们拿他怎么办？"艾莎问。"嗯。"安娜四处找主意——任何主意。

sentences.en: Usually, they came sharp and sure, but lack of sleep was making her feel fuzzy.
sentences.zh: 平时主意来得又利又准，可缺觉让她昏昏的。

sentences.en: All she could really focus on were their shadows thrown by the glowworms onto the cave wall opposite them.
sentences.zh: 她只能盯着萤虫投在对面洞壁上的影子。

sentences.en: Shadows.
sentences.zh: 影子。

sentences.en: Shadows similar to the famous shadow puppets of Zaria.
sentences.zh: 类似扎里亚有名的皮影。

sentences.en: She’d read how the puppeteers were often as famous as singers, and could fill whole theaters with their performances.
sentences.zh: 她读过，那些艺人常和歌手一样有名，能凭表演坐满整座剧院。

sentences.en: If they could ever defeat the Nattmara and make everything right again, maybe she would invite some of the puppeteers to come give a performance in Arendelle.
sentences.zh: 若他们真能打败纳特玛拉、让一切复原，也许她会请些皮影艺人来阿伦黛尔表演。

sentences.en: Everyone had liked it so much last year when Kristoff had performed his musical…. “That’s it!” Anna shouted.
sentences.zh: 去年克斯托夫演他的音乐剧时，大家都那么喜欢。"就是它！"安娜喊。

sentences.en: That’s it, it, it.
sentences.zh: 就是它，它，它。

sentences.en: Her words echoed down the rocky corridor.
sentences.zh: 她的话在岩石走廊里回荡。

sentences.en: Crouching down to be at the same level as Kristoff’s fluttering eyelashes, she began to sing: “‘Goblin toes are ugly, and Hulder tails are sweet—but you would never catch me, sweep one off his’ …paw!” It was a silly song that Kristoff had made up for the last spring festival.
sentences.zh: 她蹲到和克斯托夫扑闪的睫毛一般高，开始唱："'妖精的脚趾丑，胡尔德的尾巴甜——可你绝对抓不住我，扫走他一只'……爪！"那是克斯托夫为上个春庆编的傻歌。

sentences.en: The children in the village had loved it, and had performed it for the kingdom under Kristoff’s encouraging eye.
sentences.zh: 村里的孩子爱死了，在克斯托夫鼓励下为王国演过。

sentences.en: When Anna had first met the mountain man, he’d been snow-crusted and only grunted a few words to her.
sentences.zh: 安娜初遇这山地汉子时，他满身雪渣，只对她咕哝几个字。

sentences.en: She never would have thought that underneath the rough exterior, and a dirt patch or two, his real language was song.
sentences.zh: 她绝想不到，粗糙的外表下、一两块泥斑里，他真正的语言是歌。

sentences.en: Kristoff had a gift for melody, and though he didn’t mind the odd soup stain on his shirt and didn’t care about the difference between a salad fork and a dessert fork, he was sensitive about song lyrics.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫有旋律的天赋，虽不介意衬衫上的汤渍，分不清餐叉和甜点叉，却对歌词敏感。

sentences.en: Particularly to songs he had written. “Huh?” Kristoff’s eyes flew open. “It’s supposed to be ‘sweep one off his feet !’” Eyes sparkling, Elsa sang the next verse. “‘Goblins like to eat a lot, and Hulder like to sing—but you will never find one with a feathered’ …nose!” “No!” Kristoff surged to his feet. “That doesn’t rhyme!
sentences.zh: 尤其对自己写的歌。"哈？"克斯托夫睁大眼，"应该是'扫走他一只脚'！"艾莎眨着眼，唱下一节："'妖精爱吃，胡尔德爱唱——可你绝找不到一只长着羽毛的'……鼻子！""不！"克斯托夫蹿起身，"那不押韵！

sentences.en: And what does a feathered nose even mean?” “Now we got him,” Anna whispered to her sister, and she grabbed his hand. “Come on, Kristoff, sing it for us?” And Kristoff—poor, tired, sorrowful Kristoff—sang.
sentences.zh: 长羽毛的鼻子算什么？""这下抓住他了，"安娜对姐姐低语，抓住他的手，"来，克斯托夫，唱给我们听？"而克斯托夫——可怜、疲惫、忧伤的克斯托夫——唱了。

sentences.en: Together, the three of them moved forward through the darkness, their voices echoing so that they sounded like an entire choir rather than just three fatigued friends hoping to survive, hoping to save the kingdom that Anna loved more than anything.
sentences.zh: 三人穿过黑暗往前，声音回荡，像一整支唱诗班，而非三个盼着活命、盼着救下安娜最爱的王国的疲惫朋友。

sentences.en: She gave herself over to the sound, letting it sweep her along.
sentences.zh: 她把自己交给了声音，任它带着走。

sentences.en: They sang about the Huldrefólk.
sentences.zh: 他们唱胡尔德精灵。

sentences.en: They sang about Aren and his gallant sword.
sentences.zh: 他们唱阿伦和他英勇的剑。

sentences.en: And then they sang a silly ballad about a goose who fell in love with a duck.
sentences.zh: 接着唱了首傻乎乎的叙事歌，讲一只鹅爱上一只鸭。

sentences.en: As they reached the end of the song, Anna thought about how beautiful Elsa’s voice sounded.
sentences.zh: 唱到歌尾，安娜想着艾莎的嗓音多美。

sentences.en: She hadn’t known her sister could hit quite such high notes, or even sing harmonies.
sentences.zh: 她不知姐姐能唱这么高的音，甚至能和声。

sentences.en: Anna stopped singing, wanting to listen closer.
sentences.zh: 安娜停了唱，想听更清。

sentences.en: And that’s when she realized that Kristoff had stopped singing…and so had Elsa.
sentences.zh: 就在这时她发觉克斯托夫停了……艾莎也停了。

sentences.en: In fact, all three of them had fallen silent, and yet the song continued.
sentences.zh: 其实三人全静了，可歌还在继续。

sentences.en: It climbed around them, higher and higher.
sentences.zh: 它绕着他们升，越来越高。

sentences.en: It was as though the rocks themselves were singing.
sentences.zh: 仿佛岩石自己在唱。

sentences.en: But that couldn’t be—could it?
sentences.zh: 可那不可能——可能吗？

sentences.en: Elsa pointed down a passage to their left. “It’s coming from there.” Anna turned toward it. “Hold on!” Elsa grabbed her. “What makes you think we’re going that way?” “Why wouldn’t we?” Anna said. “We’re lost, and we need help.
sentences.zh: 艾莎指向左边一条通道。"从那儿来的。""站住！"艾莎拽住她，"你凭什么认为我们走那边？""为什么不？"安娜说，"我们迷路了，需要帮忙。

sentences.en: Besides, something so beautiful can’t possibly be dangerous!” Elsa stared at her. “Did you learn nothing from your engagement with Prince—” “Shh,” Kristoff interrupted. “The singing’s stopped.” And so it had.
sentences.zh: 再说，这么美的东西不可能危险！"艾莎盯着她。"你从和王子订婚那事上什么都没学到？——""嘘，"克斯托夫打断，"歌停了。"果然停了。

sentences.en: Anna whirled on Elsa. “We missed out on someone who could have helped us!” “Or maybe we missed out on whatever could have eaten us,” Elsa said.
sentences.zh: 安娜猛地转向艾莎。"我们错过能帮忙的人了！""也许我们错过的是能吃掉我们的东西，"艾莎说。

sentences.en: Kristoff gulped. “Or maybe they’re right behind you.” “Very funny, Kristoff,” Anna told him. “No,” he protested. “I’m…serious.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫咽口水。"也许它们就在你背后。""真逗，克斯托夫，"安娜说。"不，"他抗议，"我是……认真的。

sentences.en: Look.” While Anna had been talking with Elsa, they had walked into a new portion of the mines.
sentences.zh: 看。"安娜和艾莎说话时，他们已走进矿里新的一段。

sentences.en: Unlike the other passageways, this one had never seen the tip of a pickax.
sentences.zh: 和其他通道不同，这段从没见过镐尖。

sentences.en: Because all around were crystals—and not just any crystals.
sentences.zh: 因为四周都是水晶——还不只是普通水晶。

sentences.en: Each one was taller than Kristoff and as wide as a tree trunk.
sentences.zh: 每一株都比克斯托夫高，粗如树干。

sentences.en: They jutted from the walls and the ceiling, angled every which way to form a forest of sparkling rock.
sentences.zh: 它们从墙和顶上斜伸出来，朝各个方向，形成一片闪亮的岩石森林。

sentences.en: Each crystal was a shifting white, as though when the crystals had formed, they’d been filled with smoke.
sentences.zh: 每株水晶是流动的白色，像成形时灌进了烟。

sentences.en: But it wasn’t the crystals’ unusual size or color that made Anna gasp or caused Elsa to grip her so hard that Anna could feel Elsa’s fingernails digging into her shoulder.
sentences.zh: 可让安娜倒吸一口气、让艾莎攥紧她的，不是水晶罕见的尺寸或颜色，而是——

sentences.en: Sitting astride a crystal as large as a pony was a little child.
sentences.zh: 骑在一株小马般大的水晶上的，是个小孩。

sentences.en: At least, Anna thought it might be a child, as the figure was definitely child-sized, about as big as a three-year-old human.
sentences.zh: 至少安娜想是个孩子，因为这身影确实孩子大小，约莫三岁小孩高。

sentences.en: In the dim light of the glowworm bracelet she’d put on, Anna could just make out the gleam of an eye, and soft-looking gray leggings that glimmered slightly as the child kicked out their legs.
sentences.zh: 在她戴上的萤虫手环微光里，安娜勉强辨出一只眼睛的反光，和柔软的灰色紧身裤，孩子蹬腿时微微发亮。

sentences.en: The child began to sing again, though the melody had no words.
sentences.zh: 孩子又唱起来，只是旋律没有词。

sentences.en: Just clear, round notes.
sentences.zh: 只有清亮圆润的音。

sentences.en: With a gasp, Anna began to run toward the child, stubbing her toes and just missing occasional low-hanging rocks.
sentences.zh: 安娜倒吸一口气，朝孩子跑去，脚趾撞得生疼，勉强躲过偶尔低垂的石头。

sentences.en: But she didn’t care.
sentences.zh: 可她不在乎。

sentences.en: All that mattered was that there was a child under the mountain who had been left alone.
sentences.zh: 重要的是山下有个被独自留下的孩子。

sentences.en: And Anna never wanted anyone to feel alone or left out—not ever.
sentences.zh: 而安娜从不愿任何人觉得孤单或被落下——绝不。

sentences.en: Not if she could help it.
sentences.zh: 只要她帮得上。

sentences.en: Worry pulsed through her, followed by guilt.
sentences.zh: 担忧涌过她，接着是愧疚。

sentences.en: She hadn’t even heard of a child missing from the village.
sentences.zh: 她连村里有个孩子失踪都没听说。

sentences.en: She knew she’d been distracted with Elsa’s impending grand tour, but she couldn’t have been so busy as to not have heard about a missing child.
sentences.zh: 她知道自己在为艾莎即将开始的巡游分心，可再忙也不至于没听说孩子丢了。

sentences.en: She wondered how long the child had been down there, where the guardians were, or—she realized with a lurch—maybe the question should be, what had happened to them ?
sentences.zh: 她想知道孩子在这儿多久了， guardians 在哪儿，或者——她心里一沉——也许该问，他们出了什么事？

sentences.en: Did the Nattmara get them?
sentences.zh: 是纳特玛拉害了他们？

sentences.en: But before she could get more than a few feet from the child, she felt someone tug on the back of her cloak, yanking her. “Anna,” Elsa whispered, voice as low as could be, “do you see the ears?” Anna squinted, trying to see what Elsa saw.
sentences.zh: 可她还没走到离孩子几尺远，就觉有人拽她斗篷后襟，猛地一拉。"安娜，"艾莎极低的声音，"你看见那耳朵了吗？"安娜眯眼，想看清艾莎所见。

sentences.en: At first, she couldn’t, as the child’s curls bumped over where she expected the ears to be, except… Anna squinted so hard now that she could see her own eyelashes.
sentences.zh: 起初她看不见，因为孩子的卷发盖住了她预期耳朵的位置，只是……安娜现在眯得连自己睫毛都看见。

sentences.en: And then, she saw them: the child’s ears rose to slender points, like the tips of a dragonfly’s wings.
sentences.zh: 接着，她看见了：孩子的耳朵尖尖竖起，像蜻蜓翅膀的尖端。

sentences.en: Suddenly, Anna remembered a bedtime story from a long, long time ago, back when she and Elsa had shared a room.
sentences.zh: 忽然，安娜记起很久很久以前，她和艾莎还同住一屋时的睡前故事。

sentences.en: They are tall and strong, with sharp ears.
sentences.zh: 他们高大强壮，耳朵尖尖。

sentences.en: And they’re sensitive.
sentences.zh: 而且敏感。

sentences.en: Which is why, little Elsa, Mother had said with a tug on the hem of Elsa’s pajama bottoms, if you ever see one, you must not mention their tail!
sentences.zh: 所以，小艾莎，母亲扯了扯艾莎睡裤脚边说，若你见到一个，绝不可提他们的尾巴！

sentences.en: It’s rude.
sentences.zh: 那不礼貌。

sentences.en: And if you do —a young Anna had popped up from behind her pillow fort, making a scary face and shaping her hands into claws— they might eat you!

sentences.zh: 艾莎咯咯笑，只让安娜皱脸更凶，又加一声吼。

sentences.en: All right, enough, Mother had said, scooping Anna up in one arm to plop her beside Elsa before she sat next to them on the bed.
sentences.zh: 好了好了，母亲把安娜一把捞起，搁到艾莎身边，自己坐上床。

sentences.en: Anna had let her face fall back to normal, but she’d kept her fingers curled into claws as she cozied up next to her mother and sister and asked, Momma, what do their tails look like?
sentences.zh: 安娜把脸恢复正常，却还把手指弯成爪，依偎在母亲和姐姐间，问：妈妈，他们的尾巴什么样？

sentences.en: No one knows, Mother had said, and fixed a ribbon in Anna’s ponytail.

sentences.en: They keep them hidden under skirts or keep their backs to the wall at all times.

sentences.en: Everyone is entitled to their secrets, she’d said.

sentences.en: Especially the hidden people.

sentences.en: Or, as the Arendellians called them… “Huldrefólk,” Anna breathed.
sentences.zh: 或者说，阿伦黛尔人叫他们……"胡尔德精灵，"安娜轻唤。

sentences.en: And as she spoke the name aloud, Oaken’s words came back to her, sharp as a stalactite.
