奥布斯基伦注意到他们耷拉着的眼皮。“你们可以睡，”她说，“我认得这条河的路。”

“而且正如图书管理员国王所说，你们和我在一起是隐藏的，连纳特玛拉也寻不到。”“你确定……”克斯托夫本来要说什么，却被一个哈欠吞了下去。“纳特玛拉找不到我们的领地，”奥布斯基伦提醒他们，“我们被它遮蔽了。”

“你们可以安心在此歇息，不必担心被它影响而迷失自我。”

“睡吧。”

“歇着吧。”

“到了目的地我会叫醒你们。”奥布斯基伦话音未落，克斯托夫已经打起了呼噜，紧接着艾莎也睡着了。

可安娜，却还醒着。

尽管她方才还憧憬着能睡一觉，却发现眼睛怎么也闭不上。

每次合眼，她的胃就疼得厉害。

因为每睡过去一刻，她就有一刻没在弥补自己最大的过错：那头被她用咒语无意间迎进阿伦黛尔的纳特玛拉。

奥布斯基伦的声音打断了她的思绪，安娜把自己从中拽了出来。“抱歉，你说什么？”安娜问。“我说，”胡尔德重复道，“你也该睡了。”奥布斯基伦撑了一下篙，木筏破水而行，水声仿佛一声轻叹。

河水穿过低矮蜿蜒的隧道，虽说这儿那儿有小片沙滩探入水道，安娜觉得自己能辨认出远处有一两个胡尔德的影子在看着他们。

离一个并不想杀她的胡尔德这么近，她终于能看清更分明的轮廓。

奥布斯基伦看起来几乎像人，只是整体显得瘦长，长着尖耳朵，皮肤还会变化。

此刻，这名胡尔德的眼睛是漂亮的橘色，那种颜色让安娜想起晚秋将尽，或是早春方始。

那双眼仿佛将周遭一切尽收眼底，而当奥布斯基伦望向安娜时，安娜不禁想，这位寻物者能不能从她眼中读出最深的秘密。“奥布斯基伦，”安娜说，“你知道纳特玛拉是怎么来到阿伦黛尔的吗？”

“我想我知道，但不完全确定。”

“枯萎病（The Blight）在纳特玛拉到来之前就开始了。”

“具体细节我有点模糊。”她屏住呼吸，等着奥布斯基伦说出那几个正像牧羊人吹响图恩号（tungehorn）般在她脑中轰鸣的字眼：那道咒语。

“一定是那道咒语——尽管动物和庄稼在我念出它之前就病倒了，这怎么也说不通。”

“可我念过咒语之后，那头狼就出现了。”

“这一点安娜很确定——就像她确定这是她的错一样。”

奥布斯基伦沉默着，但那不是被无视时那种尖锐的沉默。

这份安静带着思索的意味，仿佛她在开口前要掂量每一个字。“纳特玛拉不会凭空出现，”胡尔德说，“它们是被‘造’出来的，由一个人生命中某件事滋长而成，大到再也无法藏在心里，恐惧膨胀到有了自己的生命。”安娜点了点头。

对，这正是索伦森说过的话。

“恐惧太大，藏不住了。”“那、那个，”安娜说，“所以你不觉得，会有人，我也不知道”——她把一缕红发别到耳后——“念了什么咒语之类，就把纳特玛拉带到了阿伦黛尔？”奥布斯基伦摇了摇头。“我不相信人类称作咒语的那些诗，除了诗本身，还能是什么别的东西。”

“它们或许能召唤出一幅美丽的画面，或凝固某一瞬间，但那完全是另一种魔法。”安娜不知该说什么，却感到一丝安慰。

因为安娜的确念过一道咒语……但听起来，即便她从没念出声，纳特玛拉也照样会降临这个王国。

安娜还是会无意中将它召唤而来，念不念那首诗都一样。

因为它从她梦境中现形的那一夜，正是她听见艾莎撇开她召开御前会议的那一夜，而那一刻，她的心微微碎了一块。

就在那一刻，她意识到自己最大的恐惧成真了：艾莎真的、确实根本不需要她。

也正因为如此，她的噩梦——她的恐惧——才化作了如今追踪着他们所有人的纳特玛拉。“那么我猜，”她努力让声音显得轻松，“既然没有召唤纳特玛拉的咒语，大概也就没有驱散它的咒语，对吧？”奥布斯基伦摇了摇头。“我想不会有的。”

“我只听说过一位敢直面纳特玛拉的战士，那就是阿伦（Aren），凭着他的神话之刃回旋之刃，那剑蕴含着奇异的力量。”回旋。

克斯托夫和艾莎在安娜背后沉沉睡去，贴着她；奥布斯基伦在前头，留意着安娜和她的朋友。那柄神话般的弯剑，如同灯塔般在安娜忧虑的暗河中闪耀，而她，终于让眼皮垂下，睡了过去。

sentences.en: WHILE ANNA, ELSA, AND KRISTOFF had been taking in the sights of the village below, it seemed as though a storm cloud had gathered around them.
sentences.zh: 当安娜、艾莎和克斯托夫还在欣赏脚下村庄的景色时，仿佛一团乌云正悄悄在他们四周聚拢。

sentences.en: Though, of course, storm clouds didn’t exist in the belly of the mines, nor were they capable of holding a spear to one’s throat.
sentences.zh: 当然，矿井深处可没有什么乌云，更不会有乌云把长矛抵在谁的喉咙上。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: The roiling, shifting dark shapes gathering around them were none other than Huldrefólk warriors.
sentences.zh: 那些在他们身边翻涌游移的黑色影子，其实是一群胡尔德民（Huldrefólk）的战士。

sentences.en: Like the littler Dash, these ones, too, stuck to the shadows.
sentences.zh: 和那个小不点达什（Dash）一样，这些家伙也紧紧贴着暗处。

sentences.en: In the glow, Anna could only make out the glint of an eye here, and the back of a hand there.
sentences.zh: 在微光里，安娜只能勉强辨认出这儿一只眼睛的反光，那儿一只手背的轮廓。

sentences.en: But she didn’t need to be able to see their faces to sense how they felt about three human trespassers in their secret city: they were not very happy at all. “H-h-hi,” Anna stuttered to the spear tips, trying to remember the etiquette of meeting a new group of people.
sentences.zh: 不过，她不必看清他们的脸，也能感受到他们对闯入秘密城市的三个人类外人的态度：他们一点都不高兴。“你、你、你们好，”安娜对着矛尖结巴地打招呼，努力回想见新族群时该有的礼数。

sentences.en: It wasn’t the exact same as meeting the prime minister of Torres, but she knew that dignitaries were sensitive, so polite manners seemed the safest bet.
sentences.zh: 这跟会见托雷斯（Torres）首相不完全一样，但她知道达官贵人都敏感，所以礼貌待人应该是最稳妥的选择。

sentences.en: Step one: Introduce yourself, and announce you are a friend.
sentences.zh: 第一步：自我介绍，并表明自己是朋友。

sentences.en: She dipped into a curtsy. “My name is Anna of Arendelle, and this is my sis—” A spearpoint jabbed closer to her, and Anna went silent. “Stop,” a Hulder hissed. “Say no more, thief.” “I-I think there’s been a mistake,” Anna said, forcing a cheerful smile on her face. “We’ve come to ask for help.
sentences.zh: 她行了个屈膝礼。“我是阿伦黛尔女王艾莎，这是我的姐——”一支矛尖又逼近了些，安娜顿时闭了嘴。“住口，”一名胡尔德嘶声道，“别再说了，小偷。”“我、我想是出了什么误会，”安娜强挤出一个欢快的笑容说道，“我们是来寻求帮助的。”

sentences.en: We’re not here to take anything—” “Take,” the same Hulder spoke again, repeating Anna. “Take, take, take!” “No,” Kristoff said, his back against Anna’s. “We’re not here to take anything.
sentences.zh: 我们不是来拿任何东西的——”“拿，”那名胡尔德又开口，复述着安娜的话，“拿，拿，拿！”“不，”克斯托夫背靠着安娜说，“我们不是来拿任何东西的。”

sentences.en: We followed a little one—” “Take little one,” the Hulder repeated, and Anna could hear fury swell in the Hulder’s voice. “Take little one!” The cry was repeated by another Hulder, and then another, until the entire shifting mass of spear-wielding warriors took up the chant.
sentences.zh: 我们跟着一个小家伙来的——”“抓走小家伙，”胡尔德重复道，安娜听得出他声音里的怒火在翻涌。“抓走小家伙！”另一名胡尔德跟着喊，接着又一名，直到那群手持长矛、不断游移的战士全都跟着喊起了这句。

sentences.en: Anna had a bad feeling.
sentences.zh: 安娜有种不祥的预感。

sentences.en: A very bad feeling. “I think that they’re accusing us of trying to steal Dash,” she whispered. “Ah,” Kristoff said in a low voice, “well, that’s not accurate.” “Wait!” Anna told the Huldrefólk, holding up her hand. “We weren’t trying to kidnap anyone!” The Huldrefólk’s chant changed. “Liar, liar, every word!” Anna shook her head, trying to make sense of them. “We’re not,” Elsa spoke up, her voice smooth as ice, though Anna could hear the friction beneath the surface. “The little one found us.
sentences.zh: 非常不祥的预感。“我觉得他们在指责我们想偷走达什，”她小声说。“啊，”克斯托夫低声道，“嗯，那可不对。”“等等！”安娜朝胡尔德民举起手喊道，“我们根本没有要绑架谁！”胡尔德民的口号变了。“骗子，骗子，句句谎话！”安娜摇着头，努力弄明白他们的意思。“我们不是，”艾莎开口了，声音如冰般平滑，可安娜听得出表面之下暗藏的摩擦。“是小家伙自己找到我们的。”

sentences.en: We were singing, and then my sister rescued the child from falling into a dark abyss—” “The abyss!” another Hulder with a higher voice interrupted. “The abyss!
sentences.zh: 我们当时在唱歌，然后我妹妹把那孩子从坠入黑暗深渊的边缘救了回来——”“深渊！”另一名嗓音更尖的胡尔德打断道，“深渊！”

sentences.en: Take to abyss!
sentences.zh: 扔进深渊！”

sentences.en: Take to abyss!
sentences.zh: 扔进深渊！”

sentences.en: Liar, liar, every word!” Uh-oh. “Um,” Anna said with a gulp. “I think they want to—” “Drop us off in the abyss?” Kristoff finished. “Yeah.
sentences.zh: 骗子，骗子，句句谎话！”糟了。“唔，”安娜咽了口唾沫说，“我觉得他们想——”“把我们丢进深渊？”克斯托夫接了下去，“没错。”

sentences.en: I got that, too.” “Wait!” Anna tried again. “There’s a giant wolf out there that’ll be here before you know—” Anna’s sentence was cut short as a warrior rushed forward and tied what felt like a handkerchief around Anna’s mouth, making it impossible for her to shout.
sentences.zh: 我也听出来了。”“等等！”安娜又试了一次，“外面有只巨狼，很快就要——”安娜的话被截断了，一名战士冲上前来，用一块像是手帕的东西勒住了她的嘴，让她没法喊出声。

sentences.en: But even if she could, would it help?
sentences.zh: 可就算她喊得出来，又有什么用呢？

sentences.en: They were so far underground, and the villagers who were still awake were far away, likely and hopefully already onboard Elsa’s royal ship.
sentences.zh: 他们身处地下那么深，而仍醒着的村民离得远远的，多半——也希望——已经登上了艾莎的皇家船只。

sentences.en: Sorenson was gone, having been left to face the Nattmara.
sentences.zh: 索伦森（Sorenson）已经不在了，被留下来独自面对纳特玛拉（Nattmara）。

sentences.en: And next to her, Elsa and Kristoff were also being gagged.
sentences.zh: 而在她身旁，艾莎和克斯托夫也正在被塞住嘴。

sentences.en: Hard roots pressed into the soft skin of Anna’s wrists as her hands were pulled behind her back and bound.
sentences.zh: 粗糙的树根压进安娜手腕柔嫩的皮肉里，她的双手被反剪到背后绑了起来。

sentences.en: After checking to make sure the knot was tight, the Hulder who had bound her nodded. “March.” Single file, they walked in front of the Huldrefólk.
sentences.zh: 那名绑住她的胡尔德确认绳结够紧后，点了点头。“走。”他们排成一列，走在胡尔德民的前面。

sentences.en: Anna kept her eye on Elsa’s braid as it swung, and was grateful when Kristoff accidentally stepped on her heel.
sentences.zh: 安娜紧盯着艾莎随步伐摇摆的辫子，当克斯托夫不小心踩到她的脚后跟时，她竟感到一丝安慰。

sentences.en: It made her feel better knowing they were both there.
sentences.zh: 知道他们俩都还在身边，让她心里好受些。

sentences.en: At least they were all in this mess together.
sentences.zh: 至少他们三个一起陷进了这团乱麻里。

sentences.en: Anna thought the Huldrefólk would take them away from their hidden city, back to the abyss from which they’d saved Dash, but instead, the warriors marched them down a narrow path, away from the abyss and the swarm of glowworms and fluorescent gardens.
sentences.zh: 安娜本以为胡尔德民会把他们带离隐藏的城市，回到他们救下达什的那个深渊去，可战士们却押着他们沿一条窄路走去，远离了深渊，也远离了成群的萤火虫和荧光花园。

sentences.en: Anna’s bad feeling only grew more insistent the longer they walked away from the city.
sentences.zh: 离城市越远，安娜那不祥的预感反倒越发强烈。

sentences.en: Sweat beaded on her forehead, and her ribcage felt too tight as she breathed in the stale and stuffy air.
sentences.zh: 汗珠在她额头渗出，呼吸着沉闷闭塞的空气，她只觉得胸腔被勒得发紧。

sentences.en: How far underground were they?
sentences.zh: 他们到底在地下多深处？

sentences.en: Then the smell of rotten eggs punched her nose, and her eyes watered.
sentences.zh: 接着，一股臭鸡蛋的气味直冲她的鼻子，熏得她眼泪直流。

sentences.en: It was the smell of sulfur, or else the Huldrefólk had some major issues with their plumbing.
sentences.zh: 那是硫磺的味道，要不然就是胡尔德民的管道出了大问题。

sentences.en: The air grew hotter still until it almost seemed to take on a rosy glow.
sentences.zh: 空气愈发灼热，几乎像是泛起了一层玫瑰色的红光。

sentences.en: A red light danced along the walls ahead of them, an unusual color that typically could only be found in the most spectacular summer sunsets, or in Tuva and Ada’s forge, or…no.
sentences.zh: 一道红光在前方墙壁上跃动，那是种罕见的颜色，通常只在最壮丽的夏日落霞里，或图娃（Tuva）和艾达（Ada）的锻炉中才见得到——或者……不对。

sentences.en: Anna’s heart flipped.
sentences.zh: 安娜的心猛地一沉。

sentences.en: Or in the center of an active volcano.
sentences.zh: 要么就是在活火山的正中心。

sentences.en: Liar, liar, every word plus abyss apparently equaled throwing the group of human trespassers from Arendelle into molten rock.
sentences.zh: “骗子，骗子，句句谎话”，再加上“深渊”，看来就等同于把这几个来自阿伦黛尔的人类闯入者扔进熔岩里。

sentences.en: The red glow grew brighter, and while the Huldrefólk seemed as cool as ice cream in the middle of an eternal winter, sweat now drenched Anna.
sentences.zh: 红光越来越亮，胡尔德民们仿佛身处永恒寒冬中的冰淇淋般冷静，可安娜此刻已被汗水浸透。

sentences.en: She imagined that if it got any hotter, her eyebrows would slide right off her face.
sentences.zh: 她想象着，要是再热下去，自己的眉毛怕是都要从脸上滑落了。

sentences.en: Even if Elsa could use her magic here—even if it wouldn’t draw the Nattmara straight to them—what chance did winter’s cold have against the melting powers of red-hot magma?
sentences.zh: 即便艾莎能在这里施展魔法——即便那不会立刻把纳特玛拉引到他们身边——寒冬的冰冷却又能拿炽热岩浆的融化之力奈何几分？

sentences.en: Now it was in front of them, a round circle of red that pulsed like a beating heart.
sentences.zh: 此刻它就横在眼前，一团赤红的正圆形，像一颗跳动的心脏般搏动着。

sentences.en: Anna stumbled to a stop, but the Huldrefólk shoved her forward, and though she could not believe it was possible, she grew even hotter. “Stop,” Anna garbled through her gag, her mind racing as she skipped over steps two through ten of diplomacy. “We’ll give you chocolate!” The words came out muffled.
sentences.zh: 安娜踉跄着停下脚步，可胡尔德民又把她往前推，虽然她不敢相信，但她确实感到更热了。“停下，”安娜透过塞口物含混地喊，脑子里飞快转着，直接跳过了外交步骤的第二到第十步。“我们给你们巧克力！”这句话听起来闷闷的。

sentences.en: It wasn’t actually a step of etiquette—truly, bribery didn’t belong on the list at all—and nothing in all her reading had prepared Anna for the possibility of being thrown into a river of lava by a hosting nation.
sentences.zh: 这其实算不上什么礼节——说真的，贿赂压根不该列在清单上——她读过的所有书里，都没让她做好被东道主扔进熔岩河的心理准备。

sentences.en: But it didn’t work.
sentences.zh: 可这招没用。

sentences.en: They pushed her forward.
sentences.zh: 他们把她往前推。

sentences.en: Even though it was hotter than Oaken’s sauna, Anna went numb as she saw Elsa’s boot hang over the edge, the toe turning red in the glow.
sentences.zh: 尽管比奥肯（Oaken）的桑拿房还热，可当安娜看见艾莎的靴子悬在边缘、靴尖在红光中泛红时，她整个人都麻木了。

sentences.en: Anna struggled harder.
sentences.zh: 安娜挣扎得更猛烈了。

sentences.en: If they disappeared on their mission, no one would ever know how the Nattmara came to be or how it could be stopped.
sentences.zh: 要是他们就此消失在任务途中，就再没人会知道纳特玛拉是怎样诞生的，又该如何阻止它。

sentences.en: No one would survive it.
sentences.zh: 没有人能幸免于难。

sentences.en: Being thrown into lava wouldn’t just mean the end of Kristoff, Elsa, and Anna—it would mean the end of Arendelle.
sentences.zh: 被扔进熔岩，不只是意味着克斯托夫、艾莎和安娜的终结——更意味着阿伦黛尔的终结。

sentences.en: They would have failed.
sentences.zh: 他们就失败了。

sentences.en: She would have failed.
sentences.zh: 她自己就失败了。

sentences.en: Emptiness yawned in Anna, threatening to swallow her whole.
sentences.zh: 一阵空虚在安娜心中张开大口，仿佛要将她整个人吞没。

sentences.en: All she had wanted— ever wanted—was to always do more and, out of true love for her sister, help her.
sentences.zh: 她所想要的——一直想要的——无非是做得更多，出于对妹妹真挚的爱，去帮她。

sentences.en: Although the whole kingdom had seen Anna save her sister three years ago, she had since wondered who wouldn’t save their sister.
sentences.zh: 尽管三年前全王国都目睹了安娜救下妹妹，可自那以后，她一直在想，又有谁不会去救自己的妹妹呢。

sentences.en: And still, Anna couldn’t get past that she was the one who had provoked Elsa into casting an eternal winter then, and now she was the one who had called a Nattmara to the land.
sentences.zh: 可安娜始终过不了自己这关：当年是她把艾莎激得降下了永恒寒冬，如今又是她把这纳特玛拉召唤到了这片土地上。

sentences.en: She would never feed Sven a carrot again.
sentences.zh: 她再也没法喂斯文吃胡萝卜了。

sentences.en: She would never hear more about Olaf’s warm philosophy on life.
sentences.zh: 她再也听不到奥拉夫那些温暖的人生哲理了。

sentences.en: She would never get a chance to learn about the natural and celestial worlds from Sorenson.
sentences.zh: 她再也没机会跟索伦森学习自然与天象的世界了。

sentences.en: And it was all her fault.
sentences.zh: 而这一切，都是她的错。

sentences.en: From the corner of her eye, she saw Elsa whip her head so fast that her braid slapped her Hulder captor’s nose, taking them by surprise, while Kristoff flung himself backward, slamming his captor into the wall.
sentences.zh: 眼角余光里，她看见艾莎猛地甩过头，辫子啪地抽在胡尔德俘虏者的鼻子上，打了对方一个措手不及；与此同时克斯托夫猛地向后一仰，把自己的俘虏者撞在墙上。

sentences.en: The two managed to wrestle out of their binds in the process.
sentences.zh: 两人乘势从绑缚中挣脱了出来。

sentences.en: Come on!
sentences.zh: 加油啊！”

sentences.en: Anna told herself.
sentences.zh: 安娜对自己说。”

sentences.en: They’re still fighting.
sentences.zh: 他们还在反抗。”

sentences.en: You can, too!
sentences.zh: 你也可以！”

sentences.en: She wanted to cheer them on, but she needed to save her breath.
sentences.zh: 她想为他们呐喊助威，可她得留着点力气。

sentences.en: And besides, there was still a gag in her mouth.
sentences.zh: 再说了，她嘴里还塞着东西呢。

sentences.en: Her guard dragged her forward, closer to the edge of the molten lake, while Anna freed her hands. “HALT!” A deep voice reverberated around the rock, sending tremors through the earth.
sentences.zh: 押着她的守卫把她往前拖，离那片熔岩湖的边更近了，而安娜正悄悄挣脱双手。“住手！”一个低沉的声音在岩壁间回荡，震得大地都颤了三颤。

sentences.en: But there was no way Anna was going to stop fighting.
sentences.zh: 可安娜绝不会就此停手。

sentences.en: She lunged to the side, free of the Hulder’s stony grip, and tore off her gag.
sentences.zh: 她向旁一扑，挣脱了胡尔德石般的手掌，一把扯下嘴里的塞口物。

sentences.en: She took a few running steps away from them before realizing she wasn’t being chased.
sentences.zh: 她跑开几步，才发觉并没有人在追她。

sentences.en: Instead, the Huldrefólk knelt to the ground as a fourth Hulder appeared in the red haze.
sentences.zh: 相反，胡尔德民们纷纷跪倒在地，这时第四名胡尔德在红色雾霭中现身了。

sentences.en: This Hulder seemed to be the tallest of them all, their hair a wild black mane surrounding their face, and on their head they wore a circlet of something shiny.
sentences.zh: 这名胡尔德似乎是所有人中最高的，乱蓬蓬的黑发如鬃毛般围着脸庞，头上戴着一圈闪亮的东西。

sentences.en: It took Anna a minute to realize it was gold.
sentences.zh: 安娜过了好一会儿才反应过来，那是金子。

sentences.en: The leader of the Huldrefólk.
sentences.zh: 胡尔德民的领袖。

sentences.en: And on the Hulder leader’s shoulders sat a small, familiar figure. “Horse!” Dash yanked on the Hulder leader’s hair.
sentences.zh: 而胡尔德领袖的肩头，坐着一个小小又熟悉的身影。“马！”达什拽着胡尔德领袖的头发喊道。

sentences.en: Anna sank into a curtsy, and after she coughed pointedly in Kristoff’s direction, he bowed.
sentences.zh: 安娜行了个屈膝礼，又故意朝克斯托夫的方向咳嗽了一声，他这才跟着鞠躬。

sentences.en: Elsa, however, stayed as upright as an icicle, befitting her rank. “Psst!
sentences.zh: 然而艾莎却如冰柱般笔直地站着，正合她的身份。“嘘！”

sentences.en: Rule number one,” Anna murmured loud enough so that Elsa could hear.
sentences.zh: 第一条规矩，”安娜低声嘀咕，好让艾莎能听见。

sentences.en: Elsa nodded and spoke. “Greetings.
sentences.zh: 艾莎点点头，开口道：“问候各位。”

sentences.en: I am Queen Elsa of Arendelle, and this is my sister, Princess Anna, and her…er, our guard, Kristoff Bjorgman of Nowhere in Particular.
sentences.zh: “我是阿伦黛尔女王艾莎，这是我妹妹安娜公主，以及她的……呃，我们的卫兵，来自无名之地的克斯托夫·比约格曼（Kristoff Bjorgman）。”

sentences.en: We greet you in friendship.” Anna held her breath, wondering if the leader would accept. “Friendship,” the Hulder leader repeated.
sentences.zh: “我们以友谊之名向你们致意。”安娜屏住呼吸，不知这位领袖会不会接受。“友谊，”胡尔德领袖重复道。

sentences.en: And then, to Anna’s utter astonishment, the Hulder continued in full sentences. “I apologize for my family.
sentences.zh: 接着，让安娜大吃一惊的是，胡尔德竟用完整的句子继续说了下去。“我为我的族人道歉。”

sentences.en: They can be a bit overprotective.” In the dim light, Anna saw the Hulder pat Dash’s dangling knee. “Young Echo, however, has cleared up the misunderstanding, and she and I welcome you to our domain.
sentences.zh: “他们有时候是有些过度保护。”昏暗的光里，安娜看见胡尔德轻轻拍了拍达什垂着的膝盖。“不过，小回声（Echo）已经澄清了误会，她和我们一起欢迎你们来到我们的领地。”

sentences.en: I am the king of the Huldrefólk.” “You’re not repeating everything,” Elsa said, clearly too surprised to worry about manners.
sentences.zh: “我是胡尔德民的国王。”“你没有在重复别人的话，”艾莎说，显然惊讶得顾不上礼节了。

sentences.en: The imposing Hulder king inclined his head. “We like to use other people’s words so that we can wrap ourselves up and hide within them.
sentences.zh: 威严的胡尔德国王微微颔首。“我们喜欢借用别人的话，好把自己包裹起来，藏进那些话里。”

sentences.en: It’s very rare for Huldrefólk to actually have to compose something new.
sentences.zh: “胡尔德民极少需要自己编出什么新话。”

sentences.en: That’s part of the reason why Echo found you—she wanted to collect your song.
sentences.zh: “这也是回声找到你们的部分原因——她想收集你们的歌。”

sentences.en: Songs are easy to remember.
sentences.zh: “歌最容易记住。”

sentences.en: Easy to echo back.” “Echo!” Dash—now Echo, Anna realized—repeated the word from her perch.
sentences.zh: “也容易回放。”“回声！”达什——安娜这才意识到，现在该叫她回声了——在落脚处跟着念道。

sentences.en: Anna knew she should probably let Elsa do all the talking, but her curiosity was too much. “Why do you talk in your own words?” she asked. “Because I am not only the king, but also the librarian,” said the Hulder leader. “I’ve spent years visiting the world above, collecting items as well as stories, and I have enough words at my disposal.
sentences.zh: 安娜知道自己本该让艾莎全权代言，可她好奇心太重。“你为什么用自己的话说话？”她问。“因为我不只是国王，还是图书管理员，”胡尔德领袖说，“我花了多年走访地表之上的世界，收集物件也收集故事，攒下的词儿够用。”

sentences.en: And so, I would like to apologize again for your initial greeting.” The Librarian King reached for Echo and set the child on the ground. “That’s it?” Kristoff burst out. “We’re almost thrown into a lake of lava, and all you can say is ‘I’m sorry’?” “I’m sorry!” Echo squealed, moving toward Kristoff. “Does ‘We’re very sorry’ make it any better?” the Librarian King asked. “Usually, the only humans who make it down this far want to take precious stones and gems from our mountain, or to capture a member of our domain to make them find iron ore deposits for their weapons and the like.” “We’re not looking for stones, gems, or iron,” Elsa said. “We’re looking for a sword of myth, the Revolute Blade.
sentences.zh: “所以，我想再次为你们起初受到的接待道歉。”图书管理员国王伸手把回声抱下来，放到地上。“就这样？”克斯托夫脱口而出，“我们差点被扔进熔岩湖，你就能说句‘对不起’？”“对不起嘛！”回声尖声叫着，朝克斯托夫挪过去。“那‘我们非常抱歉’会不会好一点？”图书管理员国王问。“通常，能下到这么深的人类，都只想从我们的山里拿走宝石珍矿，或是抓走我们领地的一员，逼他们去找铁矿脉来打造武器之类的东西。”“我们不是来寻石头、宝石或铁的，”艾莎说，“我们找的是一柄神话之剑，回旋之刃（Revolute Blade）。”

sentences.en: Can you please help us find it?” The Librarian King’s eyes flashed. “‘Revolving moon and spinning sun, forged a crescent blade.
sentences.zh: “你能帮我们找到它吗？”图书管理员国王眼中精光一闪。“‘旋转的月亮与流转的太阳，锻成一弯新月之刃。”

sentences.en: From light and dark within the heart, the burnished sword was made.’” He looked down at them. “That’s the one, yes?” Anna nodded, feeling this was a good sign. “And,” he continued, “I suppose this has something to do with the Nattmara that has come to Arendelle?” Anna gaped. “How did you know about the Nattmara?” “Just because you can’t see us doesn’t mean we’re not always there.” The Librarian King studied them a second more.
sentences.zh: “借心中光与暗，铸就这把锃亮之剑。’”他低头看着他们。“就是它，没错吧？”安娜点点头，觉得这是个好兆头。“而且，”他接着说，“我猜这跟降临阿伦黛尔的纳特玛拉脱不了干系？”安娜目瞪口呆。“你怎么知道纳特玛拉的？”“你们看不见我们，不代表我们就不在那儿。”图书管理员国王又端详了他们片刻。

sentences.en: It was impossible to make out any expression on the leader’s face.
sentences.zh: 根本看不出这位领袖脸上是什么表情。

sentences.en: The Hulder’s textured skin had taken on the appearance of the cracked rivulets of lava, and was hard to see against the molten backdrop.
sentences.zh: 胡尔德纹理分明的皮肤已变得如同熔岩上龟裂的细流，在熔岩背景的映衬下几乎难以辨认。

sentences.en: But then, he must have made a secret signal, because the guards bowed before each of them and then hurried away, keeping their backs to Anna and her friends.
sentences.zh: 不过，他一定是打了什么暗号，因为卫兵们朝他们每人都鞠了一躬，便匆匆退下，背对着安娜和她的朋友们。

sentences.en: It only took the hidden people a couple of steps until they seemed to have disappeared entirely, though Anna knew they must still be there, great masters of camouflage that they were.
sentences.zh: 那些隐藏者没走几步，就仿佛彻底消失不见了，可安娜知道他们一定还在那儿——他们可是伪装的大师。

sentences.en: The Librarian King turned. “Now, all of you, come with me.” Anna’s heart leapt.
sentences.zh: 图书管理员国王转过身。“现在，你们都跟我来。”安娜心头一喜。

sentences.en: At last—she had not led them astray! “We don’t always know the answer—but we do know where to find it,” the Librarian King continued.
sentences.zh: 终于——她没有把他们带错路！“我们未必总知道答案——但我们知道去哪儿找答案，”图书管理员国王接着说。

sentences.en: Allowing the humans to walk in front of them, the Librarian King and Echo escorted Anna, Elsa, and Kristoff away from the lake of molten rock and toward a tranquil tributary of water where rafts bumped and prodded against each other.
sentences.zh: 图书管理员国王和回声让人类走在前头，领着安娜、艾莎和克斯托夫离开熔岩湖，朝一条宁静的水汊走去，那里一只只木筏相互挤碰着。

sentences.en: Anna looked at Elsa and Kristoff in the gloom, and a smile spread across her face. “This could be it!” she whispered. “We may finally find the sword!” “Let’s wait and see,” said Elsa, ever the one to freeze the excited mood.
sentences.zh: 安娜在昏暗里看着艾莎和克斯托夫，脸上绽开了笑容。“说不定就是这儿了！”她低声说，“我们终于可能找到那把剑了！”“先看看再说，”艾莎说道，她向来是给热烈情绪降温的那个人。

sentences.en: Echo tugged at Kristoff’s tunic, and they began to toss stones into the water. “My assistant will help.
sentences.zh: 回声扯了扯克斯托夫的外衣，两人开始往水里扔石子。“我的助手会帮忙。”

sentences.en: She will take you to the Library of Lost Things,” the Librarian King told them. “If my people ever came across the legendary sword, it will be there—that is, if the sword truly exists.” Elsa shot Anna a look, and Anna bit her lip.
sentences.zh: “她会带你们去失物图书馆（Library of Lost Things），”图书管理员国王对他们说，“如果我的族人曾经碰到过那柄传说之剑，它一定就在那儿——当然，前提是那剑真的存在。”艾莎向安娜递了个眼神，安娜咬了咬嘴唇。

sentences.en: She hoped against hope that it did. “We are sorry for bringing the Nattmara to your door,” Elsa said.
sentences.zh: 她满心期盼它是真的。“把纳特玛拉带到你们家门口，我们很抱歉，”艾莎说。

sentences.en: It wasn’t lost on Anna that her sister had used the word we .
sentences.zh: 安娜注意到，妹妹用了“我们”这个词。

sentences.en: The Librarian King shook his head. “The Nattmara is one of the many natural enemies of the Huldrefólk—we both seek to reign the dark.
sentences.zh: 图书管理员国王摇摇头。“纳特玛拉是胡尔德民众多天敌之一——我们都想在黑暗中称王。”

sentences.en: But while the Huldrefólk love the night for its quiet privacy, the Nattmara prefers to use the dark as a weapon.
sentences.zh: 只不过胡尔德民喜爱夜晚，是因为它的静谧与隐秘；而纳特玛拉更喜欢把黑暗当作武器。

sentences.en: Fear not: the Nattmara cannot pass into the borders of our domain.
sentences.zh: 别怕：纳特玛拉进不了我们领地的边界。

sentences.en: As long as you’re within the Huldrefólk realm, the Nattmara cannot touch you.
sentences.zh: 只要你们身处胡尔德民的疆域之内，纳特玛拉就碰不到你们。

sentences.en: We are the hidden people.
sentences.zh: 我们是隐藏的民族。

sentences.en: We keep ourselves hidden, and now that you’re with us, we’ll keep you hidden as well.” Relief filled Anna, and then a thought stirred. “Umm, I have a question for you,” she said. “We lost a member of our group.
sentences.zh: 我们藏好自己，既然你们和我们在一起，我们也会把你们藏好。”安娜松了口气，随即一个念头冒了出来。“唔，我有件事想问你，”她说，“我们走失了一名同伴。”

sentences.en: Is it possible for the Huldrefólk to find him?
sentences.zh: 胡尔德民有可能找到他吗？

sentences.en: He’s kind of short and stocky, with a long silver beard that touches the floor, and he’s grumpy.” Anna paused, then added, “He’s nice!” The Librarian King inclined his head. “As you know, Huldrefólk are seekers of lost things.
sentences.zh: “他有点矮壮，留着一碰地银白长须，脾气还有点臭。”安娜顿了顿，又补了一句，“但他人很好！”图书管理员国王微微颔首。“正如你所知，胡尔德民是寻找失物的人。”

sentences.en: Collectors.
sentences.zh: 收藏家。

sentences.en: If your friend is still free of the Nattmara, then I’m sure we can locate him.” “Land ahoy!” Anna looked to the water, where a gray raft glided in front of them and bumped against the bank.
sentences.zh: “如果你的朋友还没被纳特玛拉缠上，那我肯定我们能找到他。”“陆地，到啦！”安娜朝水面望去，一只灰色木筏正滑到他们面前，撞上了岸堤。

sentences.en: A cheery-looking Hulder (as Anna thought she could make out a smile in the dim glowworms’ light) waved at them and leaned against the long pole she’d been using to steer the vessel. “Ahoy!
sentences.zh: 一名看着挺欢快的胡尔德（安娜觉得在昏暗的萤火虫光里能辨出她在微笑）朝他们挥手，身子斜靠在撑船的长篙上。“哟嗬！”

sentences.en: Ahoy!
sentences.zh: “哟嗬！”

sentences.en: Ahoy!” Echo cried out, and left the game of skipping rocks with Kristoff to fling herself onto the raft and into the new Hulder’s arms. “This is my assistant, Obscuren,” the Librarian King proclaimed. “She will help you find what you are looking for and will be your guide in my domain.” Anna scrambled onto the raft, settling herself next to Kristoff.
sentences.zh: “哟嗬！”回声喊着，丢下和克斯托夫打水漂的游戏，一下子扑到木筏上，投进那名新胡尔德的怀里。“这是我的助手奥布斯基伦（Obscuren），”图书管理员国王宣布道，“她会帮你们找到想要的东西，并在我的领地里做你们的向导。”安娜手脚并用地爬上木筏，在克斯托夫身旁坐下。

sentences.en: It was only then that she noticed the unusual material it was made of.
sentences.zh: 直到这时她才注意到木筏所用的奇特材料。

sentences.en: While rafts were almost always constructed of wood, this one seemed to be made of floating stone.
sentences.zh: 木筏几乎都是用木头造的，可这只却像是用浮石做的。

sentences.en: As she peered closer, she saw tiny holes perforating the surface, making the texture of the raft seem more like bread than rock. “I think this is a pumice raft,” Anna said to Kristoff, who nodded. “It is,” he said. “Rock from the volcano.” Anna felt a tug on her hair as Echo crawled into her lap, quietly chanting, “Row, row, row your raft!” “Say your goodbye,” the Librarian King instructed Echo. “It’s time for dinner.” The little Hulder’s eyes swam with tears. “Stay!” “I wish you could,” Anna said, and was surprised when she realized she meant it.
sentences.zh: 她凑近细看，发现表面布满细密的小孔，让筏子的质感更像面包而非石头。“我觉得这是浮石筏，”安娜对克斯托夫说，他点了点头。“是的，”他说，“火山里出来的石头。”安娜感到头发被扯了一下——回声爬到她腿上，轻声念着：“划呀，划呀，划你的筏！”“跟他们说再见吧，”图书管理员国王吩咐回声，“该吃晚饭了。”小胡尔德的眼里泛起泪光。“留下来！”“我也希望你能留下，”安娜说，随即惊讶地发现，这话她是由衷说的。

sentences.en: Miner’s Mountain was beautiful, full of unexpected surprises and even more unexpected friendships.
sentences.zh: 矿工山（Miner’s Mountain）真美，处处是不期而遇的惊喜，更有意想不到的友谊。

sentences.en: She liked the little Hulder and her penchant for flying ahead as fast as possible.
sentences.zh: 她喜欢这个小胡尔德，喜欢她总恨不得飞也似的冲在最前头的性子。

sentences.en: Anna bet Echo could show her many things—glowing crystals, ice caves, maybe even a sleeping bat or two—but she needed to fix her mistake before she could explore the wonders of the mountain further. “Besides, you’d be bored if you joined us,” Anna said. “We won’t be singing anymore, and being on a raft makes it hard for you to dash anywhere.” Head tilted, the little Hulder considered this bleak reality, then clambered out of the raft to join one of the Huldrefólk guards who’d seemingly materialized out of nowhere. “Bye!” Echo proclaimed from the riverbank, waving. “Bye-bye-bye!” Anna’s heart squeezed. “See you later.
sentences.zh: 安娜打赌，回声能带她看许多东西——发光的晶体、冰洞，或许还有一两只睡着的蝙蝠——可她得先弥补自己的过错，才能继续探索这座山的奇景。“再说，你要是跟来也会无聊的，”安娜说，“我们不会再唱歌了，而且乘着筏子，你也没法到处飞奔了。”小胡尔德歪着头，琢磨着这冷酷的现实，随后爬出木筏，去加入一名仿佛凭空冒出来的胡尔德卫兵。“再见！”回声在河岸上挥着手宣布。“拜拜拜拜！”安娜的心揪了一下。“回头见。”

sentences.en: Stay out of dark abysses, okay?” Elsa was the last to step onto the raft.
sentences.zh: “别去黑暗的深渊，好吗？”艾莎是最后一个踏上木筏的。

sentences.en: When she’d settled her cloak around her, she looked back at the Librarian King. “Thank you,” she said. “For all your help.
sentences.zh: 等她拢好披风，回头望向图书管理员国王。“谢谢你，”她说，“谢谢你所有的帮助。”

sentences.en: I promise we’ll keep your secret, and we will keep the mines closed.
sentences.zh: “我保证会替你们保守秘密，也会让矿井保持封闭。”

sentences.en: Your city will remain hidden.” The Librarian King bowed in thanks, and then Obscuren pushed them across the glassy surface of the river.
sentences.zh: “你们的城市会一直隐藏下去。”图书管理员国王鞠躬致谢，随后奥布斯基伦撑着筏子，载他们滑过如镜的河面。

sentences.en: The raft rocked as they navigated the underground waterway, the air refreshingly cooler now.
sentences.zh: 木筏在地下水道里摇晃前行，空气此刻凉爽得让人心旷神怡。

sentences.en: Obscuren took in their drooping eyelids. “You can sleep,” she said. “I know my way around the river.
sentences.zh: 奥布斯基伦注意到他们耷拉着的眼皮。“你们可以睡，”她说，“我认得这条河的路。”

sentences.en: And as the Librarian King said, you are hidden here with me, even from the Nattmara.” “Are you absolutely…” Whatever Kristoff had been going to say was lost in a yawn. “The Nattmara cannot find our domain,” Obscuren reminded them. “We are cloaked from it.
sentences.zh: “而且正如图书管理员国王所说，你们和我在一起是隐藏的，连纳特玛拉也寻不到。”“你确定……”克斯托夫本来要说什么，却被一个哈欠吞了下去。“纳特玛拉找不到我们的领地，”奥布斯基伦提醒他们，“我们被它遮蔽了。”

sentences.en: You can rest here, safely, without any fear of losing yourself over to its influence.
sentences.zh: “你们可以安心在此歇息，不必担心被它影响而迷失自我。”

sentences.en: Sleep.
sentences.zh: “睡吧。”

sentences.en: Rest.
sentences.zh: “歇着吧。”

sentences.en: I’ll wake you when we reach our destination.” Obscuren had barely finished before a snore ripped out of Kristoff, and in the next second, Elsa, too, was asleep.
sentences.zh: “到了目的地我会叫醒你们。”奥布斯基伦话音未落，克斯托夫已经打起了呼噜，紧接着艾莎也睡着了。

sentences.en: Anna, however, stayed awake.
sentences.zh: 可安娜，却还醒着。

sentences.en: Though she had been daydreaming about sleeping, she found she couldn’t close her eyes.
sentences.zh: 尽管她方才还憧憬着能睡一觉，却发现眼睛怎么也闭不上。

sentences.en: Every time she did, her stomach hurt too much.
sentences.zh: 每次合眼，她的胃就疼得厉害。

sentences.en: Because each moment asleep was a moment she wasn’t fixing her biggest mistake: the Nattmara she’d accidentally welcomed into Arendelle with a spell.
sentences.zh: 因为每睡过去一刻，她就有一刻没在弥补自己最大的过错：那头被她用咒语无意间迎进阿伦黛尔的纳特玛拉。

sentences.en: Obscuren’s voice interrupted her thoughts, and Anna pulled herself out of them. “Sorry, what was that?” Anna asked. “I said,” the Hulder repeated, “that you should sleep, too.” Obscuren pushed on the pole, and the water sighed as the raft sliced through it.
sentences.zh: 奥布斯基伦的声音打断了她的思绪，安娜把自己从中拽了出来。“抱歉，你说什么？”安娜问。“我说，”胡尔德重复道，“你也该睡了。”奥布斯基伦撑了一下篙，木筏破水而行，水声仿佛一声轻叹。

sentences.en: The river flowed through winding tunnels with low ceilings, though here and there little beaches seemed to jut into the waterway, and Anna thought she could make out the distant shape of a Hulder or two watching them.
sentences.zh: 河水穿过低矮蜿蜒的隧道，虽说这儿那儿有小片沙滩探入水道，安娜觉得自己能辨认出远处有一两个胡尔德的影子在看着他们。

sentences.en: This close to a Hulder who was not trying to kill her, she could finally make out a more definite shape.
sentences.zh: 离一个并不想杀她的胡尔德这么近，她终于能看清更分明的轮廓。

sentences.en: Obscuren looked almost human but for an overall spindly appearance, pointed ears, and changing skin.
sentences.zh: 奥布斯基伦看起来几乎像人，只是整体显得瘦长，长着尖耳朵，皮肤还会变化。

sentences.en: At the moment, the Hulder’s eyes were a beautiful shade of orange, a color that made Anna think of the end of autumn or the start of spring.
sentences.zh: 此刻，这名胡尔德的眼睛是漂亮的橘色，那种颜色让安娜想起晚秋将尽，或是早春方始。

sentences.en: They seemed to take in everything around them, and as Obscuren looked at Anna, Anna wondered if the seeker of things could find Anna’s deepest secret in her eyes. “Obscuren,” Anna said, “do you know how the Nattmara came to Arendelle?
sentences.zh: 那双眼仿佛将周遭一切尽收眼底，而当奥布斯基伦望向安娜时，安娜不禁想，这位寻物者能不能从她眼中读出最深的秘密。“奥布斯基伦，”安娜说，“你知道纳特玛拉是怎么来到阿伦黛尔的吗？”

sentences.en: I think I know, but I’m not entirely sure.
sentences.zh: “我想我知道，但不完全确定。”

sentences.en: The Blight started before the Nattmara arrived.
sentences.zh: “枯萎病（The Blight）在纳特玛拉到来之前就开始了。”

sentences.en: I’m a bit murky on the details.” She held her breath, waiting for Obscuren to somehow say the words that were blaring through her mind as loudly as a goatherd playing the tungehorn: the spell .
sentences.zh: “具体细节我有点模糊。”她屏住呼吸，等着奥布斯基伦说出那几个正像牧羊人吹响图恩号（tungehorn）般在她脑中轰鸣的字眼：那道咒语。

sentences.en: It must have been the spell, as much as it didn’t make sense that the animals and crops had grown sick before she’d read it.
sentences.zh: “一定是那道咒语——尽管动物和庄稼在我念出它之前就病倒了，这怎么也说不通。”

sentences.en: But after she read the spell, the wolf appeared.
sentences.zh: “可我念过咒语之后，那头狼就出现了。”

sentences.en: Of that much Anna was certain—just as she was certain it was her fault.
sentences.zh: “这一点安娜很确定——就像她确定这是她的错一样。”

sentences.en: Obscuren was silent, but it wasn’t the kind of sharp silence of being ignored.
sentences.zh: 奥布斯基伦沉默着，但那不是被无视时那种尖锐的沉默。

sentences.en: This quiet had a thoughtful quality to it, as though she were weighing each word before speaking. “A Nattmara doesn’t appear out of thin air,” the Hulder said. “They are made, formed from an event in a person’s life that grows so big they can’t keep it inside anymore, and the fear becomes so large that it takes on a life of its own.” Anna nodded.
sentences.zh: 这份安静带着思索的意味，仿佛她在开口前要掂量每一个字。“纳特玛拉不会凭空出现，”胡尔德说，“它们是被‘造’出来的，由一个人生命中某件事滋长而成，大到再也无法藏在心里，恐惧膨胀到有了自己的生命。”安娜点了点头。

sentences.en: Yes, that was what Sorenson had said.
sentences.zh: 对，这正是索伦森说过的话。

sentences.en: The fear is too big to keep inside. “Sooo,” Anna said, “you don’t think that someone could have, I don’t know”—she tucked a strand of ruddy hair behind her ear—“said a spell, or something, and brought the Nattmara to Arendelle?” Obscuren gave a shake of her head. “I don’t believe the poems that humans call spells are really anything other than just that: poems.
sentences.zh: “恐惧太大，藏不住了。”“那、那个，”安娜说，“所以你不觉得，会有人，我也不知道”——她把一缕红发别到耳后——“念了什么咒语之类，就把纳特玛拉带到了阿伦黛尔？”奥布斯基伦摇了摇头。“我不相信人类称作咒语的那些诗，除了诗本身，还能是什么别的东西。”

sentences.en: They may be able to conjure a beautiful image or a moment of time, but that is a different kind of magic entirely.” Anna wasn’t sure what to say, but she was comforted.
sentences.zh: “它们或许能召唤出一幅美丽的画面，或凝固某一瞬间，但那完全是另一种魔法。”安娜不知该说什么，却感到一丝安慰。

sentences.en: Because Anna had read a spell…but it sounded like even if she had never said it out loud, the Nattmara still would have come to the kingdom.
sentences.zh: 因为安娜的确念过一道咒语……但听起来，即便她从没念出声，纳特玛拉也照样会降临这个王国。

sentences.en: Anna still would have accidentally called it, with or without a poem.
sentences.zh: 安娜还是会无意中将它召唤而来，念不念那首诗都一样。

sentences.en: Because the night that it had materialized from her dreams was the same night she’d heard Elsa holding a council meeting without her, and she had felt her heart break a little.
sentences.zh: 因为它从她梦境中现形的那一夜，正是她听见艾莎撇开她召开御前会议的那一夜，而那一刻，她的心微微碎了一块。

sentences.en: It was the moment she had realized her greatest fear had come true: that Elsa really and truly had no need for her at all.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，她意识到自己最大的恐惧成真了：艾莎真的、确实根本不需要她。

sentences.en: And because of that, her nightmare—her fear —had manifested in the form of the Nattmara that was now stalking them all. “And I guess,” she said, trying to keep her voice light, “if there’s no spell to call a Nattmara, then there’s probably no spell to banish one, right?” Obscuren shook her head. “I wouldn’t think so.
sentences.zh: 也正因为如此，她的噩梦——她的恐惧——才化作了如今追踪着他们所有人的纳特玛拉。“那么我猜，”她努力让声音显得轻松，“既然没有召唤纳特玛拉的咒语，大概也就没有驱散它的咒语，对吧？”奥布斯基伦摇了摇头。“我想不会有的。”

sentences.en: I’ve only ever heard of one warrior willing to face the Nattmara, and that was Aren, with his mythical Revolute Blade that contained a strange power.” Revolute.
sentences.zh: “我只听说过一位敢直面纳特玛拉的战士，那就是阿伦（Aren），凭着他的神话之刃回旋之刃，那剑蕴含着奇异的力量。”回旋。

sentences.en: With Kristoff and Elsa asleep and nestled against her back, and Obscuren in the front, keeping an eye on Anna and her friends, the mythical curved sword shone like a lighthouse in the dark river of Anna’s worry, and, at last, she let her eyes drift shut to sleep.
sentences.zh: 克斯托夫和艾莎在安娜背后沉沉睡去，贴着她；奥布斯基伦在前头，留意着安娜和她的朋友。那柄神话般的弯剑，如同灯塔般在安娜忧虑的暗河中闪耀，而她，终于让眼皮垂下，睡了过去。

chapters.title: Chapter Nineteen
chapters.en:
WHEN OBSCUREN WOKE ANNA, she felt better rested than she had in a long, long time.

Next to her, Kristoff stretched, half his hair smooshed against his cheek where he’d lain on it. “Up, up, and away,” Kristoff said with a yawn.

Elsa, however, still managed to look regal, even though Anna could see the pattern of pumice pores on her face. Anna giggled, motioning to her sister’s cheek.

“You should take a look at yourself,” Elsa grumbled with half a smile.

Anna peered into the river. Sure enough, she looked the same as she always did when she woke up: a bit like a woodland creature with a slobber problem. Anna patted down her stray hairs with river water, and she found comfort in the way that some things stayed the same. Elsa smiled at her, and Anna guessed she was thinking the same thing, too.

“We’re here,” Obscuren said as they glided up to a post.

While they waited for Obscuren to secure the raft, Anna looked around, but even holding out her wrist with the glowworm bracelet, she couldn’t see any sign of a library…or where one could possibly be. The banks of the underground river were narrow, no wider than a foot or two, and as far as she could tell, nothing had been carved into the rock’s surface except for a few crumbly-looking steps.

“Where is it?” Anna asked. It had been nice to sleep and all, but being awake again meant she was more aware than ever of the time that was slipping away. They had only one more day of sun and a single night left before the third sunrise made the Nattmara’s reality permanent—assuming that the spell really had been what brought the Nattmara to Arendelle in the first place. Obscuren hadn’t though so, but Anna couldn’t shake Sorenson’s words. All myths contain a kernel of hard truth. The spell might not have been real magic, but that didn’t mean the warning wasn’t true. At any rate, Anna was not willing to risk it.

“Up, up, up and away,” Obscuren said, seeming to settle into another’s words comfortably, as if the conversation of the previous night had been a bit of a strain for her.

Elsa wobbled out of the raft first, followed by Kristoff. When he turned to offer his hand to help Anna step out, she ignored it and leapt over the side. Obscuren indicated with a nod that they should take off their glowworm bracelets and leave the little creatures on the post. With a wistful sigh, Anna unwrapped the glowworm and gave it a little pat in thanks.

“Will it be okay here?” she asked.

“Home is where the heart is,” Obscuren said, and when Anna looked for clarification, the Librarian King’s assistant explained, “I’ll take them back with me. They’re not needed where we’re going.”

And with that, Obscuren left the raft behind and stepped off into the darkness, silent as the moon sailing through the night sky.

Anna, Elsa, and Kristoff followed her, not nearly as gracefully, but they managed to reach the beginning of the steps and started to feel their way up the side of the rock, following the carved path that wound its way to the cave ceiling.

“Stop a moment,” Obscuren said, and there were a few quick taps, and then a creak as the Hulder pushed open a square hatch in the ceiling. Light streamed through.

Squinting her eyes against the unexpected brightness, Anna emerged from the dirt floor of a round room with stone walls carved with runes and windows blocked by grassy tussocks. She caught a glimpse of blue in the window. Her heart leapt. “Wait, is that sky?” she asked.

“We’re in a turf house,” Elsa said as she shrugged off her cloak and her mother’s scarf before stepping aside from the trapdoor to make space for Kristoff to climb up beside them.

Of course! Turf houses dotted Arendelle’s wilderness of scraggly birches and spruces. They were made by digging a dwelling-sized hole deep into the ground, which was then covered by a roof made of grass. Turf houses came in all shapes and sizes, but Anna’s favorites were the ones that looked like Earth Giants sunk into the soil, the green grass of the roofs resembling troll hair. Anna looked around, hoping to see a neat row of books. “Um, Obscuren, are you sure this is your library?” she said.

It didn’t look so much like a library as it did a too-crammed gift shop. Sure, there were a few books scattered here and there, with bleached covers that looked like they’d been forgotten long ago and left out to wither in the sun. But mostly there were items.

There were sideways chairs lying on top of rolled-up rugs next to a careful stack of mirrors. There was a pile of gardening tools, broken clay figurines, and more than one pile of rusted old keys. And there were socks—lots and lots of mismatched socks.

“Welcome to the Library of Lost Things,” Obscuren said. Above the ground and in the warm light of the turf house, the Hulder seemed to look less like rock and more like a tree, softly sprouting leaves where before there had been the rough texture of a pebble.

“Before you say anything, we did not steal any of these things. We simply find things that are lost and give them homes. That includes everything from missing spectacles, to hair bands, to legendary swords. Please,” the Hulder continued, stepping aside, “feel free to roam.”

“Thank you!” Anna cheered.

“Can the Nattmara find us up here? Or are we still hidden and all that?” Kristoff asked, peering out a window.

“With me, you are still hidden from the Nattmara,” Obscuren said.

“Phew!” Kristoff said.

“That’s a relief,” said Elsa, peering through the mess of objects.

“We should split up,” Anna said, then looked at Elsa. “Right?”

Elsa nodded, and so the three of them began their search.

Some of the lost objects were beautiful—bronze vases from another age and even a necklace of heavy sapphires that Anna thought would complement Gerda’s eyes—if Anna were able to turn them back from yellow, that is. She set the necklace down and hurried to the next pile. She picked up a round mirror. It was little, meant to slip into a pocket, and clasped cleverly to look like a clamshell. She opened it, then set it to the side. It was pretty, but not what she was looking for.

Scanning the room, Anna searched for a glint of metal, trying to find anything that could possibly be the sword of myth. She moved aside a rickety chair and a mountain of missing socks and tried to push down her disappointment, but it kept rising, like a hot-air balloon, not wanting to be weighed down. There had to be something in this library. Anna’s thoughts skidded to a halt. Her eye had caught on a statue in the center of the room. It was a figure of a human girl in a sky-blue dress with a glittering train, and a platinum blond braid. It looked to be about as tall as Elsa’s knee, and it also happened to look a lot like Elsa.

Anna gasped as she stepped closer. It was a statue of Elsa. Specifically, the one the sisters had installed in the town cuckoo clock a few years before. Last spring, the Elsa figure had disappeared in a sudden storm, blown away by unusually strong winds. Anna peered at the statue.

A little green wreath with candles had been perched on top of statue Elsa’s head, and Anna had the briefest thought that the statue looked more comfortable here, surrounded by other wondrous things, than it had looming above the masses, day in and day out. She was glad the Huldrefólk had found a new home for it, and so she kept searching.

But no matter how hard or long they looked, they did not find the coveted sword in the turf house.

The closest things to a mythical sword they’d managed to unearth were a few shields and helmets from the time of King Runeard, but nothing older than that. Anna’s shoulders slumped. If the Huldrefólk didn’t have Revolute, and if Sorenson was lost, and if the trolls had fled the Nattmara…what were they going to do? They were running out of places to find answers.

“There’s not a single sword in this library!” Elsa said to Obscuren an hour later as the gang flopped in front of a large fireplace to eat from Kristoff’s traveler’s pack.

Obscuren sighed. “So it appears.” The Hulder’s skin had taken on the runes of the turf house walls, and speaking to Obscuren now almost felt like talking to alphabet soup. She seemed to droop slightly, and it was clear to Anna that Obscuren wasn’t used to having to converse so much.

“Why not?” Kristoff asked. “Arendelle’s history seems to be full of swords, as far as I can tell. Why didn’t the Huldrefólk ever find one? Maybe it’s at another location?”

“Sometimes,” Obscuren said, settling down onto the dirt floor to rest, “great swords are buried with their heroes.”

“ARRGH!”

Anna’s heart began to pound furiously as a cry that sounded a bit like a seagull reverberated through the turf house. Wide-eyed, Anna turned to see what had made such a terrifying sound—expecting to see the Nattmara or a mob of yellow-eyed villagers coming for them—but all she saw was Elsa, who’d leapt to her feet.

“Well, that’s just great!” Elsa’s blue eyes flashed and her cheeks reddened. For the first time in a long time, Anna thought that her sister looked visibly upset.

“What’s wrong?” Anna scrambled to her feet, too. “We just need to find out where Aren was buried—”

Elsa snorted, and it was such an un-Elsa-like sound that Anna grew quiet.

“We can’t find where he was buried.” Elsa paced the floor. “Don’t you remember the story? Aren was swallowed by a dragon!”

Anna blinked. “He was?” She’d forgotten that. She glanced over at Kristoff, who was looking at Elsa with something like awe, as though he couldn’t quite believe that calm and collected Elsa was panicking.

“Yes,” Elsa said, exasperated. “A dragon came to the fjord, and it threatened to eat everyone! And so Aren, our greatest leader besides King Runeard, who loved his home and people more than anything, decided to go face the dragon…who”—Elsa paused, then changed to her most dramatic voice—“‘lives where the sea is a sky,’ and never came back.” Elsa took a deep breath. “Because the dragon swallowed him. And dragons don’t exist, and neither does this sword, and Anna, oh, I’ve tried listening, but there’s nothing we can do!”

“Curious,” Obscuren called out. During Elsa’s tirade, the Hulder had gone to a stone wall. “That’s not what all stories say.” She waved a delicate arm at the walls around them. “In that long-ago time when Huldrefólk and humans were more comfortable with each other, we would meet here, in a place of compromise between earth and sky. Each community carved their stories into these walls. This is one of the oldest turf houses. And here, the myth of Aren changes, slightly.

“This”—the Hulder pointed at a carved rune that looked like a sideways S-shape—“according to our legend, says that a great danger came from the waters, and in order to save his home and people that he loved, Aren set out in a boat and was never seen again.”

“How is that any better?” Elsa asked, and Anna was shocked to see her sister’s foot twitch, as though she had just resisted the urge to stomp her feet. “That just means Revolute is probably somewhere at the bottom of the ocean, and even if it were possible to scour all the waters, we just don’t have time.” Elsa turned sharply, sending her braid whipping out behind her and almost smacking a shocked Kristoff across the nose. “So you see,” she addressed Anna, “we’re never going to find Revolute!”

But actually…Anna did see.

Anna opened her mouth. “Elsa—”

“The Nattmara is still out there, the Blight chokes the land, and all of our friends are probably stuck in a nightmare by now!”

Kristoff flinched at her words.

“You wanted to visit the Huldrefólk because they were supposed to be able to tell us something,” Elsa continued, “to show us the way to a made-up sword. Is there anything else, any other clue—”

“Elsa—”

Her sister threw her hands in the air. “The people are all counting on me!”

“ELSA!”

Elsa’s furor stumbled to a halt, and, panting, she looked over at Anna, who pushed away a smile.

“How can you be so calm at a time like this?” Elsa demanded, and Anna had to stop from giggling.

“I’m calm because I learned from the best,” Anna said, and she could feel a fiery hope burning bright in her chest. “And because I know where Revolute is.”
chapters.zh:
当奥布斯基伦叫醒安娜时，她觉得自己睡得比许久以来都要踏实。

她身旁，克斯托夫伸了个懒腰，压在脸颊那侧的头发睡得半塌。“起，起，出发啦，”克斯托夫打着哈欠说。

可艾莎却依旧一副女王派头，尽管安娜能看到她脸上浮石气孔印出的纹路。

安娜咯咯笑起来，指了指妹妹的脸颊。“你该照照自己，”艾莎半带笑意地嘟囔道。

安娜朝河里望去。

果然，她醒来时的模样跟往常一样：有点像只流着口水的小林妖。

安娜用河水把乱翘的头发抚平，有些事始终如一，这让她感到安心。

艾莎冲她微微一笑，安娜猜妹妹想的也是同一件事。“我们到了，”奥布斯基伦说，筏子正滑向一根木桩。

等奥布斯基伦把筏子系稳的工夫，安娜环顾四周，可即便她伸出戴着萤火虫手环的手腕，也看不出半点图书馆的影子……更不知它究竟会在哪儿。

地下河的河岸很窄，不过一两尺宽，而在她看来，岩石表面除了几级看着酥脆易碎的台阶，什么也没凿出来。“它在哪儿？”安娜问。

睡上一觉固然好，可醒来后，她比以往任何时候都更清楚地感到时间在悄悄溜走。

他们只剩最后一个白昼和一夜，第三次日出就会让纳特玛拉的存在成为永久——前提是，那道咒语真的就是当初把纳特玛拉带到阿伦黛尔的元凶。

奥布斯基伦不这么认为，可安娜甩不掉索伦森的话。

所有神话都藏着一粒坚硬的真相。

那道咒语或许不是真正的魔法，可这不等于其中的警告就不真。

无论如何，安娜都不愿拿这个去赌。“起，起，起，出发啦，”奥布斯基伦说道，她似乎很自在地安进别人的话里，仿佛前一晚的对话让她有点吃不消。

艾莎先摇摇晃晃地下了筏，克斯托夫紧跟在后。

他转身伸手想扶安娜下去，她却没理会，直接翻身跳下了船舷。

奥布斯基伦点点头示意，他们该摘下萤火虫手环，把小家伙留在木桩上。

安娜怅然叹了口气，解开萤火虫，轻轻拍了拍以示感谢。“它留在这儿没事吧？”她问。“心在哪儿，家就在哪儿，”奥布斯基伦说；见安娜一脸困惑，这位图书管理员国王的助手解释道：“我会把它们带回去。”

“我们要去的地方，用不着它们。”说罢，奥布斯基伦丢下木筏，迈步走进黑暗，静得像滑过夜空的月亮。

安娜、艾莎和克斯托夫跟在她身后，姿态远没那么优雅，但他们好歹摸到了台阶起点，顺着蜿蜒通向洞顶的凿路，摸索着往岩壁上去。“停一下，”奥布斯基伦说，接着几声轻快的敲击，随即是吱呀一响——胡尔德推开了头顶一方方形活板门。

光从门里倾泻而下。

安娜眯起眼，抵挡这突如其来的明亮，从一间圆形屋子的泥地中钻了出来——石墙上刻满符文，窗户被草丛堵着。

她瞥见窗里的一抹蓝。

她心头一跳。“等等，那是天空吗？”她问。“我们在一座草皮屋里，”艾莎说着，卸下披风和母亲那条围巾，从活板门边让开，好让克斯托夫爬上来与他们并肩。

当然了！

在阿伦黛尔那片长着稀疏白桦与云杉的荒野上，草皮屋星罗棋布。

它们是往地下深挖出一个能住人的坑，再用草皮盖成屋顶。

草皮屋形形色色、大小不一，可安娜最喜欢那些像大地巨人（Earth Giants）陷进土里的样式，屋顶的绿草活像地精的头发。

安娜四下张望，盼着能看见整整齐齐一排书。“唔，奥布斯基伦，你确定这儿就是你的图书馆？”她说。

这里不像图书馆，倒更像一个塞得太满的礼品店。

当然，这儿那儿散落着几本书，封皮泛白，像是早被遗忘、搁在太阳下晒得发蔫。

但更多的，是物件。

横倒的椅子压在卷起的毯子上，旁边是一摞码得齐整的镜子。

还有一堆园艺工具、破碎的泥偶，以及不止一堆锈迹斑斑的旧钥匙。

还有袜子——许许多多配不成对的袜子。“欢迎来到失物图书馆，”奥布斯基伦说。

在地面上、在草皮屋暖洋洋的光里，这名胡尔德看着没那么像石头了，倒更像一棵树，原本粗糙如卵石的纹理处，悄悄抽出了叶芽。“在你开口之前，我们可没偷过这里任何东西。”

“我们只是找到丢失的东西，给它们一个家。”

“从失踪的眼镜、发带，到传说中的宝剑，统统包括在内。”

“请吧，”胡尔德侧过身，继续说道，“随便逛。”“谢谢！”安娜欢快地应道。“纳特玛拉能在这里找到我们吗？”

“还是说我们仍然藏得好好的？”克斯托夫问，从窗口往外张望。“有我在，你们仍对纳特玛拉隐身，”奥布斯基伦说。“呼！”克斯托夫说。“总算松口气，”艾莎透过满屋杂物望出去，说道。“我们分头找吧，”安娜说，又看向艾莎，“对吧？”艾莎点点头，于是三人开始分头搜寻。

有些失物很美——来自另一个时代的青铜花瓶，甚至还有一条沉甸甸的蓝宝石项链，安娜觉得衬格达（Gerda）的眼睛正合适——当然，得她先把格达的眼珠从黄色变回来才行。

她放下项链，赶向下一堆。

她捡起一面圆镜。

镜子很小，本是要塞进衣袋的，搭扣做得巧妙，看着像只蛤壳。

她打开看了看，便放到一旁。

是漂亮，可不是她要找的东西。

安娜扫视全屋，搜寻着金属的微光，想找出任何可能是那柄神话之剑的东西。

她拨开一把摇摇晃晃的椅子和一座由失踪袜子堆成的山，想压下失望，可它却像热气球般不断升起，不愿被压住。

这间图书馆里，必定有什么吧。

安娜的思绪猛地刹住。

她的目光被屋子中央的一座雕像攫住了。

那是一个人类女孩的像，穿着天蓝色长裙，裙裾流光溢彩，还编着一头铂金色的辫子。

它大约只到艾莎的膝盖高，而且——巧的是——长得很像艾莎。

安娜走近一步，倒吸一口气。

那是一座艾莎的雕像。

确切地说，是姐妹俩几年前装进城里布谷鸟钟里的那一尊。

去年春天，这尊艾莎像在一场突如其来的风暴中失踪，被异常猛烈的风吹走了。

安娜端详着雕像。

雕像艾莎的头上搁着一圈点着蜡烛的小绿冠，安娜闪过一个念头：比起日复一日高踞众人头顶，这尊雕像待在这儿、被其他奇物环绕，似乎更自在些。

她很高兴胡尔德民给它找了新家，于是继续搜寻。

可不管他们找得多卖力、多久，都没在那间草皮屋里找见那柄梦寐以求的剑。

他们翻出来的、最接近的所谓神话之剑，不过是鲁内尔德王（King Runeard）时代的几面盾牌和头盔，再没有更古老的东西。

安娜的肩膀垮了下来。

如果胡尔德民没有回旋之刃，如果索伦森下落不明，如果地精们也逃离了纳特玛拉……他们还能怎么办？

他们能去找答案的地方，快要用光了。“这图书馆里一把剑都没有！”一小时后，艾莎对奥布斯基伦说道，几个人正瘫在巨大的壁炉前，吃着克斯托夫行囊里的干粮。

奥布斯基伦叹了口气。“看来是这样。”胡尔德的皮肤已染上草皮屋墙上的符文，此刻跟奥布斯基伦说话，几乎像在和一锅字母汤对话。

她似乎微微耷拉着，安娜一眼就看出，奥布斯基伦不习惯说这么多话。“为什么没有？”克斯托夫问，“据我所知，阿伦黛尔的历史里好像满是剑啊。”

胡尔德民怎么就一把都没找到呢？

“也许在别的什么地方？”“有时候，”奥布斯基伦在泥地上坐下歇息，说道，“伟大的剑会和它们的英雄一起下葬。”“啊啊啊！”一声有点像海鸥的呐喊在草皮屋里回荡，安娜的心猛地狂跳起来。

安娜瞪大眼睛转头，想看清是什么发出这可怕的声响——她本以为会看见纳特玛拉，或一群黄眼村民杀过来——可她只看见艾莎，已经一跃而起。“这下可好了！”艾莎蓝眼睛一闪，脸颊涨得通红。

这是长久以来头一回，安娜觉得妹妹明显心烦意乱。“怎么了？”安娜也慌忙站起。“我们只要弄清阿伦葬在哪儿就行——”艾莎哼了一声，那声音太不像艾莎了，安娜顿时安静下来。“我们找不到他葬在哪儿。”艾莎在地板上踱步，“你不记得了吗，那个故事？”

“阿伦被龙吞了！”安娜眨了眨眼。“他被吞了？”她把这事忘了。

她瞥了克斯托夫一眼，他正带着几分敬畏望着艾莎，仿佛不敢相信冷静自持的艾莎居然也会慌神。“对，”艾莎懊恼地说，“一条龙来到峡湾，威胁要把所有人都吃掉！”

“于是阿伦——除了鲁内尔德王之外我们最伟大的领袖，他爱家乡和百姓胜过一切——决定去直面那条龙……那条龙”——艾莎顿了顿，换上最戏剧化的腔调——“‘住在大海化作天空的地方’，再也没回来。”艾莎深吸一口气，“因为龙把他吞了。”

“而龙根本不存在，这把剑也不存在，安娜，唉，我试过倾听了，可我们无能为力！”“有意思，”奥布斯基伦喊道。

方才艾莎长篇大论时，胡尔德走到了一面石墙前。“并非所有故事都这么讲。”她纤细的手臂朝四周的墙壁一挥，“在很久以前，胡尔德民和人类还相处得更自在，我们会在此相会，在这天地之间折中的一处地方。”

每个族裔都把自己的故事刻在这些墙上。

这是最古老的草皮屋之一。

而在这里，阿伦的神话略有不同。“这个——”胡尔德指着一道刻成横卧S形的符文——“按我们的传说，意思是：巨大的危险自水中而来，为了拯救他深爱的家乡与百姓，阿伦乘船出海，从此再没出现。”“这又有什么好？”艾莎问；安娜惊讶地看见妹妹的脚抽动了一下，像是刚忍住跺脚的冲动。“那只说明回旋之刃多半沉在海底某处，而就算搜遍所有水域是可能的，我们也根本没时间。”艾莎猛地转身，辫子甩在身后，差点抽中一脸震惊的克斯托夫的鼻子。“所以你看，”她对安娜说，“我们永远找不到回旋之刃了！”可实际上……安娜看懂了。

安娜张了张嘴。“艾莎——”“纳特玛拉还在外面，枯萎病扼住了大地，而我们所有的朋友这会儿怕是都困在噩梦里了！”克斯托夫被她的话刺得缩了一下。“你执意要拜访胡尔德民，是因为他们本该能告诉我们些什么，”艾莎接着说，“给我们指出那把子虚乌有的剑的方向。”

“还有什么别的吗，任何别的线索——”“艾莎——”妹妹把双手往空中一摊。“子民们都指望着我呢！”“艾莎！”艾莎的怒火戛然而止，她喘着气看向安娜，而安娜把笑意压了下去。“这种时候你怎么还能这么镇定？”艾莎质问道；安娜差点笑出声。“我镇定，是因为我向最棒的人学过，”安娜说，胸口能感到一团炽热的希望在燃烧，“还因为我知道回旋之刃在哪儿。”

sentences.en: WHEN OBSCUREN WOKE ANNA, she felt better rested than she had in a long, long time.
sentences.zh: 当奥布斯基伦叫醒安娜时，她觉得自己睡得比许久以来都要踏实。

sentences.en: Next to her, Kristoff stretched, half his hair smooshed against his cheek where he’d lain on it. “Up, up, and away,” Kristoff said with a yawn.
sentences.zh: 她身旁，克斯托夫伸了个懒腰，压在脸颊那侧的头发睡得半塌。“起，起，出发啦，”克斯托夫打着哈欠说。

sentences.en: Elsa, however, still managed to look regal, even though Anna could see the pattern of pumice pores on her face.
sentences.zh: 可艾莎却依旧一副女王派头，尽管安娜能看到她脸上浮石气孔印出的纹路。

sentences.en: Anna giggled, motioning to her sister’s cheek. “You should take a look at yourself,” Elsa grumbled with half a smile.
sentences.zh: 安娜咯咯笑起来，指了指妹妹的脸颊。“你该照照自己，”艾莎半带笑意地嘟囔道。

sentences.en: Anna peered into the river.
sentences.zh: 安娜朝河里望去。

sentences.en: Sure enough, she looked the same as she always did when she woke up: a bit like a woodland creature with a slobber problem.
sentences.zh: 果然，她醒来时的模样跟往常一样：有点像只流着口水的小林妖。

sentences.en: Anna patted down her stray hairs with river water, and she found comfort in the way that some things stayed the same.
sentences.zh: 安娜用河水把乱翘的头发抚平，有些事始终如一，这让她感到安心。

sentences.en: Elsa smiled at her, and Anna guessed she was thinking the same thing, too. “We’re here,” Obscuren said as they glided up to a post.
sentences.zh: 艾莎冲她微微一笑，安娜猜妹妹想的也是同一件事。“我们到了，”奥布斯基伦说，筏子正滑向一根木桩。

sentences.en: While they waited for Obscuren to secure the raft, Anna looked around, but even holding out her wrist with the glowworm bracelet, she couldn’t see any sign of a library…or where one could possibly be.
sentences.zh: 等奥布斯基伦把筏子系稳的工夫，安娜环顾四周，可即便她伸出戴着萤火虫手环的手腕，也看不出半点图书馆的影子……更不知它究竟会在哪儿。

sentences.en: The banks of the underground river were narrow, no wider than a foot or two, and as far as she could tell, nothing had been carved into the rock’s surface except for a few crumbly-looking steps. “Where is it?” Anna asked.
sentences.zh: 地下河的河岸很窄，不过一两尺宽，而在她看来，岩石表面除了几级看着酥脆易碎的台阶，什么也没凿出来。“它在哪儿？”安娜问。

sentences.en: It had been nice to sleep and all, but being awake again meant she was more aware than ever of the time that was slipping away.
sentences.zh: 睡上一觉固然好，可醒来后，她比以往任何时候都更清楚地感到时间在悄悄溜走。

sentences.en: They had only one more day of sun and a single night left before the third sunrise made the Nattmara’s reality permanent—assuming that the spell really had been what brought the Nattmara to Arendelle in the first place.
sentences.zh: 他们只剩最后一个白昼和一夜，第三次日出就会让纳特玛拉的存在成为永久——前提是，那道咒语真的就是当初把纳特玛拉带到阿伦黛尔的元凶。

sentences.en: Obscuren hadn’t though so, but Anna couldn’t shake Sorenson’s words.
sentences.zh: 奥布斯基伦不这么认为，可安娜甩不掉索伦森的话。

sentences.en: All myths contain a kernel of hard truth.
sentences.zh: 所有神话都藏着一粒坚硬的真相。

sentences.en: The spell might not have been real magic, but that didn’t mean the warning wasn’t true.
sentences.zh: 那道咒语或许不是真正的魔法，可这不等于其中的警告就不真。

sentences.en: At any rate, Anna was not willing to risk it. “Up, up, up and away,” Obscuren said, seeming to settle into another’s words comfortably, as if the conversation of the previous night had been a bit of a strain for her.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，安娜都不愿拿这个去赌。“起，起，起，出发啦，”奥布斯基伦说道，她似乎很自在地安进别人的话里，仿佛前一晚的对话让她有点吃不消。

sentences.en: Elsa wobbled out of the raft first, followed by Kristoff.
sentences.zh: 艾莎先摇摇晃晃地下了筏，克斯托夫紧跟在后。

sentences.en: When he turned to offer his hand to help Anna step out, she ignored it and leapt over the side.
sentences.zh: 他转身伸手想扶安娜下去，她却没理会，直接翻身跳下了船舷。

sentences.en: Obscuren indicated with a nod that they should take off their glowworm bracelets and leave the little creatures on the post.

sentences.en: With a wistful sigh, Anna unwrapped the glowworm and gave it a little pat in thanks. “Will it be okay here?” she asked. “Home is where the heart is,” Obscuren said, and when Anna looked for clarification, the Librarian King’s assistant explained, “I’ll take them back with me.

sentences.en: They were made by digging a dwelling-sized hole deep into the ground, which was then covered by a roof made of grass.

sentences.en: Turf houses came in all shapes and sizes, but Anna’s favorites were the ones that looked like Earth Giants sunk into the soil, the green grass of the roofs resembling troll hair.
sentences.zh: 草皮屋形形色色、大小不一，可安娜最喜欢那些像大地巨人（Earth Giants）陷进土里的样式，屋顶的绿草活像地精的头发。

sentences.en: Anna looked around, hoping to see a neat row of books. “Um, Obscuren, are you sure this is your library?” she said.
