sentences.zh: 借着艾莎找到并点亮的火把的光，安娜再次望向那艘龙舟空荡荡的船身，喉咙里堵得发慌。

sentences.en: Once, there might have been mounds of gold, pottery, lush cloaks, and jars of rare spices to help send Aren the warrior on his valiant voyage.
sentences.zh: 从前，这里也许堆满了黄金、陶器、华丽的斗篷和一罐罐珍稀香料，用来送勇士阿伦踏上英勇的航程。

sentences.en: Once, this might have been a splendid place of sleek polished wood, a fitting resting place for Aren and his mighty sword.
sentences.zh: 从前，这里或许曾是一处光洁木板打造的华美之地，正配做阿伦与他那柄巨剑的长眠之所。

sentences.en: But now the rotten boards were barely strong enough to hold a dusty footprint, let alone a thing of myth.
sentences.zh: 可如今，腐朽的船板连一个落满灰尘的脚印都勉强撑得住，更别说承载一件神话之物了。

sentences.en: Elsa stood in the hull with Anna, turning over a small clump of dirt with the toe of her boot.
sentences.zh: 艾莎和安娜一同站在船舱里，用靴尖拨弄着一小撮泥土。

sentences.en: A cloud of dust trailed into the air, and Anna sneezed. “We’re too late,” Elsa said as she stepped over the remains of what might have once been an oar, “by a thousand years, give or take.
sentences.zh: 一阵尘土扬到空中，安娜打了个喷嚏。“我们来得太晚了，”艾莎一边跨过那截或许曾是船桨的残骸，一边说，“晚了一千年，说不定还不止。”

sentences.en: Maybe Revolute was here once—maybe this had even been Aren’s final resting place, but…” She trailed off, her eyes lingering on the holes in the porous old wood. “I think this boat has been empty for a long, long time.” No.
sentences.zh: 也许革命之刃曾在这里——也许这里甚至就是阿伦的长眠之地，但是……”她渐渐住了口，目光停留在多孔老木上的那些孔洞上。“我觉得这艘船已经空了很久很久了。”不。

sentences.en: They had come too far, risked too much. “Revolute is around here,” Anna said, kicking another clot of dirt with her boot only to reveal…more dirt.
sentences.zh: 她们已经走得太远，冒了太大的险。“革命之刃就在附近，”安娜说着，用靴子又踢开一坨泥块，结果只露出……更多的泥。

sentences.en: She knew many boats had secret watertight compartments in the floor, but she had searched and found none. “It just has to be here!” But even as she said it, Anna knew that wasn’t necessarily true.
sentences.zh: 她知道许多船的船底都设有防水隔舱，可她搜遍了也没找到一个。“它一定就在这儿！”可即便嘴上这么说，安娜也明白这未必是真的。

sentences.en: In fact, nothing just had to be anywhere.
sentences.zh: 事实上，没有什么“一定”要待在某处。

sentences.en: If just had to be counted for anything, then a great storm would have never met Mother and Father’s ship.
sentences.zh: 如果“一定”当真能作数的话，那么那场大风暴就绝不会撞上父母亲的船。

sentences.en: It would mean that King Runeard’s life wouldn’t have been taken by dangerous northerners, and that young Elsa and Anna would have known their grandfather.
sentences.zh: 那样的话，鲁纳德国王就不会丧命于危险的北方人手中，年幼的艾莎和安娜也本该认识她们的外祖父。

sentences.en: It would mean that Sven would have never gotten the Blight, and that Anna would have never called a Nattmara to the kingdom by manifesting it from her fears and nightmares.
sentences.zh: 那样的话，斯文就绝不会染上枯萎病，安娜也绝不会因自己的恐惧与噩梦具象化，而将那头暗夜魔狼召入王国。

sentences.en: Suddenly, it was just all too much .
sentences.zh: 突然间，这一切实在令人难以承受。

sentences.en: Anna felt the weight of all the earth and sea and castle fall onto her shoulders and crush her, snuffing out her last bit of hope.
sentences.zh: 安娜感到大地、海洋与城堡的全部重压都落在肩头，将她压垮，也掐灭了她最后的一丝希望。

sentences.en: She had not found the Revolute Blade, and she never would.
sentences.zh: 她没能找到革命之刃，也永远找不到了。

sentences.en: She would never be able to defeat the Nattmara.
sentences.zh: 她永远无法击败那头暗夜魔狼。

sentences.en: She would never see Kristoff or Olaf or Sven ever again.
sentences.zh: 她再也见不到克斯托夫、奥拉夫或斯文了。

sentences.en: She stepped out of the boat and lowered her head into her hands, and tears began to fall. “Oh, Anna,” Elsa said, following her.
sentences.zh: 她走出船舱，低下头埋进双手，泪水开始滑落。“哦，安娜，”艾莎跟着她说道。

sentences.en: Anna felt pressure on her shoulder as her sister crouched down next to her in the flickering torchlight. “Please, please, please don’t cry,” Elsa said. “It’s not your fault.
sentences.zh: 在摇曳的火光中，姐姐蹲到她身旁，安娜感到肩头一沉。“求求你，求求你，别哭了，”艾莎说。“这不是你的错。”

sentences.en: If I had been doing a better job, I would have recognized the signs, and we could have stopped the Nattmara before you called it into the kingdom.” Anna knew Elsa was trying to be comforting, but her words only made Anna feel a hundred times worse.
sentences.zh: “如果我做得更好些，我早就该看出那些征兆，在你把它召入王国之前就能拦住那头暗夜魔狼了。”安娜知道艾莎是想安慰她，可这些话只让她心里更难受了一百倍。

sentences.en: They were just more proof that Elsa didn’t need Anna anymore—that, in fact, Elsa might even be better off without Anna.
sentences.zh: 这些话不过更证明了艾莎已不再需要安娜——事实上，没有安娜，艾莎或许反而过得更好。

sentences.en: Anna dragged her face away from her hands, and leaning against the rough-hewn wall, she put her head back and looked up at the dragon figurehead, its mouth opened in an eternal snarl, unable to ever really stop thieves from stealing its treasures.
sentences.zh: 安娜把脸从手中抬起，靠在粗凿的石壁上，仰起头，望向那只龙首船饰——它的嘴永远大张着，作咆哮状，却从未能真正拦住盗贼偷走它的宝藏。

sentences.en: Anna closed her eyes, shutting out its accusing wooden eyes.
sentences.zh: 安娜闭上眼睛，避开它那仿佛在控诉的木雕眼眸。

sentences.en: Maybe it would be best for Elsa and all of Arendelle if the wooden dragon could just come to life and swallow Anna and her great disappointments whole, like how the wolf had swallowed her in her nightmare.
sentences.zh: 也许，如果这木龙能活过来，把安娜连同她巨大的失望一起吞下肚，就像梦里那头狼吞掉她那样，对艾莎和整个阿伦黛尔倒是最好不过。

sentences.en: She wasn’t exactly sure what that would do, but…Anna’s runaway thoughts lurched to a halt as an idea grabbed on to them.
sentences.zh: 她并不清楚那样会有什么结果，但是……一个念头猛地攥住了安娜四处乱窜的思绪，让她戛然而止。

sentences.en: She looked back up at the wooden dragon, its mouth gaping open. “Elsa!” Anna rose to her feet.
sentences.zh: 她重新抬头望向那只木龙，它的嘴大张着。“艾莎！”安娜站起身来。

sentences.en: Elsa lifted the torch as she stood, too. “What is it, Anna?” “I think I know where the sword is!” And without waiting for her sister to interrupt, Anna continued to barrel ahead. “We were just looking in the hull of the boat, because that’s where one would end up if you were eaten—in the belly of a dragon, or in the boat.
sentences.zh: 艾莎也站起身，举起火把。“怎么了，安娜？”“我想我知道剑在哪儿了！”安娜没等姐姐插话，便一股脑儿说了下去。“我们刚才只在船舱里找，因为要是被吃掉，人就会落在那儿——要么在龙肚子里，要么在船里。”

sentences.en: But the myth doesn’t say that the dragon ate Aren, it says—” “He was swallowed,” Elsa said, eyes growing wide. “Revolute could be hidden in the dragon’s mouth!” Anna nodded. “Exactly!” The dragon’s snarling mouth reared several feet above their heads.
sentences.zh: 可神话里没说龙吃掉了阿伦，它说的是——”“他被吞了下去，”艾莎睁大了眼睛说。“革命之刃可能就藏在龙的嘴里！”安娜点头。“没错！”那条龙咆哮的嘴高悬在她们头顶好几尺之上。

sentences.en: Usually, Elsa would be able to wave her hands and make a staircase out of ice.
sentences.zh: 换作平时，艾莎只需挥挥手，就能造出一道冰阶梯。

sentences.en: But they weren’t under the Huldrefólk’s protection anymore.
sentences.zh: 可她们如今已不在胡尔德精灵的庇护之下了。

sentences.en: If Elsa used as much as a lick of her magic, the Nattmara would be upon them in seconds.
sentences.zh: 只要艾莎动用哪怕一丁点魔法，那头暗夜魔狼几秒内就会扑到她们身上。

sentences.en: Crawling out onto the dragon’s neck also wasn’t an option.
sentences.zh: 爬到龙颈上去也行不通。

sentences.en: The boat was a thousand, maybe even thousands of years old, and the peeling, splintering wood had as many holes as a sponge.
sentences.zh: 这船少说有一千年，甚至几千年的年头了，剥落、碎裂的木板像海绵一样满是孔洞。

sentences.en: The whole thing looked like it might collapse if Anna so much as breathed on it.
sentences.zh: 整艘船看上去，安娜只要轻轻呵一口气，它仿佛就会塌掉。

sentences.en: Elsa planted the torch in the ground and crouched down. “All right, get on.” “What?” Anna looked at her sister, confused. “We need to get someone up there.
sentences.zh: 艾莎把火把插在地上，蹲下身来。“好了，上来。”“什么？”安娜困惑地看着姐姐。“我们得有人上去。”

sentences.en: I think you can reach it if you get on my back.” “A piggyback ride?
sentences.zh: “我觉得你趴到我背上，就能够到了。”“背我？

sentences.en: Really?” said Anna, a grin breaking across her face. “You haven’t offered me one of those since before the gates closed.” “Well,” Elsa said with a smile, “I guess I owe you at least one more.” Kicking off her boots, Anna scrambled up onto her sister’s back.
sentences.zh: 真的吗？”安娜说着，脸上绽开笑容。“自城墙大门关闭以来，你就再没背过我了。”“嗯，”艾莎微笑着说，“我想我至少还欠你一次。”安娜踢掉靴子，连爬带蹭地上了姐姐的背。

sentences.en: Then, balancing herself against the wooden hull, she placed her feet on Elsa’s shoulders and pulled herself into a standing position so she was eye to eye with the dragon.
sentences.zh: 接着，她扶着木船身稳住身子，双脚踩上艾莎的肩，撑起身子站直，这样便与龙首平视了。

sentences.en: Even though centuries had scrubbed it clear of most of its details, up close, Anna could still see the hatch marks that hinted at scales, and the expression of the dragon.
sentences.zh: 尽管数百年已磨去了它大部分细节，但近看，安娜仍能分辨出那些暗示鳞片的刻痕，以及龙的神情。

sentences.en: From below, the expression had seemed to be of a snarling angry beast, but now, Anna thought maybe it wasn’t angry, just protective.
sentences.zh: 从下往上看时，那神情像一头咆哮的猛兽，可此刻安娜觉得，它或许并非愤怒，只是在守护。

sentences.en: Nerves bubbled throughout Anna’s body.
sentences.zh: 安娜浑身紧张得发颤。

sentences.en: This was it.
sentences.zh: 就是这里了。

sentences.en: Their one shot.
sentences.zh: 她们唯一的机会。

sentences.en: Their last chance.
sentences.zh: 最后的希望。

sentences.en: The Revolute Blade, the very thing that had carved out Arenfjord and made a home for a wandering people.
sentences.zh: 革命之刃，正是它劈出了阿伦峡湾，为流浪的民族安了家。

sentences.en: A sword forged from a curved sunbeam with an unusual power, a gift from the sun herself.
sentences.zh: 一柄以弯弯的阳光锻造、拥有非凡之力的剑，是太阳女神赠予的礼物。

sentences.en: They would defeat the Nattmara.
sentences.zh: 她们将击败那头暗夜魔狼。

sentences.en: They would cure the crops and animals and people of the Blight, and free everyone she loved from their own terrifying nightmares. “Do you have it?” Elsa asked from underfoot.
sentences.zh: 她们将治好庄稼、牲畜和人们的枯萎病，把每一个她所爱的人从各自可怕的噩梦中解救出来。“你拿到了吗？”脚下的艾莎问道。

sentences.en: Whoops.
sentences.zh: 哎呀。

sentences.en: Anna’s mind was running away again. “No, not yet!” Anna said, reining in her galloping thoughts. “Well, hurry up!
sentences.zh: 安娜的思绪又跑远了。“还没，还没拿到！”安娜说着，勒住自己狂奔的念头。“那就快点！

sentences.en: You don’t exactly weigh the same as you did when you were five.” No, Anna wasn’t five years old.
sentences.zh: 你现在可没五岁时那么轻了。”是啊，安娜早不是五岁的孩子了。

sentences.en: She was capable of making serious mistakes, but she was also just as capable of fixing them.
sentences.zh: 她会犯下大错，也同样有能力去弥补。

sentences.en: And so, she reached her hand into the dragon’s mouth.
sentences.zh: 于是，她把手伸进龙嘴里。

sentences.en: At first, there was nothing there.
sentences.zh: 起初，里面空无一物。

sentences.en: Frowning, Anna leaned farther into the dragon’s gaping maw, her elbow disappearing, followed by the rest of her arm, until the wood hit her armpit.
sentences.zh: 安娜皱起眉，更往龙张大的嘴里探去，手肘没入，接着整条手臂跟着进去，直到木头抵住了她的腋窝。

sentences.en: Worry crept through her.
sentences.zh: 担忧悄然爬上心头。

sentences.en: If the dragon’s head was hollow, would she need to crawl all the way in?
sentences.zh: 如果龙首是空的，她是不是得整个人爬进去？

sentences.en: She wasn’t sure if she would fit.
sentences.zh: 她不确定自己能不能塞得进去。

sentences.en: If only Olaf were there, he’d be able to send his hand down inside.
sentences.zh: 要是奥拉夫在就好了，他准能把整只手探进去。

sentences.en: Or even Sven would have been helpful, with his sensitive nose.
sentences.zh: 哪怕斯文在也能帮上忙，凭他那灵敏的鼻子。

sentences.en: But they weren’t, so Anna would have to do it herself. “Anna,” Elsa said, “your foot is starting to dig into my shoulder.” “Sorry,” Anna said. “Just one more second.” Taking a breath to balance herself, she rose to her tiptoes, stretching, reaching until her fingers brushed something cold and metal-smooth.
sentences.zh: 可他们都不在，所以安娜只能自己来。“安娜，”艾莎说，“你的脚开始往我肩膀里硌了。”“抱歉，”安娜说。“再给我一秒就好。”她吸了口气稳住身子，踮起脚尖，伸长手臂去够，直到手指碰到了什么冰冷而光滑的金属。

sentences.en: Something that fit comfortably in her palm as she wrapped her hand around it.
sentences.zh: 那东西被她握在掌心，大小正合适。

sentences.en: Something that sent a note of anticipation through her.
sentences.zh: 一种期待感顺着那东西传遍全身。

sentences.en: Anna pulled.
sentences.zh: 安娜往外一拉。

sentences.en: At first, there was resistance, and then a whisper of metal, a noise that almost sounded like a dragon’s sigh as its secret came loose.
sentences.zh: 起初有些阻力，接着是一声金属的低语，那声响几乎像龙叹了口气，随着秘密被揭开。

sentences.en: And then Anna’s hand was back in the rippling orange light of the torch.
sentences.zh: 随后，安娜的手回到了火把摇曳的橘色光里。

sentences.en: Could it truly be?
sentences.zh: 这真是它吗？

sentences.en: The hilt was wrought from gold, and in the center of the pommel, like a miniature sun, sat a yellow diamond.
sentences.zh: 剑柄由黄金打造，剑首中央嵌着一颗黄钻，宛如一轮小小的太阳。

sentences.en: The gold of the handguard had been worked to look like little rays of the sun, leading down to the blade.
sentences.zh: 护手上的黄金被雕成一道道细小的阳光，一路延伸向剑刃。

sentences.en: And the blade…it was made of a blue-black metal—the same color as the meteorite in Sorenson’s observation tower.
sentences.zh: 而剑刃……是用一种蓝黑色的金属制成的——和索伦森观测塔里那块陨石一个颜色。

sentences.en: It curved, the slight S -shape mirroring the inlet of Arenfjord, where myth said Aren had made the legendary cut.
sentences.zh: 剑身弯曲，那微微的S形正映出阿伦峡湾的湾口，神话里说阿伦就是在那儿完成了那传奇的一劈。

sentences.en: But Anna hardly dared to believe that what she held was what she needed it to be.
sentences.zh: 可安娜几乎不敢相信，自己手中的确就是她要找的那把剑。

sentences.en: Not until she’d carefully slipped down from Elsa’s back.
sentences.zh: 直到她小心地从艾莎背上滑下来。

sentences.en: Not until Elsa tore a scrap of cloth from her split dress and began to polish the top of the blade, right below where it met the hilt.
sentences.zh: 直到艾莎从自己撕破的裙子上扯下一块布，开始擦拭剑刃顶端、靠近剑柄的那一段。

sentences.en: Not until she could read the letters that had been etched into the sword itself did Anna believe: R-E-V-O-L-U-T-E They’d found it.
sentences.zh: 直到她能认出刻在剑身上的字母，安娜才肯相信：R-E-V-O-L-U-T-E 她们找到了。

sentences.en: The carver of the first fjord.
sentences.zh: 第一道峡湾的开辟者。

sentences.en: The myth and the solution.
sentences.zh: 神话，也是解法。

sentences.en: The Revolute Blade.
sentences.zh: 革命之刃。

chapters.title: Chapter Twenty-Three
chapters.en:
“WE DID IT!” Anna shouted, forgetting the need to be quiet and embracing Elsa.

“Careful!” Elsa twisted the sword away. “You don’t want to accidentally stick us.”

Though Elsa’s warning wasn’t really all that funny, for some reason, it planted a seed of humor in Anna. A giggle slipped out, and then, a bloom of laughter. And instead of trying to trap it down, Anna let it rush through her, throwing back her head and laughing long and loud. Elsa looked confused, which only made Anna laugh harder.

Then, ever so slowly, Elsa’s lips began to turn upward, and she giggled; then she, too, laughed, loud and free. Their laughter echoed around the Earth Giant’s Passage, bounding and rebounding, patching the tiny rip in Anna’s heart caused by constant worrying.

Because Anna had done it. She’d proven to Elsa that she still needed her little sister who made mistakes. She’d proven that she could actually accomplish exactly what she had planned to do.

Suddenly, Elsa stopped laughing, and it was only Anna’s laughter that bounced around the walls, sounding alone and by itself.

“Hey,” Anna said, somewhat breathless. “What’s wrong?”

Elsa held her finger to her lips, and Anna listened. Without the protective barrier of laughter, she could now hear another sound coming from beyond the waterfall and the passage. A long, low angry howl.

The Nattmara was nearing.

“We need to get out here,” Anna said, slipping her boots back on. “Or else it’ll trap us in the tunnel.”

“Agreed.” Elsa nodded. Already, she was tightening the band around her braid. “But Anna, I think—”

“That we need a plan,” Anna said, finishing her sister’s sentence, as they so often did. “Yes, you’re right! The plan—the-plan-the-plan-the-plan…You use your magic to distract the Nattmara—only for a second or two!—and then I’ll surprise it with Revolute. That’s a brilliant idea, Elsa!”

“But I—” Elsa began, and that was all Anna could really make out, because she’d already tugged Revolute from Elsa’s hand and begun to sprint down the passageway for the exit and the Nattmara. Fear thrummed through her veins, and yet, she had Revolute.

She had hope.

Anna squeezed the hilt tight, the yellow diamond pressing into her hand. It almost hurt, but still she kept running, trusting in the power of the myth and trusting her sister to follow behind her with an icy blast or whirl of hard wind.

The still-frozen waterfall sparkled up ahead, and Anna squeezed herself out onto the narrow ledge and exited the passageway only to stop in her tracks. Because the land sprawled before her was not the home she knew.

Her home had a cheery village with painted houses, a fjord full of rich blue waters, and a vibrant display of autumnal colors that would have made her paint set jealous. But the land before her was bleached white, as though this reality were being erased to make way for the nightmare that was settling in for eternity. Like storm clouds rolling in, the Nattmara prowled the village edge.

When Anna had first spotted the wolf in the Great Hall, it’d been bigger than any wolf she’d ever seen, but not abnormally so. Then it’d become twice the size of a normal wolf, then the size of a bull, then the size of a knoll. But now, its eyes were level with the second-floor windows of the village townhouses.

It was exactly as Sorenson had foretold. Each hour that the Nattmara had not been banished, it’d grown in strength and size as it gorged on the fear that had swept over the land. Each stride of its paw seemed to cover a mile, and wherever it passed, the trees twisted away from it, as if they, too, could sleep and dream and wanted none of the Nattmara’s offerings. As if poplars and aspens and spruces, too, wanted to run away.

Anna had thought that the Nattmara would come directly for her, its accidental summoner, but instead of tearing up the path that would take it to the waterfall and to Revolute, the Nattmara turned…and loped back toward the village.

In the time that it took Anna to blink, the giant wolf had arrived at the edge of the protective ice dome over the village. Rearing back on its hind legs, it struck the dome with a heavy paw.

THUMP!

The ice stayed whole and smooth. The dome was working—but for how long? The Nattmara swung again.

THUMP!

Anna frowned. Had that thump been followed by a cracking sound? The Nattmara only needed to make a fissure as thin as a hair for it to be able to trickle though Elsa’s barrier in its black sand form.

“Anna!” Elsa said, flying out from behind the waterfall to join Anna on the ledge overlooking the village. “I need you to—”

“We have to go help them!” Anna yelled, desperation making her voice shrill. The villagers—they had no idea of the danger they were in. They were all asleep! She took a step forward to run—but her foot stayed put, rooted to the ground as though it had been locked in place.

What? Anna looked down to see a lacy frost pattern rising up from the ground, snapping together like links on a chain and wrapping around her foot.

While Anna gaped, something tugged on Revolute, and without thinking, Anna let go. Too late, she realized what she’d done. Looking back up, she saw Elsa standing in front of her, holding Aren’s sword with both hands. She no longer looked like Anna’s older sister, or even a queen. She looked like a soldier.

“Elsa.” Her words sounded small even to her own ears. “What are you doing?”

“I’m sorry,” Elsa said, and Anna could hear the truth in her sister’s words, but still, Elsa made no move to stop the advancing frost. It circled around Anna, shuttling back and forth on itself like yarn on a loom to form a white tapestry, rising higher and higher. “I failed to protect the kingdom,” Elsa said, “but I’m not going to fail you, too!”

Failed? Anna didn’t know what Elsa was talking about. Elsa never failed at anything.

“Elsa,” Anna said as the frost crystals scattered up over her head, dancing into a domed roof. “I don’t need to be protected!”

It felt like Anna’s whole being had contracted and collapsed in on itself, like a black hole or a dark abyss. She felt as though she’d become no bigger than the head of a pin. The last frost link clicked into place, finishing not a tapestry, but a bubble-like tent. Anna found she could move her feet again, the frost chain that had held her to the ground slithering away to weave itself into the structure. It didn’t matter, though, if Anna could move her feet or not, because Elsa hadn’t bothered to make a door.

“I love you,” Elsa said, sounding for a moment like she was younger than Anna or even Echo. And then she was running, sprinting down the dirt path to the village below, Revolute a curved gleam in her hand.

“Come back!” Anna yelled. “Elsa!” She pounded her fists against the frost, but the walls were so strong, so solid, and so cold, that each pummel felt like a bite. The frost links held fast, keeping Anna locked away.

Anna was useless as she watched Elsa reach the end of the path and run toward the Nattmara. Useless as the Nattmara caught Elsa’s scent and turned toward her sister, its fearsome claws extended. And useless as Elsa strode forward, ready to become the great ruler that Arendelle needed…just as Aren had done. But it would be okay. It would be okay it would be okay it would be okay.

Elsa wielded the myth that could defeat the myth. She held in her hand the crescent blade that had carved their home on Arenfjord. If Revolute could do that, surely it could defeat a Nattmara summoned by a scared little sister. Still, Anna held her breath as she watched, too far away to help, yet at the same time too close, because she could see it all.

A howl of wind clashed with the howl of the wolf as Elsa intercepted the Nattmara at the base of the Bridge of Arches. Elsa looked like a doll in front of the monstrous wolf, which had grown so tall that its ears were at the height of the castle’s waving flags. Even from a distance, Anna could see the slip of saliva that hung from the Nattmara’s fangs as it began to circle her sister, its great yellow eyes locked on Elsa.

This was a thousand times worse than any of Anna’s nightmares. In all her nightmares but the last, she’d been in some sort of control. She’d always been able to puzzle her way out somehow, or distract the creature long enough that she could wake up. But even if Anna could break free from the frost bubble, she would not be able to wake up.

The wolf and her sister circled each other.

Elsa’s cloak and scarf flapped in great gusts of wind as she twirled one hand and clutched Revolute with the other. But something was wrong. Even though Elsa was controlling the gusts of ice, no matter which direction she commanded the snow and ice to go, the wolf would force her to turn her back into the magic so that her hair and billows of icy magicked air constantly whipped into her eyes. There was no way for Elsa to clearly see.

And then, the Nattmara attacked.

Elsa and Revolute whirled away, the Nattmara’s teeth snapping on thin air. It retreated for a moment, then struck again. This time, a terrible screech filled the air as a fang scraped across the blade. Or maybe the screech was Anna’s own scream. Because Elsa now lay between the Nattmara’s giant paws, sprawled like a spider, her limbs askew, and her hand empty.

Revolute flew through the air, a blue-black streak, and landed several feet behind Elsa. Anna saw Elsa’s hand sweep out, trying to feel for the sword without taking her eyes away from the Nattmara.

“REVOLUTE!” Anna shouted, though she knew Elsa wouldn’t be able to hear her. “TO YOUR LEFT!”

The Nattmara licked its maw, its fangs poised above Elsa.

For a moment, Anna saw in startling detail the gleam of the Nattmara’s claws and rise in her sister’s chest as Elsa took a deep breath.

Then, the Nattmara lunged down.

But in the space that it took for Anna to blink, Elsa had lunged, too. She grabbed for Revolute’s hilt. In one fluid movement, she held it up in front of her—the ancient blade flashing in the light of the setting sun—and thrust it into the roof of the Nattmara’s mouth.

Anna waited for the Nattmara to fall and disintegrate into dust, defeated at last by a thing of myth, just as Sorenson had said that it could be.

Instead, the world slowed and stilled as the Nattmara bit down. And Revolute—the great, mythic sword of Aren’s oldest hero, the sword that had carved the Arenfjord from the mountains, slain beasts, and conquered nightmares—shattered like glass. Bits of the meteorite blade sparkled as they sprayed uselessly to the ground, raining down on Elsa, who now lay completely defenseless in front of the Nattmara.

“ELSA!” Anna roared, pounding at her prison of frost. “ELSA! Use your magic!”

Maybe it was a trick of the wind, but Elsa appeared to turn her head in the waterfall’s direction. For one second, it almost seemed that Elsa looked at her. Glancing down, Anna saw that the frost bubble had started to dissolve into thin air—not good! If Elsa’s magic was dissolving, that must mean that Elsa was weakening, too.

But Anna was now free!

She began to run down the path even though she knew that she would not make it in time, but still, she had to try. Elsa would have—no, Elsa had—done the same for her.

The Nattmara threw back its leviathan head and howled its victory. And as it rose once more above her sister, its white fur shifted into a glittering black as the Nattmara morphed into a cloud of sand that stood out starkly against the faded landscape. The bits and pieces swirled together, forming a spinning column.

And then the sand slammed down into Elsa’s chest…and disappeared.

“Elsa!” Anna sobbed, stumbling into range. “Elsa!”

Her sister sprawled on the ground, her eyes closed and her blond hair coming loose from its braid and spilling onto fallen leaves. Scattered around her like a broken halo were the blue-black shards of what had once been the great sword Revolute.

And though Anna knew what would happen next, she still wasn’t prepared for when Elsa’s eyelids fluttered open to reveal glowing yellow eyes.

Anna’s stomach heaved at the sight of the wolf’s eyes in her sister’s familiar face. Her stride slowed. “Elsa?” she called out hesitantly.

Elsa opened her mouth…and screamed.

And then she raised her hands, blasting Arendelle with her powers, her usually white snow and white ice now replaced by black snow and black ice.

No, not black snow or black ice. Black sand.

As Elsa continued to scream, the sound swept through Anna, hollowing her out like the wolf’s howl had, until there was nothing left except for Elsa’s scream within her, reverberating against her ribcage, echoing again and again in her complete emptiness. In her utter aloneness.

Revolute had shattered, and Elsa’s eyes were yellow.

“Elsa,” Anna sobbed, not knowing what do. “Elsa…Elsa…Elsa!”

But the figure who had been her sister did not even turn to face her.

With great heaving gasps, Anna gathered the shards of the sword into her cloak pocket—a futile hope. Because Revolute, the famed sword of myth, had not been enough to defeat a beast of myth. The myth was no longer a myth. It had not saved her sister. And the sound of Elsa’s scream—or was it the wolf’s howl?—pulled her into the black dots gathering at the edge of her vision. Anna didn’t know which was which, but the nightmares stormed in and dragged her down.

“Elsa,” she managed to croak out one last time. No longer knowing what was real and what was a nightmare, or if they were now truly one and the same, Anna saw Elsa at last turn to her.

Elsa raised her hands, and black sand erupted from her palms toward Anna.

Darkness swirled around Anna, and then, at last, there was nothing at all.

“我们做到了！”安娜忘了需要安静，一把抱住艾莎喊道。“小心！”艾莎把剑扭到一旁。“可别一不小心扎到咱们。”虽说艾莎的提醒算不上多好笑，可不知为何，竟在安娜心里种下了一颗笑意的种子。

一声轻笑溜了出来，接着，笑声像花朵般绽放。

安娜没有试图压住它，而是任由笑意奔涌而过，仰起头，笑得又久又响。

艾莎一脸茫然，这反倒让安娜笑得更厉害了。

接着，艾莎的嘴角极其缓慢地向上扬起，也咯咯笑起来；随后，她也放声大笑，自由而畅快。

她们的笑声在大地巨人的通道里回荡，来回撞击，修补着安娜因不断担忧而在心上撕出的小裂口。

因为安娜做到了。

她向艾莎证明了，姐姐依然需要这个会犯错的小妹妹。

她证明了，自己确实能完成原本计划要做的事。

突然，艾莎止住了笑，只有安娜的笑声还在四壁间弹跳，听来孤零零的。“嘿，”安娜有点喘不过气地说。“怎么了？”艾莎把手指竖在唇前，安娜凝神去听。

没了笑声这道保护屏障，她现在能听见瀑布和通道那头传来的另一种声响。

一声漫长而低沉的怒嚎。

暗夜魔狼逼近了。“我们得离开这儿，”安娜一边把靴子套回去一边说。“不然它就会把咱们困在隧道里。”“同意。”艾莎点头。

她已经在收紧辫子上的发带。“可是安娜，我觉得——”“我们需要一个计划，”安娜接上了姐姐的话，她们经常这样。“对，你说得对！

计划——计划——计划——计划……你用魔法引开暗夜魔狼——只需一两秒！——然后我用革命之刃给它个措手不及。

这主意太妙了，艾莎！”“可是我——”艾莎刚开口，安娜就只听清了这一句，因为她已经从艾莎手中抽走革命之刃，朝通道尽头的出口和那头暗夜魔狼飞奔而去。

恐惧在她血脉里震颤，然而，她握着革命之刃。

她握着希望。

安娜紧紧攥住剑柄，那颗黄钻硌进她的手心。

几乎有些疼，可她仍在奔跑，相信神话的力量，也相信姐姐会紧随其后，用一阵冰寒的冲击或凛冽的旋风前来相助。

前方那道仍冻结的瀑布闪闪发亮，安娜挤上狭窄的岩架，出了通道，却猛地停住了脚步。

因为展现在她眼前的土地，已不是她所熟悉的家园。

她的家园有色彩明快的村庄、彩绘的房屋、满注深蓝海水的峡湾，以及一片鲜活秋色，连她的颜料盒都要为之艳羡。

可眼前的土地泛着惨白，仿佛这个现实正被抹去，好为那即将永驻的噩梦腾出位置。

暗夜魔狼像滚滚压境的乌云，在村庄边缘徘徊游荡。

安娜第一次在大厅里瞥见那头狼时，它比她见过的任何狼都大，但还不至于离奇。

后来它长到了普通狼的两倍大，接着有公牛那么大，再后来有土丘那么高。

可如今，它的眼睛已与村庄楼房的二层窗户齐平。

一切都正如索伦森所预言。

暗夜魔狼每未被驱散一小时，便随着吞噬席卷大地的恐惧而变得更强、更大。

它每跨一爪仿佛就掠过一英里，所到之处，树木纷纷扭身避开，仿佛它们也会睡眠做梦，不愿沾染暗夜魔狼赐予的任何东西。

仿佛白杨、白桦与云杉也都想要逃开。

安娜本以为暗夜魔狼会直冲她这个意外召它来的人而来，可它并没有撕开通往瀑布和革命之刃的小路，而是转过身……小跑着折返村庄。

安娜眨眼的工夫，那巨狼已抵达村庄上方那座防护冰穹的边缘。

它后腿直立，用沉重的爪子击向冰穹。

砰！

冰面依旧完好而平滑。

冰穹还在起作用——可还能撑多久？

暗夜魔狼再次挥爪。

砰！

安娜皱起眉。

那一击之后，是不是跟着一声碎裂的响动？

暗夜魔狼只需划出一道细如发丝的裂缝，便能化作黑沙从艾莎的屏障里渗进去。“安娜！”艾莎从瀑布后飞身而出，落到俯瞰村庄的岩架上与安娜会合。“我要你——”“我们得去救他们！”安娜喊道，绝望让她的声音尖利起来。

村民们——他们根本不知道自己身处险境。

他们都睡着了！

她迈步想要冲出去——可脚却钉在原地，像被锁住一般牢牢扎根地上。

什么？

安娜低头，看见一幅蕾丝般的霜花图案正从地面升起，像锁链上的环节般咔哒扣合，缠住了她的脚。

安娜正目瞪口呆，忽觉革命之刃被什么扯了一下，她想也没想就松了手。

等她明白过来，已经太迟。

她抬头，看见艾莎站在她面前，双手握着阿伦的剑。

她看上去不再像安娜的姐姐，甚至不再像一位女王。

她看上去像个战士。“艾莎。”这话连她自己听着都细弱。“你在做什么？”“对不起，”艾莎说，安娜能从姐姐的话里听出真心，可艾莎仍没有要停下蔓延的霜花之意。

霜花绕着安娜盘旋，像织机上的纱线般来回穿梭，织成一幅白色挂毯，越升越高。“我没能保护住王国，”艾莎说，“但我不会再连你也护不住！”失败？

安娜不懂艾莎在说什么。

艾莎从不会在任何事上失败。“艾莎，”安娜说着，霜晶已飞散到她头顶，舞成圆顶。“我不需要被保护！”安娜只觉得整个自我都向内收缩、坍缩，如同黑洞或深渊。

她觉得自己渺小得不过针尖大小。

最后一道霜链咔哒扣好，完成的不是挂毯，而是一个气泡般的帐篷。

安娜发现自己又能动脚了，那道将她锁在地上的霜链悄然游走，融入了这结构之中。

可动不动脚已无关紧要，因为艾莎压根没做一扇门。“我爱你，”艾莎说，那一刻她的声音听起来比安娜还小，甚至比艾柯还小。

接着她奔跑起来，顺着泥路朝下方的村庄冲去，革命之刃在她手中弯成一道寒光。“回来！”安娜喊道。“艾莎！”她用拳头捶打霜壁，可那墙如此坚固、厚实又冰冷，每一击都像被咬了一口。

霜链牢牢锁住，将安娜困在其中。

安娜眼睁睁看着艾莎跑到路尽头、朝暗夜魔狼冲去，自己却无能为力。

无能为力地看着暗夜魔狼嗅到艾莎的气味，转过身面向她姐姐，伸出可怕的利爪。

无能为力地看着艾莎大步向前，准备成为阿伦黛尔所需的那位伟大统治者……正如阿伦当年那样。

但会没事的。

会没事的，会没事的，会没事的。

艾莎手中握着能击败神话的神话。

她手中握着那柄曾在阿伦峡湾劈出他们家园的弯刃。

既然革命之刃能做到那般，它一定也能击败一头由受惊的小妹妹召来的暗夜魔狼。

即便如此，安娜仍屏住呼吸望着，距离远得帮不上忙，可同时又近得过分，因为她把一切都看在眼里。

当艾莎在拱桥桥头拦住暗夜魔狼时，风的呼啸与狼的嚎叫撞在一起。

在那头巨狼面前，艾莎渺小如玩偶，狼已长得极高，耳朵与城堡上飘扬的旗帜齐高。

即便隔着距离，安娜也能看见暗夜魔狼的獠牙上挂着一缕唾液，它开始绕着姐姐打转，巨大的黄眼死死盯住艾莎。

这比安娜做过的任何噩梦都要可怕一千倍。

在除去最后一个之外的所有噩梦里，她都还多少能掌控些什么。

她总能想出法子脱身，或把那怪物引开足够久，好让自己醒来。

可即便安娜能挣脱霜泡，她也无法醒来。

狼与她的姐姐彼此绕圈。

艾莎的斗篷与围巾在阵阵狂风里翻飞，她一手旋舞，另一手紧握革命之刃。

可有什么不对劲。

尽管艾莎操控着阵阵冰风，可无论她指挥冰雪往哪个方向去，那狼都会逼她背对魔法，于是她的头发与团团带魔的冰气不停抽打进她眼里。

艾莎根本无法看清。

接着，暗夜魔狼发动了攻击。

艾莎与革命之刃旋身避开，暗夜魔狼的利齿咬了个空。

它退开片刻，又再次扑来。

这一次，当獠牙擦过剑刃，一声凄厉的尖啸划破空气。

或许那尖啸是安娜自己的叫声。

因为此刻艾莎躺在暗夜魔狼巨大的爪间，像蜘蛛般四肢摊开，两手空空。

革命之刃飞过空中，划出一道蓝黑色的轨迹，落在艾莎身后几尺远。

安娜看见艾莎伸手向外摸索，想在不移开视线的情况下摸到剑。“革命之刃！”安娜喊道，尽管她知道艾莎听不见。“在你左边！”暗夜魔狼舔了舔嘴，獠牙悬在艾莎上方。

一瞬间，安娜清晰地看见暗夜魔狼利爪的寒光，以及艾莎深吸一口气时胸膛的起伏。

接着，暗夜魔狼猛扑而下。

可就在安娜眨眼之间，艾莎也扑了出去。

她伸手去抓革命之刃的剑柄。

一个流畅的动作，她将剑举在身前——古老的剑刃在落日余晖中闪烁——猛地刺进暗夜魔狼的上颚。

安娜等着暗夜魔狼倒下、化为尘土，终于被一件神话之物击败，正如索伦森所说那般。

然而，当暗夜魔狼咬下时，世界却放慢、凝滞了。

而革命之刃——阿伦最古老英雄那柄伟大的神话之剑，那柄从群山中劈出阿伦峡湾、斩杀猛兽、征服噩梦的剑——碎得像玻璃一般。

陨石剑刃的碎片闪闪发亮，徒劳地迸落一地，如雨般洒在艾莎身上——她此刻全然无力地躺在暗夜魔狼面前。“艾莎！”安娜咆哮着捶打自己的霜之牢笼。“艾莎！

用你的魔法！”也许是风开的玩笑，但艾莎似乎把头转向了瀑布的方向。

有那么一瞬，艾莎几乎像是在看她。

安娜低头，看见霜泡已开始消散于无形——不妙！

如果艾莎的魔法正在消散，那必定意味着艾莎也在变弱。

可安娜现在自由了！

她开始沿路奔跑，尽管明知赶不上，可她仍得试一试。

艾莎会——不，艾莎已经——为她这样做过。

暗夜魔狼仰起它巨兽般的头颅，嚎叫着胜利。

当它在姐姐上方再次升起时，它的白毛化为闪亮的黑色，暗夜魔狼化作一团沙云，在褪色的景致中格外刺眼。

沙的碎屑盘旋汇聚，形成一根旋转的沙柱。

接着沙浪猛地砸进艾莎胸口……消失了。“艾莎！”安娜抽泣着踉跄赶来。“艾莎！”姐姐瘫在地上，双眼紧闭，金发从辫子里松脱，散落在落叶上。

环绕她四周、如破碎光环般的，是曾经那柄伟大之剑革命之刃的蓝黑色碎片。

尽管安娜知道接下来会发生什么，当艾莎的眼皮颤动睁开、露出发光的黄眼时，她仍毫无防备。

看着熟悉的姐姐脸上嵌着狼的眼睛，安娜的胃一阵翻搅。

她的脚步慢了下来。“艾莎？”她迟疑地唤道。

艾莎张开嘴……尖叫起来。

接着她举起双手，以魔力轰击阿伦黛尔，往日白雪与白冰，如今换成了黑雪与黑冰。

不，不是黑雪，也不是黑冰。

是黑沙。

艾莎持续尖叫，那声音席卷过安娜，将她掏空，正如狼嚎那样，直到她体内只剩艾莎的尖叫，在肋骨间回荡，在她彻底的空无中一遍遍回响。

在她彻底的孤独里。

革命之刃已碎，艾莎的眼是黄色的。“艾莎，”安娜抽泣着，不知所措。“艾莎……艾莎……艾莎！”可那个曾是她姐姐的身影，连头都没转过来面对她。

安娜大口喘着气，把剑的碎片拢进斗篷口袋——一个徒劳的希望。

因为那柄赫赫有名的神话之剑革命之刃，竟不足以击败一头神话之兽。

神话已不再是神话。

它没能救下姐姐。

而艾莎尖叫的声音——还是狼的嚎叫？——将她拽入视野边缘聚拢的黑点。

安娜分不清哪个是哪个，可噩梦已呼啸涌入，将她拖垮。“艾莎，”她最后勉力挤出一声嘶哑的呼唤。

再也分不清何为真实、何为噩梦，也不知它们如今是否真已合而为一，安娜看见艾莎终于转向她。

艾莎举起双手，黑沙从掌心喷涌，朝安娜扑来。

黑暗在安娜周身打转，接着，终于，一切都归于虚无。

sentences.en: “WE DID IT!” Anna shouted, forgetting the need to be quiet and embracing Elsa. “Careful!” Elsa twisted the sword away. “You don’t want to accidentally stick us.” Though Elsa’s warning wasn’t really all that funny, for some reason, it planted a seed of humor in Anna.
sentences.zh: “我们做到了！”安娜忘了需要安静，一把抱住艾莎喊道。“小心！”艾莎把剑扭到一旁。“可别一不小心扎到咱们。”虽说艾莎的提醒算不上多好笑，可不知为何，竟在安娜心里种下了一颗笑意的种子。

sentences.en: A giggle slipped out, and then, a bloom of laughter.
sentences.zh: 一声轻笑溜了出来，接着，笑声像花朵般绽放。

sentences.en: And instead of trying to trap it down, Anna let it rush through her, throwing back her head and laughing long and loud.
sentences.zh: 安娜没有试图压住它，而是任由笑意奔涌而过，仰起头，笑得又久又响。

sentences.en: Elsa looked confused, which only made Anna laugh harder.
sentences.zh: 艾莎一脸茫然，这反倒让安娜笑得更厉害了。

sentences.en: Then, ever so slowly, Elsa’s lips began to turn upward, and she giggled; then she, too, laughed, loud and free.
sentences.zh: 接着，艾莎的嘴角极其缓慢地向上扬起，也咯咯笑起来；随后，她也放声大笑，自由而畅快。

sentences.en: Their laughter echoed around the Earth Giant’s Passage, bounding and rebounding, patching the tiny rip in Anna’s heart caused by constant worrying.
sentences.zh: 她们的笑声在大地巨人的通道里回荡，来回撞击，修补着安娜因不断担忧而在心上撕出的小裂口。

sentences.en: Because Anna had done it.
sentences.zh: 因为安娜做到了。

sentences.en: She’d proven to Elsa that she still needed her little sister who made mistakes.
sentences.zh: 她向艾莎证明了，姐姐依然需要这个会犯错的小妹妹。

sentences.en: She’d proven that she could actually accomplish exactly what she had planned to do.
sentences.zh: 她证明了，自己确实能完成原本计划要做的事。

sentences.en: Suddenly, Elsa stopped laughing, and it was only Anna’s laughter that bounced around the walls, sounding alone and by itself. “Hey,” Anna said, somewhat breathless. “What’s wrong?” Elsa held her finger to her lips, and Anna listened.
sentences.zh: 突然，艾莎止住了笑，只有安娜的笑声还在四壁间弹跳，听来孤零零的。“嘿，”安娜有点喘不过气地说。“怎么了？”艾莎把手指竖在唇前，安娜凝神去听。

sentences.en: Without the protective barrier of laughter, she could now hear another sound coming from beyond the waterfall and the passage.
sentences.zh: 没了笑声这道保护屏障，她现在能听见瀑布和通道那头传来的另一种声响。

sentences.en: A long, low angry howl.
sentences.zh: 一声漫长而低沉的怒嚎。

sentences.en: The Nattmara was nearing. “We need to get out here,” Anna said, slipping her boots back on. “Or else it’ll trap us in the tunnel.” “Agreed.” Elsa nodded.
sentences.zh: 暗夜魔狼逼近了。“我们得离开这儿，”安娜一边把靴子套回去一边说。“不然它就会把咱们困在隧道里。”“同意。”艾莎点头。

sentences.en: Already, she was tightening the band around her braid. “But Anna, I think—” “That we need a plan,” Anna said, finishing her sister’s sentence, as they so often did. “Yes, you’re right!
sentences.zh: 她已经在收紧辫子上的发带。“可是安娜，我觉得——”“我们需要一个计划，”安娜接上了姐姐的话，她们经常这样。“对，你说得对！

sentences.en: The plan—the-plan-the-plan-the-plan…You use your magic to distract the Nattmara—only for a second or two!—and then I’ll surprise it with Revolute.
sentences.zh: 计划——计划——计划——计划……你用魔法引开暗夜魔狼——只需一两秒！——然后我用革命之刃给它个措手不及。

sentences.en: That’s a brilliant idea, Elsa!” “But I—” Elsa began, and that was all Anna could really make out, because she’d already tugged Revolute from Elsa’s hand and begun to sprint down the passageway for the exit and the Nattmara.
sentences.zh: 这主意太妙了，艾莎！”“可是我——”艾莎刚开口，安娜就只听清了这一句，因为她已经从艾莎手中抽走革命之刃，朝通道尽头的出口和那头暗夜魔狼飞奔而去。

sentences.en: Fear thrummed through her veins, and yet, she had Revolute.
sentences.zh: 恐惧在她血脉里震颤，然而，她握着革命之刃。

sentences.en: She had hope.
sentences.zh: 她握着希望。

sentences.en: Anna squeezed the hilt tight, the yellow diamond pressing into her hand.
sentences.zh: 安娜紧紧攥住剑柄，那颗黄钻硌进她的手心。

sentences.en: It almost hurt, but still she kept running, trusting in the power of the myth and trusting her sister to follow behind her with an icy blast or whirl of hard wind.
sentences.zh: 几乎有些疼，可她仍在奔跑，相信神话的力量，也相信姐姐会紧随其后，用一阵冰寒的冲击或凛冽的旋风前来相助。

sentences.en: The still-frozen waterfall sparkled up ahead, and Anna squeezed herself out onto the narrow ledge and exited the passageway only to stop in her tracks.
sentences.zh: 前方那道仍冻结的瀑布闪闪发亮，安娜挤上狭窄的岩架，出了通道，却猛地停住了脚步。

sentences.en: Because the land sprawled before her was not the home she knew.
sentences.zh: 因为展现在她眼前的土地，已不是她所熟悉的家园。

sentences.en: Her home had a cheery village with painted houses, a fjord full of rich blue waters, and a vibrant display of autumnal colors that would have made her paint set jealous.
sentences.zh: 她的家园有色彩明快的村庄、彩绘的房屋、满注深蓝海水的峡湾，以及一片鲜活秋色，连她的颜料盒都要为之艳羡。

sentences.en: But the land before her was bleached white, as though this reality were being erased to make way for the nightmare that was settling in for eternity.
sentences.zh: 可眼前的土地泛着惨白，仿佛这个现实正被抹去，好为那即将永驻的噩梦腾出位置。

sentences.en: Like storm clouds rolling in, the Nattmara prowled the village edge.
sentences.zh: 暗夜魔狼像滚滚压境的乌云，在村庄边缘徘徊游荡。

sentences.en: When Anna had first spotted the wolf in the Great Hall, it’d been bigger than any wolf she’d ever seen, but not abnormally so.
sentences.zh: 安娜第一次在大厅里瞥见那头狼时，它比她见过的任何狼都大，但还不至于离奇。

sentences.en: Then it’d become twice the size of a normal wolf, then the size of a bull, then the size of a knoll.
sentences.zh: 后来它长到了普通狼的两倍大，接着有公牛那么大，再后来有土丘那么高。

sentences.en: But now, its eyes were level with the second-floor windows of the village townhouses.
sentences.zh: 可如今，它的眼睛已与村庄楼房的二层窗户齐平。

sentences.en: It was exactly as Sorenson had foretold.
sentences.zh: 一切都正如索伦森所预言。

sentences.en: Each hour that the Nattmara had not been banished, it’d grown in strength and size as it gorged on the fear that had swept over the land.
sentences.zh: 暗夜魔狼每未被驱散一小时，便随着吞噬席卷大地的恐惧而变得更强、更大。

sentences.en: Each stride of its paw seemed to cover a mile, and wherever it passed, the trees twisted away from it, as if they, too, could sleep and dream and wanted none of the Nattmara’s offerings.
sentences.zh: 它每跨一爪仿佛就掠过一英里，所到之处，树木纷纷扭身避开，仿佛它们也会睡眠做梦，不愿沾染暗夜魔狼赐予的任何东西。

sentences.en: As if poplars and aspens and spruces, too, wanted to run away.
sentences.zh: 仿佛白杨、白桦与云杉也都想要逃开。

sentences.en: Anna had thought that the Nattmara would come directly for her, its accidental summoner, but instead of tearing up the path that would take it to the waterfall and to Revolute, the Nattmara turned…and loped back toward the village.
sentences.zh: 安娜本以为暗夜魔狼会直冲她这个意外召它来的人而来，可它并没有撕开通往瀑布和革命之刃的小路，而是转过身……小跑着折返村庄。

sentences.en: In the time that it took Anna to blink, the giant wolf had arrived at the edge of the protective ice dome over the village.
sentences.zh: 安娜眨眼的工夫，那巨狼已抵达村庄上方那座防护冰穹的边缘。

sentences.en: Rearing back on its hind legs, it struck the dome with a heavy paw.
sentences.zh: 它后腿直立，用沉重的爪子击向冰穹。

sentences.en: THUMP!
sentences.zh: 砰！

sentences.en: The ice stayed whole and smooth.
sentences.zh: 冰面依旧完好而平滑。

sentences.en: The dome was working—but for how long?
sentences.zh: 冰穹还在起作用——可还能撑多久？

sentences.en: The Nattmara swung again.
sentences.zh: 暗夜魔狼再次挥爪。

sentences.en: THUMP!
sentences.zh: 砰！

sentences.en: Anna frowned.
sentences.zh: 安娜皱起眉。

sentences.en: Had that thump been followed by a cracking sound?
sentences.zh: 那一击之后，是不是跟着一声碎裂的响动？

sentences.en: The Nattmara only needed to make a fissure as thin as a hair for it to be able to trickle though Elsa’s barrier in its black sand form. “Anna!” Elsa said, flying out from behind the waterfall to join Anna on the ledge overlooking the village. “I need you to—” “We have to go help them!” Anna yelled, desperation making her voice shrill.
sentences.zh: 暗夜魔狼只需划出一道细如发丝的裂缝，便能化作黑沙从艾莎的屏障里渗进去。“安娜！”艾莎从瀑布后飞身而出，落到俯瞰村庄的岩架上与安娜会合。“我要你——”“我们得去救他们！”安娜喊道，绝望让她的声音尖利起来。

sentences.en: The villagers—they had no idea of the danger they were in.
sentences.zh: 村民们——他们根本不知道自己身处险境。

sentences.en: They were all asleep!
sentences.zh: 他们都睡着了！

sentences.en: She took a step forward to run—but her foot stayed put, rooted to the ground as though it had been locked in place.
sentences.zh: 她迈步想要冲出去——可脚却钉在原地，像被锁住一般牢牢扎根地上。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Anna looked down to see a lacy frost pattern rising up from the ground, snapping together like links on a chain and wrapping around her foot.
sentences.zh: 安娜低头，看见一幅蕾丝般的霜花图案正从地面升起，像锁链上的环节般咔哒扣合，缠住了她的脚。

sentences.en: While Anna gaped, something tugged on Revolute, and without thinking, Anna let go.
sentences.zh: 安娜正目瞪口呆，忽觉革命之刃被什么扯了一下，她想也没想就松了手。

sentences.en: Too late, she realized what she’d done.
sentences.zh: 等她明白过来，已经太迟。

sentences.en: Looking back up, she saw Elsa standing in front of her, holding Aren’s sword with both hands.
sentences.zh: 她抬头，看见艾莎站在她面前，双手握着阿伦的剑。

sentences.en: She no longer looked like Anna’s older sister, or even a queen.
sentences.zh: 她看上去不再像安娜的姐姐，甚至不再像一位女王。

sentences.en: She looked like a soldier. “Elsa.” Her words sounded small even to her own ears. “What are you doing?” “I’m sorry,” Elsa said, and Anna could hear the truth in her sister’s words, but still, Elsa made no move to stop the advancing frost.
sentences.zh: 她看上去像个战士。“艾莎。”这话连她自己听着都细弱。“你在做什么？”“对不起，”艾莎说，安娜能从姐姐的话里听出真心，可艾莎仍没有要停下蔓延的霜花之意。

sentences.en: It circled around Anna, shuttling back and forth on itself like yarn on a loom to form a white tapestry, rising higher and higher. “I failed to protect the kingdom,” Elsa said, “but I’m not going to fail you, too!” Failed?
sentences.zh: 霜花绕着安娜盘旋，像织机上的纱线般来回穿梭，织成一幅白色挂毯，越升越高。“我没能保护住王国，”艾莎说，“但我不会再连你也护不住！”失败？

sentences.en: Anna didn’t know what Elsa was talking about.
sentences.zh: 安娜不懂艾莎在说什么。

sentences.en: Elsa never failed at anything . “Elsa,” Anna said as the frost crystals scattered up over her head, dancing into a domed roof. “I don’t need to be protected!” It felt like Anna’s whole being had contracted and collapsed in on itself, like a black hole or a dark abyss.
sentences.zh: 艾莎从不会在任何事上失败。“艾莎，”安娜说着，霜晶已飞散到她头顶，舞成圆顶。“我不需要被保护！”安娜只觉得整个自我都向内收缩、坍缩，如同黑洞或深渊。

sentences.en: She felt as though she’d become no bigger than the head of a pin.
sentences.zh: 她觉得自己渺小得不过针尖大小。

sentences.en: The last frost link clicked into place, finishing not a tapestry, but a bubble-like tent.
sentences.zh: 最后一道霜链咔哒扣好，完成的不是挂毯，而是一个气泡般的帐篷。

sentences.en: Anna found she could move her feet again, the frost chain that had held her to the ground slithering away to weave itself into the structure.
sentences.zh: 安娜发现自己又能动脚了，那道将她锁在地上的霜链悄然游走，融入了这结构之中。

sentences.en: It didn’t matter, though, if Anna could move her feet or not, because Elsa hadn’t bothered to make a door. “I love you,” Elsa said, sounding for a moment like she was younger than Anna or even Echo.
sentences.zh: 可动不动脚已无关紧要，因为艾莎压根没做一扇门。“我爱你，”艾莎说，那一刻她的声音听起来比安娜还小，甚至比艾柯还小。

sentences.en: And then she was running, sprinting down the dirt path to the village below, Revolute a curved gleam in her hand. “Come back!” Anna yelled. “Elsa!” She pounded her fists against the frost, but the walls were so strong, so solid, and so cold, that each pummel felt like a bite.
sentences.zh: 接着她奔跑起来，顺着泥路朝下方的村庄冲去，革命之刃在她手中弯成一道寒光。“回来！”安娜喊道。“艾莎！”她用拳头捶打霜壁，可那墙如此坚固、厚实又冰冷，每一击都像被咬了一口。

sentences.en: The frost links held fast, keeping Anna locked away.
sentences.zh: 霜链牢牢锁住，将安娜困在其中。

sentences.en: Anna was useless as she watched Elsa reach the end of the path and run toward the Nattmara.
sentences.zh: 安娜眼睁睁看着艾莎跑到路尽头、朝暗夜魔狼冲去，自己却无能为力。

sentences.en: Useless as the Nattmara caught Elsa’s scent and turned toward her sister, its fearsome claws extended.
sentences.zh: 无能为力地看着暗夜魔狼嗅到艾莎的气味，转过身面向她姐姐，伸出可怕的利爪。

sentences.en: And useless as Elsa strode forward, ready to become the great ruler that Arendelle needed…just as Aren had done.
sentences.zh: 无能为力地看着艾莎大步向前，准备成为阿伦黛尔所需的那位伟大统治者……正如阿伦当年那样。

sentences.en: But it would be okay.
sentences.zh: 但会没事的。

sentences.en: It would be okay it would be okay it would be okay.
sentences.zh: 会没事的，会没事的，会没事的。

sentences.en: Elsa wielded the myth that could defeat the myth.
sentences.zh: 艾莎手中握着能击败神话的神话。

sentences.en: She held in her hand the crescent blade that had carved their home on Arenfjord.
sentences.zh: 她手中握着那柄曾在阿伦峡湾劈出他们家园的弯刃。

sentences.en: If Revolute could do that, surely it could defeat a Nattmara summoned by a scared little sister.
sentences.zh: 既然革命之刃能做到那般，它一定也能击败一头由受惊的小妹妹召来的暗夜魔狼。

sentences.en: Still, Anna held her breath as she watched, too far away to help, yet at the same time too close, because she could see it all.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，安娜仍屏住呼吸望着，距离远得帮不上忙，可同时又近得过分，因为她把一切都看在眼里。

sentences.en: A howl of wind clashed with the howl of the wolf as Elsa intercepted the Nattmara at the base of the Bridge of Arches.
sentences.zh: 当艾莎在拱桥桥头拦住暗夜魔狼时，风的呼啸与狼的嚎叫撞在一起。

sentences.en: Elsa looked like a doll in front of the monstrous wolf, which had grown so tall that its ears were at the height of the castle’s waving flags.
sentences.zh: 在那头巨狼面前，艾莎渺小如玩偶，狼已长得极高，耳朵与城堡上飘扬的旗帜齐高。

sentences.en: Even from a distance, Anna could see the slip of saliva that hung from the Nattmara’s fangs as it began to circle her sister, its great yellow eyes locked on Elsa.
sentences.zh: 即便隔着距离，安娜也能看见暗夜魔狼的獠牙上挂着一缕唾液，它开始绕着姐姐打转，巨大的黄眼死死盯住艾莎。

sentences.en: This was a thousand times worse than any of Anna’s nightmares.
sentences.zh: 这比安娜做过的任何噩梦都要可怕一千倍。

sentences.en: In all her nightmares but the last, she’d been in some sort of control.
sentences.zh: 在除去最后一个之外的所有噩梦里，她都还多少能掌控些什么。

sentences.en: She’d always been able to puzzle her way out somehow, or distract the creature long enough that she could wake up.
sentences.zh: 她总能想出法子脱身，或把那怪物引开足够久，好让自己醒来。

sentences.en: But even if Anna could break free from the frost bubble, she would not be able to wake up.
sentences.zh: 可即便安娜能挣脱霜泡，她也无法醒来。

sentences.en: The wolf and her sister circled each other.
sentences.zh: 狼与她的姐姐彼此绕圈。

sentences.en: Elsa’s cloak and scarf flapped in great gusts of wind as she twirled one hand and clutched Revolute with the other.
sentences.zh: 艾莎的斗篷与围巾在阵阵狂风里翻飞，她一手旋舞，另一手紧握革命之刃。

sentences.en: But something was wrong.
sentences.zh: 可有什么不对劲。

sentences.en: Even though Elsa was controlling the gusts of ice, no matter which direction she commanded the snow and ice to go, the wolf would force her to turn her back into the magic so that her hair and billows of icy magicked air constantly whipped into her eyes.
sentences.zh: 尽管艾莎操控着阵阵冰风，可无论她指挥冰雪往哪个方向去，那狼都会逼她背对魔法，于是她的头发与团团带魔的冰气不停抽打进她眼里。

sentences.en: There was no way for Elsa to clearly see.
sentences.zh: 艾莎根本无法看清。

sentences.en: And then, the Nattmara attacked.
sentences.zh: 接着，暗夜魔狼发动了攻击。

sentences.en: Elsa and Revolute whirled away, the Nattmara’s teeth snapping on thin air.
sentences.zh: 艾莎与革命之刃旋身避开，暗夜魔狼的利齿咬了个空。

sentences.en: It retreated for a moment, then struck again.
sentences.zh: 它退开片刻，又再次扑来。

sentences.en: This time, a terrible screech filled the air as a fang scraped across the blade.
sentences.zh: 这一次，当獠牙擦过剑刃，一声凄厉的尖啸划破空气。

sentences.en: Or maybe the screech was Anna’s own scream.
sentences.zh: 或许那尖啸是安娜自己的叫声。

sentences.en: Because Elsa now lay between the Nattmara’s giant paws, sprawled like a spider, her limbs askew, and her hand empty.
sentences.zh: 因为此刻艾莎躺在暗夜魔狼巨大的爪间，像蜘蛛般四肢摊开，两手空空。

sentences.en: Revolute flew through the air, a blue-black streak, and landed several feet behind Elsa.
sentences.zh: 革命之刃飞过空中，划出一道蓝黑色的轨迹，落在艾莎身后几尺远。

sentences.en: Anna saw Elsa’s hand sweep out, trying to feel for the sword without taking her eyes away from the Nattmara. “REVOLUTE!” Anna shouted, though she knew Elsa wouldn’t be able to hear her. “TO YOUR LEFT!” The Nattmara licked its maw, its fangs poised above Elsa.
sentences.zh: 安娜看见艾莎伸手向外摸索，想在不移开视线的情况下摸到剑。“革命之刃！”安娜喊道，尽管她知道艾莎听不见。“在你左边！”暗夜魔狼舔了舔嘴，獠牙悬在艾莎上方。

sentences.en: For a moment, Anna saw in startling detail the gleam of the Nattmara’s claws and rise in her sister’s chest as Elsa took a deep breath.
sentences.zh: 一瞬间，安娜清晰地看见暗夜魔狼利爪的寒光，以及艾莎深吸一口气时胸膛的起伏。

sentences.en: Then, the Nattmara lunged down.
sentences.zh: 接着，暗夜魔狼猛扑而下。

sentences.en: But in the space that it took for Anna to blink, Elsa had lunged, too.
sentences.zh: 可就在安娜眨眼之间，艾莎也扑了出去。

sentences.en: She grabbed for Revolute’s hilt.
sentences.zh: 她伸手去抓革命之刃的剑柄。

sentences.en: In one fluid movement, she held it up in front of her—the ancient blade flashing in the light of the setting sun—and thrust it into the roof of the Nattmara’s mouth.
sentences.zh: 一个流畅的动作，她将剑举在身前——古老的剑刃在落日余晖中闪烁——猛地刺进暗夜魔狼的上颚。

sentences.en: Anna waited for the Nattmara to fall and disintegrate into dust, defeated at last by a thing of myth, just as Sorenson had said that it could be.
sentences.zh: 安娜等着暗夜魔狼倒下、化为尘土，终于被一件神话之物击败，正如索伦森所说那般。

sentences.en: Instead, the world slowed and stilled as the Nattmara bit down.
sentences.zh: 然而，当暗夜魔狼咬下时，世界却放慢、凝滞了。

sentences.en: And Revolute—the great, mythic sword of Aren’s oldest hero, the sword that had carved the Arenfjord from the mountains, slain beasts, and conquered nightmares—shattered like glass.
sentences.zh: 而革命之刃——阿伦最古老英雄那柄伟大的神话之剑，那柄从群山中劈出阿伦峡湾、斩杀猛兽、征服噩梦的剑——碎得像玻璃一般。

sentences.en: Bits of the meteorite blade sparkled as they sprayed uselessly to the ground, raining down on Elsa, who now lay completely defenseless in front of the Nattmara. “ELSA!” Anna roared, pounding at her prison of frost. “ELSA!
sentences.zh: 陨石剑刃的碎片闪闪发亮，徒劳地迸落一地，如雨般洒在艾莎身上——她此刻全然无力地躺在暗夜魔狼面前。“艾莎！”安娜咆哮着捶打自己的霜之牢笼。“艾莎！

sentences.en: Use your magic!” Maybe it was a trick of the wind, but Elsa appeared to turn her head in the waterfall’s direction.
sentences.zh: 用你的魔法！”也许是风开的玩笑，但艾莎似乎把头转向了瀑布的方向。

sentences.en: For one second, it almost seemed that Elsa looked at her.
sentences.zh: 有那么一瞬，艾莎几乎像是在看她。

sentences.en: Glancing down, Anna saw that the frost bubble had started to dissolve into thin air—not good!
sentences.zh: 安娜低头，看见霜泡已开始消散于无形——不妙！

sentences.en: If Elsa’s magic was dissolving, that must mean that Elsa was weakening, too.
sentences.zh: 如果艾莎的魔法正在消散，那必定意味着艾莎也在变弱。

sentences.en: But Anna was now free!
sentences.zh: 可安娜现在自由了！

sentences.en: She began to run down the path even though she knew that she would not make it in time, but still, she had to try.
sentences.zh: 她开始沿路奔跑，尽管明知赶不上，可她仍得试一试。

sentences.en: Elsa would have—no, Elsa had —done the same for her.
sentences.zh: 艾莎会——不，艾莎已经——为她这样做过。

sentences.en: The Nattmara threw back its leviathan head and howled its victory.
sentences.zh: 暗夜魔狼仰起它巨兽般的头颅，嚎叫着胜利。

sentences.en: And as it rose once more above her sister, its white fur shifted into a glittering black as the Nattmara morphed into a cloud of sand that stood out starkly against the faded landscape.
sentences.zh: 当它在姐姐上方再次升起时，它的白毛化为闪亮的黑色，暗夜魔狼化作一团沙云，在褪色的景致中格外刺眼。

sentences.en: The bits and pieces swirled together, forming a spinning column.
sentences.zh: 沙的碎屑盘旋汇聚，形成一根旋转的沙柱。

sentences.en: And then the sand slammed down into Elsa’s chest…and disappeared. “Elsa!” Anna sobbed, stumbling into range. “Elsa!” Her sister sprawled on the ground, her eyes closed and her blond hair coming loose from its braid and spilling onto fallen leaves.
sentences.zh: 接着沙浪猛地砸进艾莎胸口……消失了。“艾莎！”安娜抽泣着踉跄赶来。“艾莎！”姐姐瘫在地上，双眼紧闭，金发从辫子里松脱，散落在落叶上。

sentences.en: Scattered around her like a broken halo were the blue-black shards of what had once been the great sword Revolute.
sentences.zh: 环绕她四周、如破碎光环般的，是曾经那柄伟大之剑革命之刃的蓝黑色碎片。

sentences.en: And though Anna knew what would happen next, she still wasn’t prepared for when Elsa’s eyelids fluttered open to reveal glowing yellow eyes.
sentences.zh: 尽管安娜知道接下来会发生什么，当艾莎的眼皮颤动睁开、露出发光的黄眼时，她仍毫无防备。

sentences.en: Anna’s stomach heaved at the sight of the wolf’s eyes in her sister’s familiar face.
sentences.zh: 看着熟悉的姐姐脸上嵌着狼的眼睛，安娜的胃一阵翻搅。

sentences.en: Her stride slowed. “Elsa?” she called out hesitantly.
sentences.zh: 她的脚步慢了下来。“艾莎？”她迟疑地唤道。

sentences.en: Elsa opened her mouth…and screamed.
sentences.zh: 艾莎张开嘴……尖叫起来。

sentences.en: And then she raised her hands, blasting Arendelle with her powers, her usually white snow and white ice now replaced by black snow and black ice.
sentences.zh: 接着她举起双手，以魔力轰击阿伦黛尔，往日白雪与白冰，如今换成了黑雪与黑冰。

sentences.en: No, not black snow or black ice.
sentences.zh: 不，不是黑雪，也不是黑冰。

sentences.en: Black sand .
sentences.zh: 是黑沙。

sentences.en: As Elsa continued to scream, the sound swept through Anna, hollowing her out like the wolf’s howl had, until there was nothing left except for Elsa’s scream within her, reverberating against her ribcage, echoing again and again in her complete emptiness.
sentences.zh: 艾莎持续尖叫，那声音席卷过安娜，将她掏空，正如狼嚎那样，直到她体内只剩艾莎的尖叫，在肋骨间回荡，在她彻底的空无中一遍遍回响。

sentences.en: In her utter aloneness.
sentences.zh: 在她彻底的孤独里。

sentences.en: Revolute had shattered, and Elsa’s eyes were yellow. “Elsa,” Anna sobbed, not knowing what do. “Elsa…Elsa…Elsa!” But the figure who had been her sister did not even turn to face her.
sentences.zh: 革命之刃已碎，艾莎的眼是黄色的。“艾莎，”安娜抽泣着，不知所措。“艾莎……艾莎……艾莎！”可那个曾是她姐姐的身影，连头都没转过来面对她。

sentences.en: With great heaving gasps, Anna gathered the shards of the sword into her cloak pocket—a futile hope.
sentences.zh: 安娜大口喘着气，把剑的碎片拢进斗篷口袋——一个徒劳的希望。

sentences.en: Because Revolute, the famed sword of myth, had not been enough to defeat a beast of myth.
sentences.zh: 因为那柄赫赫有名的神话之剑革命之刃，竟不足以击败一头神话之兽。

sentences.en: The myth was no longer a myth.
sentences.zh: 神话已不再是神话。

sentences.en: It had not saved her sister.
sentences.zh: 它没能救下姐姐。

sentences.en: And the sound of Elsa’s scream—or was it the wolf’s howl?—pulled her into the black dots gathering at the edge of her vision.
sentences.zh: 而艾莎尖叫的声音——还是狼的嚎叫？——将她拽入视野边缘聚拢的黑点。

sentences.en: Anna didn’t know which was which, but the nightmares stormed in and dragged her down. “Elsa,” she managed to croak out one last time.
sentences.zh: 安娜分不清哪个是哪个，可噩梦已呼啸涌入，将她拖垮。“艾莎，”她最后勉力挤出一声嘶哑的呼唤。

sentences.en: No longer knowing what was real and what was a nightmare, or if they were now truly one and the same, Anna saw Elsa at last turn to her.
sentences.zh: 再也分不清何为真实、何为噩梦，也不知它们如今是否真已合而为一，安娜看见艾莎终于转向她。

sentences.en: Elsa raised her hands, and black sand erupted from her palms toward Anna.
sentences.zh: 艾莎举起双手，黑沙从掌心喷涌，朝安娜扑来。

sentences.en: Darkness swirled around Anna, and then, at last, there was nothing at all.
sentences.zh: 黑暗在安娜周身打转，接着，终于，一切都归于虚无。

chapters.title: Chapter Twenty-Four
chapters.en:
ANNA WOKE TO HER MOTHER singing a lullaby.

She knew it was just a dream, and so she kept her eyes shut, letting herself drift in the familiar and comforting melody. Though she couldn’t make out the lyrics, she had a sense of the story behind it. A story from long ago, in that time before time, when the world was sprightly green and the rivers bubbled with enchantment. That time when the sun would step down from the sky and walk along the earth, just to feel the grass tickle her feet and to discuss philosophy with the wind. It was an olden song, a song of strength and meekness, revenge and love. The sound was sweet, but it was not real. Anna knew that.

Mother was gone. Father, too. And now Elsa…

Yellow eyes and a haunted kingdom. Tears dripped from beneath her eyelashes, but Anna still didn’t open them. She wanted to stay suspended in the dark, cocooned away until someone had cleaned up her mess.

Something cold patted her cheek. “Anna, quit joking around. Wake up.”

This voice was familiar, too.

Anna opened her eyes to find herself nose to carrot with Olaf.

“You’re leaking,” he informed her, referring to the tears she was shedding.

“Olaf, what are you doing here?” Anna swiped at her eyes and looked away from Olaf’s nose to see branchless trees swaying above her. No, not trees—masts. Three tall ones, each strung with the ropes and nets of a working ship and boasting wide billowing sails.

Above the slap of the waves, Anna could hear singing—but it wasn’t her mother, it was Tuva the blacksmith, who stared out at the dark night over the royal ship’s rail, her lilting voice filling the salt-sprayed air.

“Anna’s awake!” Olaf shouted.

“How did you get here?” Anna asked Olaf. “How did I get here?” She looked around and beside her, and saw Sven wrapped in a large blanket, still fast asleep, though his legs twitched and sweat sheened his almost now completely white coat. Only a little patch of brown fur remained on his flaring nose.

“Hoo-hoo!” Oaken said, stomping into view, his cheeks a bit redder than usual from the cold sea air. “We watched everything from the harbor! When Scary Elsa vanished inside the castle, we crept ashore and carried you back. We thought both you and Sven would rest better next to one another.”

“I thought you had already sailed away!” Anna said, perplexed. She also wondered why she hadn’t fallen under the nightmare sleep. She studied her hands, not sure what she expected to see.

“We were going to,” Tuva called from the ship’s stern, her hands on the helm. In the yellow lantern light, the blacksmith looked ragged and her curly hair had been tugged into a cloud of frizz by the wind. Her brown eyes, however, remained warm as she looked at Anna. “But then we had a change of heart. And a good thing, too—or else we wouldn’t have been able to pick up SoYun.”

“Since I live on the outskirts of the village,” SoYun said softly as she appeared from behind the post, a coil of thick rope in her arms, “the wolf ran straight by—and at that very moment, the rest of my herd fell asleep. I realized I had to go seek a solution myself. So I rowed out onto the sea, hoping to find someone awake on the water, and that’s how they”—she gestured to Tuva and Oaken—“found me.”

“I’m so glad,” Anna said, and she was pleased to note that while SoYun’s long black braid wasn’t yet in its usual tidiness, she looked less terrified than when she’d come upon Anna and Elsa in the woods. In fact, SoYun looked determined.

“But,” Anna said, looking back at Tuva, “what kind of change convinced you to return?”

“You,” Tuva said simply.

Anna blinked. “What do you mean?”

Tuva turned the wheel, and the sails above rippled in the night breeze. “I mean,” she said, “that if a young woman like you could stick around, even though all was falling apart, and you don’t have powers of snow and ice, and I doubt you can lift a blacksmith’s hammer above your head for even a minute—then why couldn’t we? After all, Arendelle is just as much our home as it is yours.

“We’d only sailed out a little ways when we realized that we needed to return. And so, we agreed to turn around in case you were still out there. And you were. So we scooped you up just in time and carried you to the ship, and now we’ve set sail again.”

“We’re keeping an eye on the castle,” SoYun added. “Elsa…she’s…”

“Still in there,” Tuva finished darkly.

“Thank you. H-how long have I been asleep?” Anna said. Her thoughts reeled with the vision of Elsa falling victim to the Nattmara.

“Only a few hours!” Olaf called from the prow. “Which is actually a short amount of time when you take in the eons of our galaxy.”

Anna’s heart sped up. It was still the same night. “And when’s sunrise?”

“In just an hour,” Oaken said.

An hour. Arendelle had a single hour before this terror became permanent. Uneasy, Anna rose to her feet and headed to the railing. She stared down at the black waters of the Arenfjord. They slapped relentlessly against the ship’s hull, giving rhythm to the terrible thoughts that swarmed through Anna’s mind: Elsa, failure, Elsa. A tear coursed down her cheek. Anna’s greatest fear wasn’t a wolf. It never had been.

It had been losing her sister.

Olaf took Anna’s hand in his. “You’re melting,” he said. “I wish I could share my permafrost with you.”

Anna smiled as she wiped her face with the back of her hand. “I’m okay, Olaf.” She paused. “Actually,” she admitted, “I’m not okay. All along I wanted to go on the grand tour with Elsa on this very ship, but now…It was supposed to be a journey that Elsa and I did together.”

And though Anna didn’t say it, she thought: Just like taking care of the castle is something we’re supposed to do together, too. But even after the trip to the Huldrefólk, Elsa still hadn’t trusted her to get rid of the Nattmara, and now, their one and only chance of defeating the nightmare—Revolute—lay in tiny jagged pieces in her cloak pocket.

Sven suddenly bellowed, and Anna looked just in time to see him thrash wildly, his legs moving as though he were running for his life, even as he slumbered.

Anna ran over and sank down beside him, her skirt billowing around her. Careful to avoid his hooves, she reached out and tenderly began to pat his nose. Slowly, Sven stopped kicking, but his ears continued to twitch.

“I ruined it all,” she said, continuing to pet Sven gently on the head. “I thought I finally had the answer. But”—she drew a long, shuddering breath—“I thought wrong. And Elsa—she was right not to trust me to come along on her grand tour, or to defeat the Nattmara, or to do anything at all.”

“Ah-hem,” came a familiar throat-clearing. She turned to see Wael climbing up out of the ship’s hull.

Quickly, she looked away and kept her head bent toward the water, using her hair as a curtain. She didn’t think she could stomach the nosy journalist’s judgment. She barely felt like she could handle anything at all.

“Ah-hem.” The throat clearing became more insistent. “I couldn’t help overhearing, but, well…have you been belowdecks yet? To Elsa’s study?”

Anna shook her head. She’d been to the royal ship to help unload rations, but she had made it a point to avoid Elsa’s cabin, unwilling to see it piled high with the luggage that would accompany Elsa far from home.

“Then I suggest you check it out.”

“I don’t know,” Anna said, thinking of the wild hair that now fanned around Elsa’s face and the yellow eyes of the Nattmara set into her sockets. That image would haunt her forever, she was certain of it. “It—it would hurt too much to see right now,” Anna said.

Olaf slid his hand into hers. “Sometimes, you walk into a cave thinking you’ll find wolves inside, but they turn out to be puppies.”

With a heavy sigh, Anna shuffled after Olaf, following him and Wael downstairs to Elsa’s study. As she walked, she kept sneaking glances at Wael. She was surprised that he’d been willing to come back and help her.

Wael caught one of her glances and exhaled. “I know what you’re thinking,” he said as he stepped onto a groaning stair.

“You do?” Anna said, her cheeks warming slightly.

Wael nodded. “You think that because I ask you and your sister hard questions about the kingdom, that I must not like you or Arendelle very much.” He opened the door to Elsa’s floating quarters and paused a moment to look at Anna. “But the truth is, I ask hard questions because I love Arendelle so much, and because I believe in you and Elsa. You know, asking questions is often the first step to accomplishing something.”

And Anna was surprised to realize that yes, she exactly knew. She smiled at Wael and said, “Thank you so much for your questions, and for coming back to help us.” And she meant it with the whole of her being.

Wael returned the smile and stepped back so that she could enter.

Anna gasped. Everywhere, there were sunflowers. Painted sunflowers danced across wooden beams and were carved into the handles of the cupboards. A plush sunflower rug, cheery yellow and spring green, lay at the base of the stairs.

Sunflowers weren’t Elsa’s favorite flowers. They were Anna’s. Elsa must have asked that the entire study be decorated to remind her of her sister. To remind her of home. And in the center of the room hung a newly commissioned portrait of two little girls, one with white-blond hair and the other chestnut brown, skating across a frozen pond. The entire room felt like a hug.

Wael went to the desk and pulled out a page from the stacks that had already accumulated in anticipation of Elsa’s grand tour. “This is the one that I thought you might like to see,” Wael said, handing it to her before slipping out, leaving Anna alone with Olaf.

Anna peered down at the paper, then did a double take. It was a proclamation written in Elsa’s elegant handwriting:

I, Elsa, Queen of Arendelle, do hereby proclaim my sister, Anna of Arendelle, Keeper of the Kingdom while I sail on the grand tour. She is kind, thoughtful, and loves Arendelle with the whole of her heart. There is none better than her to watch over the kingdom while I am away.

At last, Anna had an answer. The reason Elsa had not invited her on the grand tour—it wasn’t because Elsa thought Anna was incompetent. It was because she knew Anna was helpful, and she needed Anna at home to keep an eye on things. Of course Elsa didn’t want Anna leaving Arendelle. Arendelle needed Anna just as much as Anna needed it.

“Now that’s true love!” said Olaf, who had angled his head to read it.

“It is,” said Anna with a sad smile. All this time, Anna had thought that Elsa believed she was useless, but maybe that wasn’t the case at all. Maybe the only person who hadn’t believed that Anna was helpful…was Anna herself.

She remembered the ice bubble that Elsa had enclosed her in. She’d thought it had been Elsa doing one more protective big sister act, but what if it was meant to be more than that? What if she wasn’t trying to be protective of Anna, but she was instead arming Anna, forcing her to wait and watch, because she trusted her to figure out the solution if the worst should happen?

“Olaf,” Anna said, “would you mind getting Tuva down here, please? We don’t have much time.”

Half an hour later, though, Anna’s fragile hope had once again unraveled. She’d laid out the collected pieces of Revolute across Elsa’s desk to see if Tuva could piece them together, but the blacksmith shook her head. “The pieces are too small, and the metal—I’ve never seen anything like it before. Maybe I could do it if Ada”—her breath caught on her wife’s name—“were around and I had access to our forge, but there’s no way it can be fixed in time, and definitely not on this ship without the proper tools.”

“Why would you fix it?” Wael called from the doorway. “The sword didn’t work the first time—what makes you think it would work this time?”

“Because,” Anna said, keeping her eye on the porthole. Was the night sky beginning to brighten? “You can only defeat a myth with a thing of myth, and Revolute is definitely a thing of myth. Besides”—she turned her head to look at the map of Arendelle pinned to the wall. It reminded her of the map she had uncovered in the secret room, the one where her mother had written one of their father’s many sayings—“my father used to say the past has a way of returning.”

“And what goes around comes around again, like a sneeze in the wind,” Olaf added. He sat at the desk, examining the pieces of the shattered sword. “Maybe you should look at Revolute and Aren’s past.”

Anna sighed. “I would, but I don’t exactly have a copy of the Saga of Aren on me at the moment, and Elsa’s not here to declaim.”

“Ah-hem,” Wael coughed. “Elsa is not the only one who studied the classics.”

“Apologies, Wael,” Anna said. “Please perform, but quickly.” Unease filled her, but she tamped it down. “We’re running out of time.”

“‘Revolving moon and spinning sun, forged a crescent blade…’” Wael began, and Anna half listened as she tried to skim the other documents that might be helpful.

“Hey, Anna,” Olaf said, “don’t you think it’s funny how you can find love in the most curious places?”

Anna tried not to sigh. She loved when Olaf discussed philosophy—usually—but now, mere minutes before sunrise, was not the time. “Yeah, sure I do. Why are you asking?”

“Because,” Olaf said, “it’s sitting here on the desk.”

Anna looked over, trying to see what he was talking about. She had not realized that Olaf had been rearranging the broken pieces of Revolute, specifically the top part of the blade that had held the inscription of the sword’s name, which now spelled out:

L-O-V-E R-E-T-U

“‘The sea rushed in as hidden power flowed from the gleaming sword,’” Wael continued to proclaim—and Anna’s heart skipped a beat.

A hidden power.

Anna’s heart began beating again, but twice as fast, as thoughts tumbled through her mind and she took in the other letters. A grin spread across her face.

“Oaken!” she yelled up to the deck. “Turn this ship around again! We have a kingdom to save.”
chapters.zh:
安娜醒来时，听见母亲在唱摇篮曲。

她知道那只是个梦，于是闭着眼，任自己在那熟悉而安心的旋律里飘荡。

尽管听不清歌词，她却能感受到它背后的故事。

一个久远的、远在时光之初的故事，那时世界一派鲜嫩的绿，河流翻涌着魔法。

那时太阳会从天上走下来，在大地上漫步，只为感受青草挠着她的脚，与风探讨哲学。

那是一首古老的歌，一首关于坚强与柔顺、复仇与爱的歌。

声音甜美，却并不真实。

安娜知道。

母亲已经不在了。

父亲也一样。

而现在艾莎……黄色的眼睛，与一个被诅咒的王国。

泪珠从她的睫毛下滴落，可安娜仍没睁开眼。

她想悬在黑暗里，像裹在茧中，直到有人替她收拾好这一团乱。

有什么冰凉的东西拍了拍她的脸颊。“安娜，别开玩笑了。

醒醒。”这声音也同样熟悉。

安娜睁开眼，发现自己正和奥拉夫鼻尖对着胡萝卜鼻。“你在漏水呢，”他告诉她，指的是她正在流的眼泪。“奥拉夫，你怎么会在这儿？”安娜抹了抹眼睛，把视线从奥拉夫的鼻子移开，看见头顶上方摇晃着没有枝桠的“树”。

不，不是树——是桅杆。

三根高高的桅杆，每根都挂满作业船只的绳索与渔网，张扬着宽大的鼓帆。

在浪花的拍击声之上，安娜听见有人在唱——但不是母亲，是铁匠图娃，她正望着王家船舷外的黑夜，轻快的歌声填满咸湿的空气。“安娜醒了！”奥拉夫喊道。“你怎么到这儿来的？”安娜问奥拉夫。“我怎么到这儿来的？”她环顾四周，看见斯文裹着一条大毯子，仍在熟睡，只是腿直抽抽，几乎已全白的毛上泛着汗光。

唯有他外翻的鼻子上还留着一小块棕色毛。“呼——呼！”奥肯踏步走来，海上的冷气让他的脸颊比平时更红了些。“我们从港口把一切都看在眼里！

当可怕的艾莎消失在城堡里，我们悄悄上岸，把你背了回来。

我们觉得你跟斯文挨着睡，会都睡得好些。”“我还以为你们已经驶远了！”安娜困惑地说。

她也纳闷自己为何没陷入那噩梦般的沉睡。

她端详着自己的手，不确定自己想看到什么。“我们本要走的，”图娃从船尾传来声音，双手把着舵。

在黄灯笼的光下，这位铁匠显得疲惫不堪，卷发被风吹成一团蓬乱的毛。

可她望向安娜时，那双棕眼依旧温柔。“但后来我们改变了主意。

幸好如此——不然我们也接不上昭允了。”“我住在村庄郊外，”昭允从柱子后轻声走出，怀里抱着一卷粗绳，“狼直接从我身边跑过——而就在那一刻，我其余的鹿群都睡着了。

我意识到，我得自己去找解决办法。

于是我划船出海，盼着能在水上找到醒着的人，他们就是这么——”她指了指图娃和奥肯——“找到我的。”“我真高兴，”安娜说，她欣慰地注意到，尽管昭允长长的黑辫还没恢复平日的整齐，可她看起来比在林中撞见安娜与艾莎时少了些惊恐。

事实上，昭允神色坚定。“可是，”安娜转头看着图娃说，“是什么样的改变让你们回来的？”“你，”图娃干脆地说。

安娜眨了眨眼。“什么意思？”图娃转动船轮，上方的帆在夜风里轻颤。“我是说，”她说，“像你这样一个年轻姑娘，即便一切都分崩离析，还能留下来；你既没有冰雪的魔力，我猜你也举不起铁匠的锤子哪怕一分钟——那我们凭什么不能留下？

毕竟，阿伦黛尔既是你的家，也同样是我们的家。”“我们才驶出一小段路，就意识到该回去。

于是我们约定掉头，万一你还在外面。

而你果然在。

所以我们及时把你捞起，送上船，现在又重新起航了。”“我们正盯着城堡，”昭允补了一句。“艾莎……她……”“还在里面，”图娃阴沉地接上。“谢谢你们。

我——我睡了多久？”安娜说。

想到艾莎沦为暗夜魔狼的牺牲品，她的心思一阵翻腾。“才几个小时！”奥拉夫从船头喊道。“若放到我们银河的亿万年里，这其实很短呢。”安娜的心猛地加速。

还是同一个夜晚。“那日出是什么时候？”“再过一小时，”奥肯说。

一小时。

阿伦黛尔只剩这最后一小时，否则这场恐怖将永远凝固。

安娜不安地起身，走向船舷。

她低头凝视阿伦峡湾漆黑的海水。

海水无情地拍打着船身，为安娜脑中蜂拥的恐怖念头打着节拍：艾莎，失败，艾莎。

一滴泪顺着脸颊滑下。

安娜最大的恐惧并非狼。

从来都不是。

她最大的恐惧，是失去姐姐。

奥拉夫握住安娜的手。“你在融化，”他说。“真希望我能把我的永冻分些给你。”安娜用手背抹了把脸，微微一笑。“我没事，奥拉夫。”她顿了顿。“其实，”她承认，“我不好。

我一直想和艾莎坐这艘船去大巡游，可现在……这本该是一段由艾莎和我一起完成的旅程。”尽管安娜没说出口，她心里却想：就像打理城堡，本也是我们该一起做的事。

可即便去过胡尔德精灵那儿之后，艾莎仍不放心把除掉暗夜魔狼的事交给她，而现在，她们击败噩梦的唯一机会——革命之刃——已碎成她斗篷口袋里细小的尖片。

斯文突然发出一声吼叫，安娜正好看见他疯狂地扭动，腿像在拼命奔逃一般踢蹬，即便仍在熟睡。

安娜跑过去，在他身旁蹲下，裙摆在她周围铺开。

她小心避开他的蹄子，伸出手，轻柔地拍起他的鼻子。

斯文慢慢停止踢蹬，可耳朵还在抖。“我把一切都搞砸了，”她一边继续轻轻抚摸斯文的头，一边说。“我以为我终于找到了答案。

可——”她长长地、颤抖着吸了口气——“我想错了。

而艾莎——她不放心让我随她去大巡游，不放心让我去击败暗夜魔狼，不放心让我做任何事，她是对的。”“咳——咳，”传来一声熟悉的清嗓。

她转头，看见威尔从船舱里爬上来。

她赶紧移开视线，把头低向海面，用头发当帘子。

她觉得自己受不了那个爱打听的记者的评判。

她几乎觉得自己承受不住任何事。“咳——咳。”清嗓声变得更执着了。“我无意中听到了，不过……你下去过底舱吗？

去艾莎的书房？”安娜摇了摇头。

她来过这艘王家船帮忙卸补给，却刻意避开艾莎的舱房，不愿看见里面高高堆着将陪艾莎远行的行李。“那我建议你去看看。”“我不知道，”安娜说，脑中浮现出艾莎如今披散在脸侧的乱发，以及嵌在她眼窝里那双暗夜魔狼的黄眼。

那画面会永远缠着她，她确信无疑。“现在看……看着会太难受了，”安娜说。

奥拉夫把手滑进她手里。“有时候，你走进山洞以为里面是狼，结果却是小狗。”安娜重重叹了口气，跟在奥拉夫身后，随他和威尔下楼去艾莎的书房。

走的时候，她不住偷偷打量威尔。

她惊讶于他竟愿意回来帮她。

威尔捕捉到她的一瞥，叹了口气。“我知道你在想什么，”他踏上吱呀作响的楼梯时说。“你知道？”安娜说，脸颊微微发烫。

威尔点头。“你觉得，正因为我总问你和你姐姐关于王国的一些尖锐问题，就说明我多半不喜欢你和阿伦黛尔。”他打开艾莎那船上的舱房的门，顿了顿，看着安娜。“但事实是，我问那些尖锐的问题，正因为我对阿伦黛尔爱得深，也正因为我相信你和艾莎。

要知道，提问往往是成就一件事的第一步。”安娜惊讶地发觉，是的，她完全明白。

她朝威尔微笑着说：“非常感谢你的提问，也谢谢你回来帮我们。”这话她是用整个身心说的。

威尔回以微笑，向后退开，好让她进去。

安娜倒吸一口气。

满眼都是向日葵。

画中的向日葵在木梁上起舞，也被雕在橱柜的把手上。

楼梯脚下铺着一块毛茸茸的向日葵地毯，明快的黄与春绿。

向日葵不是艾莎最喜欢的花。

那是安娜的。

艾莎一定是让人把整个书房都布置成这样，好让她想起妹妹。

想起家。

房间中央挂着一幅新定的画像，画上两个小女孩，一个浅金发，一个栗色发，正滑过结冰的池塘。

整个房间让人感觉像是一个拥抱。

威尔走到书桌前，从为艾莎大巡游而预先堆起的文件中抽出一页。“我觉得这一页你或许想看，”威尔说着递给她，然后悄然退出，留下安娜和奥拉夫独处。

安娜低头看那张纸，随即愣了一下，又看了一眼。

那是一道用艾莎优雅笔迹写下的诏书：我，阿伦黛尔女王艾莎，特此宣布，在我出航大巡游期间，由我妹妹、阿伦黛尔的安娜担任王国守护者。

她善良、体贴，以整颗心爱着阿伦黛尔。

我离家期间，无人比她更适合守护王国。

终于，安娜有了答案。

艾莎没邀她同去大巡游的原因——并非因为艾莎觉得安娜无能。

而是因为她知道安娜有用，需要安娜留在家里照看一切。

艾莎当然不愿安娜离开阿伦黛尔。

阿伦黛尔需要安娜，正如安娜需要它。“这才叫真爱！”奥拉夫歪着头读完，说道。“是啊，”安娜带着苦涩的微笑说。

一直以来，安娜都以为艾莎觉得她没用，可也许根本不是那样。

也许唯一不相信安娜有用的人……是安娜自己。

她想起艾莎把她封进的那个冰泡。

她原以为，那不过是艾莎又一次“保护型大姐姐”的做派，可如果其意不止于此呢？

如果她并非想保护安娜，而是想武装安娜，逼她等候、观察，因为她信任安娜——若最坏的事发生，安娜能想出解法呢？“奥拉夫，”安娜说，“麻烦你去把图娃叫到这儿来好吗？

我们时间不多了。”然而半小时后，安娜那脆弱的希望再次散了线。

她把搜集来的革命之刃碎片摊在艾莎的书桌上，看图娃能否拼回原样，可铁匠摇了摇头。“碎片太小，而且这金属——我从未见过这样的东西。

若阿黛在——”她念到亡妻的名字时哽住了——“若在，又能用上我们的锻炉，或许我办得到，可绝不可能赶得及修好，在这船上没有合适的工具就更不行了。”“你何必修它？”威尔在门口喊道。“这把剑头回就没管用——你怎么觉得这回就能管用？”“因为，”安娜说着，眼睛仍盯着舷窗。

夜空是不是开始泛亮了？“你只能以神话之物击败神话，而革命之刃绝对是神话之物。

再者——”她转头望向钉在墙上的阿伦黛尔地图。

那让她想起在密室里翻出的那张地图，母亲曾在上面写下父亲诸多箴言之一——“我父亲常说，过去总有一天会回来。”“而善有善报恶有恶报，就像风里的一个喷嚏，”奥拉夫补了一句。

他坐在桌边，端详着碎剑的碎片。“也许你该看看革命之刃与阿伦的过往。”安娜叹了口气。“我也想，可我手头并没有《阿伦传奇》的副本，艾莎也不在，没人能背诵。”“咳——咳，”威尔咳嗽一声。“研究古典的又不只艾莎一个。”“抱歉，威尔，”安娜说。“请你背吧，快一点。”不安涌上她心头，可她压了下去。“我们时间快不够了。”“‘流转的月与旋转的日，锻出一把弯刃……’”威尔开口诵道，安娜一边半听半试着翻阅其他可能有用的文件。“嘿，安娜，”奥拉夫说，“你不觉得，在最奇怪的地方也能找到爱，这事儿挺有意思吗？”安娜努力不叹气。

她平时爱听奥拉夫谈哲学——通常如此——可现在，离日出只剩几分钟，不是时候。“是啊，当然觉得有意思。

你为什么问这个？”“因为，”奥拉夫说，“它就坐在桌上呢。”安娜望过去，想看清他在说什么。

她没注意到奥拉夫一直在重新摆弄革命之刃的碎片，尤其是剑身顶端刻着剑名的部分，如今拼成了：L-O-V-E R-E-T-U “海水涌进，隐秘之力自闪亮之剑流泻，”威尔继续诵念——安娜的心猛地一跳。

一股隐秘之力。

安娜的心重新跳起，却快了一倍，思绪在她脑中翻滚，她看清了另外那几个字母。

笑容在她脸上绽开。“奥肯！”她朝甲板大喊。“把船再掉过头来！

我们还有个王国要救。”

sentences.en: She studied her hands, not sure what she expected to see. “We were going to,” Tuva called from the ship’s stern, her hands on the helm.
sentences.zh: 她端详着自己的手，不确定自己想看到什么。“我们本要走的，”图娃从船尾传来声音，双手把着舵。

sentences.en: In the yellow lantern light, the blacksmith looked ragged and her curly hair had been tugged into a cloud of frizz by the wind.
sentences.zh: 在黄灯笼的光下，这位铁匠显得疲惫不堪，卷发被风吹成一团蓬乱的毛。

sentences.en: Her brown eyes, however, remained warm as she looked at Anna. “But then we had a change of heart.
sentences.zh: 可她望向安娜时，那双棕眼依旧温柔。“但后来我们改变了主意。

sentences.en: And a good thing, too—or else we wouldn’t have been able to pick up SoYun.” “Since I live on the outskirts of the village,” SoYun said softly as she appeared from behind the post, a coil of thick rope in her arms, “the wolf ran straight by—and at that very moment, the rest of my herd fell asleep.
sentences.zh: 幸好如此——不然我们也接不上昭允了。”“我住在村庄郊外，”昭允从柱子后轻声走出，怀里抱着一卷粗绳，“狼直接从我身边跑过——而就在那一刻，我其余的鹿群都睡着了。

sentences.en: I realized I had to go seek a solution myself.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，我得自己去找解决办法。

sentences.en: So I rowed out onto the sea, hoping to find someone awake on the water, and that’s how they”—she gestured to Tuva and Oaken—“found me.” “I’m so glad,” Anna said, and she was pleased to note that while SoYun’s long black braid wasn’t yet in its usual tidiness, she looked less terrified than when she’d come upon Anna and Elsa in the woods.
sentences.zh: 于是我划船出海，盼着能在水上找到醒着的人，他们就是这么——”她指了指图娃和奥肯——“找到我的。”“我真高兴，”安娜说，她欣慰地注意到，尽管昭允长长的黑辫还没恢复平日的整齐，可她看起来比在林中撞见安娜与艾莎时少了些惊恐。

sentences.en: In fact, SoYun looked determined. “But,” Anna said, looking back at Tuva, “what kind of change convinced you to return?” “You,” Tuva said simply.
sentences.zh: 事实上，昭允神色坚定。“可是，”安娜转头看着图娃说，“是什么样的改变让你们回来的？”“你，”图娃干脆地说。

sentences.en: Anna blinked. “What do you mean?” Tuva turned the wheel, and the sails above rippled in the night breeze. “I mean,” she said, “that if a young woman like you could stick around, even though all was falling apart, and you don’t have powers of snow and ice, and I doubt you can lift a blacksmith’s hammer above your head for even a minute—then why couldn’t we?
sentences.zh: 安娜眨了眨眼。“什么意思？”图娃转动船轮，上方的帆在夜风里轻颤。“我是说，”她说，“像你这样一个年轻姑娘，即便一切都分崩离析，还能留下来；你既没有冰雪的魔力，我猜你也举不起铁匠的锤子哪怕一分钟——那我们凭什么不能留下？

sentences.en: After all, Arendelle is just as much our home as it is yours. “We’d only sailed out a little ways when we realized that we needed to return.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，阿伦黛尔既是你的家，也同样是我们的家。”“我们才驶出一小段路，就意识到该回去。

sentences.en: And so, we agreed to turn around in case you were still out there.
sentences.zh: 于是我们约定掉头，万一你还在外面。

sentences.en: And you were.
sentences.zh: 而你果然在。

sentences.en: So we scooped you up just in time and carried you to the ship, and now we’ve set sail again.” “We’re keeping an eye on the castle,” SoYun added. “Elsa…she’s…” “Still in there,” Tuva finished darkly. “Thank you.
sentences.zh: 所以我们及时把你捞起，送上船，现在又重新起航了。”“我们正盯着城堡，”昭允补了一句。“艾莎……她……”“还在里面，”图娃阴沉地接上。“谢谢你们。

sentences.en: H-how long have I been asleep?” Anna said.
sentences.zh: 我——我睡了多久？”安娜说。

sentences.en: Her thoughts reeled with the vision of Elsa falling victim to the Nattmara. “Only a few hours!” Olaf called from the prow. “Which is actually a short amount of time when you take in the eons of our galaxy.” Anna’s heart sped up.
sentences.zh: 想到艾莎沦为暗夜魔狼的牺牲品，她的心思一阵翻腾。“才几个小时！”奥拉夫从船头喊道。“若放到我们银河的亿万年里，这其实很短呢。”安娜的心猛地加速。

sentences.en: It was still the same night. “And when’s sunrise?” “In just an hour,” Oaken said.
sentences.zh: 还是同一个夜晚。“那日出是什么时候？”“再过一小时，”奥肯说。

sentences.en: An hour.
sentences.zh: 一小时。

sentences.en: Arendelle had a single hour before this terror became permanent.
sentences.zh: 阿伦黛尔只剩这最后一小时，否则这场恐怖将永远凝固。

sentences.en: Uneasy, Anna rose to her feet and headed to the railing.
sentences.zh: 安娜不安地起身，走向船舷。

sentences.en: She stared down at the black waters of the Arenfjord.
sentences.zh: 她低头凝视阿伦峡湾漆黑的海水。

sentences.en: They slapped relentlessly against the ship’s hull, giving rhythm to the terrible thoughts that swarmed through Anna’s mind: Elsa, failure, Elsa.
sentences.zh: 海水无情地拍打着船身，为安娜脑中蜂拥的恐怖念头打着节拍：艾莎，失败，艾莎。

sentences.en: A tear coursed down her cheek.
sentences.zh: 一滴泪顺着脸颊滑下。

sentences.en: Anna’s greatest fear wasn’t a wolf.
sentences.zh: 安娜最大的恐惧并非狼。

sentences.en: It never had been.
sentences.zh: 从来都不是。

sentences.en: It had been losing her sister.
sentences.zh: 她最大的恐惧，是失去姐姐。

sentences.en: Olaf took Anna’s hand in his. “You’re melting,” he said. “I wish I could share my permafrost with you.” Anna smiled as she wiped her face with the back of her hand. “I’m okay, Olaf.” She paused. “Actually,” she admitted, “I’m not okay.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫握住安娜的手。“你在融化，”他说。“真希望我能把我的永冻分些给你。”安娜用手背抹了把脸，微微一笑。“我没事，奥拉夫。”她顿了顿。“其实，”她承认，“我不好。

sentences.en: All along I wanted to go on the grand tour with Elsa on this very ship, but now…It was supposed to be a journey that Elsa and I did together.” And though Anna didn’t say it, she thought: Just like taking care of the castle is something we’re supposed to do together, too.
sentences.zh: 我一直想和艾莎坐这艘船去大巡游，可现在……这本该是一段由艾莎和我一起完成的旅程。”尽管安娜没说出口，她心里却想：就像打理城堡，本也是我们该一起做的事。

sentences.en: But even after the trip to the Huldrefólk, Elsa still hadn’t trusted her to get rid of the Nattmara, and now, their one and only chance of defeating the nightmare—Revolute—lay in tiny jagged pieces in her cloak pocket.
sentences.zh: 可即便去过胡尔德精灵那儿之后，艾莎仍不放心把除掉暗夜魔狼的事交给她，而现在，她们击败噩梦的唯一机会——革命之刃——已碎成她斗篷口袋里细小的尖片。

sentences.en: Sven suddenly bellowed, and Anna looked just in time to see him thrash wildly, his legs moving as though he were running for his life, even as he slumbered.
sentences.zh: 斯文突然发出一声吼叫，安娜正好看见他疯狂地扭动，腿像在拼命奔逃一般踢蹬，即便仍在熟睡。

sentences.en: Anna ran over and sank down beside him, her skirt billowing around her.
sentences.zh: 安娜跑过去，在他身旁蹲下，裙摆在她周围铺开。

sentences.en: Careful to avoid his hooves, she reached out and tenderly began to pat his nose.
sentences.zh: 她小心避开他的蹄子，伸出手，轻柔地拍起他的鼻子。

sentences.en: Slowly, Sven stopped kicking, but his ears continued to twitch. “I ruined it all,” she said, continuing to pet Sven gently on the head. “I thought I finally had the answer.
sentences.zh: 斯文慢慢停止踢蹬，可耳朵还在抖。“我把一切都搞砸了，”她一边继续轻轻抚摸斯文的头，一边说。“我以为我终于找到了答案。

sentences.en: But”—she drew a long, shuddering breath—“I thought wrong.
sentences.zh: 可——”她长长地、颤抖着吸了口气——“我想错了。

sentences.en: And Elsa—she was right not to trust me to come along on her grand tour, or to defeat the Nattmara, or to do anything at all.” “Ah-hem,” came a familiar throat-clearing.
sentences.zh: 而艾莎——她不放心让我随她去大巡游，不放心让我去击败暗夜魔狼，不放心让我做任何事，她是对的。”“咳——咳，”传来一声熟悉的清嗓。

sentences.en: She turned to see Wael climbing up out of the ship’s hull.
sentences.zh: 她转头，看见威尔从船舱里爬上来。

sentences.en: Quickly, she looked away and kept her head bent toward the water, using her hair as a curtain.
sentences.zh: 她赶紧移开视线，把头低向海面，用头发当帘子。

sentences.en: She didn’t think she could stomach the nosy journalist’s judgment.
sentences.zh: 她觉得自己受不了那个爱打听的记者的评判。

sentences.en: She barely felt like she could handle anything at all. “Ah- hem .” The throat clearing became more insistent. “I couldn’t help overhearing, but, well…have you been belowdecks yet?
sentences.zh: 她几乎觉得自己承受不住任何事。“咳——咳。”清嗓声变得更执着了。“我无意中听到了，不过……你下去过底舱吗？

sentences.en: To Elsa’s study?” Anna shook her head.
sentences.zh: 去艾莎的书房？”安娜摇了摇头。

sentences.en: She’d been to the royal ship to help unload rations, but she had made it a point to avoid Elsa’s cabin, unwilling to see it piled high with the luggage that would accompany Elsa far from home. “Then I suggest you check it out.” “I don’t know,” Anna said, thinking of the wild hair that now fanned around Elsa’s face and the yellow eyes of the Nattmara set into her sockets.
sentences.zh: 她来过这艘王家船帮忙卸补给，却刻意避开艾莎的舱房，不愿看见里面高高堆着将陪艾莎远行的行李。“那我建议你去看看。”“我不知道，”安娜说，脑中浮现出艾莎如今披散在脸侧的乱发，以及嵌在她眼窝里那双暗夜魔狼的黄眼。

sentences.en: That image would haunt her forever, she was certain of it. “It—it would hurt too much to see right now,” Anna said.
sentences.zh: 那画面会永远缠着她，她确信无疑。“现在看……看着会太难受了，”安娜说。

sentences.en: Olaf slid his hand into hers. “Sometimes, you walk into a cave thinking you’ll find wolves inside, but they turn out to be puppies.” With a heavy sigh, Anna shuffled after Olaf, following him and Wael downstairs to Elsa’s study.
sentences.zh: 奥拉夫把手滑进她手里。“有时候，你走进山洞以为里面是狼，结果却是小狗。”安娜重重叹了口气，跟在奥拉夫身后，随他和威尔下楼去艾莎的书房。

sentences.en: As she walked, she kept sneaking glances at Wael.
sentences.zh: 走的时候，她不住偷偷打量威尔。
