sentences.en: She was surprised that he’d been willing to come back and help her.
sentences.zh: 她惊讶于他竟愿意回来帮她。

sentences.en: Wael caught one of her glances and exhaled. “I know what you’re thinking,” he said as he stepped onto a groaning stair. “You do?” Anna said, her cheeks warming slightly.
sentences.zh: 威尔捕捉到她的一瞥，叹了口气。“我知道你在想什么，”他踏上吱呀作响的楼梯时说。“你知道？”安娜说，脸颊微微发烫。

sentences.en: Wael nodded. “You think that because I ask you and your sister hard questions about the kingdom, that I must not like you or Arendelle very much.” He opened the door to Elsa’s floating quarters and paused a moment to look at Anna. “But the truth is, I ask hard questions because I love Arendelle so much, and because I believe in you and Elsa.
sentences.zh: 威尔点头。“你觉得，正因为我总问你和你姐姐关于王国的一些尖锐问题，就说明我多半不喜欢你和阿伦黛尔。”他打开艾莎那船上的舱房的门，顿了顿，看着安娜。“但事实是，我问那些尖锐的问题，正因为我对阿伦黛尔爱得深，也正因为我相信你和艾莎。

sentences.en: You know, asking questions is often the first step to accomplishing something.” And Anna was surprised to realize that yes, she exactly knew.
sentences.zh: 要知道，提问往往是成就一件事的第一步。”安娜惊讶地发觉，是的，她完全明白。

sentences.en: She smiled at Wael and said, “Thank you so much for your questions, and for coming back to help us.” And she meant it with the whole of her being.
sentences.zh: 她朝威尔微笑着说：“非常感谢你的提问，也谢谢你回来帮我们。”这话她是用整个身心说的。

sentences.en: Wael returned the smile and stepped back so that she could enter.
sentences.zh: 威尔回以微笑，向后退开，好让她进去。

sentences.en: Anna gasped.
sentences.zh: 安娜倒吸一口气。

sentences.en: Everywhere, there were sunflowers.
sentences.zh: 满眼都是向日葵。

sentences.en: Painted sunflowers danced across wooden beams and were carved into the handles of the cupboards.
sentences.zh: 画中的向日葵在木梁上起舞，也被雕在橱柜的把手上。

sentences.en: A plush sunflower rug, cheery yellow and spring green, lay at the base of the stairs.
sentences.zh: 楼梯脚下铺着一块毛茸茸的向日葵地毯，明快的黄与春绿。

sentences.en: Sunflowers weren’t Elsa’s favorite flowers.
sentences.zh: 向日葵不是艾莎最喜欢的花。

sentences.en: They were Anna’s .
sentences.zh: 那是安娜的。

sentences.en: Elsa must have asked that the entire study be decorated to remind her of her sister.
sentences.zh: 艾莎一定是让人把整个书房都布置成这样，好让她想起妹妹。

sentences.en: To remind her of home.
sentences.zh: 想起家。

sentences.en: And in the center of the room hung a newly commissioned portrait of two little girls, one with white-blond hair and the other chestnut brown, skating across a frozen pond.
sentences.zh: 房间中央挂着一幅新定的画像，画上两个小女孩，一个浅金发，一个栗色发，正滑过结冰的池塘。

sentences.en: The entire room felt like a hug.
sentences.zh: 整个房间让人感觉像是一个拥抱。

sentences.en: Wael went to the desk and pulled out a page from the stacks that had already accumulated in anticipation of Elsa’s grand tour. “This is the one that I thought you might like to see,” Wael said, handing it to her before slipping out, leaving Anna alone with Olaf.
sentences.zh: 威尔走到书桌前，从为艾莎大巡游而预先堆起的文件中抽出一页。“我觉得这一页你或许想看，”威尔说着递给她，然后悄然退出，留下安娜和奥拉夫独处。

sentences.en: Anna peered down at the paper, then did a double take.
sentences.zh: 安娜低头看那张纸，随即愣了一下，又看了一眼。

sentences.en: It was a proclamation written in Elsa’s elegant handwriting: I, Elsa, Queen of Arendelle, do hereby proclaim my sister, Anna of Arendelle, Keeper of the Kingdom while I sail on the grand tour.
sentences.zh: 那是一道用艾莎优雅笔迹写下的诏书：我，阿伦黛尔女王艾莎，特此宣布，在我出航大巡游期间，由我妹妹、阿伦黛尔的安娜担任王国守护者。

sentences.en: She is kind, thoughtful, and loves Arendelle with the whole of her heart.
sentences.zh: 她善良、体贴，以整颗心爱着阿伦黛尔。

sentences.en: There is none better than her to watch over the kingdom while I am away.
sentences.zh: 我离家期间，无人比她更适合守护王国。

sentences.en: At last, Anna had an answer.
sentences.zh: 终于，安娜有了答案。

sentences.en: The reason Elsa had not invited her on the grand tour—it wasn’t because Elsa thought Anna was incompetent.
sentences.zh: 艾莎没邀她同去大巡游的原因——并非因为艾莎觉得安娜无能。

sentences.en: It was because she knew Anna was helpful, and she needed Anna at home to keep an eye on things.
sentences.zh: 而是因为她知道安娜有用，需要安娜留在家里照看一切。

sentences.en: Of course Elsa didn’t want Anna leaving Arendelle.
sentences.zh: 艾莎当然不愿安娜离开阿伦黛尔。

sentences.en: Arendelle needed Anna just as much as Anna needed it. “Now that’s true love!” said Olaf, who had angled his head to read it. “It is,” said Anna with a sad smile.
sentences.zh: 阿伦黛尔需要安娜，正如安娜需要它。“这才叫真爱！”奥拉夫歪着头读完，说道。“是啊，”安娜带着苦涩的微笑说。

sentences.en: All this time, Anna had thought that Elsa believed she was useless, but maybe that wasn’t the case at all.
sentences.zh: 一直以来，安娜都以为艾莎觉得她没用，可也许根本不是那样。

sentences.en: Maybe the only person who hadn’t believed that Anna was helpful…was Anna herself .
sentences.zh: 也许唯一不相信安娜有用的人……是安娜自己。

sentences.en: She remembered the ice bubble that Elsa had enclosed her in.
sentences.zh: 她想起艾莎把她封进的那个冰泡。

sentences.en: She’d thought it had been Elsa doing one more protective big sister act, but what if it was meant to be more than that?
sentences.zh: 她原以为，那不过是艾莎又一次“保护型大姐姐”的做派，可如果其意不止于此呢？

sentences.en: What if she wasn’t trying to be protective of Anna, but she was instead arming Anna, forcing her to wait and watch, because she trusted her to figure out the solution if the worst should happen? “Olaf,” Anna said, “would you mind getting Tuva down here, please?
sentences.zh: 如果她并非想保护安娜，而是想武装安娜，逼她等候、观察，因为她信任安娜——若最坏的事发生，安娜能想出解法呢？“奥拉夫，”安娜说，“麻烦你去把图娃叫到这儿来好吗？

sentences.en: We don’t have much time.” Half an hour later, though, Anna’s fragile hope had once again unraveled.
sentences.zh: 我们时间不多了。”然而半小时后，安娜那脆弱的希望再次散了线。

sentences.en: She’d laid out the collected pieces of Revolute across Elsa’s desk to see if Tuva could piece them together, but the blacksmith shook her head. “The pieces are too small, and the metal—I’ve never seen anything like it before.
sentences.zh: 她把搜集来的革命之刃碎片摊在艾莎的书桌上，看图娃能否拼回原样，可铁匠摇了摇头。“碎片太小，而且这金属——我从未见过这样的东西。

sentences.en: Maybe I could do it if Ada”—her breath caught on her wife’s name—“were around and I had access to our forge, but there’s no way it can be fixed in time, and definitely not on this ship without the proper tools.” “Why would you fix it?” Wael called from the doorway. “The sword didn’t work the first time—what makes you think it would work this time?” “Because,” Anna said, keeping her eye on the porthole.
sentences.zh: 若阿黛在——”她念到亡妻的名字时哽住了——“若在，又能用上我们的锻炉，或许我办得到，可绝不可能赶得及修好，在这船上没有合适的工具就更不行了。”“你何必修它？”威尔在门口喊道。“这把剑头回就没管用——你怎么觉得这回就能管用？”“因为，”安娜说着，眼睛仍盯着舷窗。

sentences.en: Was the night sky beginning to brighten? “You can only defeat a myth with a thing of myth, and Revolute is definitely a thing of myth.
sentences.zh: 夜空是不是开始泛亮了？“你只能以神话之物击败神话，而革命之刃绝对是神话之物。

sentences.en: Besides”—she turned her head to look at the map of Arendelle pinned to the wall.
sentences.zh: 再者——”她转头望向钉在墙上的阿伦黛尔地图。

sentences.en: It reminded her of the map she had uncovered in the secret room, the one where her mother had written one of their father’s many sayings—“my father used to say the past has a way of returning.” “And what goes around comes around again, like a sneeze in the wind,” Olaf added.
sentences.zh: 那让她想起在密室里翻出的那张地图，母亲曾在上面写下父亲诸多箴言之一——“我父亲常说，过去总有一天会回来。”“而善有善报恶有恶报，就像风里的一个喷嚏，”奥拉夫补了一句。

sentences.en: He sat at the desk, examining the pieces of the shattered sword. “Maybe you should look at Revolute and Aren’s past.” Anna sighed. “I would, but I don’t exactly have a copy of the Saga of Aren on me at the moment, and Elsa’s not here to declaim.” “Ah-hem,” Wael coughed. “Elsa is not the only one who studied the classics.” “Apologies, Wael,” Anna said. “Please perform, but quickly.” Unease filled her, but she tamped it down. “We’re running out of time.” “‘Revolving moon and spinning sun, forged a crescent blade…’” Wael began, and Anna half listened as she tried to skim the other documents that might be helpful. “Hey, Anna,” Olaf said, “don’t you think it’s funny how you can find love in the most curious places?” Anna tried not to sigh.
sentences.zh: 他坐在桌边，端详着碎剑的碎片。“也许你该看看革命之刃与阿伦的过往。”安娜叹了口气。“我也想，可我手头并没有《阿伦传奇》的副本，艾莎也不在，没人能背诵。”“咳——咳，”威尔咳嗽一声。“研究古典的又不只艾莎一个。”“抱歉，威尔，”安娜说。“请你背吧，快一点。”不安涌上她心头，可她压了下去。“我们时间快不够了。”“‘流转的月与旋转的日，锻出一把弯刃……’”威尔开口诵道，安娜一边半听半试着翻阅其他可能有用的文件。“嘿，安娜，”奥拉夫说，“你不觉得，在最奇怪的地方也能找到爱，这事儿挺有意思吗？”安娜努力不叹气。

sentences.en: She loved when Olaf discussed philosophy— usually —but now, mere minutes before sunrise, was not the time. “Yeah, sure I do.
sentences.zh: 她平时爱听奥拉夫谈哲学——通常如此——可现在，离日出只剩几分钟，不是时候。“是啊，当然觉得有意思。

sentences.en: Why are you asking?” “Because,” Olaf said, “it’s sitting here on the desk.” Anna looked over, trying to see what he was talking about.
sentences.zh: 你为什么问这个？”“因为，”奥拉夫说，“它就坐在桌上呢。”安娜望过去，想看清他在说什么。

sentences.en: She had not realized that Olaf had been rearranging the broken pieces of Revolute, specifically the top part of the blade that had held the inscription of the sword’s name, which now spelled out: L-O-V-E R-E-T-U “‘The sea rushed in as hidden power flowed from the gleaming sword,’” Wael continued to proclaim—and Anna’s heart skipped a beat.
sentences.zh: 她没注意到奥拉夫一直在重新摆弄革命之刃的碎片，尤其是剑身顶端刻着剑名的部分，如今拼成了：L-O-V-E R-E-T-U “海水涌进，隐秘之力自闪亮之剑流泻，”威尔继续诵念——安娜的心猛地一跳。

sentences.en: A hidden power.
sentences.zh: 一股隐秘之力。

sentences.en: Anna’s heart began beating again, but twice as fast, as thoughts tumbled through her mind and she took in the other letters.
sentences.zh: 安娜的心重新跳起，却快了一倍，思绪在她脑中翻滚，她看清了另外那几个字母。

sentences.en: A grin spread across her face. “Oaken!” she yelled up to the deck. “Turn this ship around again!
sentences.zh: 笑容在她脸上绽开。“奥肯！”她朝甲板大喊。“把船再掉过头来！

sentences.en: We have a kingdom to save.”
sentences.zh: 我们还有个王国要救。”

chapters.title: Chapter-Twenty-Five
chapters.en:
ANNA KNEW WHERE TO FIND HER SISTER.

The nearer the night drew to sunrise, the more foreign Anna’s home had seemed to become. Knobby branches twisted every which way, as if a forest of shadows had taken root in the land. And overhead, a great sandstorm spun, its center positioned directly over Arendelle Castle. Its great winds raised up high waves, and Anna and the rest of the crew covered their noses and mouths with the silk scarves that were originally meant to be gifts to the court of Corona, but now acted as shields so that they could breathe without inhaling sand as the royal ship glided closer.

Oaken steered the ship while Tuva barked commands at Wael, and SoYun and Anna helped with a complicated system of ropes and pulleys. Wael looked a little green around the gills, and Anna was grateful that she herself had a strong stomach.

But it was Olaf, a snowman who was used to falling apart and rolling in several directions at once, who was the biggest help. He made sure that the items on deck didn’t slam into anybody and that the still-sleeping Sven stayed safely out of harm’s way.

“Sharp turn!” Oaken warned, and the next second, he’d turned the royal ship to be parallel to the castle gates. But there was still a sizable distance between the ship’s deck and land.

“This is as close as we can get without smashing the ship!” Oaken called.

Anna stared down at the choppy gray water. Black sand sullied its usually white foam. She’d have to jump! But then she saw SoYun’s rope. Remembering how she’d escaped the Nattmara from Sorenson’s tower, she called to SoYun to throw the rope and latch it securely to a streetlamp.

When it was done, Anna clambered up onto the top rail. “Wish me luck!” She took the free end of the rope from SoYun—and jumped! Three long seconds passed as she soared into the air and over the water, and then, let go. With a thump, she landed on the castle grounds.

Anna winced, not because of the pain, but because she should have made a quieter entrance. Two pairs of glowing yellow eyes suddenly appeared at the front entrance to Arendelle Castle: Kai and Gerda. And their hair, too, had turned snow-white.

They still opened their mouths in a scream, but only a rasp came out. Anna shook her head in sorrow. Kai and Gerda had been trapped in a screaming nightmare reality for almost three whole days. It was a wonder they had any voice left at all. Unfortunately, they still seemed able—and eager—to wield their household weapons. The glint of Kai’s fire poker and Gerda’s sharp scissors still cut through the black sand.

What to do what to do what to do!

“Hoo-hoo, yellow-eyed wolf helpers!” Oaken called as he swung over the water and landed with surprising ease next to Anna. “It’s not polite to attack guests!”

“Oaken! Get back on the ship!” Anna instructed. “It’s not safe!”

“Don’t worry, Anna,” Oaken said with a nod to the ship where Wael, SoYun, Tuva, and Olaf were calling out to Kai and Gerda from the deck, distracting them from Anna. “We’ve got this, ja? We’ll lure them away and make sure they don’t come to any harm—or cause any. Now, go help Elsa!” He turned to Kai and Gerda, and waved his arms. “Over here!”

Anna nodded her thanks and rushed inside to find her sister…if there was anything left of her. She didn’t have a solid plan, but she was brave, and she had hope. And that would have to be enough.

The sand seemed thickest near the entry of the Great Hall, so Anna ran there as fast as she could on the strange combination of sand and hardwood. It slowed her progress, but still Anna pushed forward toward the double doors. Sure enough, as she drew closer, she could hear sobs. Shoving the doors open, Anna raced in.

Her sister sat on her throne, her yellow eyes staring unblinking into a dream that Anna could not see. As Elsa wept, strange flurries of black ice circled above her head. Anna’s heart squeezed.

“Elsa?” she whispered. “Elsa?”

But her sister’s expression didn’t change. Not wanting to startle Elsa, Anna slowly moved toward her. Suddenly, from the corner of the room, she heard a long, low growl. It was happening again! Her nightmare! It prowled out from behind the pillar—and attacked.

But Anna was prepared. She’d left her cloak unclasped for this very reason. And as the wolf leapt at her again, Anna flung her cloak off her shoulders and for the first time, instead of running away from the wolf, she ran toward it. She held her cloak above her head like a banner as she sprinted between its two front paws, each one as large as a boulder. The wolf realized a moment too late its prey’s route. Its teeth snapped down around the cloak, catching only fabric as Anna let go of it and raced under the protection of the wolf’s belly.

Holding her breath, she paused just long enough to hear the shred of cloth as the Nattmara’s teeth ripped the cloak, not quite yet realizing it was only a decoy. The charade would not last long, but it had bought her precious seconds.

Scurrying out from under the wolf’s tail, Anna hurled herself toward the throne.

Twelve feet left. Six. Three. She was almost there!

Arooooooooooooo!

The Nattmara had realized she had tricked it!

Anna’s blood turned cold as she glanced back. She shouldn’t have.

Because the wolf was upon her.

Claws the length of butcher’s knives raked across her back. She squeezed her eyes shut, waiting for the pain…but it never came.

In fact, Anna didn’t feel a thing.

Her eyes flew open just in time to see the Nattmara attack her again, but instead of colliding with her, it sailed right through Anna as though she were the one made of sand instead of the wolf. Her heart slammed into her chest. She hadn’t felt any pain. Had she become a ghost?

The Nattmara snarled, clearly as confused as she was. It lunged again, this time teeth first, but Anna felt nothing more than a light breeze as its fangs grazed her throat, leaving not a scratch. Like wind grasping at her. And for the first time, Anna didn’t feel the suffocating pull of the Nattmara on her thoughts, making her think terrifying and helpless things. Again, and again, the Nattmara attacked her, but nothing it did could hurt her.

Anna’s mind whirled at a frantic pace. Whenever she had been around the Nattmara before, thoughts of not being good enough had filled her and held her down. But now—now Anna knew, recalling the proclamation in Elsa’s traveling study, that she was good enough, and that she had always been.

The truth in those inked words seemed to have mended the cracks in her heart.

She was no longer afraid. The Nattmara could no longer harm her…so why was Anna’s nightmare still there?

Anna couldn’t concentrate! Elsa’s scream dug at her, and though the Nattmara’s fearsome claws could not hurt her anymore, each time Elsa wailed, Anna felt as though she’d been physically punched.

“Elsa!” Anna cried, staggering toward the throne. “Whatever you’re seeing, it isn’t real! It’s just a nightmare!” Her thoughts dashed frantically, and she grabbed onto one before it slid by. “Remember Mother and Father!” she said. “Hot chocolate! Cozy stories—” Anna broke off.

Wait a second.

Pretending to give her nightmares to Frigg the Fisherman had never helped Anna. But now she recalled Elsa’s words from two days earlier. Mother’s trick worked for me. I haven’t had a nightmare since.

Another thought darted by, this time, a memory of Sorenson’s voice, and his confusing words suddenly had meaning: The act of burying fear is what manifests the Nattmara, he’d said.

And now Anna understood. Fear only grew the longer it was ignored. Avoiding a nightmare only made it more powerful, more terrifying when it finally erupted again. And if Elsa had ignored her fears for years—if she had banished her nightmares away, then maybe they had taken on their own life, taken on their own shape….

Ulf the Wolf was always my favorite, Elsa had said in Sorenson’s tower. What if, instead of handing her nightmares over to a friendly fisherman as Anna had tried, Elsa had imagined feeding her fears to a hungry wolf?

Anna’s ideas came to her even quicker. Elsa’s rejected nightmares and fears, unable to latch onto Elsa but more powerful than most people’s fears, had weaseled their way into another scared, lonely child’s dreams—a child whose loneliness had gaped wide within her, leaving room for black sand and dark dreams to creep into her heart. A heart that had cracked when the child had been separated from her sister. Anna’s heart.

Realization thundered through her: Anna had not created the Nattmara—not with a spell or her own great worries. The wolf that had first appeared to her on that night sixteen years ago was not a manifestation of Anna’s fear. There had been another scared and lonely child in the castle beside her then, one who had also feared being separated from her sister: Elsa.

The Nattmara was Elsa’s nightmare! It was Elsa’s fear that they needed to conquer!

But…Anna had no idea what her sister was afraid of. Elsa was the strongest person she knew, a great queen, brave in the face of danger, determined, and regal.

What to do what to do what to do!

The Nattmara, frustrated by its futile attempts to inflict harm to Anna, let out an earsplitting howl. The sandstorm whipped up faster. While Anna might be safe from the beast’s attacks, Arendelle was not.

Anna ran toward Elsa, and though her stomach hurt as she looked at Elsa’s yellow eyes, she didn’t look away. The Nattmara had only come when they’d been separated—either by their parents when they were young, or by Elsa’s queenly responsibilities. So it would only be defeated, Anna guessed wildly, when they were together.

All Anna needed to figure out was what scared Elsa—but she truly had no idea what that could be.

“Elsa!” she cried as she approached the throne. “Elsa, I’m here! What’s wrong? What are you so scared of that you can’t tell me?”

Elsa just screamed harder, and the rush of black sand still spilling from her palms came quicker. It began to pile into a barrier between them, filling up the Great Hall. Eventually, it would reach the rafters, and then the ceiling, burying Elsa on her throne. Wait a minute—the throne!

They were in the Great Hall; the Nattmara had chosen it, so it must be Elsa’s least favorite room in the castle. And as Anna looked at the flurry of sand circling Elsa’s throne, spiraling up above her head to form a glittering crown of darkness, the answer came to her: Elsa was scared of being a bad queen.

“The people are all counting on me!” Elsa sobbed in her nightmare-scape. “Please! I’ll be better!”

Anna, no longer afraid of the Nattmara—but much more afraid of losing her sister forever—sprinted up the dais and grabbed Elsa’s hand. Elsa yanked it away from her, but Anna held tight.

Suddenly, Anna could see into Elsa’s nightmare: the endless meetings that Elsa felt awkward leading, not knowing what to say to people after having had very little social interaction for most of her life. Anna had always just thought Elsa was a good listener. Everyone seemed to think she was so wonderfully collected, but in truth, her quietness wasn’t composed thinking, but a deer-in-the-path-of-an-arrow kind of fright.

And the Nattmara had made her a bad queen—with the Blight. It all made sense to Anna now. Before the Nattmara had the strength to take on the physical shape of a wolf, it had seeped into the kingdom as a sickness, stalking the kingdom the same way it had stalked Elsa’s mind. And with the Blight came the people’s constant worry and questions, and Elsa had become more overwhelmed and even more fearful that she could not protect them. She had begun to crack at the seams while trying to keep it all inside. She had not been able to sleep…and so, Elsa’s suppressed nightmares had found another sleeping, worried sister to haunt until, at last, the fear in Arendelle—Elsa’s fear—had grown so great and powerful that the Nattmara could at last be seen by everyone. Because above all, Elsa feared hurting the kingdom—again. Of hurting Anna, again.

“Oh, Elsa,” Anna whispered, her heart aching. “Why didn’t you just tell me?” Anna held on to her sister’s hands, even as black sand pelted them from all around. “You’re perfect just the way you are! You’re a great leader! You pay attention to details, and your quietness gives you space to listen. I’m so proud of you, Elsa. You’re a wonderful sister, and you’re a role model for me. You’re someone I look up to!”

Was it just Anna’s imagination, or was her sister now squeezing her hand back? Ignoring the thrum of the Nattmara’s anger around them in the form of black sand spraying Anna’s face from all sides, Anna continued to talk, focusing all of herself on her sister—letting her know how she felt about her, just in the same way Elsa’s proclamation had shown Anna the truth.

“You know that I am better than who I think I am!” she yelled over the wind and battering sand. “I was so scared that you didn’t need me anymore since I wasn’t invited on the grand tour. But then I saw that the tour had nothing to do with me, and I realized that you are right—I am helpful, and I am always here for you and for our people, no matter what! Just as I know you are here for me!” Anna wasn’t sure if she was getting through to Elsa, but still she hung on, despite the growing swarm of assaulting black sand.

Elsa’s eyes shut tight. And then…“Anna?”

“Elsa!” Anna cried. “I’m here! I’m always here!”

Elsa turned her head, and Anna saw that her eyes were no longer yellow, but back to their usual beautiful shade of light blue. “Anna,” Elsa said, voice raspy from all the nightmare-induced screaming. “Of course I need you.”

The Nattmara threw back its head and howled in rage, the sound echoing endlessly around the hall.

Elsa clutched tight to Anna’s hand. “Why is it still here?” Elsa whirled her other hand up, ready to blast it with ice.

“No!” Anna shouted. “You can’t fight your fear—it only makes it stronger! Just as you can’t ignore your fear, because out of sight, it grows in strange ways and mutates.”

“Then what should I do?” Elsa asked, her voice cracking. “Dawn is almost here!”

“Accept it,” Anna breathed, praying she was right. “It’s okay to be afraid, Elsa. You just can’t let the fear take control of you! Fear is the shadow of love. You only fear because you care so much about Arendelle and about me, and that’s what makes you a great queen and a great leader. And a great sister. That’s why we love you, Elsa.”

It was the riddle that Olaf had helped her solve when he had rearranged the letters of the sword. Not R-E-V-O-L-U-T-E or L-O-V-E R-E-T-U, but T-R-U-E L-O-V-E was the way to defeat the Nattmara. And that was a thing of myth.

Elsa didn’t say anything, but then she held out her hand again. The giant wolf paused, the winds calmed down, and with each step the wolf took toward the sisters, it grew smaller. By the time it reached Elsa’s outstretched hand, the wolf was the size of a little wolf-puppy. It still had sharp teeth and claws, but it was manageable and could be contained.

“My fear,” Elsa said in awe. “I was so afraid of being a bad queen, but I don’t need to worry about that anymore. Because I’ve got you, Anna.”

Anna smiled and stayed put as the white wolf pup approached. She wasn’t scared of Elsa’s fear—it was a part of her sister, and she could never be afraid of her. The Nattmara’s power was truly done at last.

The puppy touched its nose to Elsa’s hand and turned into a cloud of sand, shimmering in the air, and then…just a single grain of black sand lay before the sisters. With a flick of her wrist, Elsa captured it in an ice crystal and caught it in her hand. Then she held it up to the dawn’s first ray of light.

“How?” she breathed. “How did we defeat the Nattmara without a thing of myth?”

“Because,” Anna said, peering at the crystal, “we do have a thing of myth—we’ve had it all along. Aren didn’t become a myth because he just so happened to own a fancy sword. Swords and crowns don’t change who we are.”

Elsa slipped the single grain of sand into her pocket. “Then what does?”

“True love,” Anna said, referencing the hidden power that the Saga of Aren spoke of. “The power that carved out Arenfjord. The same power that gave Aren the strength to go out in his boat to face an unknown danger, or up a mountain to face a dragon. It doesn’t matter which really happened—what matters is the choice he made.”

Suddenly, it hit her how sleepy she was, and her thoughts came to her like a lap of quiet ocean waves.

“It’s like how Sorenson said all myths contain a kernel of hard truth. It wasn’t a magical sword that carved out a home on the fjord. The myth wasn’t about the creation of the actual fjord—it was a myth about how, through love, Aren and the others in his generation believed in each other and trusted each other and loved each other enough to settle here and carve out a home for themselves, and for their future children, families, and friends. For us. A place where Arendelle’s flags could always fly strong.”

“True love,” Elsa mused. “The thing that can move mountains and defeat nightmares.”

“Exactly,” Anna said. She led Elsa over to the window, to the curtain she’d first spotted the wolf hiding behind. “Our love is worthy of the great myths. Us. The royal sisters of Arendelle.” Anna pulled back the curtain.

Sunlight rushed in. Dawn had fully broken, and the sun streaked across the horizon, brilliant gold in a gray-satin sky, shining down on a land full of vibrant color. No trace of the angry black sand or deathly pale rot remained.

And as she squinted in the direction of the rising sun, Anna noticed a figure walking toward the castle. There was something about the clothes and the shaggy hair that looked familiar….

“Kristoff!” Anna shouted.

Elsa rested a hand on Anna’s shoulder. “Go get him,” she said.

Anna grinned at her sister, then took off, flying into the second great hall and outside the castle, and then Kristoff was in her arms, kissing her again and again. She kissed him until the memories of the past few days faded away, and for the first time in a long time, she felt like everything was going to be good again.

With tears of joy streaming down her face, she took Kristoff’s face in her hands. “I’m so glad you’re okay,” she said.

“You know I will always come back to you,” Kristoff said, giving her a playful wink.

“Me too!” a new voice commented.

Anna looked up to see Olaf sitting on Sven’s antlers. Sven’s fur was still mottled white, but his eyes were bright and shiny once again. The smell of the sea lingered on his coat.

“Sven!” Kristoff cried with delight. Planting one last kiss on Anna’s cheek, he hurried over to the reindeer and hugged him tight, while Sven nuzzled him back. “You’re finally awake!”

He wiggled the reindeer’s lower lip and added in Sven Talk, “And you look like you’re half asleep.”

“Group hug,” Elsa said as she approached, and she enveloped everyone in her arms.

And with a happy yawn, Anna leaned her head against Elsa’s shoulder as the village bells began to toll across the fjord, calling all to rise and wake.
chapters.zh:
安娜知道去哪里找姐姐。

夜色越是临近破晓，安娜的家园就变得越陌生。

疙疙瘩瘩的树枝朝四面八方扭曲伸展，仿佛一片阴影森林在这片土地上扎了根。

头顶上，一场巨大的沙尘暴正在旋转，其中心正悬在阿伦黛尔城堡的正上方。

狂风掀起了高高的浪头，安娜和船上其余的人用丝巾捂住口鼻——这些丝巾本是要送给科罗纳王宫的礼物，如今却成了盾牌，让他们能在王室之船缓缓靠近时不被沙子呛到，得以呼吸。

奥肯掌着舵，图娃冲着威尔大声发令，素允和安娜则帮忙操纵一套复杂的绳索与滑轮系统。

威尔看上去有点脸色发青，安娜暗自庆幸自己肠胃够结实。

不过出力最大的还是奥拉夫——这个雪人习惯了散了架又朝好几个方向同时滚开。

他确保甲板上的东西不会撞到任何人，也让还在熟睡的斯文安全地待在危险之外。“急转弯！”奥肯喊道，下一秒，他便将王室之船掉头，与城堡大门平行。

但甲板与陆地之间仍有相当一段距离。“再靠近就要撞碎船了，我们最多只能到这儿！”奥肯喊道。

安娜低头盯着起伏不定的灰色海面。

黑沙弄脏了本应雪白的浪花。

她只能跳过去！

可就在这时，她看见了素允的绳子。

想起自己曾在索伦森的塔楼上从纳特玛拉手中逃脱，她冲素允喊着把绳子抛过来，牢牢挂到一根路灯柱上。

绳子固定好后，安娜爬上最高的栏杆。“祝我好运！”她从素允手中接过绳子的另一端——纵身一跃！

漫长的三秒钟里，她飞过天空与海面，然后松开了手。

砰的一声，她落在了城堡的地面上。

安娜皱了皱眉，不是因为疼，而是觉得自己本该悄无声息地落地才对。

阿伦黛尔城堡正门处忽然亮起两对发光的黄眼睛：是凯和格尔达。

他们的头发也变成了雪白。

他们仍张着嘴尖叫，却只发出沙哑的嘶声。

安娜悲伤地摇了摇头。

凯和格尔达被困在这尖叫的梦魇现实里，差不多整整三天了。

他们居然还留得住一点声音，简直是奇迹。

不幸的是，他们似乎仍然能够——而且急切地想要——挥舞起家里的“武器”。

凯的火钳和格尔达的尖剪刀闪着寒光，仍在黑沙中划出一道道亮线。

怎么办怎么办怎么办！“嗬嗬，黄眼睛的狼帮手们！”奥肯一边喊，一边荡过水面，出人意料地轻松落在安娜身边。“袭击客人可不礼貌！”“奥肯！

“快回船上去！”安娜吩咐道。“这里不安全！”“别担心，安娜，”奥肯说着朝船那边点了点头——威尔、素允、图娃和奥拉夫正在甲板上冲凯和格尔达喊话，把他们的注意力从安娜身上引开。“我们能应付，对吧？

“我们会把他们引开，保证他们既不受伤——也不伤人。

“快，去帮艾莎！”他转向凯和格尔达，挥舞着手臂。“这边来！”安娜点头道了谢，冲进城堡去寻找姐姐……如果她还留有残身的话。

她没有周全的计划，但她很勇敢，也抱有希望。

这应当就足够了。

大厅入口处的沙子似乎最厚，于是安娜踩着沙子和硬木地板这种怪异的组合，拼命朝那边跑去。

这拖慢了她的脚步，但安娜仍奋力朝那两扇大门冲去。

果然，越走近，她就越能听见抽泣声。

安娜推开大门，冲了进去。

姐姐坐在王座上，黄眼睛一眨不眨地盯着一个安娜看不见的梦境。

艾莎哭泣时，一团团诡异的黑冰在她头顶盘旋。

安娜的心一阵紧缩。“艾莎？”她轻声唤道。“艾莎？”可姐姐的神情毫无变化。

安娜不想惊到艾莎，便缓缓向她靠近。

忽然，她从房间角落听见一声低沉悠长的咆哮。

又来了！

她的噩梦！

它从柱子后面踱出——扑了上来。

但安娜早有准备。

她正是为此才没把斗篷扣上。

当恶狼再次扑来，安娜一把扯下肩上的斗篷，第一次，她没有逃离恶狼，而是朝它冲了过去。

她把斗篷举在头顶像一面旗帜，从那两只如巨石般巨大的前爪之间飞奔而过。

恶狼晚了一瞬才反应过来猎物的路线。

它的牙齿咬住斗篷，可只咬到了布料——安娜松手，钻到狼腹的庇护之下疾奔。

她屏住呼吸，只稍作停顿，便听见纳特玛拉的牙齿撕扯斗篷的裂帛声——它还没意识到那只是个诱饵。

这出戏撑不了多久，但已为她赢得了宝贵的几秒。

安娜从狼尾底下钻出，朝王座猛扑过去。

还有十二英尺。

六英尺。

三英尺。

她快到了！

嗷呜————！

纳特玛拉发现自己被耍了！

安娜回头一瞥，血液都凉了。

她本不该回头。

因为恶狼已经扑到她身上。

如屠刀般长的利爪从她背上划过。

她紧紧闭上眼，等着那阵疼痛……却迟迟没有到来。

事实上，安娜什么感觉都没有。

她猛地睁眼，正好看见纳特玛拉再次扑来——可它没有撞上她，而是径直穿过了安娜的身体，仿佛沙做的不是狼，而是她。

她的心猛撞在胸口。

她没感到一丝疼痛。

她变成了幽灵吗？

纳特玛拉发出低吼，显然和她一样困惑。

它再次猛扑，这次先用牙——可安娜只感到一阵轻风，尖牙擦过她的喉咙，没留下半点伤痕。

就像风在抓挠她。

而第一次，安娜没有感到纳特玛拉对她思绪那令人窒息的拉扯——那种让她想起可怕而无助之事的力量。

纳特玛拉一遍又一遍地攻击她，可它的一切都伤不到她。

安娜的思绪飞速旋转。

以往只要在纳特玛拉身边，那种“自己不够好”的念头就会充满她、压垮她。

可现在——现在安娜回想起了艾莎旅行书房里那篇宣言，明白自己已经足够好，而且一直都是。

那些墨写下的话语里的真相，仿佛修补了她心上的裂痕。

她不再害怕了。

纳特玛拉再也伤不了她……可为什么安娜的噩梦还在？

安娜无法集中精神！

艾莎的尖叫刺痛着她，尽管纳特玛拉可怕的利爪已伤不了她，可每次艾莎哀嚎，安娜都像被实实在在打了一拳。“艾莎！”安娜喊着，踉跄地朝王座挪去。“你看到的都不是真的！

“那只是个噩梦！”她的思绪慌乱地飞掠，她抓住其中一个不让它溜走。“记得爸爸妈妈吗！”她说。“热可可！

“还有那些温馨的故事——”安娜住了口。

等等。

假装把噩梦交给渔夫弗里格，对安娜从未奏效。

可现在她回想起了艾莎两天前说的话。

“妈妈的办法对我有效。”

“从那以后我就没再做噩梦了。”

又一个念头闪过——这次是索伦森的声音，他那令人费解的话忽然有了意义：他说，埋藏恐惧，正是纳特玛拉显现的缘由。

而现在安娜明白了。

恐惧越是久被忽视，就越发壮大。

逃避噩梦，只会让它在最终再次爆发时更加强大、更加可怕。

而如果艾莎多年来一直忽视自己的恐惧——如果她把噩梦驱逐在外，那么或许它们已有了自己的生命，有了自己的形状……

“狼乌尔夫一直是我最喜欢的，”艾莎曾在索伦森的塔里说过。

如果艾莎没有像安娜那样把噩梦交给一位友善的渔夫，而是想象着把恐惧喂给一头饥饿的狼呢？

安娜的念头来得更快了。

艾莎所排斥的噩梦与恐惧，无法依附在艾莎身上，却比多数人的恐惧更加强大，它们钻进了另一个胆小又孤独的孩子的梦里——那孩子的孤独在她心里张开了大口，给黑沙和黑暗之梦腾出了潜入心房的空隙。

那颗心，在女孩与姐姐分离时裂开了缝。

安娜的心。

顿悟如雷贯耳：创造纳特玛拉的并非安娜——既不是靠咒语，也不是靠她自己的重重忧虑。

十六年前那个夜晚第一次出现在她面前的狼，并不是安娜恐惧的化身。

那时城堡里，除了她还有另一个胆小又孤独的孩子，一个同样害怕与姐姐分离的孩子：艾莎。

纳特玛拉是艾莎的噩梦！

他们需要战胜的，是艾莎的恐惧！

可是……安娜全然不知姐姐在害怕什么。

艾莎是她认识的最坚强的人，一位伟大的女王，临危不惧、意志坚定、气度不凡。

怎么办怎么办怎么办！

纳特玛拉因一次次伤害安娜的徒劳尝试而暴怒，发出一声刺耳的嚎叫。

沙尘暴转得更快了。

尽管安娜或许躲过了这怪兽的攻击，阿伦黛尔却躲不过。

安娜朝艾莎跑去，虽然看着艾莎的黄眼睛让她心头作痛，她却没有移开目光。

纳特玛拉只在她们分离时才出现——无论是小时候被父母分开，还是被艾莎的女王职责分开。

所以安娜大胆猜测，只有她们在一起时，它才会被打败。

安娜只需弄明白艾莎怕什么——可她真心不知道那会是什么。“艾莎！”她冲向王座时喊道。“艾莎，我在这里！

“怎么了？

“你到底在怕什么，连都不肯告诉我？”艾莎只是叫得更凶，从她掌心涌出的黑沙流得更急了。

黑沙开始在两人之间堆成一道屏障，渐渐填满了大厅。

终有一天，它会堆到椽木，再堆到天花板，把坐在王座上的艾莎埋起来。

等等——王座！

她们在大厅里；纳特玛拉选了这里，所以它一定是城堡里艾莎最不喜欢的房间。

安娜望着环绕艾莎王座飞旋、在她头顶盘成黑暗璀璨王冠的沙暴，答案浮现了：艾莎害怕自己是个糟糕的女王。“所有人都指望我呢！”艾莎在她的梦魇之境中啜泣。“求求你！

“我会做得更好的！”安娜不再害怕纳特玛拉——却更害怕永远失去姐姐——她冲上高台，抓住了艾莎的手。

艾莎把手抽开，可安娜抓得紧紧的。

忽然，安娜看见了艾莎的噩梦：一场接一场开不完的会议，艾莎尴尬地主持着，大半生都少有社交的她不知该对众人说些什么。

安娜一直只当艾莎是个好听众。

人人都以为她沉稳自如，可事实上，她的安静并非深思熟虑，而是像鹿面对飞箭时那种惊惶失措。

而纳特玛拉借“枯萎病”把她变成了一个糟糕的女王。

此刻一切都说得通了。

在纳特玛拉有力气化作狼的实体之前，它已作为一种疾病渗入王国，像窥伺艾莎的心智那样窥伺着整个王国。

随着枯萎病而来的，是百姓们不绝的忧虑与质问，艾莎愈发不堪重负，更害怕自己护不住他们。

她强压着一切，却已开始从接缝处崩裂。

她无法入睡……于是，艾莎被压抑的噩梦找到了另一个睡着且忧心忡忡的妹妹来纠缠，直到最后，阿伦黛尔的恐惧——艾莎的恐惧——壮大到连所有人都能看见纳特玛拉。

因为说到底，艾莎最怕的是再伤害王国一次。

怕再伤害安娜一次。“噢，艾莎，”安娜轻声道，心头作痛。“你为什么不早点告诉我？”安娜紧握姐姐的双手，哪怕黑沙从四面八方打在他们身上。“你现在的样子就完美无缺！

“你是一位了不起的领袖！

“你关注细节，而你的安静给了你倾听的空间。

“我为你骄傲，艾莎。

“你是位好姐姐，也是我的榜样。

“是我仰慕的人！”是安娜的错觉，还是姐姐正回握住她的手？

无视四周以黑沙形式喷向安娜面庞、轰鸣着纳特玛拉怒火的沙暴，安娜继续诉说，把全部心神都放在姐姐身上——让她知道自己的心意，正如艾莎的宣言曾让安娜看见真相。“你知道我比自以为的更好！”她在风声与抽打的沙粒中大喊。“我好怕你不再需要我，因为我没被邀请参加那次盛大巡游。

“可后来我明白那次巡游与我无关，也意识到你是对的——我是有用的，而且无论发生什么，我永远陪着你，陪着我们的百姓！

“就像我知道你也永远陪着我！”安娜不确定自己是否触动了艾莎，可她仍坚持着，任凭越来越多袭来的黑沙成群扑来。

艾莎紧紧闭上了眼睛。

然后……“安娜？”“艾莎！”安娜喊道。“我在这里！

“我永远在这里！”艾莎转过头，安娜看见她的眼睛不再是黄色，而是恢复了平日那美丽的浅蓝。“安娜，”艾莎说，因整夜噩梦尖叫而声音沙哑。“我当然需要你。”纳特玛拉仰头发出愤怒的嚎叫，声音在大厅里无尽回荡。

艾莎紧紧攥住安娜的手。“它为什么还在？”艾莎举起另一只手，准备用冰轰击它。“不行！”安娜喊道。“你不能和自己的恐惧对抗——那只会让它更强！

“就像你也不能忽视恐惧，因为看不见它时，它会以奇怪的方式生长、变异。”“那我该怎么做？”艾莎问，声音发颤。“天快亮了！”“接纳它，”安娜轻声说，祈祷自己是对的。“害怕没关系，艾莎。

“你只是不能让恐惧掌控你！

“恐惧是爱的影子。

“你害怕，只因你那么在乎阿伦黛尔、在乎我，而正是这份在乎让你成为伟大的女王、伟大的领袖。

“也是位伟大的姐姐。

“这就是我们爱你的原因，艾莎。”这正是奥拉夫帮她解开的那道谜题——当时他重排了那把剑上的字母。

不是 R-E-V-O-L-U-T-E，也不是 L-O-V-E R-E-T-U，而是 T-R-U-E L-O-V-E（真爱），才是战胜纳特玛拉之道。

而那，正是神话之物。

艾莎没说话，却再次伸出了手。

巨狼停下了，风也平息了，它每朝姐妹俩走近一步，身躯便缩小一分。

等它走到艾莎伸出的手边时，已缩成一只小狼崽大小。

它仍有尖牙利爪，却已可控、可被收纳。“我的恐惧，”艾莎敬畏地说。“我曾那么怕自己是个糟糕的女王，可我不必再为此担忧了。

“因为我有你，安娜。”安娜微笑着一动不动，任由那白色小狼崽靠近。

她不怕艾莎的恐惧——那本是姐姐的一部分，她永远不会害怕姐姐。

纳特玛拉的力量终于彻底消散了。

小狼用鼻子碰了碰艾莎的手，化作一团在空中微光的沙云，然后……姐妹俩面前只剩下一粒黑沙。

艾莎手腕一抖，将那粒沙封进一枚冰晶，握在手中。

她把冰晶举向破晓的第一缕光。“怎么会？”她轻叹。“没有神话之物，我们怎么打败了纳特玛拉？”“因为，”安娜凝视着冰晶说，“我们确有神话之物——而且一直都有。

“阿伦之所以成为神话，不是因为他恰好拥有一把华丽的剑。

“剑与王冠改变不了我们是怎样的人。”艾莎把那粒沙塞进衣袋。“那什么才改变？”“真爱，”安娜说，指的是《阿伦传奇》中提及的那种隐秘力量。“是它开凿出了阿伦峡湾。

“同样的力量，给了阿伦驾船迎向未知险境、或登山直面巨龙的勇气。

“究竟哪个真的发生过并不重要——重要的是他所做的选择。”忽然，她强烈感到一阵困倦，思绪如静谧的海浪般涌来。“就像索伦森说的，一切神话都含有一粒坚硬的真相。

“在峡湾边开辟家园的，并非一把魔法剑。

“那神话讲的不是真实的峡湾如何诞生——而是关于，借着爱，阿伦与他那一代的人如何彼此信任、信赖、相爱，足以让他们在此定居，为自己、也为未来的子女、家人与朋友开辟出一个家园。

“为了我们。

“一个阿伦黛尔的旗帜永远高高飘扬的地方。”“真爱，”艾莎沉思道。“那能移山、能战胜噩梦的东西。”“正是，”安娜说。

她领艾莎走到窗边，走到她最初发现狼藏身其后的窗帘前。“我们的爱，配得上那些伟大神话。

“我们。

“阿伦黛尔的王室姐妹。”安娜拉开窗帘。

阳光涌了进来。

破晓已全然到来，太阳划过地平线，在灰缎般的天空中洒下灿烂的金色，照耀着一片色彩鲜亮的大地。

愤怒的黑沙与死灰般的苍白腐朽，了无痕迹。

她眯眼望向初升太阳的方向，看见一个身影正朝城堡走来。

那衣着和凌乱的头发透着几分熟悉……“克斯托夫！”安娜喊道。

艾莎把手搭在安娜肩头。“去迎接他吧，”她说。

安娜冲姐姐咧嘴一笑，随即飞奔而出，穿过第二座大厅冲出城堡，然后克斯托夫便拥她入怀，一遍又一遍地吻她。

她吻着他，直到这几天的记忆渐渐淡去，长久以来第一次，她觉得一切都会好起来。

喜悦的泪水顺着脸颊滑落，她双手捧起克斯托夫的脸。“你平安无事，我太高兴了，”她说。“你知道我永远会回到你身边，”克斯托夫调皮地眨眨眼。“我也是！”一个新声音插话道。

安娜抬头，看见奥拉夫坐在斯文的鹿角上。

斯文的毛仍斑驳地泛着白，但他的眼睛又明亮又有神了。

他的皮毛上还残留着海的气息。“斯文！”克斯托夫欢喜地喊。

他在安娜脸颊上印下最后一吻，便匆匆奔向驯鹿，紧紧抱住他，斯文也用鼻尖蹭着他。“你可算醒了！”他拽了拽驯鹿的下唇，用“斯文语”补了一句，“而且你看起来还半睡半醒呢。”“来个大大的拥抱，”艾莎走近说道，把所有人都揽进怀里。

安娜幸福地打了个哈欠，把头靠在艾莎肩上，与此同时，村庄的钟声跨过峡湾敲响，呼唤所有人起身苏醒。

sentences.en: ANNA KNEW WHERE TO FIND HER SISTER.
sentences.zh: 安娜知道去哪里找姐姐。

sentences.en: The nearer the night drew to sunrise, the more foreign Anna’s home had seemed to become.
sentences.zh: 夜色越是临近破晓，安娜的家园就变得越陌生。

sentences.en: Knobby branches twisted every which way, as if a forest of shadows had taken root in the land.
sentences.zh: 疙疙瘩瘩的树枝朝四面八方扭曲伸展，仿佛一片阴影森林在这片土地上扎了根。

sentences.en: And overhead, a great sandstorm spun, its center positioned directly over Arendelle Castle.
sentences.zh: 头顶上，一场巨大的沙尘暴正在旋转，其中心正悬在阿伦黛尔城堡的正上方。

sentences.en: Its great winds raised up high waves, and Anna and the rest of the crew covered their noses and mouths with the silk scarves that were originally meant to be gifts to the court of Corona, but now acted as shields so that they could breathe without inhaling sand as the royal ship glided closer.
sentences.zh: 狂风掀起了高高的浪头，安娜和船上其余的人用丝巾捂住口鼻——这些丝巾本是要送给科罗纳王宫的礼物，如今却成了盾牌，让他们能在王室之船缓缓靠近时不被沙子呛到，得以呼吸。

sentences.en: Oaken steered the ship while Tuva barked commands at Wael, and SoYun and Anna helped with a complicated system of ropes and pulleys.
sentences.zh: 奥肯掌着舵，图娃冲着威尔大声发令，素允和安娜则帮忙操纵一套复杂的绳索与滑轮系统。

sentences.en: Wael looked a little green around the gills, and Anna was grateful that she herself had a strong stomach.
sentences.zh: 威尔看上去有点脸色发青，安娜暗自庆幸自己肠胃够结实。

sentences.en: But it was Olaf, a snowman who was used to falling apart and rolling in several directions at once, who was the biggest help.
sentences.zh: 不过出力最大的还是奥拉夫——这个雪人习惯了散了架又朝好几个方向同时滚开。

sentences.en: He made sure that the items on deck didn’t slam into anybody and that the still-sleeping Sven stayed safely out of harm’s way. “Sharp turn!” Oaken warned, and the next second, he’d turned the royal ship to be parallel to the castle gates.
sentences.zh: 他确保甲板上的东西不会撞到任何人，也让还在熟睡的斯文安全地待在危险之外。“急转弯！”奥肯喊道，下一秒，他便将王室之船掉头，与城堡大门平行。

sentences.en: But there was still a sizable distance between the ship’s deck and land. “This is as close as we can get without smashing the ship!” Oaken called.
sentences.zh: 但甲板与陆地之间仍有相当一段距离。“再靠近就要撞碎船了，我们最多只能到这儿！”奥肯喊道。

sentences.en: Anna stared down at the choppy gray water.
sentences.zh: 安娜低头盯着起伏不定的灰色海面。

sentences.en: Black sand sullied its usually white foam.
sentences.zh: 黑沙弄脏了本应雪白的浪花。

sentences.en: She’d have to jump!
sentences.zh: 她只能跳过去！

sentences.en: But then she saw SoYun’s rope.
sentences.zh: 可就在这时，她看见了素允的绳子。

sentences.en: Remembering how she’d escaped the Nattmara from Sorenson’s tower, she called to SoYun to throw the rope and latch it securely to a streetlamp.
sentences.zh: 想起自己曾在索伦森的塔楼上从纳特玛拉手中逃脱，她冲素允喊着把绳子抛过来，牢牢挂到一根路灯柱上。

sentences.en: When it was done, Anna clambered up onto the top rail. “Wish me luck!” She took the free end of the rope from SoYun—and jumped!
sentences.zh: 绳子固定好后，安娜爬上最高的栏杆。“祝我好运！”她从素允手中接过绳子的另一端——纵身一跃！

sentences.en: Three long seconds passed as she soared into the air and over the water, and then, let go.
sentences.zh: 漫长的三秒钟里，她飞过天空与海面，然后松开了手。

sentences.en: With a thump, she landed on the castle grounds.
sentences.zh: 砰的一声，她落在了城堡的地面上。

sentences.en: Anna winced, not because of the pain, but because she should have made a quieter entrance.
sentences.zh: 安娜皱了皱眉，不是因为疼，而是觉得自己本该悄无声息地落地才对。

sentences.en: Two pairs of glowing yellow eyes suddenly appeared at the front entrance to Arendelle Castle: Kai and Gerda.
sentences.zh: 阿伦黛尔城堡正门处忽然亮起两对发光的黄眼睛：是凯和格尔达。

sentences.en: And their hair, too, had turned snow-white.
sentences.zh: 他们的头发也变成了雪白。

sentences.en: They still opened their mouths in a scream, but only a rasp came out.
sentences.zh: 他们仍张着嘴尖叫，却只发出沙哑的嘶声。

sentences.en: Anna shook her head in sorrow.
sentences.zh: 安娜悲伤地摇了摇头。

sentences.en: Kai and Gerda had been trapped in a screaming nightmare reality for almost three whole days.
sentences.zh: 凯和格尔达被困在这尖叫的梦魇现实里，差不多整整三天了。

sentences.en: It was a wonder they had any voice left at all.
sentences.zh: 他们居然还留得住一点声音，简直是奇迹。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, they still seemed able—and eager—to wield their household weapons.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，他们似乎仍然能够——而且急切地想要——挥舞起家里的“武器”。

sentences.en: The glint of Kai’s fire poker and Gerda’s sharp scissors still cut through the black sand.
sentences.zh: 凯的火钳和格尔达的尖剪刀闪着寒光，仍在黑沙中划出一道道亮线。

sentences.en: What to do what to do what to do! “Hoo-hoo, yellow-eyed wolf helpers!” Oaken called as he swung over the water and landed with surprising ease next to Anna. “It’s not polite to attack guests!” “Oaken!
sentences.zh: 怎么办怎么办怎么办！“嗬嗬，黄眼睛的狼帮手们！”奥肯一边喊，一边荡过水面，出人意料地轻松落在安娜身边。“袭击客人可不礼貌！”“奥肯！

sentences.en: Get back on the ship!” Anna instructed. “It’s not safe!” “Don’t worry, Anna,” Oaken said with a nod to the ship where Wael, SoYun, Tuva, and Olaf were calling out to Kai and Gerda from the deck, distracting them from Anna. “We’ve got this, ja ?
sentences.zh: “快回船上去！”安娜吩咐道。“这里不安全！”“别担心，安娜，”奥肯说着朝船那边点了点头——威尔、素允、图娃和奥拉夫正在甲板上冲凯和格尔达喊话，把他们的注意力从安娜身上引开。“我们能应付，对吧？

sentences.en: We’ll lure them away and make sure they don’t come to any harm—or cause any.
sentences.zh: “我们会把他们引开，保证他们既不受伤——也不伤人。

sentences.en: Now, go help Elsa!” He turned to Kai and Gerda, and waved his arms. “Over here!” Anna nodded her thanks and rushed inside to find her sister…if there was anything left of her.
sentences.zh: “快，去帮艾莎！”他转向凯和格尔达，挥舞着手臂。“这边来！”安娜点头道了谢，冲进城堡去寻找姐姐……如果她还留有残身的话。

sentences.en: She didn’t have a solid plan, but she was brave, and she had hope.
sentences.zh: 她没有周全的计划，但她很勇敢，也抱有希望。

sentences.en: And that would have to be enough.
sentences.zh: 这应当就足够了。

sentences.en: The sand seemed thickest near the entry of the Great Hall, so Anna ran there as fast as she could on the strange combination of sand and hardwood.
sentences.zh: 大厅入口处的沙子似乎最厚，于是安娜踩着沙子和硬木地板这种怪异的组合，拼命朝那边跑去。

sentences.en: It slowed her progress, but still Anna pushed forward toward the double doors.
sentences.zh: 这拖慢了她的脚步，但安娜仍奋力朝那两扇大门冲去。

sentences.en: Sure enough, as she drew closer, she could hear sobs.
sentences.zh: 果然，越走近，她就越能听见抽泣声。

sentences.en: Shoving the doors open, Anna raced in.
sentences.zh: 安娜推开大门，冲了进去。

sentences.en: Her sister sat on her throne, her yellow eyes staring unblinking into a dream that Anna could not see.
sentences.zh: 姐姐坐在王座上，黄眼睛一眨不眨地盯着一个安娜看不见的梦境。

sentences.en: As Elsa wept, strange flurries of black ice circled above her head.
sentences.zh: 艾莎哭泣时，一团团诡异的黑冰在她头顶盘旋。

sentences.en: Anna’s heart squeezed. “Elsa?” she whispered. “Elsa?” But her sister’s expression didn’t change.
sentences.zh: 安娜的心一阵紧缩。“艾莎？”她轻声唤道。“艾莎？”可姐姐的神情毫无变化。

sentences.en: Not wanting to startle Elsa, Anna slowly moved toward her.
sentences.zh: 安娜不想惊到艾莎，便缓缓向她靠近。

sentences.en: Suddenly, from the corner of the room, she heard a long, low growl.
sentences.zh: 忽然，她从房间角落听见一声低沉悠长的咆哮。

sentences.en: It was happening again!
sentences.zh: 又来了！

sentences.en: Her nightmare!
sentences.zh: 她的噩梦！

sentences.en: It prowled out from behind the pillar—and attacked.
sentences.zh: 它从柱子后面踱出——扑了上来。

sentences.en: But Anna was prepared.
sentences.zh: 但安娜早有准备。

sentences.en: She’d left her cloak unclasped for this very reason.
sentences.zh: 她正是为此才没把斗篷扣上。

sentences.en: And as the wolf leapt at her again, Anna flung her cloak off her shoulders and for the first time, instead of running away from the wolf, she ran toward it.
sentences.zh: 当恶狼再次扑来，安娜一把扯下肩上的斗篷，第一次，她没有逃离恶狼，而是朝它冲了过去。

sentences.en: She held her cloak above her head like a banner as she sprinted between its two front paws, each one as large as a boulder.
sentences.zh: 她把斗篷举在头顶像一面旗帜，从那两只如巨石般巨大的前爪之间飞奔而过。

sentences.en: The wolf realized a moment too late its prey’s route.
sentences.zh: 恶狼晚了一瞬才反应过来猎物的路线。

sentences.en: Its teeth snapped down around the cloak, catching only fabric as Anna let go of it and raced under the protection of the wolf’s belly.
sentences.zh: 它的牙齿咬住斗篷，可只咬到了布料——安娜松手，钻到狼腹的庇护之下疾奔。

sentences.en: Holding her breath, she paused just long enough to hear the shred of cloth as the Nattmara’s teeth ripped the cloak, not quite yet realizing it was only a decoy.
sentences.zh: 她屏住呼吸，只稍作停顿，便听见纳特玛拉的牙齿撕扯斗篷的裂帛声——它还没意识到那只是个诱饵。

sentences.en: The charade would not last long, but it had bought her precious seconds.
sentences.zh: 这出戏撑不了多久，但已为她赢得了宝贵的几秒。

sentences.en: Scurrying out from under the wolf’s tail, Anna hurled herself toward the throne.
sentences.zh: 安娜从狼尾底下钻出，朝王座猛扑过去。

sentences.en: Twelve feet left.
sentences.zh: 还有十二英尺。

sentences.en: Six.
sentences.zh: 六英尺。

sentences.en: Three.
sentences.zh: 三英尺。

sentences.en: She was almost there!
sentences.zh: 她快到了！

sentences.en: Arooooooooooooo!
The Nattmara had realized she had tricked it!
sentences.zh: 纳特玛拉发现自己被耍了！

sentences.en: Anna’s blood turned cold as she glanced back.
sentences.zh: 安娜回头一瞥，血液都凉了。

sentences.en: She shouldn’t have.
sentences.zh: 她本不该回头。

sentences.en: Because the wolf was upon her.
sentences.zh: 因为恶狼已经扑到她身上。

sentences.en: Claws the length of butcher’s knives raked across her back.
sentences.zh: 如屠刀般长的利爪从她背上划过。

sentences.en: She squeezed her eyes shut, waiting for the pain…but it never came.
sentences.zh: 她紧紧闭上眼，等着那阵疼痛……却迟迟没有到来。

sentences.en: In fact, Anna didn’t feel a thing .
sentences.zh: 事实上，安娜什么感觉都没有。

sentences.en: Her eyes flew open just in time to see the Nattmara attack her again, but instead of colliding with her, it sailed right through Anna as though she were the one made of sand instead of the wolf.
sentences.zh: 她猛地睁眼，正好看见纳特玛拉再次扑来——可它没有撞上她，而是径直穿过了安娜的身体，仿佛沙做的不是狼，而是她。

sentences.en: Her heart slammed into her chest.
sentences.zh: 她的心猛撞在胸口。

sentences.en: She hadn’t felt any pain.
sentences.zh: 她没感到一丝疼痛。

sentences.en: Had she become a ghost?
sentences.zh: 她变成了幽灵吗？

sentences.en: The Nattmara snarled, clearly as confused as she was.
sentences.zh: 纳特玛拉发出低吼，显然和她一样困惑。

sentences.en: It lunged again, this time teeth first, but Anna felt nothing more than a light breeze as its fangs grazed her throat, leaving not a scratch.
sentences.zh: 它再次猛扑，这次先用牙——可安娜只感到一阵轻风，尖牙擦过她的喉咙，没留下半点伤痕。

sentences.en: Like wind grasping at her.
sentences.zh: 就像风在抓挠她。

sentences.en: And for the first time, Anna didn’t feel the suffocating pull of the Nattmara on her thoughts, making her think terrifying and helpless things.
sentences.zh: 而第一次，安娜没有感到纳特玛拉对她思绪那令人窒息的拉扯——那种让她想起可怕而无助之事的力量。

sentences.en: Again, and again, the Nattmara attacked her, but nothing it did could hurt her.
sentences.zh: 纳特玛拉一遍又一遍地攻击她，可它的一切都伤不到她。

sentences.en: Anna’s mind whirled at a frantic pace.
sentences.zh: 安娜的思绪飞速旋转。

sentences.en: Whenever she had been around the Nattmara before, thoughts of not being good enough had filled her and held her down.
sentences.zh: 以往只要在纳特玛拉身边，那种“自己不够好”的念头就会充满她、压垮她。

sentences.en: But now—now Anna knew, recalling the proclamation in Elsa’s traveling study, that she was good enough, and that she had always been.
sentences.zh: 可现在——现在安娜回想起了艾莎旅行书房里那篇宣言，明白自己已经足够好，而且一直都是。

sentences.en: The truth in those inked words seemed to have mended the cracks in her heart.
sentences.zh: 那些墨写下的话语里的真相，仿佛修补了她心上的裂痕。

sentences.en: She was no longer afraid.
sentences.zh: 她不再害怕了。

sentences.en: The Nattmara could no longer harm her…so why was Anna’s nightmare still there?
sentences.zh: 纳特玛拉再也伤不了她……可为什么安娜的噩梦还在？

sentences.en: Anna couldn’t concentrate!
sentences.zh: 安娜无法集中精神！

sentences.en: Elsa’s scream dug at her, and though the Nattmara’s fearsome claws could not hurt her anymore, each time Elsa wailed, Anna felt as though she’d been physically punched. “Elsa!” Anna cried, staggering toward the throne. “Whatever you’re seeing, it isn’t real!
sentences.zh: 艾莎的尖叫刺痛着她，尽管纳特玛拉可怕的利爪已伤不了她，可每次艾莎哀嚎，安娜都像被实实在在打了一拳。“艾莎！”安娜喊着，踉跄地朝王座挪去。“你看到的都不是真的！

sentences.en: It’s just a nightmare!” Her thoughts dashed frantically, and she grabbed onto one before it slid by. “Remember Mother and Father!” she said. “Hot chocolate!
sentences.zh: “那只是个噩梦！”她的思绪慌乱地飞掠，她抓住其中一个不让它溜走。“记得爸爸妈妈吗！”她说。“热可可！

sentences.en: Cozy stories—” Anna broke off.
sentences.zh: “还有那些温馨的故事——”安娜住了口。

sentences.en: Wait a second.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: Pretending to give her nightmares to Frigg the Fisherman had never helped Anna.
sentences.zh: 假装把噩梦交给渔夫弗里格，对安娜从未奏效。

sentences.en: But now she recalled Elsa’s words from two days earlier.
sentences.zh: 可现在她回想起了艾莎两天前说的话。

sentences.en: Mother’s trick worked for me.
sentences.zh: “妈妈的办法对我有效。”

sentences.en: I haven’t had a nightmare since.
sentences.zh: “从那以后我就没再做噩梦了。”

sentences.en: Another thought darted by, this time, a memory of Sorenson’s voice, and his confusing words suddenly had meaning: The act of burying fear is what manifests the Nattmara , he’d said.
sentences.zh: 又一个念头闪过——这次是索伦森的声音，他那令人费解的话忽然有了意义：他说，埋藏恐惧，正是纳特玛拉显现的缘由。

sentences.en: And now Anna understood.
sentences.zh: 而现在安娜明白了。

sentences.en: Fear only grew the longer it was ignored.
sentences.zh: 恐惧越是久被忽视，就越发壮大。

sentences.en: Avoiding a nightmare only made it more powerful, more terrifying when it finally erupted again.
sentences.zh: 逃避噩梦，只会让它在最终再次爆发时更加强大、更加可怕。

sentences.en: And if Elsa had ignored her fears for years—if she had banished her nightmares away, then maybe they had taken on their own life, taken on their own shape….
sentences.zh: 而如果艾莎多年来一直忽视自己的恐惧——如果她把噩梦驱逐在外，那么或许它们已有了自己的生命，有了自己的形状……

sentences.en: Ulf the Wolf was always my favorite, Elsa had said in Sorenson’s tower.
sentences.zh: “狼乌尔夫一直是我最喜欢的，”艾莎曾在索伦森的塔里说过。

sentences.en: What if, instead of handing her nightmares over to a friendly fisherman as Anna had tried, Elsa had imagined feeding her fears to a hungry wolf?
sentences.zh: 如果艾莎没有像安娜那样把噩梦交给一位友善的渔夫，而是想象着把恐惧喂给一头饥饿的狼呢？

sentences.en: Anna’s ideas came to her even quicker.
sentences.zh: 安娜的念头来得更快了。

sentences.en: Elsa’s rejected nightmares and fears, unable to latch onto Elsa but more powerful than most people’s fears, had weaseled their way into another scared, lonely child’s dreams—a child whose loneliness had gaped wide within her, leaving room for black sand and dark dreams to creep into her heart.
sentences.zh: 艾莎所排斥的噩梦与恐惧，无法依附在艾莎身上，却比多数人的恐惧更加强大，它们钻进了另一个胆小又孤独的孩子的梦里——那孩子的孤独在她心里张开了大口，给黑沙和黑暗之梦腾出了潜入心房的空隙。

sentences.en: A heart that had cracked when the child had been separated from her sister.
sentences.zh: 那颗心，在女孩与姐姐分离时裂开了缝。

sentences.en: Anna’s heart.
sentences.zh: 安娜的心。

sentences.en: Realization thundered through her: Anna had not created the Nattmara—not with a spell or her own great worries.
sentences.zh: 顿悟如雷贯耳：创造纳特玛拉的并非安娜——既不是靠咒语，也不是靠她自己的重重忧虑。

sentences.en: The wolf that had first appeared to her on that night sixteen years ago was not a manifestation of Anna’s fear.
sentences.zh: 十六年前那个夜晚第一次出现在她面前的狼，并不是安娜恐惧的化身。

sentences.en: There had been another scared and lonely child in the castle beside her then, one who had also feared being separated from her sister: Elsa .
sentences.zh: 那时城堡里，除了她还有另一个胆小又孤独的孩子，一个同样害怕与姐姐分离的孩子：艾莎。

sentences.en: The Nattmara was Elsa’s nightmare!
sentences.zh: 纳特玛拉是艾莎的噩梦！

sentences.en: It was Elsa’s fear that they needed to conquer!
sentences.zh: 他们需要战胜的，是艾莎的恐惧！

sentences.en: But…Anna had no idea what her sister was afraid of.
sentences.zh: 可是……安娜全然不知姐姐在害怕什么。

sentences.en: Elsa was the strongest person she knew, a great queen, brave in the face of danger, determined, and regal.
sentences.zh: 艾莎是她认识的最坚强的人，一位伟大的女王，临危不惧、意志坚定、气度不凡。

sentences.en: What to do what to do what to do!
sentences.zh: 怎么办怎么办怎么办！

sentences.en: The Nattmara, frustrated by its futile attempts to inflict harm to Anna, let out an earsplitting howl.
sentences.zh: 纳特玛拉因一次次伤害安娜的徒劳尝试而暴怒，发出一声刺耳的嚎叫。

sentences.en: The sandstorm whipped up faster.
sentences.zh: 沙尘暴转得更快了。

sentences.en: While Anna might be safe from the beast’s attacks, Arendelle was not.
sentences.zh: 尽管安娜或许躲过了这怪兽的攻击，阿伦黛尔却躲不过。

sentences.en: Anna ran toward Elsa, and though her stomach hurt as she looked at Elsa’s yellow eyes, she didn’t look away.
sentences.zh: 安娜朝艾莎跑去，虽然看着艾莎的黄眼睛让她心头作痛，她却没有移开目光。

sentences.en: The Nattmara had only come when they’d been separated—either by their parents when they were young, or by Elsa’s queenly responsibilities.
sentences.zh: 纳特玛拉只在她们分离时才出现——无论是小时候被父母分开，还是被艾莎的女王职责分开。

sentences.en: So it would only be defeated, Anna guessed wildly, when they were together.
sentences.zh: 所以安娜大胆猜测，只有她们在一起时，它才会被打败。

sentences.en: All Anna needed to figure out was what scared Elsa—but she truly had no idea what that could be. “Elsa!” she cried as she approached the throne. “Elsa, I’m here!
sentences.zh: 安娜只需弄明白艾莎怕什么——可她真心不知道那会是什么。“艾莎！”她冲向王座时喊道。“艾莎，我在这里！

sentences.en: What’s wrong?
sentences.zh: “怎么了？

sentences.en: What are you so scared of that you can’t tell me?” Elsa just screamed harder, and the rush of black sand still spilling from her palms came quicker.
sentences.zh: “你到底在怕什么，连都不肯告诉我？”艾莎只是叫得更凶，从她掌心涌出的黑沙流得更急了。

sentences.en: It began to pile into a barrier between them, filling up the Great Hall.
sentences.zh: 黑沙开始在两人之间堆成一道屏障，渐渐填满了大厅。

sentences.en: Eventually, it would reach the rafters, and then the ceiling, burying Elsa on her throne.
sentences.zh: 终有一天，它会堆到椽木，再堆到天花板，把坐在王座上的艾莎埋起来。

sentences.en: Wait a minute—the throne!
sentences.zh: 等等——王座！

sentences.en: They were in the Great Hall; the Nattmara had chosen it, so it must be Elsa’s least favorite room in the castle.
sentences.zh: 她们在大厅里；纳特玛拉选了这里，所以它一定是城堡里艾莎最不喜欢的房间。

sentences.en: And as Anna looked at the flurry of sand circling Elsa’s throne, spiraling up above her head to form a glittering crown of darkness, the answer came to her: Elsa was scared of being a bad queen. “The people are all counting on me!” Elsa sobbed in her nightmare-scape. “Please!
sentences.zh: 安娜望着环绕艾莎王座飞旋、在她头顶盘成黑暗璀璨王冠的沙暴，答案浮现了：艾莎害怕自己是个糟糕的女王。“所有人都指望我呢！”艾莎在她的梦魇之境中啜泣。“求求你！

sentences.en: I’ll be better!” Anna, no longer afraid of the Nattmara—but much more afraid of losing her sister forever—sprinted up the dais and grabbed Elsa’s hand.
sentences.zh: “我会做得更好的！”安娜不再害怕纳特玛拉——却更害怕永远失去姐姐——她冲上高台，抓住了艾莎的手。

sentences.en: Elsa yanked it away from her, but Anna held tight.
sentences.zh: 艾莎把手抽开，可安娜抓得紧紧的。

sentences.en: Suddenly, Anna could see into Elsa’s nightmare: the endless meetings that Elsa felt awkward leading, not knowing what to say to people after having had very little social interaction for most of her life.
sentences.zh: 忽然，安娜看见了艾莎的噩梦：一场接一场开不完的会议，艾莎尴尬地主持着，大半生都少有社交的她不知该对众人说些什么。

sentences.en: Anna had always just thought Elsa was a good listener.
sentences.zh: 安娜一直只当艾莎是个好听众。

sentences.en: Everyone seemed to think she was so wonderfully collected, but in truth, her quietness wasn’t composed thinking, but a deer-in-the-path-of-an-arrow kind of fright.
sentences.zh: 人人都以为她沉稳自如，可事实上，她的安静并非深思熟虑，而是像鹿面对飞箭时那种惊惶失措。

sentences.en: And the Nattmara had made her a bad queen—with the Blight.
sentences.zh: 而纳特玛拉借“枯萎病”把她变成了一个糟糕的女王。

sentences.en: It all made sense to Anna now.
sentences.zh: 此刻一切都说得通了。

sentences.en: Before the Nattmara had the strength to take on the physical shape of a wolf, it had seeped into the kingdom as a sickness, stalking the kingdom the same way it had stalked Elsa’s mind.
sentences.zh: 在纳特玛拉有力气化作狼的实体之前，它已作为一种疾病渗入王国，像窥伺艾莎的心智那样窥伺着整个王国。

sentences.en: And with the Blight came the people’s constant worry and questions, and Elsa had become more overwhelmed and even more fearful that she could not protect them.
sentences.zh: 随着枯萎病而来的，是百姓们不绝的忧虑与质问，艾莎愈发不堪重负，更害怕自己护不住他们。

sentences.en: She had begun to crack at the seams while trying to keep it all inside.
sentences.zh: 她强压着一切，却已开始从接缝处崩裂。

sentences.en: She had not been able to sleep…and so, Elsa’s suppressed nightmares had found another sleeping, worried sister to haunt until, at last, the fear in Arendelle—Elsa’s fear—had grown so great and powerful that the Nattmara could at last be seen by everyone.
sentences.zh: 她无法入睡……于是，艾莎被压抑的噩梦找到了另一个睡着且忧心忡忡的妹妹来纠缠，直到最后，阿伦黛尔的恐惧——艾莎的恐惧——壮大到连所有人都能看见纳特玛拉。

sentences.en: Because above all, Elsa feared hurting the kingdom—again.
sentences.zh: 因为说到底，艾莎最怕的是再伤害王国一次。

sentences.en: Of hurting Anna, again. “Oh, Elsa,” Anna whispered, her heart aching. “Why didn’t you just tell me?” Anna held on to her sister’s hands, even as black sand pelted them from all around. “You’re perfect just the way you are!
sentences.zh: 怕再伤害安娜一次。“噢，艾莎，”安娜轻声道，心头作痛。“你为什么不早点告诉我？”安娜紧握姐姐的双手，哪怕黑沙从四面八方打在他们身上。“你现在的样子就完美无缺！

sentences.en: You’re a great leader!
sentences.zh: “你是一位了不起的领袖！

sentences.en: You pay attention to details, and your quietness gives you space to listen.
sentences.zh: “你关注细节，而你的安静给了你倾听的空间。

sentences.en: I’m so proud of you, Elsa.
sentences.zh: “我为你骄傲，艾莎。

sentences.en: You’re a wonderful sister, and you’re a role model for me.
sentences.zh: “你是位好姐姐，也是我的榜样。

sentences.en: You’re someone I look up to!” Was it just Anna’s imagination, or was her sister now squeezing her hand back?
sentences.zh: “是我仰慕的人！”是安娜的错觉，还是姐姐正回握住她的手？

sentences.en: Ignoring the thrum of the Nattmara’s anger around them in the form of black sand spraying Anna’s face from all sides, Anna continued to talk, focusing all of herself on her sister—letting her know how she felt about her, just in the same way Elsa’s proclamation had shown Anna the truth. “You know that I am better than who I think I am!” she yelled over the wind and battering sand. “I was so scared that you didn’t need me anymore since I wasn’t invited on the grand tour.
sentences.zh: 无视四周以黑沙形式喷向安娜面庞、轰鸣着纳特玛拉怒火的沙暴，安娜继续诉说，把全部心神都放在姐姐身上——让她知道自己的心意，正如艾莎的宣言曾让安娜看见真相。“你知道我比自以为的更好！”她在风声与抽打的沙粒中大喊。“我好怕你不再需要我，因为我没被邀请参加那次盛大巡游。

sentences.en: But then I saw that the tour had nothing to do with me, and I realized that you are right—I am helpful, and I am always here for you and for our people, no matter what!
sentences.zh: “可后来我明白那次巡游与我无关，也意识到你是对的——我是有用的，而且无论发生什么，我永远陪着你，陪着我们的百姓！

sentences.en: Just as I know you are here for me!” Anna wasn’t sure if she was getting through to Elsa, but still she hung on, despite the growing swarm of assaulting black sand.
sentences.zh: “就像我知道你也永远陪着我！”安娜不确定自己是否触动了艾莎，可她仍坚持着，任凭越来越多袭来的黑沙成群扑来。

sentences.en: Elsa’s eyes shut tight.
sentences.zh: 艾莎紧紧闭上了眼睛。

sentences.en: And then…“Anna?” “Elsa!” Anna cried. “I’m here!
sentences.zh: 然后……“安娜？”“艾莎！”安娜喊道。“我在这里！

sentences.en: I’m always here!” Elsa turned her head, and Anna saw that her eyes were no longer yellow, but back to their usual beautiful shade of light blue. “Anna,” Elsa said, voice raspy from all the nightmare-induced screaming. “Of course I need you.” The Nattmara threw back its head and howled in rage, the sound echoing endlessly around the hall.
sentences.zh: “我永远在这里！”艾莎转过头，安娜看见她的眼睛不再是黄色，而是恢复了平日那美丽的浅蓝。“安娜，”艾莎说，因整夜噩梦尖叫而声音沙哑。“我当然需要你。”纳特玛拉仰头发出愤怒的嚎叫，声音在大厅里无尽回荡。

sentences.en: Elsa clutched tight to Anna’s hand. “Why is it still here?” Elsa whirled her other hand up, ready to blast it with ice. “No!” Anna shouted. “You can’t fight your fear—it only makes it stronger!
sentences.zh: 艾莎紧紧攥住安娜的手。“它为什么还在？”艾莎举起另一只手，准备用冰轰击它。“不行！”安娜喊道。“你不能和自己的恐惧对抗——那只会让它更强！

sentences.en: Just as you can’t ignore your fear, because out of sight, it grows in strange ways and mutates.” “Then what should I do?” Elsa asked, her voice cracking. “Dawn is almost here!” “Accept it,” Anna breathed, praying she was right. “It’s okay to be afraid, Elsa.
sentences.zh: “就像你也不能忽视恐惧，因为看不见它时，它会以奇怪的方式生长、变异。”“那我该怎么做？”艾莎问，声音发颤。“天快亮了！”“接纳它，”安娜轻声说，祈祷自己是对的。“害怕没关系，艾莎。

sentences.en: You just can’t let the fear take control of you!
sentences.zh: “你只是不能让恐惧掌控你！

sentences.en: Fear is the shadow of love.
sentences.zh: “恐惧是爱的影子。

sentences.en: You only fear because you care so much about Arendelle and about me, and that’s what makes you a great queen and a great leader.
sentences.zh: “你害怕，只因你那么在乎阿伦黛尔、在乎我，而正是这份在乎让你成为伟大的女王、伟大的领袖。

sentences.en: And a great sister.
sentences.zh: “也是位伟大的姐姐。

sentences.en: That’s why we love you, Elsa.” It was the riddle that Olaf had helped her solve when he had rearranged the letters of the sword.
sentences.zh: “这就是我们爱你的原因，艾莎。”这正是奥拉夫帮她解开的那道谜题——当时他重排了那把剑上的字母。

sentences.en: Not R-E-V-O-L-U-T-E or L-O-V-E R-E-T-U , but T-R-U-E L-O-V-E was the way to defeat the Nattmara.
sentences.zh: 不是 R-E-V-O-L-U-T-E，也不是 L-O-V-E R-E-T-U，而是 T-R-U-E L-O-V-E（真爱），才是战胜纳特玛拉之道。

sentences.en: And that was a thing of myth.
sentences.zh: 而那，正是神话之物。

sentences.en: Elsa didn’t say anything, but then she held out her hand again.
sentences.zh: 艾莎没说话，却再次伸出了手。

sentences.en: The giant wolf paused, the winds calmed down, and with each step the wolf took toward the sisters, it grew smaller.
sentences.zh: 巨狼停下了，风也平息了，它每朝姐妹俩走近一步，身躯便缩小一分。

sentences.en: By the time it reached Elsa’s outstretched hand, the wolf was the size of a little wolf-puppy.
sentences.zh: 等它走到艾莎伸出的手边时，已缩成一只小狼崽大小。

sentences.en: It still had sharp teeth and claws, but it was manageable and could be contained. “My fear,” Elsa said in awe. “I was so afraid of being a bad queen, but I don’t need to worry about that anymore.
sentences.zh: 它仍有尖牙利爪，却已可控、可被收纳。“我的恐惧，”艾莎敬畏地说。“我曾那么怕自己是个糟糕的女王，可我不必再为此担忧了。

sentences.en: Because I’ve got you, Anna.” Anna smiled and stayed put as the white wolf pup approached.
sentences.zh: “因为我有你，安娜。”安娜微笑着一动不动，任由那白色小狼崽靠近。

sentences.en: She wasn’t scared of Elsa’s fear—it was a part of her sister, and she could never be afraid of her.
sentences.zh: 她不怕艾莎的恐惧——那本是姐姐的一部分，她永远不会害怕姐姐。

sentences.en: The Nattmara’s power was truly done at last.
sentences.zh: 纳特玛拉的力量终于彻底消散了。

sentences.en: The puppy touched its nose to Elsa’s hand and turned into a cloud of sand, shimmering in the air, and then…just a single grain of black sand lay before the sisters.
sentences.zh: 小狼用鼻子碰了碰艾莎的手，化作一团在空中微光的沙云，然后……姐妹俩面前只剩下一粒黑沙。

sentences.en: With a flick of her wrist, Elsa captured it in an ice crystal and caught it in her hand.
sentences.zh: 艾莎手腕一抖，将那粒沙封进一枚冰晶，握在手中。

sentences.en: Then she held it up to the dawn’s first ray of light. “How?” she breathed. “How did we defeat the Nattmara without a thing of myth?” “Because,” Anna said, peering at the crystal, “we do have a thing of myth—we’ve had it all along.
sentences.zh: 她把冰晶举向破晓的第一缕光。“怎么会？”她轻叹。“没有神话之物，我们怎么打败了纳特玛拉？”“因为，”安娜凝视着冰晶说，“我们确有神话之物——而且一直都有。

sentences.en: Aren didn’t become a myth because he just so happened to own a fancy sword.
sentences.zh: “阿伦之所以成为神话，不是因为他恰好拥有一把华丽的剑。

sentences.en: Swords and crowns don’t change who we are.” Elsa slipped the single grain of sand into her pocket. “Then what does?” “True love,” Anna said, referencing the hidden power that the Saga of Aren spoke of. “The power that carved out Arenfjord.
sentences.zh: “剑与王冠改变不了我们是怎样的人。”艾莎把那粒沙塞进衣袋。“那什么才改变？”“真爱，”安娜说，指的是《阿伦传奇》中提及的那种隐秘力量。“是它开凿出了阿伦峡湾。

sentences.en: The same power that gave Aren the strength to go out in his boat to face an unknown danger, or up a mountain to face a dragon.
sentences.zh: “同样的力量，给了阿伦驾船迎向未知险境、或登山直面巨龙的勇气。

sentences.en: It doesn’t matter which really happened—what matters is the choice he made.” Suddenly, it hit her how sleepy she was, and her thoughts came to her like a lap of quiet ocean waves. “It’s like how Sorenson said all myths contain a kernel of hard truth.
sentences.zh: “究竟哪个真的发生过并不重要——重要的是他所做的选择。”忽然，她强烈感到一阵困倦，思绪如静谧的海浪般涌来。“就像索伦森说的，一切神话都含有一粒坚硬的真相。

sentences.en: It wasn’t a magical sword that carved out a home on the fjord.
sentences.zh: “在峡湾边开辟家园的，并非一把魔法剑。

sentences.en: The myth wasn’t about the creation of the actual fjord—it was a myth about how, through love, Aren and the others in his generation believed in each other and trusted each other and loved each other enough to settle here and carve out a home for themselves, and for their future children, families, and friends.
sentences.zh: “那神话讲的不是真实的峡湾如何诞生——而是关于，借着爱，阿伦与他那一代的人如何彼此信任、信赖、相爱，足以让他们在此定居，为自己、也为未来的子女、家人与朋友开辟出一个家园。

sentences.en: For us.
sentences.zh: “为了我们。

sentences.en: A place where Arendelle’s flags could always fly strong.” “True love,” Elsa mused. “The thing that can move mountains and defeat nightmares.” “Exactly,” Anna said.
sentences.zh: “一个阿伦黛尔的旗帜永远高高飘扬的地方。”“真爱，”艾莎沉思道。“那能移山、能战胜噩梦的东西。”“正是，”安娜说。

sentences.en: She led Elsa over to the window, to the curtain she’d first spotted the wolf hiding behind. “Our love is worthy of the great myths.
sentences.zh: 她领艾莎走到窗边，走到她最初发现狼藏身其后的窗帘前。“我们的爱，配得上那些伟大神话。

sentences.en: Us.
sentences.zh: “我们。

sentences.en: The royal sisters of Arendelle.” Anna pulled back the curtain.
sentences.zh: “阿伦黛尔的王室姐妹。”安娜拉开窗帘。

sentences.en: Sunlight rushed in.
sentences.zh: 阳光涌了进来。

sentences.en: Dawn had fully broken, and the sun streaked across the horizon, brilliant gold in a gray-satin sky, shining down on a land full of vibrant color.
sentences.zh: 破晓已全然到来，太阳划过地平线，在灰缎般的天空中洒下灿烂的金色，照耀着一片色彩鲜亮的大地。

sentences.en: No trace of the angry black sand or deathly pale rot remained.
sentences.zh: 愤怒的黑沙与死灰般的苍白腐朽，了无痕迹。

sentences.en: And as she squinted in the direction of the rising sun, Anna noticed a figure walking toward the castle.
sentences.zh: 她眯眼望向初升太阳的方向，看见一个身影正朝城堡走来。

sentences.en: There was something about the clothes and the shaggy hair that looked familiar…. “Kristoff!” Anna shouted.
sentences.zh: 那衣着和凌乱的头发透着几分熟悉……“克斯托夫！”安娜喊道。

sentences.en: Elsa rested a hand on Anna’s shoulder. “Go get him,” she said.
sentences.zh: 艾莎把手搭在安娜肩头。“去迎接他吧，”她说。

sentences.en: Anna grinned at her sister, then took off, flying into the second great hall and outside the castle, and then Kristoff was in her arms, kissing her again and again.
sentences.zh: 安娜冲姐姐咧嘴一笑，随即飞奔而出，穿过第二座大厅冲出城堡，然后克斯托夫便拥她入怀，一遍又一遍地吻她。

sentences.en: She kissed him until the memories of the past few days faded away, and for the first time in a long time, she felt like everything was going to be good again.
sentences.zh: 她吻着他，直到这几天的记忆渐渐淡去，长久以来第一次，她觉得一切都会好起来。

sentences.en: With tears of joy streaming down her face, she took Kristoff’s face in her hands. “I’m so glad you’re okay,” she said. “You know I will always come back to you,” Kristoff said, giving her a playful wink. “Me too!” a new voice commented.
sentences.zh: 喜悦的泪水顺着脸颊滑落，她双手捧起克斯托夫的脸。“你平安无事，我太高兴了，”她说。“你知道我永远会回到你身边，”克斯托夫调皮地眨眨眼。“我也是！”一个新声音插话道。

sentences.en: Anna looked up to see Olaf sitting on Sven’s antlers.
sentences.zh: 安娜抬头，看见奥拉夫坐在斯文的鹿角上。

sentences.en: Sven’s fur was still mottled white, but his eyes were bright and shiny once again.
sentences.zh: 斯文的毛仍斑驳地泛着白，但他的眼睛又明亮又有神了。

sentences.en: The smell of the sea lingered on his coat. “Sven!” Kristoff cried with delight.
sentences.zh: 他的皮毛上还残留着海的气息。“斯文！”克斯托夫欢喜地喊。

sentences.en: Planting one last kiss on Anna’s cheek, he hurried over to the reindeer and hugged him tight, while Sven nuzzled him back. “You’re finally awake!” He wiggled the reindeer’s lower lip and added in Sven Talk, “And you look like you’re half asleep.” “Group hug,” Elsa said as she approached, and she enveloped everyone in her arms.
sentences.zh: 他在安娜脸颊上印下最后一吻，便匆匆奔向驯鹿，紧紧抱住他，斯文也用鼻尖蹭着他。“你可算醒了！”他拽了拽驯鹿的下唇，用“斯文语”补了一句，“而且你看起来还半睡半醒呢。”“来个大大的拥抱，”艾莎走近说道，把所有人都揽进怀里。

sentences.en: And with a happy yawn, Anna leaned her head against Elsa’s shoulder as the village bells began to toll across the fjord, calling all to rise and wake.
sentences.zh: 安娜幸福地打了个哈欠，把头靠在艾莎肩上，与此同时，村庄的钟声跨过峡湾敲响，呼唤所有人起身苏醒。

chapters.title: Chapter Twenty-Six
chapters.en:
AUTUMN LEAVES BLAZED in a golden glory.

The sky was a blue so clear that when Anna looked up, she thought she could practically see the domed palace of the sun where Aren had supposedly retrieved Revolute. She smiled to herself as she made her way through town back to Arendelle Castle, greeting everyone she saw.

“Nice to see you, Baker Blodget! Good day to you, Gabriella! Hello, Ada!”

“Hello, Anna!” Tuva’s wife called from behind a cart of beautiful golden wheat. Her hazel eyes sparkled. Not a hint of yellow lupine eyes to be seen.

“I’m glad to see you!” Anna said with a grin and a wave. She was practically skipping in her skirts. “We’ll have the best harvest festival ever tomorrow.”

“I hope so,” SoYun said as she herded a healthy Hebert along the road.

Madam Eniola curtsied, her arms laden with green zucchini. “I’m just glad the aphid outbreak that affected all my crops has cleared up.”

Anna arranged her face into what she hoped was an understanding—and not in any way knowing—expression. It had been one month since the events of the Nattmara. She wasn’t used to keeping secrets, and she didn’t particularly like it, but the villagers who’d fallen under the Nattmara’s enchantment had no memory about the danger they had all come so close to. In fact, all it seemed anyone could remember—apart from SoYun, Wael, Tuva, Olaf, and Elsa—was a light aphid breakout on some of the crops that had coated the harvest in white scales.

Even Kristoff and the others who hadn’t been under the Nattmara’s spell for all that long seemed to remember events differently. He recollected some of what had happened, but wasn’t able to parse out which memories had been real and which had been simply figments of his nightmare.

“Extra, extra, read all about it! Get your copy of the Village Crown!”

Anna looked over to see Wael selling his newspaper. Already, he had a crowd of villagers gathered. Many didn’t bother to wait before spreading open the paper and reading the day’s events right then and there. She caught a glimpse of the current headline: “More Than Royal: Sisters Are True Friends of the Kingdom.” Anna grinned.

Entering the castle, she took the steps three at a time, the letter she had picked up clutched in her fingers. She went to Elsa’s council chambers and knocked. Six staccato raps followed by two spaced-out ones. Do you want to build a snowman?

“Come in!” Elsa’s voice floated through the door.

So much had changed in the past month—at least, that’s how it felt to Anna, whose heart was much lighter than it had been in a long time. But she knew things hadn’t really changed for Elsa. After all, she still had to face the stress of leading the kingdom, and somehow, the stacks of papers seemed higher than ever before. As Anna entered the council chambers, she saw that Elsa, as always, was leaning over her table, her long quill scratching away at the reams of parchment.

Elsa remembered the whole thing, as did Anna. Anna suspected it was because her sister had been the reason the Nattmara came to Arendelle in the first place. It had been with both of them for much, much longer than a few nightmarish days. It had been with them for practically their entire lives, and was not easily forgotten.

Anna knew, too, that if Gerda or one of the royal handlers reached into the secret pocket sewn into the left sleeve of Elsa’s dress, they would find an ice crystal, perfect in its clarity except for the single grain of black sand at its center. Elsa would keep it with her always, close to her heart, acknowledging it, allowing her fear to motivate her, but not letting it take control.

“Elsa,” Anna said, flapping the letter under Elsa’s nose until her sister looked up from her paperwork. “Guess what I got!”

Elsa propped her chin on her hand and smiled. “A letter. I can see it in your hand.”

Anna rolled her eyes. “Yes, okay, but guess from whom I got it!” But she didn’t bother to wait for Elsa’s guess and plopped it down onto the table.

“Ugh, stop adding to my piles! Wait a second,” she said as she read the address. “It’s from Sorenson?”

Anna smiled. “It is! He wants to come visit. He says that he had a dream about us, and that he thought Mother would have liked for us to meet.”

Anna liked the grumpy old man and was pleased he hadn’t come to any lasting damage after the Nattmara attack, though she still felt bad that his life’s work had been ruined on the observation deck of his tower. She was looking forward to showing him the library in the castle, as well as the even bigger one down in the village. And she was eager to find out what he would have to teach her about the stars and about seeking answers in the world around them—and about the secret room. If being Elsa’s sister weren’t a full-time job, Anna thought she might want to become a scientist herself one day.

Elsa smiled. It was a true smile, if also a tired one.

“Are you feeling better?” Anna asked.

“Yes—actually, no,” Elsa said, catching herself. She was trying to be more honest with Anna—and herself—about what she was feeling. “I’ve been distracted of late.”

“Perfect,” Anna said.

Elsa’s eyebrows rose in surprise. “Perfect? What do you mean?”

“Because I know exactly how to help. Come with me.” She led Elsa out of the room and into the library.

There, Anna waltzed over to the horse statue and gave the hoof a tug. The bookcase swung open to reveal the secret room, but this time, no dust flew into the air.

She beckoned Elsa inside, and smiled when she heard Elsa’s gasp of delight.

When Elsa had been busy in the council chambers, Anna had been busy herself, prettying up the secret room and making it a fully cozy Elsa hideaway. She’d brought in more lanterns and settled comfy pillows around the floor, and even had the portrait of Aren restored. It now hung prominently on the wall, Revolute shining at its center as a symbol of hope and a reminder of what actually shaped the world.

“I know you’re tired and people keep interrupting you,” Anna said. “You give so much to the kingdom, but you need to take care of yourself, too. This can be a place for you to get away and just be you. Where you can rest and take a quiet moment to yourself, where no one will know where to find you. The past is in here, Elsa, but so is the future. I want you to remember that I will always believe in you.”

“Thank you, Anna.” Elsa turned to give her younger sister a hug. “This is magnificent.”

“And,” Anna said with a cheeky smile, “I’m reinstituting family game night.”

Elsa twisted her lips into a wry smile. “I would like that, but I always have so much work…”

“Sure.” Anna shrugged. “And it’s not going anywhere.”

“Game night…” Elsa said, looking around at the notes, books, and records their parents had collected. Anna had carefully placed Secrets of the Magic Makers in the center of the worktable alongside their father’s sketchbook. Even though it didn’t contain any actual spells, Anna sensed that it was important. After all, every story held some truth.

“Remember how we used play charades with Mother and Father?” Elsa asked.

Anna nodded. “You know,” she said, not sure how exactly to put her feelings into words, “I like this room because I can see a glimpse of who they were. I feel like here maybe they’re not so lost to us after all. Though I still wonder why they never told us about this room. And I wonder what they were looking for. And why Mother visited Sorenson.”

“Maybe we can ask him when he comes to visit,” Elsa said. “But maybe,” she added, fiddling with her sleeve cuff, “they were looking at magic. What must they have thought of my having magic, when no one else does? I mean, I can create these magical, wonderful things.…”

“Could be,” Anna said. “Speaking of your creations, I haven’t seen Olaf all day. Do you know where he is?”

Elsa smiled. “I do. And this time, I have a surprise for you.”

“But it’s not my birthday,” Anna said, all the while running through a catalogue of things she could possibly be getting.

“You’re not the only one who can plan a surprise,” Elsa said with a smile. They dashed up to Anna’s favorite turret, and Elsa led her out onto the little balcony.

“How did you find the time to plan a surprise?” Anna asked.

“There,” Elsa said, pointing in the direction of the open sea. “What do you see?”

Anna squinted. She couldn’t be certain at first, but then…“Elsa!” She gasped. “Those are ships! And they’re flying the royal flags of…Is that Zaria? And that one has the royal flag of Corona! And the third one—that’s the flag of Eldora!”

Elsa nodded. “Exactly right. The grand tour was cancelled, but the dignitaries understood. So much so, that they accepted my invitation to visit Arendelle now that the gates are open. This way, neither one of us has to leave home, where we are both needed.”

Anna’s grin felt so big that her cheeks couldn’t contain it. And as she looked down, watching the villagers meet the arriving visitors, Anna thought she saw a shiver in the shadows, and maybe, just maybe, a flick of a tail. Anna waved down, and she could have sworn that she saw a small Hulder waving at her from the shoulders of a taller one before slipping away again.

There was a slam of the door, and then Anna heard a thumping on the stairs before Kristoff burst onto the balcony, Sven with Olaf on his back following in his wake.

“Sorry!” Kristoff said. “I didn’t mean to be late. I was having an argument with Sven about something I just brought back from the trolls! He’s been funny lately. I keep thinking that he’s trying to tell me something—maybe about a ship?” He shrugged his shoulders. “But as far as I know, Sven’s never been on a ship.”

Sven nudged Kristoff with his antlers while Anna and Elsa exchanged a look of surprise. Other than their small group, the others didn’t seem to remember the Nattmara—but maybe the animals did.

Sven looked better than ever, Anna noticed. His curly reindeer hair was back to a rich brown without any unusual sprinkling of white. The Nattmara hadn’t caused any lasting damage.

In fact, it had taught Anna that Elsa didn’t have to be perfect, just as Anna didn’t have to be perfect. She could make mistakes—and to be honest, she would make mistakes. And that was okay. She had Elsa and Kristoff and Olaf to help her. And the gates were open. And yes, there were still secrets, there was still so much she didn’t know, but finding the answers to those questions would be an adventure…and she would not have to go on the journey alone.

There was nothing to fear.

“Look!” Olaf said, pointing toward a streak of light in the sky. “A chunk of space rock is falling through the atmosphere and burning up!”

“Or,” Elsa said with a smile, “you could just say it’s a falling star.”

“A shooting star,” Kristoff offered as he leaned against the rail and took Anna’s hand in his.

She squeezed it back. “A wishing star,” she said.

But at that moment, standing with her friends, looking up at the brilliant light of the meteor shower arcing over Arendelle, Anna had nothing to wish for at all—because everything she could have wished for was right there beside her.
