秋叶燃起一片金色的辉煌。

天空蓝得透彻，安娜抬头时，几乎觉得自己能看见那座太阳的穹顶宫殿——传说中阿伦取回雷伏卢特的地方。

她一边穿过小镇往阿伦黛尔城堡走，一边向每个遇见的人打招呼，心里暗自微笑。“见到你真高兴，面包师布洛杰特！

“日安，加布里埃拉！

“你好，艾达！”“你好，安娜！”图娃的妻子从一辆装满美丽金麦的推车后喊道。

她淡褐色的眼睛闪闪发亮。

一点黄眼睛的影子都看不到了。“真高兴见到你！”安娜咧嘴笑着挥手。

她提着裙摆几乎要跳着走了。“明天的丰收节一定会是史上最棒的。”“但愿如此，”素允一边沿路赶着健壮的赫伯特一边说。

埃尼奥拉夫人行了个屈膝礼，臂弯里堆满绿西葫芦。“我真高兴那场毁了我所有庄稼的蚜虫灾害总算过去了。”安娜摆出一副尽量显得理解——且绝不让自己显得知情——的表情。

纳特玛拉事件已过去一个月了。

她不习惯藏着秘密，也不怎么喜欢这样，可那些曾落入纳特玛拉魔咒的村民，对大家曾近在咫尺的危险毫无记忆。

事实上，除了素允、威尔、图娃、奥拉夫和艾莎，旁人记得的似乎只是一场轻微的蚜虫爆发，让部分庄稼蒙上了一层白色鳞屑。

就连克斯托夫和其他没被纳特玛拉缠太久的人，对事件的记忆也好像变了样。

他记得发生过的一些事，却分不清哪些记忆是真的、哪些只是他噩梦的碎片。“号外，号外，看最新消息！

“买份《村庄之冠》吧！”安娜转头，看见威尔在卖他的报纸。

他身旁已聚起一群村民。

许多人都等不及，当场就把报纸摊开读起当日的新闻。

她瞥见当下的头条：《不止是王室：姐妹俩是王国真正的朋友》。安娜露齿一笑。

走进城堡，她一步跨三级台阶，手里攥着刚取到的信。

她来到艾莎的议事厅前敲了敲门。

六下急促的敲门声，随后是两下间隔稍长的。

“要堆雪人吗？”“进来！”艾莎的声音隔着门飘了出来。

过去这一个月改变了许多——至少安娜是这么觉得的，她的心比很久以来都要轻松。

但她知道，对艾莎而言其实并无改变。

毕竟她仍要面对治理王国的压力，而那一摞摞公文，不知怎的似乎比以往更高了。

安娜走进议事厅，看见艾莎一如往常伏在桌前，长羽毛笔在成卷的羊皮纸上沙沙写着。

艾莎记得整件事，安娜也一样。

安娜猜想，这是因为姐姐本就是纳特玛拉最初降临阿伦黛尔的根源。

它伴随她们两人的时间，远比那几个噩梦般的日子要长得多。

它几乎贯穿了她们整个童年，难以轻易遗忘。

安娜也知道，若格尔达或某位王室侍从伸手探入缝在艾莎衣袖左侧的暗袋，会摸出一枚冰晶——通体澄澈，唯独中心嵌着那粒黑沙。

艾莎会永远把它带在身边、贴近心房，承认它的存在，让恐惧成为动力，却不任它掌控。“艾莎，”安娜说着，在姐姐鼻尖下抖着那封信，直到姐姐从公文里抬起头。“猜我拿到了什么！”艾莎手托下巴笑了。“一封信。

“我看见它在你手里了。”安娜翻了个白眼。“是啦是啦，可你猜是谁寄来的！”她却懒得等艾莎猜，直接把信拍在桌上。“唉，别再往我这儿添东西了！

“等等，”她读着收件地址说。“是索伦森寄来的？”安娜笑了。“就是他！

“他想来拜访。

“他说他梦到了我们，觉得妈妈应该会乐意让我们相识。”安娜很喜欢这臭脾气的老头，也高兴他在纳特玛拉袭击后没落下什么永久损伤，尽管她仍为他毕生心血毁于塔楼观测台而遗憾。

她盼着带他看城堡里的图书馆，还有村子里那座更大的。

她也急于想知道，关于星辰、关于在周遭世界里寻找答案——还有关于那间密室，他能教自己些什么。

安娜想，要不是当艾莎的妹妹已是全职工作，说不定有朝一日她自己也想当个科学家。

艾莎笑了。

那是真心的一笑，尽管也带着倦意。“你感觉好些了吗？”安娜问。“好些了——不，其实没有，”艾莎改口道。

她正试着对安娜——也对自己——更坦诚地面对感受。“近来我总是心不在焉。”“太好了，”安娜说。

艾莎惊讶地挑眉。“太好了？

“什么意思？”“因为我知道该怎么帮你。

“跟我来。”她领艾莎出了房间，走进图书馆。

在那里，安娜翩然走到那座马雕像前，拽了拽马掌。

书架转开，露出密室，但这次没有扬起灰尘。

她招手让艾莎进去，听到艾莎惊喜的吸气声，便笑了。

艾莎在议事厅忙碌时，安娜也没闲着，她把密室装点一新，打造成一个温馨十足的“艾莎小天地”。

她添了更多灯笼，在地面四周铺上舒服的靠垫，甚至让人修复了阿伦的画像。

如今它醒目地挂在墙上，雷伏卢特在画面中央熠熠生辉，既是希望的象征，也提醒着世人什么真正塑造了这个世界。“我知道你累了，又总有人来打扰你，”安娜说。“你为王国付出那么多，但也得照顾好自己。

“这里可以是你躲开一切、只做自己的地方。

“你可以休息，享受独处的安静时光，谁也不知道去哪儿找你。

“过去在这里，艾莎，未来也在这里。

“我要你记住，我会永远相信你。”“谢谢你，安娜。”艾莎转身为妹妹送上拥抱。“这真是太棒了。”“还有，”安娜俏皮一笑，“我要恢复家庭游戏之夜。”艾莎抿嘴苦笑。“我乐意，可我总是有那么多工作……”“没事，”安娜耸耸肩。“它又不会跑掉。”“游戏之夜……”艾莎环顾父母收集的笔记、书籍与札记说道。

安娜把《魔法创造者之谜》小心地放在工作台中央，旁边是父亲的速写本。

尽管书里并无真正的咒语，安娜却感到它很重要。

“毕竟每个故事都藏着几分真相。“还记得我们以前常和爸爸妈妈玩猜词游戏吗？”艾莎问。

安娜点头。“你知道吗，”她说，不太确定该如何措辞，“我喜欢这间屋子，因为我能瞥见他们曾经的样子。

“我觉得在这里，他们或许并不曾真正离我们而去。

“虽然我还是想知道，为什么他们从没告诉过我们这间屋子。

“也想知道他们在寻找什么。

“还有妈妈为何去拜访索伦森。”“等他来访时或许可以问问，”艾莎说。“不过也许，”她摆弄着袖口补充，“他们是在研究魔法。

“当别人都没有魔法，而我却拥有时，他们究竟会怎么想？

“我是说，我能造出这些神奇美妙的东西……”“有可能，”安娜说。“说到你造的东西，我今天一整天都没见着奥拉夫。

“你知道他在哪儿吗？”艾莎笑了。“我知道。

“而且这次，我要给你个惊喜。”“可今天不是我生日啊，”安娜说，脑子里却已把可能被送的东西列了一遍。“会准备惊喜的不止你一个，”艾莎笑道。

她们冲上安娜最喜欢的角楼，艾莎领她走到小阳台上。“你哪来的时间准备惊喜？”安娜问。“那儿，”艾莎指向开阔海面的方向。“你看见了什么？”安娜眯起眼。

起初她不敢确定，但随后……“艾莎！”她倒吸一口气。“那是船！

“而且挂着……那是扎里亚的王室旗帜吗？

“那一艘挂着科罗纳的王室旗帜！

“第三艘——那是埃尔多拉的旗帜！”艾莎点头。“完全正确。

“盛大巡游取消了，但那些使节都理解。

“正因为理解，他们接受了我的邀请，趁城门大开之时来访阿伦黛尔。

“这样，我们谁都不必离开家园——而这里正需要我们俩。”安娜笑得脸颊都快装不下了。

她低头望着村民迎接来访宾客，觉得自己看见阴影里微微一动，也许，只是也许，有一截尾巴轻轻一甩。

安娜朝下面挥手，她几乎可以发誓，瞥见一只小胡尔德从一只更高大的胡尔德肩头朝她挥手，随后又溜走了。

门砰地一声被推开，安娜听见楼梯上一阵咚咚声，接着克斯托夫冲上阳台，斯文背着奥拉夫紧随其后。“抱歉！”克斯托夫说。“我不是故意迟到的。

“我刚从地精那儿带回来一样东西，正跟斯文争那个呢！

“他最近怪怪的。

“我总觉得他想告诉我什么——也许是有关船？”他耸耸肩。“可据我所知，斯文从没上过船。”斯文用鹿角轻轻顶了顶克斯托夫，安娜和艾莎则交换了一个惊讶的眼神。

除了他们这个小圈子，旁人似乎都不记得纳特玛拉了——但动物们也许记得。

安娜注意到，斯文气色前所未有的好。

他卷曲的鹿毛恢复了浓密的棕色，再没有那些反常的白色斑点。

纳特玛拉没有留下任何永久伤害。

事实上，它教会了安娜：艾莎不必完美，正如安娜自己也不必完美。

她会犯错——老实说，她确实会犯错。

而那没关系。

她有艾莎、克斯托夫和奥拉夫帮她。

而且城门敞开着。

没错，仍有秘密，仍有许多她不知道的事，但寻找这些答案将是一场冒险……而这段旅程，她不必独自踏上。

没什么好怕的。“快看！”奥拉夫指着天边一道流光说。“一块太空石头正穿过大气层燃烧起来！”“或者，”艾莎笑道，“你也可以只说那是颗陨星。”“流星，”克斯托夫靠在栏杆上、握住安娜的手补充道。

她回握了一下。“一颗许愿星，”她说。

但那一刻，她和朋友们并肩而立，仰望划过阿伦黛尔上空的璀璨流星雨，却什么都不想许愿——因为凡是她所能企盼的，都已近在身旁。

sentences.zh: 她不习惯藏着秘密，也不怎么喜欢这样，可那些曾落入纳特玛拉魔咒的村民，对大家曾近在咫尺的危险毫无记忆。

sentences.en: In fact, all it seemed anyone could remember—apart from SoYun, Wael, Tuva, Olaf, and Elsa—was a light aphid breakout on some of the crops that had coated the harvest in white scales.
sentences.zh: 事实上，除了素允、威尔、图娃、奥拉夫和艾莎，旁人记得的似乎只是一场轻微的蚜虫爆发，让部分庄稼蒙上了一层白色鳞屑。

sentences.en: Even Kristoff and the others who hadn’t been under the Nattmara’s spell for all that long seemed to remember events differently.
sentences.zh: 就连克斯托夫和其他没被纳特玛拉缠太久的人，对事件的记忆也好像变了样。

sentences.en: He recollected some of what had happened, but wasn’t able to parse out which memories had been real and which had been simply figments of his nightmare. “Extra, extra, read all about it!
sentences.zh: 他记得发生过的一些事，却分不清哪些记忆是真的、哪些只是他噩梦的碎片。“号外，号外，看最新消息！

sentences.en: Get your copy of the Village Crown !” Anna looked over to see Wael selling his newspaper.
sentences.zh: “买份《村庄之冠》吧！”安娜转头，看见威尔在卖他的报纸。

sentences.en: Already, he had a crowd of villagers gathered.
sentences.zh: 他身旁已聚起一群村民。

sentences.en: Many didn’t bother to wait before spreading open the paper and reading the day’s events right then and there.
sentences.zh: 许多人都等不及，当场就把报纸摊开读起当日的新闻。

sentences.en: She caught a glimpse of the current headline: “More Than Royal: Sisters Are True Friends of the Kingdom.” Anna grinned.
sentences.zh: 她瞥见当下的头条：《不止是王室：姐妹俩是王国真正的朋友》。安娜露齿一笑。

sentences.en: Entering the castle, she took the steps three at a time, the letter she had picked up clutched in her fingers.
sentences.zh: 走进城堡，她一步跨三级台阶，手里攥着刚取到的信。

sentences.en: She went to Elsa’s council chambers and knocked.
sentences.zh: 她来到艾莎的议事厅前敲了敲门。

sentences.en: Six staccato raps followed by two spaced-out ones.
sentences.zh: 六下急促的敲门声，随后是两下间隔稍长的。

sentences.en: Do you want to build a snowman? “Come in!” Elsa’s voice floated through the door.
sentences.zh: “要堆雪人吗？”“进来！”艾莎的声音隔着门飘了出来。

sentences.en: So much had changed in the past month—at least, that’s how it felt to Anna, whose heart was much lighter than it had been in a long time.
sentences.zh: 过去这一个月改变了许多——至少安娜是这么觉得的，她的心比很久以来都要轻松。

sentences.en: But she knew things hadn’t really changed for Elsa.
sentences.zh: 但她知道，对艾莎而言其实并无改变。

sentences.en: After all, she still had to face the stress of leading the kingdom, and somehow, the stacks of papers seemed higher than ever before.
sentences.zh: 毕竟她仍要面对治理王国的压力，而那一摞摞公文，不知怎的似乎比以往更高了。

sentences.en: As Anna entered the council chambers, she saw that Elsa, as always, was leaning over her table, her long quill scratching away at the reams of parchment.
sentences.zh: 安娜走进议事厅，看见艾莎一如往常伏在桌前，长羽毛笔在成卷的羊皮纸上沙沙写着。

sentences.en: Elsa remembered the whole thing, as did Anna.
sentences.zh: 艾莎记得整件事，安娜也一样。

sentences.en: Anna suspected it was because her sister had been the reason the Nattmara came to Arendelle in the first place.
sentences.zh: 安娜猜想，这是因为姐姐本就是纳特玛拉最初降临阿伦黛尔的根源。

sentences.en: It had been with both of them for much, much longer than a few nightmarish days.
sentences.zh: 它伴随她们两人的时间，远比那几个噩梦般的日子要长得多。

sentences.en: It had been with them for practically their entire lives, and was not easily forgotten.
sentences.zh: 它几乎贯穿了她们整个童年，难以轻易遗忘。

sentences.en: Anna knew, too, that if Gerda or one of the royal handlers reached into the secret pocket sewn into the left sleeve of Elsa’s dress, they would find an ice crystal, perfect in its clarity except for the single grain of black sand at its center.
sentences.zh: 安娜也知道，若格尔达或某位王室侍从伸手探入缝在艾莎衣袖左侧的暗袋，会摸出一枚冰晶——通体澄澈，唯独中心嵌着那粒黑沙。

sentences.en: Elsa would keep it with her always, close to her heart, acknowledging it, allowing her fear to motivate her, but not letting it take control. “Elsa,” Anna said, flapping the letter under Elsa’s nose until her sister looked up from her paperwork. “Guess what I got!” Elsa propped her chin on her hand and smiled. “A letter.
sentences.zh: 艾莎会永远把它带在身边、贴近心房，承认它的存在，让恐惧成为动力，却不任它掌控。“艾莎，”安娜说着，在姐姐鼻尖下抖着那封信，直到姐姐从公文里抬起头。“猜我拿到了什么！”艾莎手托下巴笑了。“一封信。

sentences.en: I can see it in your hand.” Anna rolled her eyes. “Yes, okay, but guess from whom I got it!” But she didn’t bother to wait for Elsa’s guess and plopped it down onto the table. “Ugh, stop adding to my piles!
sentences.zh: “我看见它在你手里了。”安娜翻了个白眼。“是啦是啦，可你猜是谁寄来的！”她却懒得等艾莎猜，直接把信拍在桌上。“唉，别再往我这儿添东西了！

sentences.en: Wait a second,” she said as she read the address. “It’s from Sorenson?” Anna smiled. “It is!
sentences.zh: “等等，”她读着收件地址说。“是索伦森寄来的？”安娜笑了。“就是他！

sentences.en: He wants to come visit.
sentences.zh: “他想来拜访。

sentences.en: He says that he had a dream about us, and that he thought Mother would have liked for us to meet.” Anna liked the grumpy old man and was pleased he hadn’t come to any lasting damage after the Nattmara attack, though she still felt bad that his life’s work had been ruined on the observation deck of his tower.
sentences.zh: “他说他梦到了我们，觉得妈妈应该会乐意让我们相识。”安娜很喜欢这臭脾气的老头，也高兴他在纳特玛拉袭击后没落下什么永久损伤，尽管她仍为他毕生心血毁于塔楼观测台而遗憾。

sentences.en: She was looking forward to showing him the library in the castle, as well as the even bigger one down in the village.
sentences.zh: 她盼着带他看城堡里的图书馆，还有村子里那座更大的。

sentences.en: And she was eager to find out what he would have to teach her about the stars and about seeking answers in the world around them—and about the secret room.
sentences.zh: 她也急于想知道，关于星辰、关于在周遭世界里寻找答案——还有关于那间密室，他能教自己些什么。

sentences.en: If being Elsa’s sister weren’t a full-time job, Anna thought she might want to become a scientist herself one day.
sentences.zh: 安娜想，要不是当艾莎的妹妹已是全职工作，说不定有朝一日她自己也想当个科学家。

sentences.en: Elsa smiled.
sentences.zh: 艾莎笑了。

sentences.en: It was a true smile, if also a tired one. “Are you feeling better?” Anna asked. “Yes—actually, no,” Elsa said, catching herself.
sentences.zh: 那是真心的一笑，尽管也带着倦意。“你感觉好些了吗？”安娜问。“好些了——不，其实没有，”艾莎改口道。

sentences.en: She was trying to be more honest with Anna—and herself—about what she was feeling. “I’ve been distracted of late.” “Perfect,” Anna said.
sentences.zh: 她正试着对安娜——也对自己——更坦诚地面对感受。“近来我总是心不在焉。”“太好了，”安娜说。

sentences.en: Elsa’s eyebrows rose in surprise. “Perfect?
sentences.zh: 艾莎惊讶地挑眉。“太好了？

sentences.en: What do you mean?” “Because I know exactly how to help.
sentences.zh: “什么意思？”“因为我知道该怎么帮你。

sentences.en: Come with me.” She led Elsa out of the room and into the library.
sentences.zh: “跟我来。”她领艾莎出了房间，走进图书馆。

sentences.en: There, Anna waltzed over to the horse statue and gave the hoof a tug.
sentences.zh: 在那里，安娜翩然走到那座马雕像前，拽了拽马掌。

sentences.en: The bookcase swung open to reveal the secret room, but this time, no dust flew into the air.
sentences.zh: 书架转开，露出密室，但这次没有扬起灰尘。

sentences.en: She beckoned Elsa inside, and smiled when she heard Elsa’s gasp of delight.
sentences.zh: 她招手让艾莎进去，听到艾莎惊喜的吸气声，便笑了。

sentences.en: When Elsa had been busy in the council chambers, Anna had been busy herself, prettying up the secret room and making it a fully cozy Elsa hideaway.
sentences.zh: 艾莎在议事厅忙碌时，安娜也没闲着，她把密室装点一新，打造成一个温馨十足的“艾莎小天地”。

sentences.en: She’d brought in more lanterns and settled comfy pillows around the floor, and even had the portrait of Aren restored.
sentences.zh: 她添了更多灯笼，在地面四周铺上舒服的靠垫，甚至让人修复了阿伦的画像。

sentences.en: It now hung prominently on the wall, Revolute shining at its center as a symbol of hope and a reminder of what actually shaped the world. “I know you’re tired and people keep interrupting you,” Anna said. “You give so much to the kingdom, but you need to take care of yourself, too.
sentences.zh: 如今它醒目地挂在墙上，雷伏卢特在画面中央熠熠生辉，既是希望的象征，也提醒着世人什么真正塑造了这个世界。“我知道你累了，又总有人来打扰你，”安娜说。“你为王国付出那么多，但也得照顾好自己。

sentences.en: This can be a place for you to get away and just be you.
sentences.zh: “这里可以是你躲开一切、只做自己的地方。

sentences.en: Where you can rest and take a quiet moment to yourself, where no one will know where to find you.
sentences.zh: “你可以休息，享受独处的安静时光，谁也不知道去哪儿找你。

sentences.en: The past is in here, Elsa, but so is the future.
sentences.zh: “过去在这里，艾莎，未来也在这里。

sentences.en: I want you to remember that I will always believe in you.” “Thank you, Anna.” Elsa turned to give her younger sister a hug. “This is magnificent.” “And,” Anna said with a cheeky smile, “I’m reinstituting family game night.” Elsa twisted her lips into a wry smile. “I would like that, but I always have so much work…” “Sure.” Anna shrugged. “And it’s not going anywhere.” “Game night…” Elsa said, looking around at the notes, books, and records their parents had collected.
sentences.zh: “我要你记住，我会永远相信你。”“谢谢你，安娜。”艾莎转身为妹妹送上拥抱。“这真是太棒了。”“还有，”安娜俏皮一笑，“我要恢复家庭游戏之夜。”艾莎抿嘴苦笑。“我乐意，可我总是有那么多工作……”“没事，”安娜耸耸肩。“它又不会跑掉。”“游戏之夜……”艾莎环顾父母收集的笔记、书籍与札记说道。

sentences.en: Anna had carefully placed Secrets of the Magic Makers in the center of the worktable alongside their father’s sketchbook.
sentences.zh: 安娜把《魔法创造者之谜》小心地放在工作台中央，旁边是父亲的速写本。

sentences.en: Even though it didn’t contain any actual spells, Anna sensed that it was important.
sentences.zh: 尽管书里并无真正的咒语，安娜却感到它很重要。

sentences.en: After all, every story held some truth. “Remember how we used play charades with Mother and Father?” Elsa asked.
sentences.zh: “毕竟每个故事都藏着几分真相。“还记得我们以前常和爸爸妈妈玩猜词游戏吗？”艾莎问。

sentences.en: Anna nodded. “You know,” she said, not sure how exactly to put her feelings into words, “I like this room because I can see a glimpse of who they were.
sentences.zh: 安娜点头。“你知道吗，”她说，不太确定该如何措辞，“我喜欢这间屋子，因为我能瞥见他们曾经的样子。

sentences.en: I feel like here maybe they’re not so lost to us after all.
sentences.zh: “我觉得在这里，他们或许并不曾真正离我们而去。

sentences.en: Though I still wonder why they never told us about this room.
sentences.zh: “虽然我还是想知道，为什么他们从没告诉过我们这间屋子。

sentences.en: And I wonder what they were looking for.
sentences.zh: “也想知道他们在寻找什么。

sentences.en: And why Mother visited Sorenson.” “Maybe we can ask him when he comes to visit,” Elsa said. “But maybe,” she added, fiddling with her sleeve cuff, “they were looking at magic.
sentences.zh: “还有妈妈为何去拜访索伦森。”“等他来访时或许可以问问，”艾莎说。“不过也许，”她摆弄着袖口补充，“他们是在研究魔法。

sentences.en: What must they have thought of my having magic, when no one else does?
sentences.zh: “当别人都没有魔法，而我却拥有时，他们究竟会怎么想？

sentences.en: I mean, I can create these magical, wonderful things.…” “Could be,” Anna said. “Speaking of your creations, I haven’t seen Olaf all day.
sentences.zh: “我是说，我能造出这些神奇美妙的东西……”“有可能，”安娜说。“说到你造的东西，我今天一整天都没见着奥拉夫。

sentences.en: Do you know where he is?” Elsa smiled. “I do.
sentences.zh: “你知道他在哪儿吗？”艾莎笑了。“我知道。

sentences.en: And this time, I have a surprise for you .” “But it’s not my birthday,” Anna said, all the while running through a catalogue of things she could possibly be getting. “You’re not the only one who can plan a surprise,” Elsa said with a smile.
sentences.zh: “而且这次，我要给你个惊喜。”“可今天不是我生日啊，”安娜说，脑子里却已把可能被送的东西列了一遍。“会准备惊喜的不止你一个，”艾莎笑道。

sentences.en: They dashed up to Anna’s favorite turret, and Elsa led her out onto the little balcony. “How did you find the time to plan a surprise?” Anna asked. “There,” Elsa said, pointing in the direction of the open sea. “What do you see?” Anna squinted.
sentences.zh: 她们冲上安娜最喜欢的角楼，艾莎领她走到小阳台上。“你哪来的时间准备惊喜？”安娜问。“那儿，”艾莎指向开阔海面的方向。“你看见了什么？”安娜眯起眼。

sentences.en: She couldn’t be certain at first, but then…“Elsa!” She gasped. “Those are ships!
sentences.zh: 起初她不敢确定，但随后……“艾莎！”她倒吸一口气。“那是船！

sentences.en: And they’re flying the royal flags of…Is that Zaria?
sentences.zh: “而且挂着……那是扎里亚的王室旗帜吗？

sentences.en: And that one has the royal flag of Corona!
sentences.zh: “那一艘挂着科罗纳的王室旗帜！

sentences.en: And the third one—that’s the flag of Eldora!” Elsa nodded. “Exactly right.
sentences.zh: “第三艘——那是埃尔多拉的旗帜！”艾莎点头。“完全正确。

sentences.en: The grand tour was cancelled, but the dignitaries understood.
sentences.zh: “盛大巡游取消了，但那些使节都理解。

sentences.en: So much so, that they accepted my invitation to visit Arendelle now that the gates are open.
sentences.zh: “正因为理解，他们接受了我的邀请，趁城门大开之时来访阿伦黛尔。

sentences.en: This way, neither one of us has to leave home, where we are both needed.” Anna’s grin felt so big that her cheeks couldn’t contain it.
sentences.zh: “这样，我们谁都不必离开家园——而这里正需要我们俩。”安娜笑得脸颊都快装不下了。

sentences.en: And as she looked down, watching the villagers meet the arriving visitors, Anna thought she saw a shiver in the shadows, and maybe, just maybe, a flick of a tail.
sentences.zh: 她低头望着村民迎接来访宾客，觉得自己看见阴影里微微一动，也许，只是也许，有一截尾巴轻轻一甩。

sentences.en: Anna waved down, and she could have sworn that she saw a small Hulder waving at her from the shoulders of a taller one before slipping away again.
sentences.zh: 安娜朝下面挥手，她几乎可以发誓，瞥见一只小胡尔德从一只更高大的胡尔德肩头朝她挥手，随后又溜走了。

sentences.en: There was a slam of the door, and then Anna heard a thumping on the stairs before Kristoff burst onto the balcony, Sven with Olaf on his back following in his wake. “Sorry!” Kristoff said. “I didn’t mean to be late.
sentences.zh: 门砰地一声被推开，安娜听见楼梯上一阵咚咚声，接着克斯托夫冲上阳台，斯文背着奥拉夫紧随其后。“抱歉！”克斯托夫说。“我不是故意迟到的。

sentences.en: I was having an argument with Sven about something I just brought back from the trolls!
sentences.zh: “我刚从地精那儿带回来一样东西，正跟斯文争那个呢！

sentences.en: He’s been funny lately.
sentences.zh: “他最近怪怪的。

sentences.en: I keep thinking that he’s trying to tell me something—maybe about a ship?” He shrugged his shoulders. “But as far as I know, Sven’s never been on a ship.” Sven nudged Kristoff with his antlers while Anna and Elsa exchanged a look of surprise.
sentences.zh: “我总觉得他想告诉我什么——也许是有关船？”他耸耸肩。“可据我所知，斯文从没上过船。”斯文用鹿角轻轻顶了顶克斯托夫，安娜和艾莎则交换了一个惊讶的眼神。

sentences.en: Other than their small group, the others didn’t seem to remember the Nattmara—but maybe the animals did.
sentences.zh: 除了他们这个小圈子，旁人似乎都不记得纳特玛拉了——但动物们也许记得。

sentences.en: Sven looked better than ever, Anna noticed.
sentences.zh: 安娜注意到，斯文气色前所未有的好。

sentences.en: His curly reindeer hair was back to a rich brown without any unusual sprinkling of white.
sentences.zh: 他卷曲的鹿毛恢复了浓密的棕色，再没有那些反常的白色斑点。

sentences.en: The Nattmara hadn’t caused any lasting damage.
sentences.zh: 纳特玛拉没有留下任何永久伤害。

sentences.en: In fact, it had taught Anna that Elsa didn’t have to be perfect, just as Anna didn’t have to be perfect.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它教会了安娜：艾莎不必完美，正如安娜自己也不必完美。

sentences.en: She could make mistakes—and to be honest, she would make mistakes.
sentences.zh: 她会犯错——老实说，她确实会犯错。

sentences.en: And that was okay.
sentences.zh: 而那没关系。

sentences.en: She had Elsa and Kristoff and Olaf to help her.
sentences.zh: 她有艾莎、克斯托夫和奥拉夫帮她。

sentences.en: And the gates were open.
sentences.zh: 而且城门敞开着。

sentences.en: And yes, there were still secrets, there was still so much she didn’t know, but finding the answers to those questions would be an adventure…and she would not have to go on the journey alone.
sentences.zh: 没错，仍有秘密，仍有许多她不知道的事，但寻找这些答案将是一场冒险……而这段旅程，她不必独自踏上。

sentences.en: There was nothing to fear. “Look!” Olaf said, pointing toward a streak of light in the sky. “A chunk of space rock is falling through the atmosphere and burning up!” “Or,” Elsa said with a smile, “you could just say it’s a falling star.” “A shooting star,” Kristoff offered as he leaned against the rail and took Anna’s hand in his.
sentences.zh: 没什么好怕的。“快看！”奥拉夫指着天边一道流光说。“一块太空石头正穿过大气层燃烧起来！”“或者，”艾莎笑道，“你也可以只说那是颗陨星。”“流星，”克斯托夫靠在栏杆上、握住安娜的手补充道。

sentences.en: She squeezed it back. “A wishing star,” she said.
sentences.zh: 她回握了一下。“一颗许愿星，”她说。

sentences.en: But at that moment, standing with her friends, looking up at the brilliant light of the meteor shower arcing over Arendelle, Anna had nothing to wish for at all—because everything she could have wished for was right there beside her.
sentences.zh: 但那一刻，她和朋友们并肩而立，仰望划过阿伦黛尔上空的璀璨流星雨，却什么都不想许愿——因为凡是她所能企盼的，都已近在身旁。

chapters.title: 尾声
chapters.en:
ANNA DREAMED.

In the darkness, a single ember drifted. It tumbled endlessly through a void until, at last, it tangled in black branches. It pulsed, once, twice, and then, the spark began to lengthen. Like a salamander, the fire spread wide and flames began to crawl, creeping, illuminating an entire wood. First a twig, then a branch, then a tree. A tree, then a forest, then a world. Smoke and white-hot heat wrapped around the trees, twin ribbons that tightened and obscured. That tightened and choked. Screams rose, and the whole forest vanished in a plume of thick smoke, and then…A shift.

Anna dreamed.

Back into the void, and this time, the darkness moved. It slipped and slid, a rough whisper scraping against her ear. The darkness was not dark at all, but a never-ending desert of black sand. Sand filled her ears, her eyes, her nose, her mouth. She waded through, unable to see, unable to breathe, unable to know, and then…A shift.

Anna dreamed.

No longer rough, the sand melted, turning to liquid, growing heavy, and falling in a soft black rain to a great crater, until it brimmed, overflowing. The dark was an ocean now. Each slap of a wave left a swirling froth of white, brilliant against black water. Brilliant against the dripping mane of a midnight horse. The stallion reared from the Dark Sea’s deepest depths, screaming its freedom as it shrugged off the ocean’s weight and galloped across the waves toward her. Its heavy hooves drummed a rhythm that took over her heart, and then it bucked, and it was not Anna whom the horse chased, but Elsa. Its eyes glowed white as it bore down on her sister…

Anna woke up.

Her heart slammed against her chest as though she’d been running, and the questions scrolled through her mind: Was it happening again? Was the nightmare back? Anna felt a bit disoriented. It took her a moment to register that she wasn’t in her own room. She was in their parents’ room. That was right. She and Elsa had fallen asleep together after Anna sang one of their mother’s old lullabies, a favorite about a secret river. Elsa had seemed distracted and pensive during the night’s game of charades, so Anna had sung to bring a bit of lightness back into Elsa’s heart.

Anna stared up at the frothy canopy of the bed, and then glanced away. It looked too much like the white sea-foam that the rippling stallion had spat out as it galloped toward her. A water horse, she realized, reminding her of the statue outside the secret room.

Relief sighed though her. These were just normal nightmares, then. No wolf. The Nattmara was gone. She had nothing to fear. They were just a collection of images from the week’s events, from things around her home. There was no need to be afraid of her dreams, not anymore. And with that thought, Anna’s eyes slowly began to close…

And then they flew open. They had fallen asleep together. But Elsa was not there. Elsa wasn’t leaving Anna behind….She wouldn’t do that again. Right? Anna tried to keep calm. Elsa had probably gotten up extra early to tackle the stacks of papers waiting for her.

A breeze curled through the room, and Anna shivered. At least she knew why she was cold: the balcony door had somehow blown open while they had been asleep. Slipping out of Elsa’s bed, Anna grabbed their mother’s scarf from where Elsa had draped it across an armchair. Wrapping it around her shoulders, Anna stepped toward the balcony doors.

She expected to see what she always saw: the village ensconced in deep blue shadows, only punctured here and there by the orange flames of lanterns in the courtyard directly below. But as she drew closer to the balcony, a strange feeling flitted through her. An unease. A sense. Or, as Olaf might say nowadays, a “gut-wrenching trepidation.” She knew, in the way that maybe only a sister could know, that something was about to change forever. And when Anna stepped out onto the balcony, she saw that it already had.

The night glittered—the air glittered—the world glittered—as a million ice crystals of what looked like frozen rain hung suspended, like diamonds or glass shards that had forgotten gravity existed. Beautiful and sparkling. Fierce and deadly. Each crystal was razor-sharp, and each pointed in the same direction, toward a figure who stood far away, alone in the night.

“Elsa?”

Her sister stood in the twilight, the waves of the Arenfjord behind her. And though it should have been impossible for Elsa to see Anna from such a great distance, Anna saw her sister shift—and lock eyes with her.

A brilliant white light in the distance shattered the darkness, illuminating for a single breath the look of awe on Elsa’s face.

And then the ice crystals began to fall.

Anna flung herself away from the balcony, dashing through the halls and down the stairs. Her feet thudded against the flagstones. Reaching the bottom floor, Anna threw open the castle doors.

She stared at the ice crystals still suspended in front of her. “What?” she asked herself. The ice crystals filled the night with an eerie whistle as they tore through the air, only to end with a shout as they splintered across the cobblestones at her feet, making Anna’s path to Elsa slippery and dangerous. But when was it not? And when had it ever mattered?

Securing their mother’s scarf, she raced out into the streets to find Elsa. The wind tugged at Anna, it howled, and then—the lanterns blew out. Something was wrong. Anna passed villagers peering out of their suddenly dark homes. In the place where Arendelle’s flags always flew strong, they had gone deathly still.

Darkness, once again.
chapters.zh:
安娜做了个梦。

黑暗中，一粒火星飘荡。

它在虚空中无尽翻滚，终于缠进了黑色的枝桠。

它搏动了一下，两下，随后那火星开始拉长。

如蝾螈般，火势蔓延开来，火焰开始爬行、蔓延，照亮了整片树林。

先是一根细枝，再是一根粗枝，然后是一棵树。

一棵树，然后一片森林，然后一个世界。

烟与白热的烈焰缠绕着树木，像两条收紧、遮蔽视线的缎带。

收紧，令人窒息。

尖叫声四起，整片森林在一股浓烟中消失，然后……一转场。

安娜做了个梦。

回到虚空，而这一次，黑暗动了起来。

它滑溜溜地移动，粗糙的低语擦过她的耳畔。

那黑暗根本不暗，而是一片无边无际的黑沙沙漠。

沙塞满了她的耳、她的眼、她的鼻、她的嘴。

她在其中跋涉，看不见、喘不上气、无从知晓，然后……一转场。

安娜做了个梦。

沙不再粗糙，它融化成了液体，变得沉重，化作温软的黑雨落进巨大的陨石坑，直到坑满溢出。

此刻黑暗成了一片海洋。

每一记浪拍都留下打着旋的白色泡沫，在黑水上格外耀眼。

在午夜之马滴水的鬃毛上格外夺目。

那雄马从暗海最深处直立而起，嘶鸣着它的自由，抖落海水的重压，踏浪朝她疾驰而来。

沉重的蹄声敲出摄住她心跳的节律，随后它后蹄一蹬，追逐的竟不是安娜，而是艾莎。

它双眼泛白，朝姐姐逼近……安娜醒了。

她的心像刚跑过步般猛撞胸口，一连串疑问在脑中滚动：又要来了吗？

噩梦回来了吗？

安娜有点恍惚。

她过了片刻才意识到自己不在自己的房间。

她在父母的房间里。

对了。

她和艾莎是一起睡着的——安娜唱了一首妈妈的老摇篮曲，那是首关于隐秘河流、她们都喜欢的歌。

夜里玩猜词游戏时，艾莎显得心不在焉、若有所思，于是安娜唱起歌，想把一点轻盈重新带回艾莎心底。

安娜抬头盯着床上如浪花般的帐顶，随即移开目光。

那模样太像那匹奔腾的雄马朝她冲来时吐出的白色海沫了。

一匹水马，她意识到，这让她想起密室外的那座雕像。

她长舒一口气。

那么，这些只是平常的噩梦。

没有狼。

纳特玛拉已经消失了。

她没什么好怕的。

它们不过是这一周发生的事、家中周遭事物拼凑出的画面。

不必再害怕自己的梦了，再也不必了。

怀着这个念头，安娜的眼睛慢慢合上……随即又猛地睁开。

她们是一起睡着的。

可艾莎不在那儿。

艾莎不会把安娜丢下的……她不会再那样做了。

对吧？

安娜努力保持镇定。

艾莎大概是格外早起，去对付那些等着她的成堆公文了。

一阵微风在房中盘旋，安娜打了个寒颤。

至少她知道自己为什么冷：阳台门不知怎的在她们睡着时吹开了。

安娜溜下艾莎的床，抓起妈妈那条被艾莎搭在扶手椅上的围巾。

把围巾裹上肩头，安娜朝阳台门走去。

她料想会看到往常的景象：村庄沉在深蓝的阴影里，只有下方庭院中橘色的灯笼火苗零星刺破黑暗。

可当她走近阳台，一种奇怪的感觉掠过心头。

一丝不安。

一种预感。

或者，用奥拉夫现在的说法，一种“揪心的不安”。她以或许只有姐妹才懂的方式知道，有什么即将永远改变。

而当安娜踏出阳台，她看见改变已经发生。

夜在闪烁——空气在闪烁——世界在闪烁——仿佛百万枚像冻雨般的冰晶悬在半空，像忘记重力存在的钻石或玻璃碎片。

美丽而熠熠生辉。

凌厉而致命。

每枚冰晶都如剃刀般锋利，且都指向同一方向——一个远远伫立在夜色中的身影。“艾莎？”姐姐站在暮色里，身后正是阿伦峡湾的波浪。

尽管从那么远的距离，艾莎本不可能看见安娜，安娜却看见姐姐转过身——与她四目相对。

远处一道耀眼的白光撕裂黑暗，在刹那间照亮了艾莎脸上惊愕的神情。

随后冰晶开始坠落。

安娜从阳台猛地闪身，冲过走廊、奔下楼梯。

她的脚重重踏在石板上。

冲到楼下，安娜猛地推开城堡大门。

她盯着仍悬在面前的冰晶。“什么？”她问自己。

冰晶划破空气，给夜晚填上诡异的呼啸，最终在脚下的鹅卵石上碎裂、发出一声脆响，让安娜通往艾莎的路变得湿滑而危险。

可这条路何曾不如此？

而它又何曾要紧过？

她系紧妈妈的围巾，冲上街道去寻找艾莎。

风拉扯着安娜，呼啸着，随后——灯笼灭了。

出事了。

安娜走过纷纷从骤然变暗的家中探头张望的村民。

在阿伦黛尔旗帜永远高高飘扬之处，此刻却死一般寂静。

黑暗，再度降临。

sentences.en: The ice crystals filled the night with an eerie whistle as they tore through the air, only to end with a shout as they splintered across the cobblestones at her feet, making Anna’s path to Elsa slippery and dangerous.
sentences.zh: 冰晶划破空气，给夜晚填上诡异的呼啸，最终在脚下的鹅卵石上碎裂、发出一声脆响，让安娜通往艾莎的路变得湿滑而危险。

sentences.en: But when was it not?
sentences.zh: 可这条路何曾不如此？

sentences.en: And when had it ever mattered?
sentences.zh: 而它又何曾要紧过？

sentences.en: Securing their mother’s scarf, she raced out into the streets to find Elsa.
sentences.zh: 她系紧妈妈的围巾，冲上街道去寻找艾莎。

sentences.en: The wind tugged at Anna, it howled, and then—the lanterns blew out.
sentences.zh: 风拉扯着安娜，呼啸着，随后——灯笼灭了。

sentences.en: Something was wrong.
sentences.zh: 出事了。

sentences.en: Anna passed villagers peering out of their suddenly dark homes.
sentences.zh: 安娜走过纷纷从骤然变暗的家中探头张望的村民。

sentences.en: In the place where Arendelle’s flags always flew strong, they had gone deathly still.
sentences.zh: 在阿伦黛尔旗帜永远高高飘扬之处，此刻却死一般寂静。

sentences.en: Darkness, once again.
sentences.zh: 黑暗，再度降临。
